So we too should obey the commands of our magistrates: not only those which we can carry out to our own advantage, as when the laws prescribe to us the frequenting of the sacred sermons, or forbid mercenary service, luxury, usury and other such things, but also in those which are difficult and inconvenient, as when they command us to pay taxes often. 1 Peter 2 bids servants obey their masters even when they are harsh. Those Gentiles gave the Israelites more than the king asked for. How many today there are who defraud their magistrate, as regards public debts, saying that they are in any case wealthy enough!

units.la: Etsi vero in rebus quantumuis iniquis parendum sit, non tamen in illicitis & illis quæ salua conscientia à nobis fieri non possunt, qua in re multi grauiter errant, dicentes quid facerem? cogor eogor audire missas, procumbere ante idola, &c. expecto melio-ra tempora. Vita potius amittenda est, quàm vt hæc faciamus. Quid enim in huiusmodi casibus faciendum sit, exempla nos docent. Obstetrices Ægyptiorum Exod.1.cap. noluerunt mascu-los fœtus occidere, licet rex, qui in eos necis ius habebat, eis hoc imperaret. Serui Saulis 1.Sam.22. noluerunt Abimelechum & sacerdotes, quorum octoginta quinque erant, interficere, sciebant enim illis fieri iniuriam. Socij Danielis noluerunt Colossum adorare, à rege erectum. Dan.cap.3. Apostoli in Actis Apostolorum dicunt, Deo plus est obediendum, quàm hominibus. Martyres noluerunt idolis sacrificare, per fortunam Cæsaris iurare, &c. Magistratus non debebat petere à subditis suis, vt contra Deum facerent, cogitandum illis erat, se clientes Dei esse, cui reddenda sit ratio. Tanta autem est, proh dolor, subditorum cæcitas, vt fere in rebus illicitis suo magistratui obtemperent, in rebus iustis nequaquam, aut grauatim. Quæruntur magistratus interdum de inobedientia suorum subditorum, sed si ipsi prius Deo obtemperarent, vt hoc loco Cyrus fecit, qui cum audiret Deum velle, vt populum manumitteret, absque mora id fecit, etiam ipsi obedientiam à subditis suis, facilius impetrarent. Solomon quoque obsequentes habuit subditos, quamdiu Deo obedientiam debitam præstitit.
units.tr: Yet although one must obey in matters however unjust, one must not obey in what is unlawful and in what cannot be done by us with a clear conscience; and in this matter many go badly wrong, saying: "What am I to do? I am forced, I am compelled to hear Mass, to bow down before idols, etc.; I am waiting for better times." Life should rather be lost than that we do these things. For what must be done in such cases, the examples teach us. The midwives of the Egyptians (Exodus 1) would not kill the male offspring, although the king, who had the right of life and death over them, commanded them to do so. The servants of Saul (1 Samuel 22) would not kill Abimelech and the priests, of whom there were eighty-five, for they knew that a wrong would be done to them. The companions of Daniel refused to worship the colossus set up by the king (Daniel chapter 3). The apostles in the Acts of the Apostles say: "We ought to obey God rather than men." The martyrs refused to sacrifice to idols, to swear by the fortune of Caesar, etc. A magistrate ought not to ask his subjects to act against God; they must reflect that they are clients of God, to whom an account must be rendered. Yet, alas, such is the blindness of subjects that they generally obey their magistrate in unlawful matters, but in just matters not at all, or only with reluctance. Magistrates sometimes complain of the disobedience of their subjects; but if they themselves first obeyed God, as Cyrus did in this place, who, when he heard that God wished the people to be set free, did so without delay, they would more easily obtain obedience from their subjects too. Solomon also had obedient subjects for as long as he rendered due obedience to God.

units.la: Ex his gentilibus hæc discimus.
units.tr: From these Gentiles we learn the following.

units.la: 1. Quodnam sit vicinorum officium. Qui circum ipsos erant. Est vicinorum periphrasis. Iuuant eos suis opibus, ita hu-mani esse debemus erga vicinos, commoda eorum promouere, damna auertere. Interim non ad eorum scelera conniuendum est, sed emendanda sunt. Iuuant Iudæos, vt institutum iter possint conficere. Nos iter facientibus, humanitatem præstemus: eos amicè excipientes & dimittentes, monstrates errantibus viam. In primis qui viam vitæ ingressi sunt, non sunt retardandi. Multi similes sunt Pharisæis & Scribis illis Matthæi 23. qui cum ipsi nolint ingredi regnum cœlorum, alios quoque ab eius ingressu prohibent. Canes sunt in præsepi.
units.tr: 1. What the duty of neighbours is. "Those who were around them": this is a periphrasis for neighbours. They help them with their resources; so we ought to be humane towards our neighbours, advancing their advantages and turning away their harms. Yet we must not wink at their sins, but correct them. They help the Jews so that they can complete the journey they had undertaken. We ought to show kindness to travellers, welcoming them in a friendly way, sending them on their way, and showing the way to those who are lost. Above all, those who have set out on the way of life must not be held back. Many are like those Pharisees and Scribes in Matthew 23, who, though they themselves refuse to enter the kingdom of heaven, also prevent others from entering it. They are dogs in the manger.

units.la: 2. Ex eo quod plus contulerunt, quàm iusti erant facere, nimirum ad conseruationem pauperum, & templi ædificium, docamus nos quoque exercendam esse liberalitate erga pauperes, item ad conseruandas ecclesiæ ædificia. Sponte autem conferamus aliquid. Hilarem enim datorem amat Deus.
units.tr: 2. Since these men contributed more than they were bound to do, namely for the support of the poor and for the building of the Temple, we are taught that we too should practise generosity towards the poor, and likewise for the upkeep of the church buildings. Let us give something willingly, for God loves a cheerful giver.

units.la: 3. Typus etiam sunt vocationis gentium, à quibus ecclesia fuit extructa.
units.tr: 3. They are also a type of the calling of the Gentiles, by whom the Church was built.

units.la: { } Vicinorum officium.
units.tr: { } The duty of neighbours.

units.la: HOMILIA V.
units.tr: HOMILY V.

units.la: Cyrus Iudæis vasa templi restituit. 7 Rex autem Chores protulit vasa domus Iehovæ, quæ transtulerat Nebuchadnesar de Ierusalaim, & posuerat in domo Dei sui. 8 Protulit inquam eà Chores rex Paras per manum Mithredatis thesaurarij, qui numerauit ea ipsi Sesbasar principi tribus Iehudah. 9 Et iste numerus eorum: polubra aurea triginta, polubra argentea mille, cultri nouem & viginti: 10 Crateras aurei, triginta: crateras argentei, secundi, quadringenti & decem: vasa alia mille. 11 Omnium vasorum aureorum & argenteorum, quinque millia quadringenta: Omnia extulit Sesbasar quando ascendit captiuitas è Babel in Ierusalaim.
units.tr: Cyrus restores the vessels of the temple to the Jews. (7) King Cyrus also brought out the vessels of the house of the LORD, which Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem and put in the house of his god. (8) Cyrus king of Persia brought them out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, who counted them out to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah. (9) And this is their number: thirty gold basins, a thousand silver basins, twenty-nine knives, (10) thirty gold bowls, four hundred and ten silver bowls of the second sort, and a thousand other vessels. (11) All the gold and silver vessels numbered five thousand four hundred. Sheshbazzar brought all these up when the captives were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

units.la: IN tertia parte huius Capitis, commemoratur quod Cyrus sacra vasa, quæ Nabuchodonosor ex templo Hierosolymitano abstulerat, Iudæis restituerit.
units.tr: In the third part of this chapter it is recalled that Cyrus restored to the Jews the sacred vessels which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple of Jerusalem.

units.la: Vt autem hanc partem melius intelligamus, quædam altius repetenda sunt. In tabernaculo Domini, & postea in templo Salomonis, multa & varia vasa & vtensilia fuerunt ex auro, argento, ære, & alijs metallis. Exod. 27.30.38.3. Regum 7.2. Paralipomenon 4. Hæc ad diuersos vsus adhibita sunt, ad mactanda, excorianda, secanda, abluenda pecora sacrificijs destinata, ad excipiendum eorum sanguinem, coquendas carnes, item ad libationes, fumigationes. Breuiter, ad externù Dei cultum exercendum. Significatum autem fuit, in domo Dei non vnum genus hominum (qui vasa appellantur) dissimilia officia, & diuersa etiam dona esse: vtque vasa illa in prophanos vsus conuertenda non erant, ita homines polluere suum corpus non debere scortatione, ebrietate, crapula, 1. Thess. 4. Hæc est voluntas Dei sanctificatio vestra, &c. Hæc vasa & instrumenta Nabuchodonosor vt in vltimis Capitibus libri Regum, Chronicorum & Ieremiæ legitur, ex templo Hierosolymitano sustulit, primum cum Ioachimù, deinde cum Iechoniam filium eius abduceret, quod eo anno factum est. 2. Reg. 24. dicitur Iechonias egressus esse ad regem,
units.tr: To understand this part better, some things must be taken up from further back. In the tabernacle of the LORD, and afterwards in the temple of Solomon, there were many and various vessels and utensils of gold, silver, bronze and other metals (Exod. 27, 30, 38; 3 Kings 7; 1 Chron. 4). These were used for various purposes: for slaughtering, flaying, cutting up and washing the animals destined for sacrifice, for catching their blood, for boiling the flesh, and likewise for libations and incense. In short, they served for the outward worship of God. It was signified that in the house of God there are not only one kind of men (who are called vessels) with different duties, and also different gifts; and just as those vessels were not to be turned to profane uses, so men ought not to defile their bodies with fornication, drunkenness and gluttony (1 Thess. 4: "For this is the will of God, your sanctification," etc.). As we read in the last chapters of the books of Kings, Chronicles and Jeremiah, Nebuchadnezzar carried these vessels and instruments away from the temple of Jerusalem, first when he took Jehoiakim, and then when he led away Jehoiachin his son, which happened in that year (2 Kings 24, where it is said that Jehoiachin went out to the king).

units.la: vasa sacra gem, qui non modo regios thesauros abstulerit, sed & difcerpfe rit (ענ kazaz fignificar abscindere, detruncare, amputare) omnia vasa quæ fecerat Solomon in templo Dei, sicut loquutus fuerit Dominus. Hic locus non ita intelligendus est (vt obiter hoc dicam) quòd vasa comminuta sint, sed quòd parietes auro veltiti,sint detruncati,& ornamenta auulsa.
units.tr: Nebuchadnezzar not only carried off the royal treasures but also cut to pieces (the Hebrew word kazaz [קצץ] means to cut off, hack or lop) all the vessels that Solomon had made in the temple of God, just as the LORD had said. (To say this in passing: this passage should not be understood to mean that the vessels were crushed, but that the walls covered with gold were hacked and the ornaments torn off.)

units.la: Quomodo autem dicútur hæc vasa à Solomone facta,cum ab exteris & domesticis regibus, templum toties spoliatum fuerit,à Sefacho, Ioa, Achazo & Ezechias quoque thesauros templi hostibus dedit,vt eos placaret. Respondendum est,quæ ab alijs in locum eorú facta fuerút, nomine Salomonis fuisse appellata.
units.tr: But how can these vessels be said to have been made by Solomon, when the temple was so often plundered by foreign and domestic kings? Shishak, Joash and Ahaz plundered it, and Hezekiah too gave the treasures of the temple to the enemy to appease him. The answer is that whatever was made by others in place of those vessels was called by the name of Solomon.

units.la: Tandem post annos vndecim,vrbe direpta & incensa,hostis omnia sacra vasa abstulit,quæ reparata fuerant. Ifaias prædixerat Ezechiæ cum Babylonijs thesauros suos ostenderet, 4. Reg. 20.cap.& Ifa.39.fore vt Babylonij omnes thesauros regis & templi auferrent. Nabuchodonofor autem vasa illa non in propha nú usum conuertit, neq; illis adidololatriam vsus est,sed reposuit in templo Dei fui, cui hanc illustrem victoriam tribuit. Neque legitur velipfum hæc vasa inde protulisse, vel Euilmeroda chum filium eius. Balthaffar verò in luxurioso suo conuiuio, Danielis cap.5. proferri iussit,ex illis bibit,mirifice suorum deorum laudes prædicans. Illa autem ipsa nocte,capta Babylone,& hic thesaurus & alij,in Cyri potestatem peruenerunt.
units.tr: At last, after eleven years, the city was plundered and burned, and the enemy carried off all the sacred vessels that had been restored. Isaiah had foretold to Hezekiah, when he showed the Babylonians his treasures, that the Babylonians would carry away all the treasures of the king and of the temple (4 Kings 20; Isa. 39). But Nebuchadnezzar did not turn those vessels to profane use, nor did he use them for idolatry; he placed them in the temple of his god, to whom he attributed this splendid victory. Nor do we read that he himself or his son Evil-Merodach brought these vessels out again. But Belshazzar, at his riotous banquet, ordered them to be brought out (Daniel 5); he drank from them while extolling the praises of his gods with marvellous lavishness. And on that very night, when Babylon was taken, this treasure and the others came into the power of Cyrus.

units.la: Cyrus thesaurum illum quem bello acquisierat, protulit & per Mythridatem thefaurarium suum, Sesbazaro, hoc est, vt plerique voluntZorobabeli, qui cum primis Hierosolymam ascendit,numerari iussit. Videtur eius nomen mutatum.vt Danielis & sociorum eius. Vel,Sezbafar ille, dux viæ à rege Iudæis datus est:& etiam,vt videtur, præses,qui tamen Persicum imperium agnofcceret. De hoc infra 5. capite etiam legitur. Numeran tur pretiosiora particulatim: pelues, quibus hostiarum sanguis excipiebatur: cultri, quibus vtebantur ad secandas victimas illas,quarum pars sacerdotibus & offerentibus cedebat: phialæ, quarum vsus in libationibus,& alijs rebus fuit. Secundi.)Id est, inferioris dignitatis. Dicuntur vasa aurea & argentea in summa fuisse 5400. Si colligas summam eorum, quæ hic nominantur, non tot erunt,igitur preciofiora & maiora duntaxat per partes numerata sunt, quibus includuntur etiam minoris valoris seu pretij:tædiofum enim fuisset omnia sigillatim enumerare. Hæc omnia Sesbazar cum captiuitate,hoc est,captiuus ex Babylone Hierosolyma transtulit.
units.tr: Cyrus brought out the treasure which he had won in war, and through Mithredath his treasurer he ordered it to be counted out to Sheshbazzar, that is, as most think, Zerubbabel, who went up to Jerusalem among the first. His name seems to have been changed, as were the names of Daniel and his companions. Or else that Sheshbazzar was appointed by the king as leader of the way for the Jews, and also, as it seems, governor, though he nevertheless acknowledged the Persian empire. Of him we also read below in chapter 5. The more precious things are counted out one by one: the basins, in which the blood of the victims was caught; the knives, with which they cut up those victims, part of which went to the priests and to those who offered them; the bowls, whose use was in libations and other things. Of the second sort. That is, of lower value. The gold and silver vessels are said to have amounted in total to 5,400. If you add up the items named here, they will not come to that number; so only the more precious and larger items were counted out by name, and the smaller items of lesser value or price are included in them, since it would have been tedious to list everything one by one. Sheshbazzar brought all of these with the captivity, that is, the captive who was brought from Babylon to Jerusalem.

units.la: Quando ascendit captiuitas.) Vatablus interpretatur, quando summo desiderio, ac summa animi lætitia qui transmigrauerát in Babylonem, ascenderunt vt reuerterentur in Ierusalé. Verbum enim Hebræum in secunda coniugatione studium significare quoddam. Quale autem gaudium eorum fuerit quando Deus eos ab exilio reduxit, & in patriam restituit, exprimitur Psalm. 126. Cum reduceret Iehoua captiuitatem Sion, facti sumus tanquam somniantes. Tunc implebatur risu os nostrum, & lingua nostra exultatione: tunc dicebant inter gentes: Magna fecit Iehoua ad agendum cum istis, &c.
units.tr: When the captivity went up. Vatablus interprets it as: when those who had been carried into Babylon went up with the greatest longing and the greatest joy of mind to return to Jerusalem. For the Hebrew verb in the second conjugation signifies a certain eagerness. What joy they had when God led them back from exile and restored them to their country is expressed in Psalm 126: "When the LORD brought back the captivity of Zion, we were like those who dream. Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with rejoicing; then they said among the nations: The LORD has done great things for them," etc.

units.la: Facit autem hoc ad nostram consolationem, quod Deus illa vasa, quæ ad tempus tantum duratura erant tam diligenter conseruauit, in catalogum referri voluit, numerauit. Quanto enim maiorem fidelium suorum rationem habet, quorum comparatione hæc vasa nihil sunt? Ipse nouit suos, nomina eorum in librum vitæ retulit, numerauit pilos capitis ipsorum, nemo peribit ex illis, nemo rapiet eos ex manu sua.
units.tr: This also serves our comfort: that God wanted those vessels, which were to last only for a time, to be carefully preserved, recorded in a list and counted. How much greater an account, then, does he take of his faithful people, compared with whom these vessels are nothing? He knows his own, he has written their names in the book of life, he has numbered the hairs of their heads; none of them will perish, and no one will snatch them out of his hand.

units.la: Exemplum hoc loco regiæ beneficentiæ nobis commendatur, iure belli thesauri illi ipsius erant, potuisset dicere, Deus no auro & argento colitur, alioqui non passus esset, hæc vasa in hostium potestatem peruenire, & templum toties diripi: perinde fore si ligneis, fictilibus, aut æreis vtantur: non partitur cum illis vasa, sed cum primo cultui diuino dedicata intelligit, omnia Iudæis restituit. Neq; solum alios hortatur ad beneficentiam, sed ipse regiam beneficentiam ostendit.
units.tr: By this example we are commended to royal generosity. By the right of war those treasures were his own, and he could have said that God is not worshipped with gold and silver; otherwise he would not have allowed these vessels to fall into the power of enemies and the temple to be plundered so often; it would be the same if they used vessels of wood, clay or bronze. He does not divide the vessels with them, but, understanding them as dedicated from the beginning to the divine worship, he restored them all to the Jews. He not only urges others to generosity, but himself shows royal generosity.

units.la: Posteris quoq; temporibus, multi principes liberaliter suos opes ad Dei cultum profuderunt: magna monasteria extruxerunt, sperantes se hac ratione remissionem peccatorum merere. Et quamquam bono animo illos fumus fecerint: tamen hac via orbi Christiano plurima damna attulerunt. Monachi enim libertate & opibus, alios sub religionis plausibili titulo spoliarunt. Monasteria potius domus prædatoriæ fuerunt, quàm vt vulgo eas appellant, domus Dei. Nostra ætate non desunt, qui quod alij largiti sunt ad conseruationem cultus Dei, in priuatos vsus conuertant, & temere profundant.
units.tr: In later times too, many princes have lavishly poured out their wealth on the worship of God; they built great monasteries, hoping by this means to earn the forgiveness of their sins. And although they acted with a good intention, nevertheless by this way they brought very many harms upon the Christian world. For the monks, by their freedom and their wealth, plundered others under the plausible title of religion. The monasteries were rather plundering dens than, as they are commonly called, houses of God. In our own day there are not lacking those who turn to private uses what others have given for the maintenance of the worship of God, and squander it recklessly.

units.la: Ex hoc loco & alijs similibus, colligunt Papistæ, templa nostra auro, argento, gemmis ornanda, & in administratione Sacramentorum, pretiosis vasis vtendum, quia templū Dei his rebus fuerit ornatum. Respondemus, Deū hac pædagogia, rudem suum populū, & ad idololatriam proclinem, in suo cultu retinere voluisse, ne alibi illa ornamenta quærerent. Deinde hæc vasa aurea & ar&c argetea,in veteri Teftameto vsurpata quidé fuisse:sed Christi aduetu fuisse abrogata.Sublatis enim ceremonijs,huiusmodi in strumetis nihil amplius est opus.Vera tépli ornamenta sunt trà statio verbi diuini,preces, recta administratio Sacramétoru,be neficetia in pauperes,&c. Item si homines,qui sunt templu Dei exculti &ornati sintvera fide,dilestione,patietia,&alijs id gen*.
units.tr: From this passage and others like it, the Papists gather that our churches should be adorned with gold, silver and jewels, and that precious vessels should be used in the administration of the sacraments, because the temple of God was adorned with these things. We reply that God wanted to keep his rude people, and one prone to idolatry, in his worship by this kind of schooling, lest they should seek those ornaments elsewhere. Furthermore, these gold and silver vessels were indeed used in the Old Testament, but they were abrogated with the coming of Christ. For with the ceremonies removed, such instruments are no longer needed. The true ornaments of the temple are the preaching of the divine Word, prayers, the right administration of the sacraments, beneficence to the poor, and so on. Likewise, if the people who are the temple of God are adorned and beautified with true faith, love, patience and other such graces.

units.la: Ex historijsEcclefiasticis&Patru scriptis constat,primquam ecclesiam caruisse illo apparatu ceremoniarū. Temporibus demum Constantini Magni, ȧ veteri simplicitate &puritate ad externum cultū &ritus varios deflexit.PrimosChristianos in celebratione cœnę,ligneis vasis vsos esse,ipsemetGratianusin De creto testatur.Videbatur enim mysterium crucis Christi magis exprimi.Christus enim in ligno,vtPetrus dicit,hoc est,in cruce mortem pertulit.Circa annum Domini 370.cœpit vsus sacrorū vasorum ex auro & argento,liberalitate principum in ecclesias inuehi. Non quidem reprehendimus illas ecclesias,quæ aureis vasis in cœnæ Dominicæ administratione vtuntur, modo alij non vitio vertant,qui lignea retinent.Hac de re multa leguntur in scriptis Martyris, Vadiani, Bullingeri & aliorum,quæ hoc loco repetere superuacaneum esset.
units.tr: It is clear from ecclesiastical histories and the writings of the Fathers that the Church at first lacked that apparatus of ceremonies. It was only in the time of Constantine the Great that it turned from its old simplicity and purity to outward worship and various rites. That the first Christians used wooden vessels in the celebration of the Supper, Gratian himself testifies in the Decretum; for the mystery of Christ's cross seemed to be better expressed by them, since Christ, as Peter says, bore death "in the wood," that is, on the cross. Around the year of the Lord 370, the use of sacred vessels of gold and silver began to be introduced into the churches through the generosity of princes. We do not indeed reproach those churches which use golden vessels in the administration of the Lord's Supper, provided that others do not find fault with those who keep wooden ones. Much has been written on this subject by Martyr, Vadianus, Bullinger and others, and it would be superfluous to repeat it here.

units.la: Deinde accusant Papistæ, non solum in concionibus suis, sed publicis scriptis, Euágelicos principes & magistratus,quòd opes ecclesiæ & ornamenta, sacrilego ausu in prophanos vsus conuertant. Accusant concionatores Euangelicos,quòd suum magistratum ad sacrilegia perpellant. Felicianus Episcopus Scalensis,Ingolstadij hoc anno 1583. librum precationum,quas Carolus Caluus Imperator, Ludouici pij filius,sibi adolescenti pro quotidiano vsu, in vnum colligi, & literis aureis scribere mandarit: In honorem ac vsum ferenissimi Principis Maximiliani, Guilielmi vtriusq; Bauariæ ducis primogeniti,Latina lingua in lucem edidit,quem postea quidam in Germanicū sermo nem transtulit. In Præfatione ad Maximilianum Bauariæ ducem,scribit Carolo Caluo imperante, Ludouicum eius fratrem maiorem natu , Tiguri monasterium illustribus Virginibus construxisse, & magnis opibus ac preciofarum rerum thesau-ro honorificè donasse , quod postea successorum eius libera-litate & munificentia , cumulatius diuitijs & priuilegijs au-stum & decoratum sit : præfuisse ei monasterio omnium pri-mam Reginam Hildegardin , eiusdem Regis Ludouici funda-toris filiam , cui morienti statim successerit Bertha eius so-ror germana , quam Bertham consequutæ sint postea multæ aliæ abbatissæ longa temporum serie ac ordine subsecutæ ... ccedetes vsq; ad annum Domini 1524. quo tempore Catharina à Zimbe-ren vltima abbatissa & baronissa discedens, in eius locum potestate monasterium reliquerit. Addit anno Domini 1528. diebus Septembris 14. & Octobris 7. euacuato ecclesiæ sacrario, omnia cienodia aurea, argentea, & gemmis affabre facta atque ornata ingenti pretio & numero, à Tigurinis distracta & ablata esse, quorum catalogum ad libelli finem adijcit, vt quanta auri, argenti, gemmarum, sacrorum ornamentorum, & rerum aliarum praeciosarum vis & copia in eo monasterio fuerit, intelligi, & veterum principum pietas & religio percipi & considerari possit.
units.tr: Then the Papists accuse the evangelical princes and magistrates, not only in their sermons but in published writings, of sacrilegiously turning the wealth and ornaments of the Church to profane uses. They accuse the evangelical preachers of driving their magistrate into sacrilege. In 1583 at Ingolstadt, Felicianus, bishop of Scala, published in Latin a book of prayers, which Charles the Bald, emperor and son of Louis the Pious, had ordered to be collected for his young self for daily use and written in gold letters. He published it for the honour and use of the most serene prince Maximilian, first-born son of William, duke of Bavaria, and someone later translated it into German. In the preface to Duke Maximilian of Bavaria, he writes that in the reign of Emperor Charles the Bald, Louis, his elder brother, founded a monastery of illustrious virgins at Zurich and honoured it with great riches and a treasury of precious things. Afterwards, by the generosity and munificence of its successors, it was more abundantly enriched and adorned with wealth and privileges. Over this monastery the first ruler was Queen Hildegard, daughter of King Louis, its founder. On her death she was immediately succeeded by Bertha, her full sister, and after Bertha many other abbesses followed in a long succession of time and order ... down to the year of the Lord 1524, when Catharina von Zimmern, the last abbess and baroness, gave up the office and handed the monastery over into the power (of the city). He adds that on 14 September and 7 October 1528, the sacristy of the church having been emptied, all the golden and silver vessels and the objects made and adorned with gems, of great price and number, were sold and carried off by the Zurichers. He appends a catalogue of them to the end of the booklet, so that one may understand how great was the quantity of gold, silver, gems, sacred ornaments and other precious things in that monastery, and may perceive and consider the piety and devotion of the ancient princes.

units.la: Quis vero non videat hunc librum eo consilio ab eo editum, & catalogum rerum preciosarum in fine adiectum esse, vt vna eademq; opera Papisticam superstitionem alat & confirmet, & etiam Tigurinis odium & invidiam apud principes cöflet? Nam ab isto episcopo hic liber multis nobilibus hinc in dono missus est, &c. Respondeo ad illam episcopi narrationem, de voluntate & consensu abbatiss, monasterium hoc, vt alia quoq; in melio-rem vsum mutatum esse. Conuersum enim est ab amplissimo Senatu Tigurino in scholam & collegium, in quo aliquot bonarum literarum & artium studiosi adolescentes cum paedagogo alan-tur. Nō discessit abbatissa illa Tiguro, quōd iniuria esset affecta, vt iste innuere videtur, sed Euangelicam doctrinam amplexa, Eberhardo à Rischach, viro nobilitate generis & virtute praestanti, nupsit, ac ad finem vitæ vsq; Tiguri permansit, ibidemq; sepulta est. Res illæ preciose, quarū ille catalogum nescio quàm bona fide, contexit, aurum, argentum, vestes, ad subleuandam hominum necessitatem distractæ sunt. Quis negabit præstare, vt viuæ Dei imagines, hoc est, pauperes vestiantur, quàm lignea & lapideas? Peccarūt episcopi & sacerdotes, & graviter quidem, qui regibus, principibus & nobilibus persuaserunt, quōd Christus auro, argento, & preciosis anathematis, quæ ipsi mirantur & magnificiunt, per templa suspensis, coli velit.
units.tr: Who does not see that this book was published by him with this aim, and that the catalogue of precious things was added at the end, so that by one and the same effort he may nourish and confirm Papist superstition and also stir up hatred and envy against the Zurichers among the princes? For this bishop has sent the book as a gift to many noblemen here, etc. In reply to that bishop's account, I say that this monastery too was changed to better use, with the will and consent of the abbess. For it was converted by the most distinguished Senate of Zurich into a school and college, in which several young men devoted to good letters and the arts are maintained together with a tutor. The abbess did not leave Zurich because she had been wronged, as he seems to hint, but embraced evangelical doctrine, married Eberhard von Rischach, a man outstanding in noble birth and virtue, and remained at Zurich until the end of her life, and was buried there. Those precious things, whose catalogue he has put together with I know not how much good faith, gold, silver and garments, were sold to relieve the necessity of men. Who will deny that it is better for the living images of God, that is the poor, to be clothed, than wooden and stone images? Bishops and priests have sinned, and gravely, who persuaded kings, princes and nobles that Christ wishes to be worshipped with gold, silver and precious votive objects, hung up in the temples, which they themselves admire and magnify.

units.la: Quis thesaurorum ecclesiæ vsus sit, non est obscurum, conseruandi ex illis sunt ministri, alendi studiosi bonarum literarum, pauperes, ædificia necessaria ex his extruenda, pars ad futuras calamitates reponenda est. D. Ambrosius lib. Offic. 2. cap. 28. Qui sine auro misit Apostolos, etiam ecclesias sine auro congregauit. Aurum ecclesia habet, non vt feruet, sed vt eroget & subueniat in necessitatibus. Quid opus custodire, quod nihil adiuuat? Ignoramus quantū auri & argenti de templo Domini
units.tr: What the use of the Church's treasures is, is not unclear: from them the ministers are to be kept, students of good letters fed, the poor relieved, necessary buildings erected, and a part set aside against future calamities. St Ambrose, On the Duties, book 2, chapter 28: "He who sent the Apostles without gold also gathered the churches without gold. The Church has gold not so that it may lie idle, but so that it may be spent and give help in need. Why keep what does no good?" We do not know how much gold and silver was carried off from the temple of the Lord

units.la: Assyrij sustulerint? Nonne melius conflat sacerdos propter alimoniam paupernm, fi alia subsidia desint, quàm sacrilegus contaminata asportet hostis? Nonne difturus est dominus, Cur pauf es tot inopes fame emori? Et certè habebas aurum, vt mini ftraffes alimoniam. Cur tot captiui deducti in commertium sunt, nec redempti? cur tot ab hoste occisi sunt? Melius fuerat vt vasa viuentium seruares, quàm metallorum. His non posset responsum referri. Quid enim diceres? Timui ne templo Dei ornatus deesset. Responderet, aurum sacramenta non quærunt, neq; auro placent, quæ auro non emuntur. Ornatus sacramentorum redemtio captiuorum est. Et verè illa sunt pretiosa vasa, quæ redimunt animas à morte. Ille verus thesaurus est domini qui operatur quod sanguis eius operatus est, &c. Lege quæ de ornamentis templorum Laftant. de origine erroris lib. 2. cap. 4. scribit. Cum à Laurentio diacono quererentur thesauri ecclesiæ, promisit se demonstraturum: sequenti die pauperes adduxit, interrogatus vbi essent thesauri quos promiserat, ostendit pauperes, dicés: Hi sunt thesaurus ecclesiæ: testes sunt idem Ambrosius & Prudentius. Achatius Amidæ episcopus, vt legitur in Ecclesiastica historia, vasis aureis & argenteis, quæ ecclesia ex oblatione Christianorum habebat, diuenditis, exercitum captiuorum Persarum liberauit. Cyrillus episcopus Hierosolymis, vasa sacrata, quæ vela distraxit, vt furientem turbam aleret. Exuperantius episcopus Tolofanus à D. Hieronymo hoc nomine laudatur, quod nihil auri vel argenti in ecclesijs reliquerit, sed omne distribuerit in pauperes, ita vt corpus domini in canistro vimineo, sanguinem in vitro portarit. Idem alios episcopos fecisse legimus, quis verò eos vnquam sacrilegos vocauit? Hi laudantur quòd vasa sacris vsibus aptata distraxerint: Nunc vitio datur Christianis principibus, quod aurum idolis consecratum, in alimoniam pauperum conferunt, quos Christus è terris abiturus nobis commendauit. Veteres episcopos opibus ecclesiæ, donarijs, redditibus superfluis, pauperes consolatos esse & fouisse iam diftum est; hodie è diuerso exugunt pontificij pauperes, debita exigunt magna importunitate, vt templa diuis extruere, fimulachris & varijs instrumentis implere possint. Melius esse iudicant saxa, ligna vestire, quàm pauperes Christi. Alitur in monasterijs hinc inde, inutilis otioso-rum & libidinosorum hominum turba: An non præstaret homines tam indoctos, tam inertes, stiuæ admouere, quàm tam lautè in illis suis latibulis alere? Si quis nobis obijciat, contra fundatorum mentem & voluntatem, opes quas ecclesiis donarunt,in alios vsus transferri.Respondendum est temporum iniuria, illos omnino putasse se Deo gratum facere, si templa & monasteria locupletarent,eorum consilium fuit ad propagandam Dei gloriam illam cōferre.Nunc cūm ex verbo Dei didicerimus,Deū his externis non coli,sed in spiritu & veritate: Christum quoq; nobis hæc externa non comendasse, sed pauperes tanquam seipsum,nequaquam contra illorū voluntate agitur, si diuitiæ illæ superuacaneę templorum & donaria,in verè pauperes,non in illos otiosos ventres transferuntur.
units.tr: by the Assyrians? Is it not better for a priest to melt it down to feed the poor, if other resources are lacking, than for a sacrilegious enemy to carry off the defiled metal? Will not the Lord say, "Why do so many poor people die of hunger? Surely you had gold to give me food. Why were so many captives led away and not ransomed? Why were so many killed by the enemy? It would have been better for you to keep living vessels rather than vessels of metal." To this there could be no answer. For what would you say? "I feared that the temple of God would lack adornment." He would reply: gold does not seek sacraments, nor is it pleased by gold; things that are not bought with gold. The adornment of the sacraments is the ransom of captives. Truly those are precious vessels which redeem souls from death. That is the true treasure of the Lord, which accomplishes what his blood accomplished, etc. Read what Lactantius writes about the ornaments of temples, On the Origin of Error, book 2, chapter 4. When the deacon Laurence was asked for the treasures of the Church, he promised to show them. The next day he brought in the poor, and when asked where the treasures he had promised were, he pointed to the poor and said, "These are the treasures of the Church." Ambrose and Prudentius are the same witnesses. Achatius, bishop of Amida, as is read in the Ecclesiastical History, sold the golden and silver vessels which the Church had from the offerings of Christians, and freed an army of captive Persians. Cyril, bishop of Jerusalem, sold the sacred vessels, and even the veils, to feed a raging mob. Exuperantius, bishop of Toulouse, is praised by St Jerome for this, that he left no gold or silver in the churches but distributed it all to the poor, so that he carried the body of the Lord in a wicker basket and the blood in a glass. We read that other bishops did the same; but who ever called them sacrilegious? These men are praised because they sold vessels fitted for sacred uses. Now it is held against Christian princes that they bestow on the feeding of the poor gold consecrated to idols, the poor whom Christ, about to leave the earth, commended to us. The earlier bishops, as has already been said, comforted and cherished the poor from the wealth, offerings and superfluous revenues of the Church. Today, on the contrary, the Papist ministers squeeze the poor, demanding debts with great importunity, so that they may build temples to the saints and fill them with images and various instruments. They judge stones and wood better to clothe than the poor of Christ. In monasteries here and there is fed a useless crowd of idle and lustful men. Would it not be better to put such unlearned and sluggish men to the plough than to feed them so luxuriously in their hiding-places? If someone objects that the wealth which men gave to the churches is transferred to other uses, contrary to the mind and will of the founders, it must be answered that, given the circumstances of the times, they thought they were surely pleasing God if they enriched temples and monasteries; their intention was to devote those riches to the spreading of God's glory. Now that we have learned from the Word of God that God is not worshipped with these external things but in spirit and truth, and that Christ did not commend these external things to us but the poor as himself, it is by no means against their will when these superfluous riches of the temples and votive offerings are transferred to the truly poor, and not to those idle bellies.

units.la: Si qui sunt vel principes vel œconomi,qui opes illas non recte administrant , sed ea sibi retinent quæ non debebant, illos nequaquā defendo.Sed esto principes aliqui ,vulgares in vsus has opes conuertant,præstat tamen hoc fieri,quàm si ad superstitiones,imò idololatriam illis abuterentur, vt hactenus à Papanis factum est, cum ligna, ossa mortuorum auro inclusa,& preciosis margaritis & gemmis ornata,opere acu pictorio præparata fuerunt,lampades argenteæ,candelabra,vestes,varia instrumenta ecclesijs data. Coguntur principes inuiti interdum vti ecclesiæ thesauris propter Antichristi insidias,quas ipsis tendit,& propter bella quæ contra eos gerit, coguntur plurimos alere,quos Antichristiani suis possessionibus iniuste eijciunt, omnibusq; bonis spoliant , propter veram religionem, quòd truncos,panem,ossa ,adorare nolunt, nec papæ Romano diuinos honores tribuere.Quid igitur sacrilegos appellatis eos,qui opes sacras in meliores vsus conuertunt, vobis interim placetis,qui tam fœdè illis abutimini?Quot quæso bona,solo incorporationis vt vocatis titulo,ecclesijs eripuerūt monachi, quantus luxus in conuiuijs, vestitu,equis, & alijs apud vos episcopos conspicitur? Ne igitur illos traducatis apud principes & vulgus qui id fecerunt,quod ex sacris literis ,& veterum exemplis didicerunt,sed potius inspicite vestrum sinum , qui opes illas quas ex superstitione maximas corrasistis, pesime collocatis.
units.tr: If there are any princes or stewards who do not administer those resources rightly, but keep for themselves what they ought not, I by no means defend them. But even if some princes turn these resources to common uses, it is still better that this be done than that they be abused for superstitions, indeed for idolatry, as the Papists have hitherto done, when wooden objects and the bones of the dead, enclosed in gold and adorned with precious pearls and gems, prepared with needlework and painting, silver lamps, candelabra, garments and various instruments were given to the churches. Princes are sometimes compelled, against their will, to use the treasures of the Church because of the snares that Antichrist lays for them and the wars he wages against them. They are compelled to feed very many whom the Antichristians unjustly drive from their possessions and strip of all their goods for the sake of true religion, because they refuse to adore stumps, bread and bones, and to pay divine honours to the Roman pope. Why then do you call sacrilegious those who turn sacred wealth to better uses, while you yourselves are content to abuse it so foully? I ask you, what goods have the monks snatched away from the churches, under the mere title, as you call it, of incorporation? How much luxury is seen among you bishops in banquets, clothing, horses and other things? Therefore do not slander before princes and the common people those who have done what they learned from the Holy Scriptures and the examples of the ancients. Rather, look into your own bosom, you who have badly disposed of the great riches which you amassed from superstition.

units.la: Catalogus illorum qui in patriam suam redierunt & de donarijs ad templi instaurationem datis.
units.tr: A catalogue of those who returned to their homeland, and of the gifts given for the restoration of the temple.

units.la: Isti autem sunt filij prouinciæ, qui ascenderunt de captiuitate transmigrationis, quos transmigrare fecerat Nebuchadnefar Rex Babel in Babel: & reuersi sunt in Ierusalaim, & in Iehudah, singuli in ciuitatem suam.
units.tr: These are the children of the province who came up out of the captivity of the exile, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away into Babylon; and they returned to Jerusalem and to Judah, each to his own city.

units.la: 58 Omnes Nethinæi, & filij seruorum Selomoh, trecenti nonaginta duo.
units.tr: 58 All the temple servants, and the sons of the servants of Solomon, three hundred and ninety-two.

units.la: 59 Hi quoque qui ascenderunt de Thelmelah, Thelharsa, Cherub, Addan, Immer, qui non potuerunt indicare domum patrum suorum, & semen suum, an ex Israele essent.
units.tr: 59 These also who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Kerub, Addon, and Immer, but could not show the house of their fathers and their seed, whether they were of Israel.

units.la: 60 Filij Delaiah, filij Tobijah, filij Necoda, sexcenti quinquaginta duo.
units.tr: 60 The sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, the sons of Nekoda, six hundred and fifty-two.

units.la: 61 Et de filijs sacerdotum: filij Habaiah, filij Cos, filij Barzillai, qui accepit de filiabus Barzillai Giladitis uxorem, & vocatus est de nomine earum.
units.tr: 61 And of the sons of the priests: the sons of Habaiah, the sons of Koz, the sons of Barzillai, who took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called by their name.

units.la: 62 Hi quaesierunt scripturam suam, id est, genealogias: & non sunt inuenti, & elongati sunt à sacerdotio.
units.tr: 62 These sought their register, that is, their genealogies, and they were not found; and they were removed from the priesthood.

units.la: 63 Dixitque Thirsatha illis ne comederent de sanctitate sanctitatum, donec staret sacerdos cum Urim & Thummim.
units.tr: 63 And the Tirshatha said to them that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest stood up with the Urim and Thummim.

units.la: 64 Tota congregatio tanquam vir unus, quater decem millia atque duo millia trecenti sexaginta.
units.tr: 64 The whole congregation together, as one man, was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty.

units.la: 65 Præter seruos eorum & ancillas eorum, hi erant septem millia trecenti triginta septem. Erant autem illis cantores & cantatrices ducenti.
units.tr: 65 Besides their male and female servants, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; and they had two hundred singing men and singing women.

units.la: 66 Equi eorum, septingenti triginta sex: muli eorum, ducenti quadraginta quinque.
units.tr: 66 Their horses, seven hundred and thirty-six; their mules, two hundred and forty-five.

units.la: 67 Cameli eorum, quadringenti triginta quinque, asini, sex millia septingenti & viginti.
units.tr: 67 Their camels, four hundred and thirty-five; their asses, six thousand seven hundred and twenty.

units.la: 68 Et de principibus patrum, quum ingressi sunt domum Iehouæ, quæ erat in Ierusalaim, sponte obtulerunt in domum Dei, ut erigerent eam super basim suam.
units.tr: 68 And some of the heads of the fathers, when they came to the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem, offered freely for the house of God, to set it up in its place.

units.la: 69 Secundum vires suas dederunt in thesaurum operis auri drachmarum sexies decem millia & mille: argenti vero minarum quinq; millia: & tunicas sacerdotales centum.
units.tr: 69 According to their ability they gave into the treasury of the work sixty-one thousand drachmas of gold, five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priestly garments.

units.la: 70 Habitauerunt itaque sacerdotes, & Leuitæ, & de populo, & cantores, & ianitores, atque Netinæi in vrbibus suis, & vniuersus Israel in vrbibus suis.
units.tr: 70 So the priests, and the Levites, and some of the people, and the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the temple servants dwelt in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.

units.la: Dè Ræcedente capite in genere dictum est, Iudæos ex Babylone in patriam suam reuersos esse, iam per maximam huius capitis partem, catalogus eorum contexitur quem Nehemias repetit capite 7. Verùm quia maxime proprijs nominibus constat, nolui verba prælegere, domi qui volunt perlegant. In calce capitis, donaria recensentur primum & aliorum.
units.tr: Regarding the preceding chapter, it has been said in general that the Jews returned from Babylon to their homeland. Now for the greater part of this chapter, a catalogue of them is set out, which Nehemiah repeats in chapter 7. But since it consists mostly of proper names, I did not wish to read the words aloud; let those who want to read them through do so at home. At the end of the chapter, the gifts of the others as well as of the people are listed.

units.la: Habet hoc caput suam difficultatem. De multis enim nominibus dubitatur, an sint nomina propria virorum, an ciuitatum. Nam incolæ earum filij nominantur: sicut & ipsæ ciuitates nominantur filiæ: item hic catalogus ab illo in Nehemia non-nihil discrepare videtur.
units.tr: This chapter has its own difficulty. For in many names it is doubtful whether they are the names of men or of cities. For the inhabitants are named as sons, just as the cities themselves are named as daughters. Likewise, this catalogue seems to differ somewhat from that in Nehemiah.

units.la: Isti sunt filij prouinciæ (scilicet Babylonis qui diu habitarunt in Chaldæa, alij ad Iudæam referunt, quæ in formam prouinciæ redacta fuit. In catalogo ascendentium hic ordo seruatur. Primum commemorat auhor huius libri, vndecim ex præcipuis patribus seu patriarchis tribuum, qui nimirum duces fuerunt illius populi. Mox numerat populum, qui locorum tribus Iuda & Beniamin, & patrum nominibus appellatur. Postea Leuitas recensét, qui in suos ordines distincti sunt, in sacerdotes & Leuitas, & hi rursus in cantores, ianitores. His annumerantur Nethinæi, dati vel donati, id est, consecrati ministerio templi qui orti sunt à Gibeonitis, constituti à Iosue, postea à Dauide, vt ligna cederent, comportarent aquam ad sacrificia, Iosue 9.2. Samuelis 21. capite, & serui Solomonis, quorum officium fuisse videtur, vt templum fartum tectum conseruarent, & collapsa reficerent. Incerti & obscuri quoque numerantur, qui non potuerunt prosapiam suam indicare, an essent ex Israelitis nec ne: & quidam qui officium sacerdotale sibi vsurpare volebant, quorum maiores duxerant filias Barzilai Gileaditæ amici Dauidis, de cuius affinitate & genere gloriantes, voluerunt potius Berzalaitæ vocari quàm Aaronitæ, vt genus suum retinerent, atque sic memoria excidit ex catalogo sacerdotum. Hi scrutati sunt catalogum generis fui, quem quum inuenire non possent,reiecti sunt. Thirfatha mandauit illis, ne ederent de sanctitate sanctitatum,id est,cibis solis sacerdotibus concef-fis (vt erant aliquæ partes hostiarum, panes propositionis, &c.) donec staret sacerdos cum Vrim & Thumim,id est,donec veniret cui Deus reuelaret hanc rem, per instrumenta diuinationis sacerdotalis. Voluit enim Deus, vt habetur in Exodo & Leuitico, ne quisquam ad sacerdotale officium admitteretur,qui ex Aaronica familia ortus non effet. Per Thirfatam plerique Nehemiam intelligunt:id enim infra narratur, iussisse. Tandem ponitur summa omnium, dicuntur fuisse 42360.
units.tr: These are the children of the province (namely of Babylon, those who had long lived in Chaldea; others refer it to Judea, which was reduced to the form of a province). In the catalogue of those who went up, this order is kept. First the author of this book recalls eleven of the chief fathers or patriarchs of the tribes, who were evidently the leaders of that people. Next he counts the people, who are called by the names of places, the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and by the names of fathers. Afterwards he lists the Levites, who were distinguished into their own orders: priests, Levites, and in turn singers and gatekeepers. To these are added the Nethinim, the given or donated ones, that is, those consecrated to the temple ministry, who sprang from the Gibeonites, appointed by Joshua and afterwards by David to cut wood and carry water for the sacrifices (Joshua 9; 2 Samuel 21). Also counted are the servants of Solomon, whose duty seems to have been to keep the temple roofed and repaired and to restore what had fallen. Also counted, uncertain and obscure, are those who could not show their family line, whether they were of Israel or not; and some who wished to claim the priestly office for themselves, whose ancestors had taken wives from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, a friend of David. Boasting of this kinship and descent, they preferred to be called Barzillaites rather than Aaronites, in order to keep their stock, and so they dropped out of memory from the catalogue of priests. They searched the register of their family, and when they could not find it, they were rejected. The Tirshatha ordered them not to eat of the most holy things, that is, of the foods granted to the priests alone (such as some parts of the sacrifices, the showbread, etc.), until a priest stood up with the Urim and Thummim, that is, until someone came to whom God would reveal this matter through the instruments of priestly divination. For God willed, as is found in Exodus and Leviticus, that no one should be admitted to the priestly office unless he was born of the family of Aaron. Most understand the Tirshatha to be Nehemiah, for it is related below that he gave this order. Finally the sum of all is stated: they are said to have been 42,360.

units.la: Si colligas numeros qui hic politi sunt, non inuenies tantam summam. Dicendum est numerari qui ex cæteris quoque tribubus, fe tribui Iuda & Beniamin adiunxerant, illos in præcedente narratione non recensuit, in vnum vero numerum collectis, resultabit hic numerus :plures redierunt quàm abducti fuerint,de quo mox postea.
units.tr: If you add up the numbers given here, you will not find such a large total. It must be said that those who came from the other tribes, who had joined the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, were not counted in the preceding narrative. When they are gathered into one number, this total results: more returned than were carried away, a point I will take up shortly.

units.la: Videri potest hæc pars sterilis esse, tantumque continere nuda nomina hominum & locorum. At nihil est in sacris literis otiosum, quodque non fit à spiritu sancto proditum. Si nobis videntur loci nonnulli parum fructuosi, non illis, sed tarditati nostræ id est ascribendum. Ioannes Chryfoftomus de verbis Ifaiæ: Vidi dominum,homilia tertia, Scripturarum lectio est referatio cœlorum. Prophetarum ora,Dei sunt os. Hoc autem os nihil dixit obiter: quamobrem & nos non obiter & aliud agentes audiamus. Etenim fi hi qui fodiunt metalla, ne minima quidem fruftula prætereunt, verum vbi nacti sint aliquam auri venam, meatus omnes exactè circumspiciunt:multo magis nos hoc facere oportet in sacris scriptu-ris.Et mox:Hæc non temerè à me dicta sunt,neq; fortuito veni in eum sermonem.Sed quia sunt homines quidam opifices, qui posteaquam sacros libros in manus sumpserint, deinde vel reperererint vel annorum numerum positum,vel nominum catalogum,illico prætercurrunt,& incusantibus respondent: Nomina tantum sunt & non habent quicquam vtilitatis. Quid ais? Deus loquitur:& tu audes dicere,Dictorum nulla est vtilitas? Lege reliqua.
units.tr: This part may seem barren and to contain nothing but bare names of men and places. But nothing in the sacred letters is idle, and nothing is set down by the Holy Spirit without purpose. If some passages seem to us of little profit, that must be ascribed not to them but to our sluggishness. John Chrysostom, on the words of Isaiah, "I saw the Lord," homily three: "The reading of the Scriptures is a reflection of the heavens. The mouths of the prophets are the mouth of God. This mouth spoke nothing in passing; therefore let us also listen not in passing and while attending to something else. For if those who dig for metals do not pass over even the smallest crumbs, but once they have found some vein of gold, they examine every passage closely, we ought much more to do the same in the Holy Scriptures." And soon: "I have not spoken these things rashly, nor did I come to this discourse by chance. But there are certain workmen who, after they have taken the sacred books into their hands, then either find a number of years or a catalogue of names, and immediately run past them, and answer those who object: They are only names and have no usefulness at all. What do you say? God speaks, and do you dare to say that his words have no use? Read on."

units.la: Vsus huius loci.
units.tr: The use of this passage.

units.la: Ex eo quod nominatim recensentur, qui relicta Babylone,
units.tr: From the fact that those who left Babylon and returned to Jerusalem are named individually,

units.la: Hierosolyma in patriam redierunt; colligimus semper forte homines qui munnum & Antichristum deserentes, se veræ Ecclesiæ adiungant, & desyderio cœlestis patriæ tangantur, Deumque illorum non oblivisci: eosque semper suam laudem & gloriam habituros. Secundum illud Psalmi 112. In memoria æterna erit iustus. Quid non faciunt gloriæ cupidi homines, ut nomen magnum consequantur? Vide Valerium Maximum libro octavo de de Cupiditate gloriæ. Ediuerso illorum quoque nomina Deus tenet, qui relictis Hierosolymis, hoc est, vera Ecclesia, in Babylonem se conferunt, hoc est, deficiunt ad mundum & Antichristum, sive fracti præsentis vitæ ærumnis id faciant, sive spe commodorum.
units.tr: we gather that perhaps there are people who, forsaking the world and Antichrist, join themselves to the true Church, are moved by longing for the heavenly homeland, and that God does not forget them, and that they will always have their praise and glory. According to Psalm 112: "The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance." What will not lovers of glory do in order to obtain a great name? See Valerius Maximus, book eight, on the desire for glory. Conversely, God also keeps the names of those who, leaving Jerusalem, that is, the true Church, betake themselves to Babylon, that is, fall away to the world and Antichrist, whether they do this broken by the hardships of present life or in hope of advantages.

units.la: Quod tam multi nominantur & numerantur, argumento nobis est, quod Deus plures habeat in media Babylone, qui data occasione, se coniungant illis qui puriorem doctrinam profitentur: vel si non possint; animis tamen sunt coniuncti, summoque patriæ cœlestis desyderio teneantur. Sæpe Ecclesia ad paucos videtur redacta: sed Deus, sicut Heliæ temporibus, habet sua 7000. Lucæ 12. capite Dominus suos appellat pusillum gregem, quod respectu illorum intelligendum est, qui pereunt. Nam per se numerus credentium non est paruus. Apocalypseos 7, Cap. consignatorum ad salutem magnus est: numerus, &c.
units.tr: That so many are named and numbered is an argument for us that God has many in the midst of Babylon who, when the occasion is given, will join themselves to those who profess the purer doctrine, or, if they cannot, are nonetheless joined to them in heart and are held by a great longing for the heavenly homeland. The Church is often reduced to a few, but God, as in the days of Elijah, has his seven thousand. In Luke 12 the Lord calls his flock "a little flock," which must be understood with respect to those who perish; for in itself the number of believers is not small. In Revelation 7 the number of those sealed for salvation is great, &c.

units.la: Ad consolationem nostram facit, quod in hoc catalogo fit mentio mulierum, quanquam non nominatim, feruorum, ancillarum, hominum contemptorum & ignotorum atque obscurorum, qui genus suum indicare non poterant. Putant nonnunquam illi se propter indignitatem a Deo reijci, sed via omnibus in patriam cœlestem patet. 1. Timoth. 2. cap. Deus vult omnes homines saluos fieri, &c. Deus non respicit personas. Omnes item possunt aliquo modo iuuare ædificium templi.
units.tr: It serves our comfort that in this catalogue mention is made of women, although not by name, of male and female servants, of men who were despised and unknown and obscure, who could not show their family. Such people sometimes think that because of their unworthiness they are rejected by God; but the way into the heavenly homeland lies open to all. 1 Timothy 2: "God wills that all men be saved," &c. "God does not respect persons." Likewise all can in some way help to build the temple.

units.la: Ex eo quod illi qui genus suum indicare non poterant; ad officium sacerdotum non admissi sunt, discimus nę hodie quidem munus ecclesiasticum temere esse committendum hominibus ignotis & erroribus. Debent enim, ut Paulus in 1. ad Timotheum tertio Capite dicit, qui ad hoc munus vocantur, bonum habere testimonium ab exteris, ne in probrum incidant & laqueum calumniatoris. Capite quinto. Manus cito ne imponas, neque communices peccatis alienis. Sub Alexandro Seuero Imperatore, teste Ælio Lampridio, hæc consuetudo seruata fuit, vt nomen pastoris præficiendi ec-clefiæ alicui, publicè proponeretur, vt fi indignus effet, ab officio repelleretur.
units.tr: From the fact that those who could not show their family were not admitted to the priestly office, we learn that even today the ecclesiastical office must not be entrusted rashly to men who are unknown and of doubtful character. For, as Paul says in 1 Timothy 3, those who are called to this office ought to have a good testimony from outsiders, so that they do not fall into reproach and the snare of the slanderer. In chapter 5: "Lay hands on no one hastily, nor share in other men's sins." Under the emperor Alexander Severus, as Aelius Lampridius attests, this custom was observed: the name of the one to be set over a church as minister was published publicly, so that if he were unworthy he might be removed from office.

units.la: 5. Si catalogum consideres, videbis multò plures redijsse, quàm abductilegantur : creuit enim numerus eorum in Babylone, quo indicatur populum Dei non posse extingui. Crescit ecclesia perseguutione.
units.tr: 5. If you consider the catalogue, you will see that many more returned than were led away. For their number grew in Babylon, which shows that the people of God cannot be extinguished. The Church grows through persecution.

units.la: In calce huius Capitis, commemoratur quòd principes magnifica munera obtulerint ad templi ædificium. Simul hic iunguntur procerum & vulgi donaria, quæ in Nehemia seperantur. Aliquot ex præcipuis patribus siue Patriarchis tribuum, cum ingresi sunt templum, vel potius ruinas vbi templum steterat, obtulerunt de opibus suis munera, vt illud ab iis fundamentis instaurarent. Pro virili autem sua, hoc est, pro facultatibus suis, contulerunt in thesaurum operis, id est, templi aurum, argentum & vestes sacerdotales centum. Ponderum & mensurarum ratio nobis non certo constat, fortasis in capti uitate retinuerunt sua pondera & mensuras.
units.tr: At the end of this chapter it is recorded that the princes offered magnificent gifts for the building of the temple. Here the gifts of the leaders and of the common people are joined together, which in Nehemiah are set apart. Some of the chief fathers, or rather patriarchs, of the tribes, when they entered the temple, or rather the ruins where the temple had stood, offered gifts from their own resources so that they might restore it from its foundations. According to their means, that is, according to their substance, they contributed to the treasury of the work, namely gold, silver, and one hundred priestly garments. The standard of weights and measures is not certainly known to us; perhaps they kept their own weights and measures during the captivity.

units.la: Hinc discimus principum officium esse, vt plebi bono exemplo præeant; & templi instaurandi studio flagrent.
units.tr: From this we learn that it is the duty of princes to go before the common people with a good example, and to burn with zeal for restoring the temple.

units.la: Deinde habes liberalitatis (vt supra in Cyro) religiosæ, insigne exemplum. Sicut illi principes de suis opibus obtulerunt munera, aurum, argentum, vestes, non coacte, sed sua sponte & liberaliter, vt templum ædificaretur: ita hodie viri opulenti & illustres faciant. Deus non quidem vult amplius externa templa fumtuosa ornari, sed potius templa viua, hoc est, pauperes. Licet autem dies non sis, potes tamen & tu aliquid in viua tem pla conferre. Vt cum consolaris pauperes, eosque instruis, dasillis eleemosynam, quam patres spiritualem vocant. Quanto vero nunc sceleri fe astringunt, sacrilegi; item qui alios quibus opem ferre debebant, suis opibus & vita interdum spoliant.
units.tr: Next you have a notable example of religious generosity, as in Cyrus above. Just as those princes offered gifts from their own resources, gold, silver, and garments, not under compulsion but of their own accord and freely, so that the temple might be built, so let wealthy and distinguished men do today. God does not indeed wish church buildings to be adorned any more with costly externals, but rather living temples, that is, the poor. Although you are not a prince, you too can contribute something to the living temples: when you console the poor, instruct them, and give them alms, which the Fathers call spiritual alms. How much more do those now bind themselves to wickedness, the sacrilegious, and likewise those who sometimes plunder of their goods and even of their lives those whom they ought to be helping.

units.la: CAPUT III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: HOMILIA VII.
units.tr: HOMILY VII.

units.la: Altare extruunt.
units.tr: They set up the altar.

units.la: Vum, aduenisset mensis septimus, essent filij Israelis in srbibus, congregati sunt populus D 3. canquam vir vnus in Ierusalaim.
units.tr: Now when the seventh month had come, and the children of Israel were in their cities, the people gathered together as one man at Jerusalem.

units.la: 2 Tum surrexit Iesua filius Iosadac, & fratres eius sacerdotes, & Zerubabel filius Sealthiel, & fratres eius, aedificauerunt altare Dei Israelis, vt offerret super illud holocausta, sicut scriptum est in lege Moseh viri Dei.
units.tr: Then Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and his brethren the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and his brethren, rose up and built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings upon it, as it is written in the law of Moses the man of God.

units.la: 3 Firmauerunt autem altare super illud bases suas, quod timerent sibi a populis terrarum: & obtulerunt super illud holocausta Iehovae, holocausta (inquam) mane & vesperi.
units.tr: Though they were afraid of the peoples of the lands, they set the altar firmly on its bases, and offered upon it burnt offerings to the LORD, burnt offerings morning and evening.

units.la: DIXIMVS Cyrum concessisse reditum in patriam Iudaeis, vt templum Deo suo construant, mox aliquot viam ingressos, qui postea 2.cap.nominantur & numerantur: iam hoc Capite audiemus, quomodo se accinxerint ad aedificandum templum.
units.tr: We have said that Cyrus allowed the Jews to return to their homeland so that they might build the temple for their God, and that soon afterwards some set out on the journey, who are named and counted later in the second chapter. In this chapter we shall now hear how they girded themselves to build the temple.

units.la: 2. Populus conuenisse scribitur Hierosolymis, ex omnibus vrbibus in quibus confederat. 2. Mox altari instaurato, sacrificarunt & celebrarunt festum tabernaculorum. 3. Conductis artificibus, operam dederunt vt ligna & lapides conueherentur: exactores item operis constituerunt. 4. Iactis fundamentis templi, Iudaei varie affecti sunt.
units.tr: (1) The people are said to have assembled at Jerusalem from all the cities in which they had settled. (2) Soon after the altar was restored, they offered sacrifices and kept the Feast of Tabernacles. (3) They hired craftsmen and saw to it that timber and stones were carried in; they also appointed overseers of the work. (4) After the foundations of the temple were laid, the Jews were variously affected.

units.la: 1. Primo loco Iudaei reuersi ex captiuitate Babylonica (vt in fine superioris Capitis audiuimus) se in suas vrbes contulerunt, ibi occupati, nimirum circa res domesticas, aliquandiu morati sunt, tandem accedente mense 7. congregati sunt Hierosolymis: nimirum vt consultarent de extruendo templo, & Deo publicè gratias agerent. Mensis septimus Thisri appellatur, & partim Septembri, partim Octobri nostro respondet. Antequam Israelitae exAegypto egressi sunt, fuit primus mensis. Quo mense viam ingressi sint, aut in Iudaeam peruenerint, non exprimitur, forte primo aut secundo. Qui cum liberis, vxoribus, & impedimentis se itineri committunt, tarde, progrediuntur. De Ezdra legitur, quod quinto demum mense ex Persia in Iudaeam peruenerit: longè enim ab ea distat.
units.tr: First, the Jews who had returned from the Babylonian captivity (as we heard at the end of the previous chapter) went to their own cities. There, occupied, no doubt, with household affairs, they stayed for some time; at last, when the seventh month came, they gathered at Jerusalem, namely to consult about building the temple and to give public thanks to God. The seventh month is called Tishri, and corresponds partly to our September and partly to October. Before the Israelites left Egypt, it was the first month. It is not stated in which month they set out on the journey or reached Judea, perhaps the first or second. Since they travelled with children, wives and baggage, they advanced slowly. We read that Ezra reached Judea from Persia only in the fifth month, for it is a long way off.

units.la: Quifuir vnus.) Hoc est, Omnes, nullo excepto, Hierosolymis conuenerunt. Vel, de animorum coniunctione haec phrasis intelligitur, quod omnes vnanimes & concordes fuerint. Actorum 4.de primaeua ecclesia scribitur: Multitudinis autem credentium erat cor vnum & anima vna, &c. Si instaurandum
units.tr: Who were as one man. That is, all of them, without exception, came together at Jerusalem. Or this phrase is understood of the union of their minds, that they were all of one accord and harmony. Of the early Church Acts 4 says: "The multitude of those who believed were of one heart and one soul," etc.

units.la: Mensis 7.
units.tr: The seventh month.

units.la: Concordia. randum est templum Dei, requiritur concordia. Hanc ob cau-fam Christus & difcipu'i eius, concordiæ & charitatis studium vrgent. In Euangelio Ioannis tessaram Christianorum charitatem constituit. i.ad Corint.12.Ephef.4. Dolendum est quód ho die inter illos qui vnam eandemq; religionem profitentur,tan-ta sint certamina, quibus ædificium ecclesiæ impeditur : multi enim deficiunt iterum à vera religione ad Papatum, vel Papatum mordicus retinent, dicentes,Se expectaturos donec ipsis Euangelicis interse conueniat, & priusquam de religione aliquid statuant. Multi religionem fusq; deq; ferunt, Epicurei & Athei potius quàm Christiani euadunt. Politijs etiam conseruandis necessaria est vera concordia. Christus enim dicit, nullum regnum inter se diuisum consistere. Micipsæ verba ad filios suos apud Salustium nota sunt: Ego regnum vobis trado firmū, si boni, hoc est, cóicordes eritis, (sequentia enim ostendūt, hæc verba ita exponeda esse) sin mali,id est,discordes,infirmū. Nam concordia paruæ res crescunt, discordia maximæ dilabuntur. Iustinus lib.8. scribit, Philippum Græcos discordes fecisse, postea sua libertate eos spoliasse. Turci propter mutuam concordiam, ex humili conditione, ad tantam potentiam conscenderunt,& propter discordiam Christianorum, in Europam venerunt. Oeconomiæ quoq; concordia est necessaria, corpus enim morbo infestum, nihil agere potest, ita si pestis perniciosa discordia, familiam aliquam corripiat. Accusant quidam prædicationem Euangelij, quód turbas excitet, in quos merito culpa retorqueri potest: nolunt enim Deo obedire. Nihil autem cótra Dei mandata faciendum est, vt concordia conseruari possit.
units.tr: Concord. If the temple of God is to be rebuilt, concord is required. For this reason Christ and his disciples urge the pursuit of concord and love. In the Gospel of John he establishes Christian love as the mark (of his disciples); see 1 Corinthians 12 and Ephesians 4. It is to be lamented that today among those who profess one and the same religion there are such great quarrels that the building of the Church is hindered. Many fall away again from the true religion to Papacy, or cling stubbornly to Papacy, saying that they will wait until the evangelical men agree among themselves, and before they decide anything about religion. Many treat religion carelessly and become Epicureans and atheists rather than Christians. True concord is also necessary for preserving commonwealths. For Christ says that no kingdom divided against itself can stand. The words of Micipsa to his sons in Sallust are well known: "I hand over to you a kingdom that is firm if you are good, that is, if you are of one mind" (for what follows shows that these words should be explained this way), "but weak if you are bad, that is, divided." For by concord small things grow, by discord the greatest things fall apart. Justin, in book 8, writes that Philip made the Greeks discordant and afterwards robbed them of their liberty. The Turks, by mutual concord, rose from a humble condition to such power, and because of the discord of Christians they came into Europe. Concord is also necessary for household management: just as a body infected with disease can do nothing, so a ruinous discord, like a plague, seizes any family. Some accuse the preaching of the Gospel of stirring up disturbances; but blame can rightly be turned back upon them, for they are unwilling to obey God. Nothing, however, must be done against God's commands if concord is to be preserved.

units.la: Secundo agitur de extructione altaris, quando, à quo, cui, vbi, quomodo & quare extructum fit. Priusquam templum ædificare cepissent, surrexerunt Iefua & fratres eius, item Zerubabel, & extruxerunt altare Domino. Iefua filius Iozedek fuit, nepos Saraiæ, quem Nabuchodonosor capite truncauit, & fratres eius, vel secundum naturam, vel collegæ eius, & Zerubabel filius Sealthiel.) non generatione, vt Vatablus annotat, siue natura: sed educatione. Educarat eum, Sealthiel patruus suus: erat igitur pater ipsius nutritius, vel ab eo adoptatus fuit. Ioachim filius Iofiæ, genuit Iechoniam, Iechonias vero Sealthiel & Phedaiam, Phedaias Zerobabelem, 1.Paralip. 3. Propheta Haggæus Zerobabelem etiam filium Sealthielis vocat, cum reuera nepos eius fuerit ex fratre Phedaia, qui verus eius pater fuit. Illi extruxerunt altare Domino. Discunt hoc exemplo, ministri ecclesiæ & proceres Reipublicæ vt curam gerant veræ religionis & veræ cultus acfpiritualis templi ædificationem, consentientibus animis vrgeant. Plurimum enim refert illos ordines vnanimes esse. Deinde ex hoc loco & aliis intelligitur quod quando Deus præcipit honorandos esse parentes, non solum illos intelligat à quibus orti sumus, sed & qui nos educarunt, & beneficia nobis contulerut.
units.tr: Second, the passage deals with the building of the altar: when, by whom, for whom, where, how and why it was set up. Before they began to build the temple, Jeshua and his brethren rose up, and likewise Zerubbabel, and they built an altar to the LORD. Jeshua was the son of Jozadak, grandson of Seraiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar put to death. His brethren were either his brothers by nature or his colleagues. Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel: not by begetting, as Vatablus notes, or by nature, but by upbringing. Shealtiel his uncle had brought him up, so that his foster-father was his father, or he had been adopted by him. Jehoiakim the son of Josiah begot Jeconiah; Jeconiah begot Shealtiel and Pedaiah, and Pedaiah begot Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 3). The prophet Haggai also calls Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, though in fact he was his grandson through his brother Pedaiah, who was his true father. They built an altar to the LORD. From this example, ministers of the Church and the leaders of the commonwealth learn to take care of true religion, and with united minds to press on the building of the true worship and of the spiritual temple. For it matters greatly that those orders be of one mind. Further, from this place and others it is understood that when God commands that parents be honoured, he means not only those from whom we were born, but also those who brought us up and conferred benefits upon us.

units.la: In ijsdem fundamentis, quæ olim à Salomone iacta erant, in atrio fecerdotum, ante Hechal, sub diuo altare illud constituerunt. Finis, vt super illud altare, holocausta offerrent,
units.tr: On the same foundations that Solomon had once laid, in the court of the priests, before the Hechal, they set up that altar in the open air. The purpose was that they might offer burnt offerings upon that altar.

units.la: Addit, Sicut scriptum est in lege Mosis vir Dei.) Quemadmodum Deus præceperat in Exodo, Leuitico & libro Numerorum. Non enim bona, vt vocant, intentione in cultu Dei vtendum; sed verbum Dei est sequendum. Etenim quæ nobis placent, plerunque Deo displicent. Dauid bona intentione templum ædificare voluit, adhibito in consilium Nathane propheta. Saul bona intentione pingues pecudes in holocaustum ferauerat, sed hoc pugnabat cum iussu & mandato Domini.
units.tr: He adds: As it is written in the law of Moses the man of God. As God had commanded in Exodus, Leviticus and the book of Numbers. For God is not to be worshipped with what are called good intentions, but the Word of God must be followed. For what pleases us is very often displeasing to God. David wished to build the temple with a good intention, taking the prophet Nathan into his counsel. Saul, with a good intention, had spared the fat sheep to offer in sacrifice, but this was contrary to the command and order of the LORD.

units.la: Moses vir Dei hoc loco vocatur. Vnde elicimus, quid de Mose & aliis prophetis sentiendum, quamq; honorificè de ipsis loquendum sit. Iosue 14. Calebus quoque Mosem vocat virum Dei. 1. Paralipom. 23. etiam nominatur, vt aliis multis in locis, seruus Dei. Hodie viros Dei, hæreticos vulgo vocant, hostibus interim ecclesiæ tantum non diuinos honores tribuentes.
units.tr: Moses is here called the man of God. From this we gather what should be thought of Moses and the other prophets, and how honourably they ought to be spoken of. Joshua 14: Caleb also calls Moses the man of God. In 1 Chronicles 23 he is named, as in many other places, the servant of God. Today men commonly call heretics the men of God, while giving almost divine honours to the enemies of the Church.

units.la: Non distulerunt ædificationem altaris, donec templum ex tructum esset. Quoniam terror populorum terræ erat super eos.) Quotidie audiebant vicinorum minas, quod eos oppressuri essent. Solet enim Satan miris artibus & varijs rationibus, per suos satellites ædificio templi, & aliis sanctis operibus, se opponere & varia impedimenta obijcere. At quanto rabiosius illi grassantur, tanto maiore diligentia Dei negotia procurari debent. Multi rebus duris & periculosis, multa aduersarijs concedenda putant, ne magis exasperentur, qui extructionem altaris in aliud tempus reiecissent. Populus verò Dei festinat, vt cum holocaustis preces fundens ad Deum, ipsius auxilium contra hostes suos impetret.
units.tr: They did not delay building the altar until the temple was finished. Because the fear of the peoples of the land was upon them. Every day they heard the threats of their neighbours, that they would oppress them. For Satan is wont, by wonderful arts and various devices, through his henchmen to oppose the building of the temple and other holy works, and to throw in various hindrances. But the more savagely these men rage, the greater diligence ought to be applied to the affairs of God. Many think that in hard and dangerous times many concessions should be made to adversaries, lest they be exasperated more; but those who had put off the setting up of the altar had done so. The people of God, however, hastens to obtain, by offering burnt offerings and pouring out prayers to God, his help against their enemies.

units.la: Obtulerunt quotidie holocausta Domino, holocausta matutina & vespertina. Exod. 29. Leuit. 6. Num. 28. Singulis diebus mane & vesperi agni duo offerebantur: appellatur autem iuge sacrificium. Adumbrabat Christum, de quo Ioannes Baptista dicit: Ecce agnus ille Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi. In Apocalypsi dicitur agnus qui occisus sit ab origine mundi. Sacrificium enim semel peractum in cruce, omnes expiat à peccatis. De sacrificijs alio loco agemus.
units.tr: They offered burnt offerings to the LORD every day, morning and evening burnt offerings (Exodus 29; Leviticus 6; Numbers 28). Two lambs were offered every day, morning and evening; this is called the continual sacrifice. It foreshadowed Christ, of whom John the Baptist says: "Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world." In the Apocalypse he is called the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world. For the sacrifice once offered on the cross expiates all from sins. We shall treat of sacrifices in another place.

units.la: Dicendum iam aliqui d est de altaribus, id est, locis in quibus Deo sacrificia fiebant. Grammatici hanc differentiam statuunt inter altare & aram : quòd altaria tantùm superis, aræ inferis & superis Dijs constitutæ fuerint. Ab altitudine altaria dicta, quòd veteres Dijs superis in ædificijs à terra erectis ; dijs terrestribus in terra, dijs inferis in effosa terra sacrificia faciebant. Aræ verò dictæ quasi ansæ, ab ansis quas habuerunt. Quidam ab ardore deducút: vel quòd sicut aræ in vrbe puræ sunt, vel esse debent: ita etiam aræ Deorum. Ego aram ab αἴρειν dictam putarem, à tollendo, quia est ædificium è terra exaltatum, vel altum quid à terra. De altaribus vide plura apud Gyraldum de dijs gentium syntag. 17.
