Græcè dicitur βωμὸς & θυσιαστήριον. Ara suffimenti θυσιαστήριον τῶ θυμιατῶ. Est autem altare, locus sacrificijs offerendis dicatus, in quo animalia destinata immolantur, vel odores incenduntur. Cain & Abel primi sacrificasse leguntur, ille de frugum primitijs, hic de gregibus, de altaribus verò quibus vsi sunt, nihil commemoratur. Noe primus omnium altare extruxisse, & super illud holocaustum Domino obtulisse in Genesi legitur. Postea Patriarchæ sua altaria habuerunt, ad quæ constitutis diebus suos conuocasse, & eos de religione instituisse, admodum est probabile. Sacerdotio institu-to, Aaron cum filijs, deinde alij sacrificarunt. Non autem alio in loco id licebat (nisi Dei dispensatione) quàm vbi tabernaculum & postea templum erat. Duo autem altaria duntaxat Dei populus habuit. Primum, altare holocaustorum. מזבח vel mizbeach Heb. quòd super illud holocausta sacrificarentur: alterum altare suffimenti. מקטר mikthar ab adolendo, quòd odores in eo adolerentur. De forma & materia illorum altarium, vide lib. Mosis.
units.tr: Now I must say something about altars, that is, the places where sacrifices were offered to God. The grammarians draw this distinction between altare and ara: altars were set up only for the gods above, while altars (arae) were set up for both the gods below and the gods above. Altaria are named from their height, because the ancients offered sacrifices to the heavenly gods on structures raised above the earth, to the earthly gods on the ground, and to the gods below in dug-out earth. Arae, however, are named as if from ansae, the handles they had. Some derive the word from ardor (heat): either because the altars in a city are, or ought to be, pure, and so too the altars of the gods. I would rather think ara comes from airein [αἴρειν], to lift up, because it is a structure raised from the earth, or something high above the ground. On altars see more in Gyraldus, On the Gods of the Gentiles, Syntagma 17. In Greek the altar is called bomos [βωμὸς] and thysiasterion [θυσιαστήριον], and the altar of incense thysiasterion tou thymiatou [θυσιαστήριον τοῦ θυμιάματος]. An altar is a place dedicated to the offering of sacrifices, where the animals designated for the purpose are slaughtered or incense is burned. We read that Cain and Abel were the first to sacrifice: the one from the first fruits of the crops, the other from his flocks; but nothing is recorded about the altars they used. In Genesis we read that Noah was the first of all to build an altar and to offer a burnt offering to the Lord upon it. Afterwards the patriarchs had their own altars, at which, it is quite probable, they gathered their households on appointed days and instructed them in religion. Once the priesthood was instituted, Aaron with his sons offered sacrifices, and then others did. Yet this was not permitted in any other place (except by God's arrangement) than where the tabernacle and afterwards the temple stood. God's people had only two altars. The first was the altar of burnt offerings, Hebrew mizbeach [מזבח], because burnt offerings were sacrificed upon it. The second was the altar of incense, Hebrew mikthar [מקטר], from adolere (to burn), because incense was burned on it. On the form and material of those altars, see the book of Moses.

units.la: Quia verò illa externa sacrificia, in Christo abolita sunt, etiam altaria locum non amplius habent in ecclesia. Paulus dicit ad Heb. 13. altare nostrum Christum esse: in quo offerendæ sunt preces nostræ. Ipse enim dicit, Quicquid petieritis patrem meum in nomine meo, accipietis. Ad Cœnæ dominicæ administrationem requiritur mensa, quæ lignea ne an lapidea esse debeat, nolumus cum quoquam contendere. Hoc enim liberum fuisse ecclesijs, non dubitamus.
units.tr: But since those outward sacrifices have been abolished in Christ, altars also no longer have a place in the Church. Paul says in Hebrews 13 that Christ is our altar, on which our prayers are to be offered. For he himself says: "Whatever you ask the Father in my name, you will receive." For the administration of the Lord's Supper a table is required; whether it ought to be wooden or stone we do not wish to contend with anyone about. For we do not doubt that this was left free to the churches.

units.la: {E} Antichristus vero,vt alias ceremonias iam abolitas reduxit, ita etiam altaria: imò illa multiplicauit, & in illis Christi corpus à sacerdotibus pro viuis & defunctis in missę celebratione dicit offerri.Nullum est templum celebre, in quo non sint multa altaria,in superiore parte,in inferiore,etiá in cryptis sub terra. Iam nil dicam de aris fixis & portatilibus in priuatis ædibus.Etenim quia monachorum & sacrificorû ac monialium numerus in immensum creuit,templorû etiam & monasteriorû, otiosi illi homines,sua hypocrisi effecerūt,vt reges,principes,nobiles,ciues & rustici,multas aras erexerint, sacellanos conduxerint,& certas prębendas illis constituerint. Altaria consecrantur ceremonijs varijs,nec licet cófecrare, secundum iura Pontificia,nisi illa in quibus sunt reliquię,hoc est,ossa sanctorum.Sed quia omnes anguli pleni sunt altaribus, episcopi suffraganei accipiunt ossa ex coemiterijs,quę huius vel illius diui esse dicunt:cum nihil minus sint. Adhæc altaria non dedicant vel consecrant soli Deo:sed diuis,quos pro suis patronis agnoscunt: atqj ita auocantur homines à Christo, vt in periculis implorent opem diuorum,non solius Dei.Celebrantur etiam dedicationes illorum altarium. Indulgentijs adhæc multis ornantur à Papa & Cardinalibus, atqj ita in immensum crescit idololatria,& Christiana libertas prorsus opprimitur.Ex his liquido vides, quàm necessaria fuerit emendatio doctrinæ.
units.tr: {E} The Antichrist, just as he revived other ceremonies already abolished, did so with altars too: indeed he multiplied them, and claims that in the celebration of the Mass the body of Christ is offered on them by the priests for the living and the dead. There is no famous temple in which there are not many altars, in the upper part, in the lower part, and even in crypts beneath the earth. I say nothing now of fixed and portable altars in private houses. And since the number of monks, priests and nuns has grown without measure, those idle men, by their hypocrisy, have brought it about that kings, princes, nobles, citizens and country folk have erected many altars, hired chaplains and assigned fixed stipends to them. Altars are consecrated with various ceremonies, and according to Papist law one may not consecrate an altar unless relics are in it, that is, the bones of saints. But since every corner is full of altars, suffragan bishops take bones from cemeteries, which they say belong to this or that saint, although they are nothing of the kind. Moreover, these altars are not dedicated or consecrated to God alone, but to the saints, whom they acknowledge as their patrons; and so men are drawn away from Christ, so that in dangers they implore the help of the saints and not of God alone. The dedications of those altars are also celebrated. Furthermore, they are adorned with many indulgences by the Pope and the Cardinals, and so idolatry grows without measure and Christian liberty is utterly oppressed. From these things you see clearly how necessary the reform of doctrine was.

units.la: HOMILIA VIII.
units.tr: HOMILIA VIII.

units.la: Reduces ex Babylone,festum tabernaculorum & alia festa celebrant,Deoqj sacrificia offerunt.
units.tr: Returning from Babylon, they celebrate the feast of tabernacles and other feasts, and offer sacrifices to God.

units.la: 4 Fecerunt q; solennitatem Tabernaculorum, sicut scriptum est, & holocausta per singulos dies, iuxta numerum secundum consuetudinem, per singulos dies.
units.tr: 4 And they kept the feast of tabernacles, as it is written, and offered the burnt offerings day by day, according to the number and the custom, each day as it required.

units.la: 5 Et postea holocaustum inge, & in Calendis, & (in)omnibus solennitatibus Iehoue sanctificatis, & omnium sponte offerentium sponte offerentium Iehoue.
units.tr: 5 And afterwards the continual burnt offering, and at the new moons, and at all the holy feasts of the LORD, and at every one who offered a freewill offering to the LORD.

units.la: 6 A die primo mensis (illius) septimi cœperunt offerre holocausta Iehoue: templum autem Iehoue non erat fundatum.
units.tr: 6 From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, but the temple of the LORD was not yet founded.

units.la: AVdiuimus reduces ex Babylone, mense septimo vnanimes congregatos esse Hierosolymis, ex tota ragione in qua confederant, partim vt gratias Deo agerent, quod suum populum feruallet & liberaflet, vtq; ardentibus votis peterent, eu nunc aduersus diaboli & vicinarum gentium furores defendaret, partim vt de templo extruedo deliberarent. Primu conftrueruntaltare Domino, illo ipso in loco vbi positum fuerat antea, vt super illud holocausta offerrent. Vicinae enim gentes minabantur illis. Ex hoc discimus, res arduas à religione & precibus ordiendas esse. Sacrificijs enim preces iungebant: & quo grauius est periculum, tanto ardentius Deum colere debemus. Pericula enim precibus auertuntur. Quanquam alijs quoque praesidijs interim vtendum fit.
units.tr: We have heard that those returning from Babylon assembled at Jerusalem in the seventh month, all of one mind. They met for the whole reason for which they had joined together: partly to give thanks to God that he had preserved and delivered his people, and with fervent prayers to ask that he would now defend them against the fury of the devil and of the neighbouring nations; partly to deliberate about building the temple. First they set up the altar to the Lord in the very place where it had stood before, so that they could offer burnt offerings upon it. For the neighbouring nations threatened them. From this we learn that great undertakings must be begun with religion and prayer. They joined their prayers to their sacrifices, and the greater the danger, the more fervently we ought to worship God. For dangers are averted by prayer. Yet meanwhile other defences must also be used.

units.la: Fecerunt folennitatem taberuaculorum.) Incidit enim hoc festum in die 15. mensis septimi, & durabat septem diebus. De festi tabernaculorum celebratione, vberius scripsi in caput 8. Nehemiae. Sicut scriptum est.) Non celebrarunt suo arbitratu, sed secundum Legem. Peccatur enim fi fecundum humanam rationem Deum volumus co-ere, sicut gentiles & alij fecerut. Deum enim, qui spiritus est, colere voluerunt, auro, argento, gemmis, holosericis vestibus, pictuoб, musico concentu, odoribus & id genus rebus alijs. At Deus etiam in veteri Testamento, nisi fide praediti effent, haec externa non morabatur. Et holocausta per singulos dies, iuxta numerum, fecundum consuetudinem, per singulos dies.) Deus Lege sua praescripserat, quae sacrificia diebus testis, quae profestis effent immolanda. Illi igitur seruata ratione numeri victimarum, pro ratione & dignitate dierum sacrificabat. Quae intelliguntur ex Num. 29. quid enim quoquo die, quamdiu festum durabat, offerendum fuerit, ordine ibi recensetur. Et postea holocaustum iuge.) Etiam peracto tabernaculorum festo, iuge sacrificium quod holocaustis annumeratur, obtulerunt. Et in calendis.) Singulae Neomeniae proprium holocaustum habuerunt, non autem cessationem ab opere. In has autem calendas, etiam festum tubarum incidit. Et in omnibus folennitatibus I ho ua sanctificatis.) In praecipuis & celebribus illis festis legis scilicet, holocaustum obtulerunt. In hunc septimum mensem inciderunt multa festa. Hinc ethanim fortium vel fortitudines, quidam dictum volunt. Calendis huius mensis septimi, fuit festum tubarum fiue clangoris, in memoriam liberationis Ifaac, cum immolandus effet: vel, bellorum populi Dei. Leuit. 23. Die 3. fuit iubilaeum Godoliae, Iere. 41 & 42. Die 10. fuit feftu expiationis vel propitiationis, in memoriam peccati quod contraxerant adorando vitulum. Leuit. 16. 23. Et omnium sponte nec offerentium.)
units.tr: They kept the feast of tabernacles.) This feast fell on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and lasted seven days. I have written more fully about the celebration of the feast of tabernacles in chapter 8 of Nehemiah. As it is written.) They did not celebrate at their own discretion, but according to the Law. For people sin when they want to worship God by human reasoning, as the Gentiles and others have done. They wanted to worship God, who is spirit, with gold, silver, gems, silken garments, paintings, musical harmony, perfumes and other things of that kind. But God, even in the Old Testament, did not regard these outward things unless those who offered them were endowed with faith. And burnt offerings every day, by number, according to the custom, every day.) God had prescribed in his Law which sacrifices were to be offered on festival days and which on ordinary days. They therefore sacrificed according to the proper number of victims, in keeping with the nature and dignity of each day. These are understood from Num. 29, for there it is set out in order what was to be offered each day while the feast lasted. And afterwards the continual burnt offering.) Even after the feast of tabernacles was over, they offered the continual sacrifice, which is counted among the burnt offerings. And at the new moons.) Each new moon had its own burnt offering, yet they did not cease from work. The feast of trumpets also fell on these new moons. And at all the solemn feasts, which are sanctified.) That is, at the principal and famous feasts of the Law they offered burnt offerings. Many feasts fell in this seventh month. Some want the name 'Ethanim' to mean 'of the strong' or 'strengths' from this. On the New Moon of this seventh month was the feast of trumpets, or clangour, in memory of the deliverance of Isaac when he was about to be sacrificed, or of the wars of God's people. Lev. 23. On the third day was the jubilee of Gedaliah, Jer. 41 and 42. On the tenth day was the feast of expiation or propitiation, in memory of the sin they had committed by worshipping the calf. Lev. 16, 23. And of those who offered voluntarily, not from vow.)

units.la: Celebratio taberaculorum. Festi tabernaculorum. Festa calendarum 7. mensis. Quod quisquis nō ex voto vel ex lege, sed sponte obtulit,etiam facrificarunt. A die primo mensis.) Non 15.demum die orsi sunt, quo festum tabernaculorum incipit,sed à primo die mensis,festa celebrauere, neq; ceffarunt,quanquam fundamenta templi iacta nondum effent.
units.tr: The celebration of the tabernacles. The feast of tabernacles. The feasts of the calends of the seventh month. Whoever offered not from a vow or by law, but of his own free will, also sacrificed. From the first day of the month.) They did not begin only on the fifteenth day, when the feast of tabernacles begins, but from the first day of the month they celebrated the feasts, and they did not cease, although the foundations of the temple had not yet been laid.

units.la: Vt hæc apertius explicentur,sciendum est Hebræos præter Sabbathum,nō ita multas ferias habuisse,quarū quasdam Deus illis præscripserat,quasdam ipsi sponte receperát.Tria folennia festa fuerunt, ad quæ omnes mares quotannis confluere, exomnibus terræ Israelis finibus debuerunt in vnum locū, qui primō nō expressus fuit,postea dicitur Deu.16.què Deus monstra bit:is fuit tabernaculū,mox templū in vrbe Hierofolymorū.De fœminis nihil dicitur,nō enim semper ad iter paratę iunt.Quan quam illas quoq; festa illa celebraffe legatur, vt Anna mater Samuelis, Diua virgo & aliæ. Ne autem Israelitæ dicerent,terram ab hostibus vicinis interea occupandam,promittit eis Deus Exod.32.quòd defensurus eos fit ab hostibus.
units.tr: To explain these matters more clearly, it must be understood that the Hebrews, apart from the Sabbath, did not have so many holy days, some of which God had prescribed for them and some of which they had taken up of their own accord. There were three solemn feasts, to which all the males were to come together every year from all the borders of the land of Israel to one place. At first this place was not named; later God says in Deut. 16 that he would show it: first it was the tabernacle, then the temple in the city of Jerusalem. Nothing is said about women, for they were not always ready for the journey. Yet we read that they too celebrated those feasts, as Hannah, Samuel's mother, Deborah the virgin, and others did. Lest the Israelites should say that the land would meanwhile be seized by neighbouring enemies, God promises them in Exod. 32 that he would defend them from their enemies.

units.la: Primum ex his folennibus festis,fuit festum paschæ,in quo mense Nisan 14.sub vesperam singulæ familiæ mactabant sibi agnum,quem affatum cum azymis comedebant.15.pascha,& dies prima azymorum dicitur: dicitur & festum azymorū, nam per dies 7. vescebantur azymis. Celebrabatur ad memoriam illius beneficij specialis, quòd Deus eos liberarat ex seruitute Ægyptiaca:deinde futurę &vniuersalis illius liberationis monumentum erat,quę per Christum facta est.Dicitur festum primitiarū: Frugum enim quæ maturescere incipiebant,manipulus Deo offerebatur.Gentiles quoq; primitias suis dijs immolarunt.
units.tr: The second solemn feast was the feast of Pentecost. It was so called because it was celebrated fifty days after the Passover. It was also called the feast of weeks, because it follows the Passover after seven weeks, and it was in memory of the giving of the Law. It is also called the feast of new fruits, because loaves made from the new grain were offered to God.

units.la: Secundum feftū folenne,fuit festum Pentecostes,quod quia 50.die à pafchate celebrabatur, sic dictū est.Hebdomadū quoq; dicebatur,quòd pascha post 7. hebdomadas sequatur,in memoriam fuit inftitutū datæ legis.Dicitur etiam feftū nouarum frugum,quia panes è nouis fi ugibus Deo oblati sunt.
units.tr: The second solemn feast was the feast of Pentecost. Because it was celebrated fifty days after the Passover, it was so called. It was also called the feast of weeks, because the Passover is followed by seven weeks, in memory of the giving of the Law. It is also called the feast of the first fruits, because loaves were offered to God from the new grain.

units.la: Tertium est festum tabernaculorum vel scenopegias,quod inchoabatur die 15. mensis Septembris, & celebrabatur totis 7. diebus.Institutum aut fuit, vt memoria celebraretur illius temporis quo populus in deferto sub tabernaculis, in castris vixit. Gratias etiam agebant Deo,pro iam collectis & conditis omnibus fructibus atq; frugibus.
units.tr: The third is the feast of tabernacles, or Scenopegia, which began on the fifteenth day of the month of September and was celebrated for the full seven days. It was instituted so that the time when the people lived in the wilderness, in tents and camps, might be remembered. They also gave thanks to God for all the fruits and crops now gathered in and stored.

units.la: Optimè autem hęc tria festa fuerunt distributa,primum in vere,alterum in æstate,tertium in autumno fuit:nullum in hyemem incidit, quando dies contractiores, & itinera aspera sunt. Festi dies ceremonijs annumerantur, quæ in Christo abrogatæ sunt,ad Galatas 4.5.Colossenses 2.Quia vero dies efferne-cesse est,quibus pij conueniant, & verbum Dei audiant,ac sacramenta vsurpent, placuit Christianis diem, qui sequitur Sabbatum,seligere. Paucas præterea ferias Christo duntaxat sacras, prisci Christiani habuerunt. Liberum autem fuit ecclesijs, has vel illas ferias recipere vel non: nemo propterea eas excommunicauit, aut contra eas carnale brachium, vt nunc dicunt, implorauit. Progressu temporis,festi dies valdè aucti sunt. Hac de re plura annotaui in homilia 46. super librum Hester. Antichristus non solum Iudæorum ferias, sed Ethnicorum etiam multas inuexit in ecclesiam.
units.tr: These three feasts were very well distributed: the first in spring, the second in summer, the third in autumn. None falls in winter, when the days are shorter and the roads are rough. Festival days are counted among the ceremonies that have been abolished in Christ, Gal. 4, 5; Col. 2. But since there must be days on which the godly may gather, hear the word of God and receive the sacraments, the Christians chose the day that follows the Sabbath. Moreover, the early Christians kept only a few holy days, dedicated to Christ alone. It was left free to the churches to accept these or those days or not; no one therefore excommunicated them, or called on the secular arm against them, as they now say. As time went on, the feast days were greatly multiplied. I have noted more on this matter in homily 46 on the book of Esther. Antichrist brought into the Church not only the feasts of the Jews but also many feasts of the Gentiles.

units.la: De sacrificijs etiam Leuiticis, quorum hoc loco fit mentio paucula quædam annotanda sunt.Sacrificia varia apud Hebræos fuerunt, & non nisi Deo fiebant. Videntur autem ad duas species reuocari posse. Alia enim sunt ἱλαστήρια propitiatoria, quæ offerebantur pro peccatis sacerdotis, totius populi, vulgarium & priuatorum. Huc pertinent holocausta, item sacrificium Chatat,pro peccatis inuoluntarijs: Asham pro voluntarijs. Alia verò sunt Eucharistica, quibus Deo pro suis beneficijs gratias egerunt. Cæterum non putandum,sacrificia propitiatoria per se vim habuisse remittendi peccata.In epistola ad Hebræos,fieri non potest dicitur,vt sanguine taurorum & hircorum peccata deleantur.Fuerunt typi victimæ illius piacularis,hoc est,Christi venturi,qui peccata generis humani aufer ret,& patrem suum nobis placaret. Christiani non agnoscunt aliud sacrificium expiatorium,quàm mortem Christi. Ideoque illa quæ in lege dicebantur propitiatoria abolitæ sunt,postquàm Christus apparuit, & in ara crucis seipsum Deo patri hostiam obtulit.Sacrificia vero sua Eucharistica Christiani habent.
units.tr: Concerning the Levitical sacrifices, which are mentioned at this point, a few things must be noted. The Hebrews had various sacrifices, and these were offered only to God. They seem to be reducible to two kinds. Some are propitiatory sacrifices [ἱλαστήρια], which were offered for the sins of the priest, of the whole people, of the common people and of private persons. To these belong the burnt offerings, likewise the sacrifice of the sin offering for unintentional sins, and the guilt offering for voluntary sins. Others are eucharistic sacrifices, by which they gave thanks to God for his benefits. Yet we must not think that the propitiatory sacrifices had by themselves any power to remit sins. In the Epistle to the Hebrews it is said that it is not possible that sins should be taken away by the blood of bulls and goats. They were types of that expiatory victim, that is, of the coming Christ, who would take away the sins of the human race and reconcile his Father to us. Christians acknowledge no other expiatory sacrifice than the death of Christ. Therefore those things that were called propitiatory in the Law were abolished after Christ appeared and offered himself as a victim to God the Father on the altar of the cross. But Christians have their own eucharistic sacrifices.

units.la: 1 Vt agnoscamus corruptionem nostram, nihil nobis, sed Deo omnia bona tribuamus:item corpora nostra offeramus Deo, & non viuamus secundum hoc seculum, Roman.12.cap. mactemus affectus belluinos,necesse itate postulante,nos totos Deo immolemus. 2. Preces piorum, laus & gratiarum actio, sunt sacrificia Christianorum, Psalmo 50.ad Hebræos 13.
units.tr: 1. That we may acknowledge our corruption and attribute all good things to God and not to ourselves; likewise that we may offer our bodies to God and not live according to this age (Rom. 12); that we may put to death brutish affections; and, as necessity requires, that we may sacrifice ourselves wholly to God. 2. The prayers of the godly, praise and thanksgiving, are the sacrifices of Christians: Ps. 50; Heb. 13.

units.la: 3 Eleemosynæ etiam huc referri possunt, & alia opera charitatis,quæ Deus à nobis postulat.
units.tr: 3. Alms too may be referred here, and the other works of charity that God requires of us.

units.la: Quod sacrificuli dicunt,se quotidie in missa Christum sacrificare pro peccatis mortuorum & viuentium,caret testimonio sacrarum literarum. Christus enim non potest amplius sacrisicari. Cœna Domini est memoria sacrificij peracti in ara crucis.
units.tr: What the priests say, that they daily sacrifice Christ in the mass for the sins of the dead and the living, lacks the testimony of the sacred letters. For Christ cannot be sacrificed any more. The Lord's Supper is the memorial of the sacrifice completed on the altar of the cross.

units.la: HOMILIA IX.
units.tr: HOMILY IX.

units.la: Conducuntur qui ligna aduehant ad instau randum templum, & exactores operis constituuntur
units.tr: The men who carried timber to rebuild the temple are hired, and overseers of the work are appointed.

units.la: 7 Dederunt autem pecuniam latomis & opificibus, cibum & potum, atque oleum Sidonijs ac Tyrijs vt adducerent ligna cedrina de Lebanon ad mare Iappo, iuxta voluntatem Chores regis Paras super eos.
units.tr: 7 They gave money to the stonemasons and the craftsmen, and food and drink and oil to the Sidonians and Tyrians, that they should bring cedar wood from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa, according to the permission of Cyrus, king of Persia, given to them.

units.la: 8 Anno autem secundo aduentus eorum ad domum Dei in Ierusalaim, mense secundo, coeperunt Zerubbabel filius Sealthiel, & Iesua filius Iosadac, & reliqui fratres eorum, Sacerdotes & Leuitae, & omnes qui venerant de captiuitate in Ierusalaim: statuerunt- que Leuitas a filio viginti annorum & supra, vt praeessent operi domus Iehouae.
units.tr: 8 Now in the second year after their coming to the house of God at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and the rest of their brethren, the priests and the Levites, and all who had come out of captivity to Jerusalem, began the work; and they appointed the Levites from twenty years old and upward to oversee the work of the house of the LORD.

units.la: 9 Steterq; Iesua, filij eius, & fratres eius: Cadmiel & filij eius, filij Iehudah, tanquam (vir) vnus, vt praeessent facientibus opus in domo Dei: filij Henadad, & filij eorum, & fratres ipsorum Leuitae.
units.tr: 9 Then stood Jeshua with his sons and his brethren, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, as one man, to oversee those who did the work in the house of God: the sons of Henadad, with their sons and their brethren the Levites.

units.la: REductos de exilio, ex tota regione Hierosolymis conuenisse dximus, partim vt Deo pro reuersione gratias agerent, partim vt cum de rebus alijs, tum de templi extructione consultarent: Sequitur quomodo comparata materia, & conductis artificibus, operi manum admouerint.
units.tr: We have said that those brought back from exile had gathered at Jerusalem from the whole region, partly to give thanks to God for their return, and partly to consult about other matters as well as about the building of the temple. There follows how, once the materials were prepared and the workmen hired, they set their hand to the work.

units.la: Dederunt autem pecuniam latomis & opificibus. charasch artificem vel fabrum significat. Faber autem apud Hebraeos accipitur vt apud Latinos: sunt fabri lignarij, aerarij, ferrarij, &c.
units.tr: They gave money to the stonemasons and the craftsmen. Charasch means a craftsman or smith. Among the Hebrews, however, "smith" is understood as it is among the Latins: there are carpenters, bronzeworkers, ironworkers, and so on.

units.la: Hae duae vrbes Sidon ac Tyrus plerunque in sacris libris coniunguntur, vt Lucae.10.Marci 7. Vicinae enim fuerunt: abundarunt autem non solum mercatoribus, sed & ingeniosis artificibus, & peritissimis architectis, vt hodie Venetiae & Neroberga.
units.tr: These two cities, Sidon and Tyre, are usually joined together in the sacred books, as in Luke 10 and Mark 7. For they were neighbouring cities, and they abounded not only in merchants but also in clever craftsmen and most skilled architects, as Venice and Nuremberg do today.

units.la: Iudaei artifices conduxerunt, & nautas qui ligna cedrina ex Libano (cui illae vrbes vicinae erant) ad mare Ioppe, hoc est, ad littus maris mediterranei, iuxta quod sita est Ioppe, deduceret. Ioppe oppidum Iapham nunc vocant. Nam ab Iaphet filio Noe conditum esse dicunt. A Romanis in bellis illis, quae contra Iudaeos gesserunt, aliquoties direptum, tandem euersum est. Postea instauratum, Christiani in bellis quae gesserunt pro recupe ratione sepulchri dominici, euerterunt. Hoc oppidum primum in Palaestinam peregrinantes excipit. Hospitium praebuit D. Petro, qui Tabitham ibi e mortuis suscitauit, Act. 9. cap. Hinc ligna commodè Hierosolyma deduci potuerunt. Iuxta voluntatem (Cyri.) Hoc est mandatum. Iosephus lib. 11. Antiquitatum Iudaicarum cap. 2. testatur, quod Cyrus rex iusserit de suo sumtus in omnibus fieri. Vel secundum facultatem a Cyro eis datam. 3. Reg. 5. cap. Salomon etiam petit ab Hiramo rege, ut sibi sit auxilio, in aedificio templi, ut mittat sibi ligna cedrina & artifices, quibus promittit mercedem, quam ipsum statuere iubet, se enim bonis artificibus deditui, &c. non quod nullos haberet, sed non tam peritos & excellentes.
units.tr: The Jews hired craftsmen, and sailors to bring the cedar wood from Lebanon (to which those cities were near) to the sea at Joppa, that is, to the shore of the Mediterranean Sea beside which Joppa lies. The town is now called Japha. They say it was founded by Japheth, the son of Noah. In the wars that the Romans waged against the Jews it was plundered several times and at last overthrown. Later it was restored, and the Christians overthrew it in the wars they fought for the recovery of the Lord's sepulchre. This town is the first to receive pilgrims arriving in Palestine. It gave lodging to St Peter, who raised Tabitha from the dead there, Acts 9. From there the timber could conveniently be brought to Jerusalem. "According to the permission (of Cyrus)" means according to his command. Josephus, in Book 11 of the Jewish Antiquities, chapter 2, testifies that King Cyrus ordered that everything be done at his expense, or according to the means given them by Cyrus. In 1 Kings 5, Solomon also asks King Hiram to help him in the building of the temple, that he send him cedar wood and craftsmen, to whom he promises the wage that Solomon himself orders to be set; for he says that he is inferior to the good craftsmen, etc., not that he had none, but that they were not so skilled and excellent.

units.la: In eo quod Tyriorum & Sidoniorum opera vtuntur in extructione templi, sicut ante eos Solomon fecerat, habemus praeludium vocationis gentium, quarum opera necessaria sit in aedificatione ecclesiae. Multi enim episcopi ex gentibus oriundi, sanguine etiam suo ecclesiam plantarunt.
units.tr: In that the Tyrians and Sidonians are employed in building the temple, as Solomon had earlier done, we have a foretaste of the calling of the Gentiles, whose labour is needed in the building of the Church. Indeed many bishops born of the Gentiles have planted the Church even with their own blood.

units.la: Ex eo quod pecuniam, cibum & potum, latomis, opificibus & vectoribus dederunt, discimus feruis & aliis operarijs dandum cibum & potum conuenientem. Prouerb. 12. Vir humanus curam habet etiam umenti sui: quanto magis feruorum & mercenariorum? Item merces illis danda est. Peccatur illa in re, si non das illis quod iuste petunt, sed συμφωνίας contendis cum illis, Franglish lang: deinde si solutionem differs. Item, si pecuniam adulterinam illis numeras, aut alia pecuniae vice obtrudis. Peccant autem grauissime qui debitum negant, aut vitae insidiantur illius, cui merces persoluenda esset. Leuitici 19. versu 13. Non morabitur opus mercenarij, id est, precium operis, apud te vsq; mane. Deut. 24. versu 14. 15. Non vim inferes (non opprimes) mercenario pauperi & egeno, tam de fratribus tuis, quam de peregrinis tuis, qui sunt in terra tua, intra portas tuas. In die suo dabis mercedem eius: neque succumbet super eam Sol, quoniam pauper est, & cum ea sustentat animam suam: ne clamet contra te ad Iehouam, & sit in te peccatum. Tobiae 4. cap. versu decimoquinto. Ne moretur apud te mercedes illius hominis, qui tibi opera dederit, sed ea statim ei reddet. Nam si Deo seruieris, tibi quoq; ab eo reddetur, &c. Iacobi 5. Ecce merces operariorum qui messuerunt, in aures Domini introierunt. Non quosuis mercenarios, sed messores nominat, eo quod labores eorum durissimi sunt. Quomodo pauperi aliquid sponte largietur, qui tam crudelis est erga suos operarios, vt quod eis debet non persoluat?
units.tr: From the fact that they gave money, food and drink to the stonemasons, craftsmen and carters, we learn that suitable food and drink must be given to servants and other workmen. Proverbs 12: "A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast." How much more, then, that of servants and hired workers? Likewise, their wages must be paid. One sins in this matter if one does not give them what they justly ask, but haggles with them over the agreement, and then delays payment. Likewise, if one counts out to them counterfeit money, or foists something else in place of money on them. Those sin most gravely who deny what is owed, or plot against the life of the one to whom the wage ought to be paid. Leviticus 19, verse 13: "The wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning," that is, the price of the work. Deuteronomy 24, verses 14 and 15: "Thou shalt not oppress an hired servant that is poor and needy, whether he be of thy brethren, or of thy strangers that are in thy land within thy gates. At his day thou shalt give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down upon it; for he is poor, and setteth his heart upon it: lest he cry against thee unto the LORD, and it be sin unto thee." Tobit 4, verse 15: "The wages of any man, which hath served thee, shall not tarry with thee, but shall be paid him presently. For if thou serve God, he will repay thee." James 5: "Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth." He names not any hired workers but reapers, because their labour is most hard. How will a man who is so cruel to his own workers, that he does not pay them what he owes, willingly give anything to the poor?

units.la: Serui autem & mercenarij, sui quoq; sint officij memores. Æquum item est, vt alij quoq; qui in extructione spiritualis templi laborant, mercede sua non fraudentur. Operarius enim est dignus mercede sua, Matth. 10.
units.tr: Yet servants and hired workers too should remember their own duty. It is likewise fair that those who labour in the building of the spiritual temple also should not be cheated of their wage. For "the labourer is worthy of his hire," Matthew 10.

units.la: Deinde commemoratur quod anno secundo Cyri, vel reditus sui, parata materia, cum venissent ad domum Dei, hoc est locum vbi templum steterat, mense secundo (qui Zif dicitur & Iair) illi quorum praecipua erat dignitas & authoritas in hoc populo, ceperint, scilicet aedificare templum: vel ceperunt statuerunt, vel ordinarunt (hubend an vnd staltend) Leuitas a 20. annis & supra, vt praeessent facientibus opus in domo Iehouae. Vetus translatio habet, vt vrgerent opus Domini: fuerunt ἐπιστάται, quales etiam Solomon habuit cum templum extrueret. Additur Ητετίφε Iesua, Cadmiel & filios Iehuda, (an ex filijs Leuitarum, vel ex tribu Iuda fuerint, nescio) tanquam vnus vir, id est simul.
units.tr: Next it is recorded that in the second year of Cyrus, or of their return, when the materials had been prepared and they had come to the house of God, that is, the place where the temple had stood, in the second month (which is called Ziv or Iyar), those whose dignity and authority among this people was chief began, namely to build the temple; or they began, appointed, or ordained (set up and established) the Levites from twenty years old and upward to oversee those who did the work in the house of the LORD. The old translation has "to urge on the work of the Lord." They were the overseers (epistatai), such as Solomon also had when he built the temple. It is added that Jeshua, Kadmiel and the sons of Judah (whether they were of the sons of the Levites or of the tribe of Judah I do not know) stood as one man, that is, together.

units.la: Obedientiae hoc loco habemus insigne exemplum. Numerorum capite 4. versu 3. legimus, Leuitas qui ministraturi erant tabernaculo, anno demum 30. aetatis admissos fuisse, & anno aetatis 25. ad exercitia sacra, postea 50. anno rude donatos, vt non cogerentur amplius onera tabernaculi portare. Qui igitur hoc loco constituuntur Leuitae, ad structuram solicitandam a 20. annis? Dicendum videtur, ex dispensatione hoc factum, quia eorum pauci erant.
units.tr: Here we have a notable example of obedience. In Numbers 4, verse 3, we read that the Levites who were to serve at the tabernacle were admitted only at thirty years of age, and at twenty-five were given to sacred exercises, and afterwards, at fifty, were discharged so that they were no longer compelled to carry the burdens of the tabernacle. Why, then, are the Levites here appointed to press forward the building from twenty years old? It seems to be said that this was done by dispensation, because there were few of them.

units.la: Deinde Deus saepe iuuenes ornat sapientia & dexteritate. Ieremias, Timotheus & alij, iuuenes fuerunt, cum ad munus docendi vocarentur. 1. Timoth. 4. Nemo tuam iuuentutem despiciat, &c.
units.tr: Then, God often adorns young men with wisdom and skill. Jeremiah, Timothy and others were young men when they were called to the office of teaching. 1 Timothy 4: "Let no man despise thy youth," etc.

units.la: Necessarium autem fuit, vt duces & exactores haberent, vel praefectos qui opus vrgerent. Nisi enim sint qui opus vrgeant, omnia negligenter administrantur. Equis quantumuis genero sis, interdum calcaria admouentur: boues aratrum trahentes, stimulo subinde vrgentur. Multa sunt quae nos retrahant ab aedificio ecclesiae, & rebus sacris. Caeterum fructu suo non caret ad hortatio assidua. Quod spirituale aedificium ecclesiae attinet, Deus etiam operis exactores constituit, iuuenes & senes, nempe ecclesias & politicum magistratum, qui subinde in hoc esse debent, vt aedificium illud spirituale procedat. Hortari homines debent ad poenitentiam, hoc est, vt idololatriam & scelera abijciant, & aream purgent: deinde fundamentum locent. Paulus 1. ad Corinthios 3. capite dicit: Vt sapiens architectus fundamentum posui, alius autem super illud aedificat. Porro quisque videat quomodo superstruat. Nam fundamentum nemo aliud potest ponere, praeter hoc quod positum est, quod est Iesus Christus. Subinde incitandi sunt homines, vt fide Christo superstruantur, illi adhaereant, neque perfequutione, neque malis exemplis, sed a Christo auelli & dimoueri patiantur.
units.tr: It was necessary, too, that there should be leaders and overseers, or prefects, to press on the work. For unless there are those who urge the work on, everything is carried on carelessly. However generous the horse, spurs are sometimes applied; oxen drawing the plough are from time to time urged on with a goad. There are many things that draw us back from building the Church and from sacred things. Yet constant exhortation does not lack its fruit. As far as the spiritual building of the Church is concerned, God also appoints overseers of the work, young and old, that is, the ministers of the Church and the civil magistrate, who must from time to time see to it that this spiritual building goes forward. They ought to exhort people to repentance, that is, to cast off idolatry and wickedness, and to clear the area, and then to lay the foundation. Paul, in 1 Corinthians 3, says: "As a wise masterbuilder I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ." From time to time people must be urged to build themselves up on Christ by faith, to cleave to him, and to allow themselves not to be torn away and removed from Christ by persecution or by bad examples.

units.la: Ministri ecclesiae non solum ἐπιστάται, sed etiam architecti in scripturis dicuntur: qui aedificare ecclesiam sana doctrina, & vitae integritate Deo colligere populum debent: ac cauere, ne ipsi hoc aedificium diruant: aut illorum furores imitentur, qui exemplo seniorum, qui Christum lapidem angularem reiecerunt, etiam illos reijciunt qui vera membra sunt ecclesiae, & cum domum Dei extruere deberent, primi in hoc incumbunt, vt hoc aedificium diruatur, & Ecclesia funditus euertatur.
units.tr: Ministers of the Church are called not only overseers [ἐπιστάται] but also architects in the Scriptures. They ought to build the Church with sound doctrine and integrity of life, and to gather the people to God. They must take care not to pull this building down themselves, or to imitate the madness of those who, following the example of the elders, rejected Christ, the cornerstone, and also reject those who are true members of the Church. Although they ought to be raising up the house of God, they are the first to set to work to tear this building down and utterly overthrow the Church.

units.la: Exactores autem & architecti, non existimare debent, suas curas & labores fore frustraneos. Deus enim semper suos habet.
units.tr: Overseers and architects, however, must not suppose that their cares and labours will be in vain. For God always has his own.

units.la: HOMILIA X.
units.tr: HOMILY X.

units.la: Iudaei gratias agunt Deo, ob iacta fundamenta templi.
units.tr: The Jews give thanks to God for the laying of the foundations of the temple.

units.la: 10 Fundamenta, itaque iecerunt architecti templi Iehoua, constituerunt, sacerdotes (aliquot) indutos cum tubis, & Leuitas filios Asaph cum cymbalis, vt laudarent Iehouam per manus Dauidis Regis Israelis.
units.tr: 10 So the builders laid the foundations of the temple of Jehovah, and they set in place the priests, (some of them) clothed and with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise Jehovah by the hand of David, king of Israel.

units.la: 11 Concinebant autem, dum laudarent, & confiterentur Iehoua, Quoniam bonus, quoniam in saeculum misericordia eius super Israelem. Vniuersus praeterea populus vociferabatur vociferatione magna, dum laudarent Iehouam, quod fundata esset domus Iehoua.
units.tr: 11 They sang in turns as they praised and confessed Jehovah, "For he is good, for his mercy endures for ever toward Israel." Moreover all the people shouted with a great shout as they praised Jehovah, because the house of Jehovah was founded.

units.la: F
units.tr: F

units.la: 12 Quamplurimi autem de sacerdotibus & Leuitis ac principibus patrum, senes qui viderant domum priorem, dum fundarent hanc domum in oculis eorum flebant voce magna, & (alij) multi vociferabantur prae laetitia, alta voce:
units.tr: 12 But many of the priests and Levites and heads of the fathers' houses, the old men who had seen the former house, wept with a loud voice as they saw this house being founded before their eyes, and (others) many shouted aloud for joy.

units.la: 13 Ita vt populus non discerneret vocem vociferationis laetam a voce fletus populi: quod populus ille vociferaretur vociferatione magna, adeo vt exaudiri tur vox procul.
units.tr: 13 So that the people could not distinguish the joyful shout from the sound of the people's weeping, because the people shouted with a great shout, so that the sound could be heard from afar.

units.la: IN fine huius capitis, commemoratur quomodo Iudaei iactis fundamentis templi, hoc est, coepto aedificio illo, se gesserint, nempe quod Deo gratias egerint. Principium enim, vt prouer bio dicitur, est dimidium totius. Maxima difficultatis pars in agrediundo est sita. Historiam primo loco paucis interpretabimur, deinde ad vsum vitae nostrae eam accomodabimus.
units.tr: At the end of this chapter it is recalled how the Jews behaved when the foundations of the temple had been laid, that is, when that building was begun: namely, that they gave thanks to God. For the beginning, as the proverb says, is half of the whole; the greatest part of the difficulty lies in making a start. We shall first explain the history briefly, and then apply it to the use of our life.

units.la: 1. Sacerdotes & Leuitae, voce & musicis instrumentis Deum celebrarunt. Iactis fundamentis constituti sunt sacerdotes induti, scilicet vestibus sacerdotalibus. Summus pontifex & reliqui pontifices, adhaec ministri eorum Leuitae, suas peculiares vestes habuerunt: de quibus Exodi 28. Leuitici 8.
units.tr: 1. The priests and Levites celebrated God with voice and musical instruments. Once the foundations were laid, the priests were appointed clothed, that is, in priestly garments. The high priest and the other priests, and likewise their ministers the Levites, had their own distinctive garments; concerning these see Exodus 28 and Leviticus 8.

units.la: Cum tubis.) De vario tubarum vsu in rebus sacris & prophanis, Numeri 10. capite agitur. Conuocabantur his coetus sacri. Ioel, Clangite tuba in Zion, indicite coetu &c. Quod etiam quando sacrificia obtulerunt, tubas interdum inflarint, ex 2. Paralip. 29. cap. colligitur. Et Leuitas filios Asaph cum cymbalis.) Leuitae oriundi ex Asapho, constituti erant vt cymbala pulsarent. Cymbalum genus est instrumenti musici, sub cymbalis forte alia quoque instrumenta musica comprehendit, vt Psalterium, nablum, citharam, &c. Asaph prophetico spiritu ornatus, floruit tempo ribus Dauidis, aliquot Psalmos copofuit & cantor insignis fuit.
units.tr: With trumpets.) The varied use of trumpets in sacred and profane matters is treated in Numbers chapter 10. By these sacred assemblies were summoned. Joel: "Blow the trumpet in Zion, call an assembly," etc. That they also sometimes sounded trumpets when they offered sacrifices is gathered from 2 Chronicles chapter 29. And the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals.) The Levites descended from Asaph were appointed to strike the cymbals. The cymbal is a kind of musical instrument; under "cymbals" perhaps other musical instruments are also included, such as the psaltery, the nebel, the harp, etc. Asaph, endowed with prophetic spirit, flourished in the times of David, composed several Psalms and was a notable singer.

units.la: Vt laudarent Iehouam per manus Dauidis.) Hoc est, vt ille ordinauerat, 2. Paralip. 29. vel decantando psalmos Dauidis. Dauid enim multos psalmos praecentoribus, Ieduthun, filijs Core, id est, Coritis, & alijs in publico coetu decantandos tradidit.
units.tr: To praise Jehovah by the hand of David.) That is, as David had ordained (2 Chronicles 29), or by singing the Psalms of David. For David handed over many psalms to be sung in public assembly by the chief singers, Jeduthun, the sons of Korah, that is, the Korahites, and others.

units.la: Concinebant autem dum laudabant & confitebantur (hoc est gratias agerent) Iehouae.) Alternis canebant, & musica instrumenta pulsabant.
units.tr: They sang in turns as they praised and confessed (that is, gave thanks) to Jehovah.) They sang alternately and struck the musical instruments.

units.la: Quoniam bonus, quoniam in seculum misericordia eius super Israelem.) Hoc est, super fideles. Israelitae enim alij sunt carnales, alij spirituales, quemadmodum & Abrahami filij. Ideo ad nos quoq; pertinent promissiones, de rebus spiritualibus Israeli & reliquis patribus factæ. Hoc argumentum præcipuum & materia fuit: celebrarunt bonitatem & clementiam Dei, quam multis rebus ostendit. Multi autem psalmi huius sunt argumenti. Psalmus 106. 107. 117. 118. 147. quos præcipue videntur cecinisse. Pertinet autem ad nostram consolationem, quod Dei misericordia dicitur perpetuo durare. Nam si durat perpetuo, etiam in poenis temporarijs quando nobis maximè irasci videtur du rat: proinde animus abijciendus non est, multo minus fremen-dum aduersus Deum. Psalmo 36. repetitur vigesies sexies, clementiam eius durare in perpetuum. Quod in tentatione illa cogitandum est, quando metuimus ne in vltimo vitæ articulo, no stra fides deficiat, & Deus nos deserat. In Threnis Ieremiæ 3. capite: Non deseret, inquit, in seculum Dominus. Nam si dolore af fecerit, & miserebitur secundum multitudinem misericordiarum suarum. Exempla multa huius rei afferri possunt.
units.tr: For he is good, for his mercy endures for ever toward Israel.) That is, toward the faithful. For the Israelites are some carnal and some spiritual, just as the sons of Abraham are. Therefore the promises made to Israel and the other fathers concerning spiritual things also pertain to us. This was the principal theme and subject: they celebrated the goodness and clemency of God, which he showed in many things. Many psalms are of this kind; Psalms 106, 107, 117, 118 and 147 are those which they seem especially to have sung. It serves our consolation that the mercy of God is said to endure perpetually. For if it endures perpetually, then even in temporal punishments, when he seems most angry with us, it still endures; therefore the spirit should not be cast down, much less should we rage against God. Psalm 136 repeats twenty-six times that his mercy endures for ever. This must be remembered in that temptation when we fear that at the last moment of life our faith will fail and God will forsake us. In Lamentations 3 it says: "The Lord will not cast off for ever. For if he causes grief, he will have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies." Many examples of this can be brought forward.

units.la: Durandus libro primo diuinorum officiorum capite primo scribit: In ædificatione alicuius ecclesiæ seu templi, parato fundamenti loco, iubetur episcopus vel sacerdos eius nomine & de eius licentia, ibi aquam aspergere benedictam ad abigendas ibi dæmonum phantasias, & primarium lapidem cui impressa sit crux in fundamento ponere, &c. Hic nihil simile legitur.
units.tr: Durandus, in book one of the Divine Offices, chapter one, writes: "In the building of any church or temple, once the place for the foundation is prepared, the bishop or his priest, in his name and with his permission, is ordered to sprinkle holy water there to drive away the phantasms of demons, and to place as the first stone one on which a cross is impressed, in the foundation," etc. Nothing similar is read here.

units.la: Deinde vniuersus populus clamauit, dum sacerdotes & Leuitæ Deum celebrarent, quod iacta essent templi fundamenta. Clamore autem suo testati sunt animi gaudium: ⁂ habent gaudiugeset von fremden.
units.tr: Then the whole people shouted, while the priests and Levites celebrated God, because the foundations of the temple had been laid. By their shout they bore witness to the joy of their spirit. ⁂ They have joy, set down by strangers.

units.la: Quoad Musicam sacram, referenda est illa partim ad Ceremonias, à quibus liberi sumus. Cantum initio non in omnibus Ecclesijs fuisse, alibi dictum est, item qua occasione cantus receptus sit ab occidentalibus ecclesijs, & quomodo tandem in abusum venerit, vt sine mente sacrificuli sacra carmina cecinerint. Non tamen reprehendimus illos, qui moderate cantu vtuntur. Organa vero, vt vocant, nouum sunt inuentum.
units.tr: As for sacred music, it must be referred partly to ceremonies, from which we are free. That song was not at first in all churches has been said elsewhere, as has the occasion on which singing was received by the western churches, and how at last it came to abuse, so that they sang sacred songs without any mind behind them. Yet we do not blame those who use singing in moderation. Organs, as they are called, are a new invention.

units.la: Quoad priuatas cantiones, & instrumenta musica, illa etiam ad laudes Dei conuertenda sunt, non ad turpes amores, vel voluptates & luxuriam. Qui ludunt instrumentis, interim res necessarias non debent intermittere.
units.tr: As for private songs and musical instruments, these too are to be turned to the praise of God, not to base loves, pleasures and luxury. Those who play instruments should not in the meantime neglect necessary duties.

units.la: Docet nos exemplum Sacerdotum, Leuitarum & populi, vt cum spiritualia templi fundamenta iacta sunt, hoc est, cùm plures vel singuli auocantur ab erroribus & superstitionibus, Christum amplexi vera fide,qui vnicum elt ecclesiæ fundamentum, item si pœnitentiam agunt,lætemur.Lucæ 15. dicuntur qui in cœlis sunt,lætari de illis qui pœnitentiam agunt. In alijs quoq; beneficijs,quæ Deus nobis & alijs exhibet, cognoscenda est eius bonitas & celebranda: Si dat alicuius negotij boni, inchoationem fœlicem. E diuerso si ecclesiæ collabuntur,aut priuati homines fraudibus Antichristi iugulantur,aut deficiut à fide,dolendum est. Orandus est Dominus, vt omnibus constantiam largiatur in vera fide,& vitæ innocentia.
units.tr: The example of the priests, Levites and people teaches us that when the spiritual foundations of the temple are laid, that is, when several or individuals are called away from errors and superstitions and embrace Christ in true faith, who is the only foundation of the Church, and likewise when they do repentance, we should rejoice. In Luke 15 it is said that those who are in heaven rejoice over those who do repentance. In other benefits too, which God bestows on us and on others, his goodness is to be recognised and celebrated, when he gives a happy beginning to some good undertaking. Conversely, if churches collapse, or private persons are slaughtered by the frauds of Antichrist, or fall away from the faith, it is to be lamented. The Lord is to be prayed to, that he may grant constancy in true faith and innocence of life to all.

units.la: Additur,non paucos ex sacerdotibus,Leuitis,proceribus populi,senibus,qui Solomonicum templum longè augustiss-mum viderant,voce magna fleuisse,cum fundamenta noui templi cernerent. Tradunt enim Iudæi,mensuram noui templi multò minorem fuisse,quàm templi prioris fuerat:Deinde reuocantin mentem ærumnas quas in obsidione & expugnatione vrbis pertulerant.
units.tr: It is added that not a few of the priests, Levites, nobles of the people and elders, who had seen Solomon's temple, far more magnificent, wept with a loud voice when they saw the foundations of the new temple. For the Jews relate that the measure of the new temple was much smaller than that of the former temple. Then they recalled the hardships they had endured in the siege and storming of the city.

units.la: Quia verò alij,præsenti forte contenti,alta voce clamabant præ gaudio & lætitia, orta est tanta vocum confusio, vt inter lætos clamores,& lachrymas,discerni non posset: procul autem voces illæ exaudirentur.
units.tr: But since others, perhaps content with the present, shouted aloud for joy and gladness, such a confusion of voices arose that amid the joyful shouts and the tears it could not be distinguished; those voices, however, could be heard from afar.

units.la: Dum surgit ædificium spiritualis templi, multis externam formam inspicientibus,& primitiuam ecclesiam in mentem reuocantibus,lachrymæ excidunt. Vident enim quantum ecclesiæ recentes ab illa differant. At à paruis initijs vlterius procedendum est. Si ecclesiæ non respondent expectationi nostræ, implorandum est Dei auxilium,vt quod cœpit perficiat.
units.tr: While the building of the spiritual temple rises, many who look upon its outward form and call the primitive Church to mind shed tears. For they see how far the recent churches differ from that one. But one must proceed further from small beginnings. If the churches do not answer to our expectation, the help of God must be implored, that he may complete what he has begun.

units.la: Nascitur hoc loco quæstio,quomodo Propheta Haggæus 2.capite dicat:Maiorem fore gloriam domus istius posterioris, quàm prioris,hoc est,Solomonici. Cùm seniores qui priorem viderant,in lachrymas eruperint, cum viderent tam illustrem non fore.Respondeo maiorem fore gloriam eius, non propter ædificium,sed propter Christum,qui se in hoc templo manifestauit. Vel Propheta loquutus est de spirituali templo, quod Christus Deo excitauit, nempe de ecclesia Catholica per totum orbem, cuius architectus & caput est Iesus Christus.
units.tr: A question arises here: how does the prophet Haggai, in chapter 2, say that the glory of this later house will be greater than that of the former, that is, Solomon's? Since the elders who had seen the former burst into tears, seeing that this one would not be so illustrious. I answer: its glory will be greater, not because of the building, but because of Christ, who manifested himself in this temple. Or the prophet spoke of the spiritual temple, which Christ raised up for God, namely the Catholic Church throughout the whole world, whose architect and head is Jesus Christ.

units.la: CAPUT IIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER 4.

units.la: HOMILIA IX.
units.tr: HOMILY 9.

units.la: Quorum culpa impeditum sit opus templi.
units.tr: Whose fault it was that the building of the temple was hindered.

units.la: Audierunt autem hostes Iehudah & Biniamin, quod filij transmigrationis ædificarent templum Iehouæ Deo Israelis:
units.tr: Now the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity were building a temple to the LORD God of Israel.

units.la: 2 Et accesserunt ad Zerubbabel, & ad capita patrum, dixeruntq; eis, Ædificabimus vobiscum: quia sicut vos, quæremus Deum vestrum, & ei immolavimus à diebus Esarhaddon regis Assur, qui ascendere fecit nos huc.
units.tr: 2 And they came to Zerubbabel and to the chief of the fathers, and said unto them, Let us build with you: for we seek your God, as ye do; and we have sacrificed unto him since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assur, which brought us up hither.

units.la: 3 Tum dixit eis Zerubbabel, & Iesua, ac reliqui principes patrum Israelis, Non vestra, sed nostra stra interest ædificare domum Deo nostro: idcirco nos pariter ædificabimus Iehouæ Deo Israelis, quemadmodum præcepit nobis rex Chores rex Paras.
units.tr: 3 But Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, and the rest of the chief of the fathers of Israel, said unto them, Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our God; but we ourselves together will build unto the LORD God of Israel, as king Cyrus the king of Persia hath commanded us.

units.la: HOC Capite narratur, quæ impedimenta obiecta sint Iudæis, quo minus templum feliciter ædificari coeptum, absoluere potuerint, sed res ad annos aliquot fuerit protracta. Circumstantias expendemus, per quos, quare, quomodo, quando, & quamdiu ædificatio templi impedita sit, item quis inde fructus ad nos redeat.
units.tr: In this chapter it is related what obstacles were put in the way of the Jews, so that they could not bring to a happy completion the temple they had begun to build, and how the work was drawn out over several years. We shall weigh the circumstances: by whom, why, how, when and for how long the building of the temple was hindered, and also what fruit of this comes back to us.

units.la: Primum. Audiuerunt hostes Iuda & Beniamin.) Nempe quod Iudæi, vt sequitur, templum ædificare coeperint, sive ex vago rumore, sive suos coryceos habuerint. Nostro tempore hostes ecclesiæ per suos exploratores cognoscunt, quid hinc inde ab Euangelium amplexis geratur. Vtile esset idem Euangelicos facere rebus periculosis & asperis, sed plerunque sunt securi. Quod filij transmigrationis ædificarent templum Iehouæ Deo Israelis.) Filios transmigrationis vocat, qui in Babylonem transmigrauerant, & inde redierant: Vel simpliciter potius illos, qui reuersi sunt ex Babylonica seruitute in patriam. Hostes illi populi Dei, operam suam eis obtulerunt in extructione templi, repulsam vero passi, eam totis viribus impediuerunt.
units.tr: First: "The enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard." That is, that the Jews, as follows, had begun to build the temple, whether from a vague rumour or because they had their own informants. In our own time the enemies of the Church learn through their spies what is going on, on every side, among those who have embraced the Gospel. It would be useful for the evangelicals to do the same in dangerous and difficult matters, but for the most part they are careless. "That the children of the captivity were building a temple to the LORD God of Israel." He calls them children of the captivity, those who had been carried off into Babylon and had returned from there; or rather, simply those who came back from Babylonian servitude to their homeland. These enemies of the people of God offered their help in building the temple, but when they were rebuffed, they hindered it with all their might.

units.la: Videndum est quinam & quales fuerint illi hostes. Postea dicet, populos qui habitant in vrbibus Samariæ. Samaria nomen est vrbis & regionis, in media ferè via inter Ierusalem & Galilæam. Legimus 4. Reg. 17. cap. Salmanasfarem regem Assyriorum cepisse metropolim decem tribuum Samariam, & vicinas regiones. Eiectis autem Israelitis, colonias ex variis gentibus in terrâ Israelis deduxisse. Qui vno nomine Samaritæ vel Samaritani vocati sunt. Hi cum idola sua colerent, Deus ipsis leones immisit, & alias bestias. Petüt itaque à rege suo, aliquem sacerdotem ex captiuis sibi mitti, qui eos doceat quomodo Deus Israelis colendus sit. Missus est igitur quidam, qui in Bethel considens, Samaritanos religionem Israelitici Dei docuit. Illi Deum Israelis coluerunt quidem, non solum, neque purè, sed simul cum vero Deo, Deos suos & ceremonias retinuerūt. Deus autem vult solus coli, non cum alijs neq; ex diuinis & humanis consarcinatam & mixtam religionem probat, &c. Mos fuit victorum vt colonias deducerent, ne si victi in patria remanerent, studerent rebus nouis. Iosephus lib. 11. Antiq. cap. vltimo scribit: Huiusmodi naturæ sunt Samaritæ, vt calamitatibus immersis Iudæis negent se esse Iudæorum cognatos, in eo veritatem confitentes: cum autem viderint clarum aliquid eis oblatum, tunc socios se Iudaico generi profitentur, originem suam à nepotibus Ioseph, Ephraim & Manasse recensentes, &c. Qui plura de his legere velit, consulat Epitome temporum à condito vrbe vsque ad excidium Hierosolymæ Henrici Bullingeri.
units.tr: We must consider who and what sort of enemies these were. Later he says they are the peoples who dwell in the cities of Samaria. Samaria is the name of a city and region, lying roughly midway along the road between Jerusalem and Galilee. We read in 4 Kings 17 that Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, took Samaria, the metropolis of the ten tribes, and the neighbouring regions. After the Israelites had been expelled, he settled colonists from various nations in the land of Israel; these were called by the one name Samaritans. Since they worshipped their own idols, God sent lions and other wild beasts among them. So they asked their king to send them one of the captive priests to teach them how the God of Israel should be worshipped. Someone was therefore sent, who settled in Bethel and taught the Samaritans the religion of the God of Israel. They did indeed worship the God of Israel, but not only, nor purely; along with the true God they retained their own gods and ceremonies. God, however, wills to be worshipped alone, and does not approve a religion patched together and mixed from divine and human elements, etc. It was the custom of conquerors to plant colonies, so that if the conquered remained in their homeland they would not be inclined to revolt. Josephus, in book 11 of the Antiquities, last chapter, writes: "The Samaritans are of such a nature that, when the Jews are plunged into calamities, they deny that they are kin of the Jews, confessing the truth in this; but when they see something advantageous offered to them, then they profess themselves companions of the Jewish race, reckoning their origin from the grandsons of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh," etc. Whoever wishes to read more about these matters, let him consult Heinrich Bullinger's Epitome of the Times from the founding of the city until the destruction of Jerusalem.

units.la: Samaritani illi accedentes ad Zerubbabel, ac reliquos populi proceres, dicunt eis: Ædificabimus vobiscum. Dicunt se cupere ipsis præstò esse suis consilijs & opera. Prouerbio dicitur: Multæ manus, onus leuius reddunt. Addunt suas rationes. Quia sicut vos quærimus Deum vestrum, Deum etiam colimus, vel colemus vt vos, aut quæremus, id est, erimus socij in cultu. Ne eis obijciat, quòd diuersæ sint religionis. Eos autem non ex animo loquutos esse, res ipsa postea probauit. Volebant explorare Iudæorum animum & consilia, beneuolentiam illam foris simulantes, interim versabant fraudes & dolos in cordibus suis.
units.tr: Those Samaritans came to Zerubbabel and the rest of the leaders of the people, and said to them: "Let us build with you." They say they wish to be at their side with their counsel and labour. There is a proverb: many hands make the burden lighter. They add their reasons. "For as you do, we seek your God," we also worship God, or will worship him as you do; or we will seek him, that is, we will be partners in the worship. This is so that the Jews cannot object that they belong to a different religion. That they did not speak from the heart, the event itself afterwards proved. They wished to test the minds and plans of the Jews, pretending outwardly this goodwill, while in their hearts they were devising deceits and tricks.

units.la: Et ei immolauimus à diebus Assar-haddon regis Assur, qui ascendere nos fecit huc. Quæritur quomodo Asar-haddon eos in hanc regionem transtulerit, cum Salmanassarem eius auum hoc fecisse scriptura testetur? Salmanassar filium habuit, Sanherib, is genuit Assaraddon, 4. Regum 19. Respondendum est, multis incolis à feris, & forte peste, extinctis, postea ab hoc multo plures fuisse missos: illamque terram hominibus impletam. pletam. Alij legunt,Et non immolauimus: videlicet alteri Deo, quàm vestro. Quomodo autem Deum verum colebant,cum idola pariter colerent? si Deum credidissent omnipotentem,clementisimum,non ei alios adiunxissent.
units.tr: "And we have sacrificed to him since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assur, who brought us up hither." It is asked how Esarhaddon transferred them into this region, when Scripture bears witness that his grandfather Shalmaneser had done this. Shalmaneser had a son, Sennacherib; he begat Esarhaddon (4 Kings 19). The answer must be that, many inhabitants having been destroyed by wild beasts and perhaps by plague, many more were afterwards sent by this king, and that land was filled with people. Others read: "And we have not sacrificed", namely to another God than yours. But how did they worship the true God while worshipping idols alongside him? If they had believed him to be almighty and most merciful, they would not have joined other gods with him.

units.la: Zerobabel, Iesus & reliqui proceres, prudenter eos reijciunt, dicentes : Non vobis fratres, sed nostra interest, ædificare domum Deo nostro.) Ad verbum legitur, Non vobis & nobis,vel nihil scilicet vobis nobiscum commune est, vt ædificetis. Vos estis idololatræ, nos colimus verum Deum. Vatablus coniungit proceres politicos, & Iesum Pontificem. Debet enim magna inter magistratum politicum, & ministros ecclesiæ esse coniunctio, conferre inter se debent consilia de propgaanda ecclesia,&c.
units.tr: Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the rest of the leaders wisely reject them, saying: "Not for you, brethren, but for us it is a concern to build a house to our God." Literally it reads: "Not to you and to us," that is, you have nothing at all in common with us so as to build. You are idolaters; we worship the true God. Vatablus joins the civil leaders and Jeshua the High Priest together. For there ought to be a great union between the civil magistrate and the ministers of the Church; they ought to confer their counsels with one another about the advancement of the Church, etc.

units.la: Non autem propterea vicinos suos excludunt, quòd gentes essent. Etenim Sidonijs & Tyrijs vtebantur, sicut in priore templo Solomon quoque fecerat : at hi fideles & amici fuerunt.Samaritæ mox ab initio hostes dicuntur. Sub simulatione amicitiæ,damnum Iudæis inferre conabantur, & impedire hoc sanctū opus. Minus enim nocere potest hostis verus,quàm amicus falsus. Caueri enim ille potest:hic omnium arcanorū consiliorum est conscius. D.Paulus in suis Epistolis de falsis illis fratribus quæritur, ad Galatas 2.2. ad Corinthios capite 11. Res multis exemplis,& ipsa experientia constat. In castris exploratores fingunt se amicos, & omnia speculantur. Item consiliarij qui simulant amorem patriæ, & interim hosti fauent, multa bona consilia possunt astutè impedire: & efficere, vt omnes bene gerendæ rei occasiones effluant. Quàm egregiè elusit Chusai consilia astuta Achitophelis? In Senatu,qui res bonas impedire volunt , id facilè possunt, reijciunt enim in alia tempora, quæ nulla mora interposita, facienda erant, volunt prius explorare quid alij factum sint, vt ita animos hominum alacres, diuturna mora frangant. Nostro tempore, quando Euangelij lux denuò emersit, multi se in cœtus fidelium clandestinos infinuarunt, simulantes se quoque puram doctrinam amplexos, postea Euangelium professos omnes prodiderunt: multi quoque veniunt sub prætextu Euangelij,qui propter sacinora ab aliis relegati sunt.
units.tr: Nor did they exclude their neighbours for the reason that they were Gentiles. For they had made use of the Sidonians and Tyrians, just as Solomon also had done in the former temple; but these men were faithful and friends. The Samaritans are called enemies from the very beginning. Under the pretence of friendship they tried to inflict harm on the Jews and to hinder this holy work. For a true enemy can do less harm than a false friend. The former can be guarded against; the latter is privy to all secret counsels. St Paul in his Epistles complains of those false brothers (Galatians 2:4; 2 Corinthians 11:26). The matter is established by many examples and by experience itself. In camps, spies pretend to be friends and spy on everything. Likewise counsellors who feign love of the fatherland, and in the meantime favour the enemy, can cunningly obstruct many good plans and bring it about that every opportunity for carrying out a good undertaking slips away. How excellently did Hushai elude the crafty counsels of Ahithophel! In the Senate, those who wish to hinder good measures can do so easily, for they postpone to other times what ought to have been done without any delay; they wish first to find out what others have done, so that by long delay they break the eagerness of men's minds. In our own time, when the light of the Gospel has emerged again, many have insinuated themselves into the clandestine assemblies of the faithful, pretending that they too had embraced pure doctrine; afterwards they betrayed everyone who had professed the Gospel. Many also come under the pretext of the Gospel who have been banished by others for their crimes.

units.la: Vsus huius loci.
units.tr: The use of this passage.

units.la: 1. Discimus satanam & eius satellites ferre nequaquam posse,vt templum Dei spirituale ædificetur.Si regio aliqua vel oppidum, pulsa superstitione, veram religionem amplectatur, se
units.tr: 1. We learn that Satan and his underlings can by no means endure the spiritual temple of God being built. If some region or town casts out superstition and embraces the true religion, Satan opposes it as hard as he can.

units.la: Sic in Hieroglyphicis. opponit quantum potest. Si priuati homines abnegata impie-tate & sceleribus, viuum Dei templum esse incipiant, satan fre-mit.Quamdiu scintilla verae fidei & doctrinae superest,satan su-rit: excitat hostes varios, Antichristum cum membris suis,hae-reticos,tyrannos,falsos fratres, homines sceleratos.Causa est in promtu,quia hostis est Dei & hominum:non Dei,sed suum ipsi us regnum promotum cupit.
units.tr: So in the Hieroglyphics. If private persons renounce impiety and wickedness and begin to become a living temple of God, Satan rages. As long as a spark of true faith and doctrine remains, Satan storms: he stirs up various enemies, the Antichrist with his members, heretics, tyrants, false brethren and wicked men. The cause is obvious: he is the enemy of God and of men, and he desires not God's kingdom but his own to be advanced.

units.la: 2. Quibus artibus,vijs,consilijs,instrumentis, pios bono-rum conatus & spiritualis templi aedificium satan impediat, e- tiam hoc Capite docetur. Innumeras quidem habet, est enim τωολυμηχαν. Instrumenta sunt ingenium, literae, eloquen-tia,opes, robur,blandit ae,minae,largitiones.Hoc loco hypocri-fi & simulatione amicitiae, impedire templi extructionem co-natus est. Simulant amorem,dicentes: Se velle iuuare Iudaeos, profitentur fe eiusdem Dei cultores esse,cum sint idololatrae & infenfifimi hostes populi.
units.tr: 2. This chapter also teaches by what arts, ways, plans and instruments Satan hinders the pious efforts of good men and the building of the spiritual temple. He has countless means, for he is very resourceful [πολυμήχανος]. His instruments are cleverness, letters, eloquence, wealth, strength, flattery, threats and bribes. Here he has tried to hinder the building of the temple by hypocrisy and the pretence of friendship. They pretend love, saying that they wish to help the Jews, and they profess that they are worshippers of the same God, though they are idolaters and the most bitter enemies of the people.

units.la: Nostris quoque temporibus aduersarij nostri nobis occi-nunt: etiam nos cupimus saluari, sacras literas & symbolum A-poftolicum vobiscum profitemur: In Christo nostra spem quo que fixam habemus, simplices putant ex animo eos & ferio lo-qui.Cur igitur tot patronos sibi asciscunt,tot opera quibus pec cata deleant comminiscuntur? Cur Christum non vnicum ca-put ecclesiae,saluatorem,mediatorem agnoscunt? Parua dicut, Inter nostram & vestram doctrinam est differentia. Cur igitur nostros tam crudeliter persequimini? Fatentur interdum fe er-raffe in multis, pollicentur etiam errorum emendationem. In exortu Euangelicae doctrinae,legatus Hadriani pontificis in Co mitijs Nerobergae habitis, publice confessus est, in doctrina & vita spiritualium,recessum esse a regula verbi diuini: Reforma-tionem ecclesiae in capitibus & membris esse necessariam,vt hac confessione cursum Euangelij impediret.
units.tr: In our own times too our adversaries sing the same tune to us: "We also wish to be saved; we profess the holy Scriptures and the Apostles' Creed with you; we too have our hope fixed in Christ." Simple people think they speak from the heart and in earnest. Why then do they acquire so many patrons for themselves, and devise so many works by which sins may be blotted out? Why do they not acknowledge Christ as the one head of the Church, its Saviour and Mediator? They say, "The difference between our doctrine and yours is slight. Why then do you persecute our people so cruelly?" Sometimes they confess that they have erred in many things, and even promise the correction of their errors. At the beginning of the Gospel teaching, at the Diet held at Nerobergae, the legate of Pope Hadrian publicly confessed that in doctrine and in the life of the spiritual estate there had been a departure from the rule of the divine Word, and that a reformation of the Church in head and members was necessary. He said this so as to hinder the course of the Gospel by that confession.

units.la: Cum apud nos Tiguri, mox ab initio praedicati Euangelij, publica & folennis de religione disputatio haberetur, Episcopi Conftantienfis legatus, multis ofteridere voluit, non esse pau-corum emendationem doctrinae instituere, intra anni spacium celebrandum Cocilium Pontificis & Imperatoris iussu, in quo de controuersis religionis articulis effet agendum.Zuinglius re fpondit, ex verbo Dei disceptandum de controuersis religio-nis capitibus,legatum illum astute quaerere vt res protrahatur, vtque re infecta discederent.Neminem ex illis qui aderant,imo neque nepotes ipsorum,visuros tale Concilium,quale ille pro-mittemittebat. Interea quædam celebrata nouimus,in quibus Pontificij, errores suos non confesi sunt, sed suam stabiliuerunt tyrannidem, & decreuerunt vt qui iugum illud abijciunt, ferro & flammis ad obedientiam reuocentur. Discamus igitur cognoscere Antichristi dolos, quibus nos in erroribus retinere cupit. Vtile enim est artes hostis cognoscere, vt melius cauepи posint.
units.tr: When at Zurich, soon after the Gospel was first preached, a public and solemn disputation on religion was held among us, the legate of the Bishop of Constance wished to show many people that it was not difficult to set in train a correction of doctrine: a council was to be convened within the space of a year, by command of the Pope and the Emperor, in which the controverted articles of religion would be dealt with. Zwingli replied that the controverted heads of religion must be disputed from the Word of God, and that the legate was craftily seeking to delay the matter, so that they might depart with nothing accomplished. He said that none of those present, nor even their grandchildren, would see such a council as he promised. Meanwhile we have learned of certain councils that were held, in which the Papists did not confess their errors but rather strengthened their tyranny, and decreed that those who cast off that yoke should be brought back to obedience by the sword and by fire. Let us therefore learn to recognise the wiles of Antichrist, by which he wishes to keep us in error. For it is useful to know the arts of the enemy, so that we may be better able to guard against them.

units.la: 3. Exemplo Zerobabelis & aliorum principum populi,di-scamus blandis verbis & pollicitationibus,non statim fidem esse adhibendam. Suspectos potius illos habere debemus,qui no bis blandiuntur. Vtaucupes suas aues habent, quæ alias ad se, suo cantu inuitent, suas fistulas & instrumenta,quibus eas decipiant & attrahant: ita illi qui ecclesiæ incrementa impedire volunt. Illi amicis verbis eos ablegant, idem nos faciamus. Sciebant quidem quales essent, quid quærerent Samaritani,non tamen dicebant,Proditores estis & nebulones. Cautendum enim est, ne alios temere & vltro in nos prouocemus. De malis accersitis multa extant prouerbia, vt, Irritare crabrones, Cornutam bestiam petere,Scorpium excitare, Suem irritare,Leonem stimulare,&c.
units.tr: 3. Following the example of Zerubbabel and the other princes of the people, let us learn that we must not at once give credence to smooth words and promises. Rather we ought to regard with suspicion those who flatter us. As fowlers keep decoy birds which by their song invite others to themselves, and have pipes and instruments with which they deceive and draw them in, so do those who wish to hinder the growth of the Church. They dismiss us with friendly words; let us do the same. The Samaritans indeed knew what sort of men they were and what they were seeking, yet they did not call them traitors and scoundrels. For we must take care not to provoke others rashly and needlessly against us. There are many proverbs about evils brought on by oneself: to stir up hornets, to attack a horned beast, to rouse a scorpion, to provoke a sow, to goad a lion, and so on.
