units.la: Scimus interdum quales sint alij, non autem probare pof-femus tales esse. Imprimis autem idololatræ suspectos nobis esse debent. Cicero Q. Fratri Asiæ proconsuli multa vtilia præcepta tradens : In prouincia ipsa,inquit,si quem es nactus,qui in tuam familiaritatem penitus intrauit,qui nobis ante fuerit ignotus, huic quantum credendum sit vide: non quin posint multi esse prouinciales viri boni, sed hoc sperare licet, indicare periculosum est. Multis enim simulationū inuolucris tegitur,& qua si velis quibusdam obtenditur vniufcuiufq; natura,frons,oculi, vultus, sæpe mentiuntur, oratio vero sæpissimè. Quamobrem qui potes reperire ex eo genere hominum,qui pecuniæ cupiditate adducti,careat his rebus omnibus,à quibus nos diuulsi esse nō possumus : te autem alienum hominum ament ex animo, ac non sui commodi causa simulent.Mihi quidem permagnum videtur, præsertim si ijdem homines priuatū non ferè quenquam prætores semper omnes ament. Quo ex genere si quem fortè tui cognosti amantiorem (fieri enim potuit) quàm temporis, hunc ad tuum numerum libenter adscribito. Sin autem id non perspicies, nullum erit genus in familiaritate cauendum magis. Propterea quod & omnes vias pecuniæ norunt, & omnia pecuniæ causa faciunt, & qui cum victuri non sunt, eius exitu. mation i consulere non curant,&c. Hocipfum nobis hodie quo que inter tot perfidos homines versantibus, diligenter est co- gitandum.
units.tr: We sometimes know what kind of people others are, but we could not prove that they are such. Above all, idolaters must be regarded by us with suspicion. Cicero, giving many useful precepts to his brother Quintus, proconsul of Asia, says: "In the province itself, if you have met someone who has entered deeply into your intimacy, who was previously unknown to us, consider how far he is to be trusted. Not that there may not be many good men among the provincials, but it is dangerous to hope so, and to point it out. For men are covered with many wrappings of pretence, and the nature of each person is, as it were, put forward to suit whatever you wish: the forehead, the eyes, the face often lie, and speech most often of all. Therefore, how can you find anyone of that kind who, led by desire for money, is free of all those vices from which we cannot be separated, but who truly loves you and does not pretend for his own advantage? To me it seems very great, especially if the same men who scarcely love any private person love the praetors always. If by chance you recognise someone of that sort as more loving to you than to the time (for it can happen), gladly enter him in your number. But if you do not see this, there will be no kind of person to be guarded against more in intimacy, because they know all the ways of money, and do everything for money's sake, and do not care to consult the outcome of those with whom they are not going to live." This very thing must be carefully pondered by us too, who live today among so many treacherous men.

units.la: HOMILIA XII.
units.tr: HOMILIA XII.

units.la: Samaritae absterrent Iudaeos ab aedificio templi, & conducunt consiliarios contra eos.
units.tr: The Samaritans frighten the Jews away from the building of the temple, and hire counsellors against them.

units.la: 4 Populus autem(eius)regionis dissoluebat manus populi Iehudah,& perturbabat eos ne aedificarent.
units.tr: 4 The people of that region, however, weakened the hands of the people of Judah and troubled them, so that they would not build.

units.la: 5 Et conduxerunt contra eos consiliarios,ut dissiparent consilium eorum omnibus diebus Chores Regis Paras,& vsq; ad regnum Dariaues Regis Paras.
units.tr: 5 And they hired counsellors against them, to frustrate their plan all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.

units.la: 6 Quum autem regnaret Ahasueros,in principio regni eius scripserunt accusationem contra habitatores Iehudah & Ierusalaim,
units.tr: 6 And when Ahasuerus reigned, at the beginning of his reign they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.

units.la: 7 Nam in diebus Arthahsasthe scripsit in pace Mithredath, Tabel,&reliqui socij eius,ad Arthahsaft he Regem Paras: porro scriptura(eius)epistolae scripta erat Syriace,& explicata Syriace.
units.tr: 7 For in the days of Artaxerxes, Mithredath, Tabel and their other associates wrote in peace to Artaxerxes king of Persia; the writing of the letter, however, was written in Syriac and translated into Syriac.

units.la: 8 Rehum a comentarijs, & Simsai scriba scripse runt epistolam vnam contra Ierusalaim ad Arthahsaft he Regem,huiusmodi.
units.tr: 8 Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote one letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes, as follows.

units.la: 9 Tunc Rehum a commentarijs,& Simsai scri- ba,& reliqui socij eorum, Dinaie,& Apharsathchaie, Tarpelaie, Apharsaie, Archauaie, Bablaie, Susan- chaie,Dehaue,Elmaie,
units.tr: 9 Then Rehum the commander, and Shimshai the scribe, and their other associates, the Dinaites, the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Archevites, the Babylonians, the Susanchites, the Dehaites, the Elamites,

units.la: 10 Et reliqui populi quos transtulit Asuappar magnus & gloriosus, & habitare fecit eos in vrbibus Samariae, & reliqui(populi qui sunt) trans Flumen,& Cheeneth.
units.tr: 10 and the other peoples whom the great and glorious Osnappar transported and settled in the cities of Samaria, and the rest of the peoples beyond the River, and Cheeneth.

units.la: CVm Iudaei aedificium templi inchoassent, coniunxerunt se illis Samaritani, suam quoq; operam in aedificando eis promittentes, at illi noluerunt eos admittere. Sciebant enim quod non aedificare vellent,sed eos potius,exploratis eorum con silijs,impedire ac opprimere.
units.tr: When the Jews had begun to build the temple, the Samaritans joined themselves to them, promising their help in the building too; but the Jews were unwilling to admit them. For they knew that the Samaritans did not wish to build, but rather, having discovered their plans, to hinder and oppress them.

units.la: Quid vero repulsam passi fecerint, iam deinceps explicatur. Produnt malignum suum ingenium: simulatio enim non diu latere potest. Primum Samaritani dissoluebant manus populi Iudah, et perturbabant eos, ne aedificarent.) Manus dissoluere, & robora re vel confortare, contraria sunt. Dissoluerunt manus, id est, re- missos & pigros effecerunt. Varijs rationibus vti potuerút, quibus eos ab aedificio templi auerterent. Nempe primos Dei servos caruisse templo. Nam tum demum tabernaculum extructum legitur, cum populus Dei in deserto esset perductus. Annis quoque ilIis 70. captiuitatis, eos templum no habuisse. Vtilius item esse, vt suas res curent, domos extruant, agros colant, quàm vt lapideum templum aedificent. Etsi vero magno labore id faciant: tamen fore vt iterum deijciatur. Cyrum quidem concessisse ipsis, vt aedificent, mox alium regem venturum, cui longe aliud videatur. Vtile igitur esse, vt si omnino aedificare velint, hoc commodioribus temporibus faciant. Multa alia quoque pericula fingere pote- runt, & terrere eis obijcere. Nostra aetate etiam multi clamant, vos soli estis, nihil potestis cotra tot efficere: pericula magna vos circumstant, hęc religio no poterit obtinere: frustra tot laboresfufcipitis. Argumentum est nostrae imbecillitatis, quod Iudaei labascere incipiunt, nullo quoque aedificandi studio amplius tentur. Cauendum igitur ab illis, qui corruptis sermonibus Euangelicae doctrinae & virtutis studium, in nobis extinguere conantur: Corrumpunt bonos mores colloquia praua.
units.tr: What the Samaritans did after being rebuffed is now explained next. They reveal their malicious nature, for pretence cannot long remain hidden. First, the Samaritans weakened the hands of the people of Judah and troubled them, so that they would not build. To weaken the hands and to strengthen are opposites; they weakened their hands, that is, they made them slack and lazy. They could use various arguments by which they might turn them away from the building of the temple. Indeed, they said, God's first servants had lacked a temple: for the tabernacle is read of as set up only once the people of God had been led into the wilderness. Likewise, during those seventy years of captivity they had had no temple. It is also more useful for them to look after their own affairs, build houses and cultivate fields, than to construct a temple of stone. And even if they did this with great labour, it would soon be thrown down again: Cyrus indeed had granted them permission to build, but soon another king would come, whose mind was quite different. It would therefore be better, if they wished to build at all, to do it at more favourable times. They could also invent many other dangers and set them before them to frighten them. In our own age too many cry out: "You are alone; you can accomplish nothing against so many; great dangers surround you; this religion will not be able to hold its ground; you undertake these labours in vain." It is a proof of our weakness that the Jews begin to waver and are no longer moved by any zeal for building. We must therefore beware of those who, by corrupt speech, try to extinguish in us the zeal for gospel doctrine and virtue: "Evil conversations corrupt good morals."

units.la: Secundo, Conduxerunt contra eos consiliarios, vt disiparent consilium eorum.)Hunc locum ita interpretes intelligunt, quòd Samaritani subornarint certos homines, qui consulerent eis, vt desisterent ab incepto aedificio, sed ita potius videtur intelligendus, quòd consiliarios regum Persicorum, item praefectos, & fortasis etiam ex coniiiarijs populi Dei aliquot coduxerint & coruperint, (nam primores non omnes bonos fuisse, suo loco dicemus) qui in publicis deliberationibus, concilijs, comitijs, Iudaeis obsistèrent, eorumq; cōsilium de instaurando templo, tur barent. Conduxerunt eos, nimirum muneribus corrumpentes. Dy habendo Geschenke und Geschoben.
units.tr: Second, they hired counsellors against them, to frustrate their plan. Interpreters understand this place to mean that the Samaritans suborned certain men who would advise the Jews to give up the building they had begun. But it seems rather to be understood thus: that they hired and corrupted some of the counsellors of the Persian kings, likewise the prefects, and perhaps also some of the leading men of the people of God (for not all the nobles were good, as we shall say in its place), who would oppose the Jews in public deliberations, councils and assemblies, and would hinder their plan of restoring the temple. They hired them, that is, by corrupting them with bribes. Bribing with gifts and presents.

units.la: Munera autem magnum effectum habere vsu comperimus. Dominus vetat Exod.23. & Deut.17. in iudicijs munera accipere, dicit enim: Nec munus accipies, quia munus excaecat videntes, & peruertit verba iustorum. Solomon quoque in Prouerb. [...] xanimâ vim eis tribuit. Qui nos donat, videtur nos magni aestimare, deinde plerique natura auari sumus. Multi dicunt se licet munera accipiant, tamé nihilominus officiu facturos, at Deus nouit melius quales sumus, quàm nosipsi. Philippus rex Macedoniæ, nullam vrbem, nullam arcem tam munitā esse dixit, quæ si asinus auro onustus in eam ingrediatur, non expugnari & capi posset. Idem in singulis Græciæ vrbibus conduxit oratores & alios, sibiq; muneribus eos concíliauit, qui proderent consilia. Iugurtha senatores Romanos magno auro ita corrupit, vt eius parricidia inciperent excusare. Bileam à Baraco rege conductus, contra conscientiam populo Dei maledixit, Numer. 23. Antichristus homines, vt Daniel de eo prædixit, donis varijs sibi coniungit. Nos vero munera quæ ad tentandos & corrumpendos animos nostros, nobis offeruntur, accipere non debemus, ne in suspicionem veniamus, quod his moti aliquid contra honestatem facturi simus. Illa vero quæ testandæ & confirmandæ amicitiæ gratia, aliáue honesta de causa offeruntur, accipere, nihil vetat. Antichristus non solum in suas partes pertrahere iudices nititur, sed rem eò deduxit, vt Principes & Senatores, imò omnis ordinis homines, in ipsius verba iurare cogantur.
units.tr: Moreover, we find by experience that gifts have a great effect. The Lord forbids, in Exodus 23 and Deuteronomy 17, the taking of gifts in judgments, for he says: "You shall take no gift, for a gift blinds those who see and perverts the words of the righteous." Solomon also, in Proverbs [...], ascribes power to them. He who gives us a gift seems to value us highly; and besides, most of us are naturally greedy. Many say that although they accept gifts, they will nonetheless do their duty; but God knows better what sort of people we are than we ourselves do. Philip king of Macedon said that no city and no citadel was so well fortified that it could not be taken and captured if a donkey laden with gold went into it. He likewise hired orators and others in the individual cities of Greece and won over to himself, by gifts, those who would betray their counsels. Jugurtha corrupted the Roman senators with so much gold that they began to excuse his parricides. Balaam, hired by King Balak, cursed the people of God against his conscience (Numbers 23). Antichrist, as Daniel foretold of him, binds men to himself with various gifts. We indeed ought not to accept gifts that are offered to us in order to test and corrupt our minds, lest we fall under suspicion that we are about to do something dishonourable because we were moved by them. But to accept those things which are offered for the sake of bearing witness to and confirming friendship, or for some other honest reason, is not forbidden. Antichrist not only strives to draw judges to his side, but has brought matters to such a pass that princes and senators, indeed men of every rank, are compelled to swear to his words.

units.la: Omnibus diebus Cyri regis Persarum vsque ad regnum Darij.
units.tr: All the days of Cyrus king of the Persians, until the reign of Darius.

units.la: Cum bona spes esset instaurandi templi & ciuitatis, tantum effecerunt illi Samaritani, per præfectos vicariosq; quos muneribus corruperūt, vt intermissum fuerit opus toto tempore quo Cyrus regnauit. Bella enim illi continuo gerêda erat cótra Schytas & alios, & fieri potest, vt illarō rerum quæ apud Iudæos gerebantur, ignarus fuerit Successit illi filius Cambyses, quo mortuo, Magi regnum inuaserunt, quos Darius Hiftaspis occidit, cuius anno secundo demum, concessum est, vt ædificium absolucrent. Dilata igitur est ædificatio annis circiter 42. Hinc colligimus, quòd cursus prædicationis Euägelij ad tempus quidem ignauia fidelium, & insidijs atq; dolis infidelium posse impediri: sed non prorsus opprimi. Suo tempore Deus Euangelio latisimam fenestram aperit. Cæterum si nos occasiones negligimus, diu multis commodis carere cogimur.
units.tr: Although there was good hope of restoring the temple and the city, those Samaritans achieved so much, through the governors and deputies whom they corrupted with bribes, that the work was suspended for the whole time that Cyrus reigned. For he was constantly obliged to wage war against the Scythians and others, and it is possible that he was ignorant of what was going on among the Jews. His son Cambyses succeeded him, and after Cambyses died, the Magi seized the kingdom. Darius, son of Hystaspes, killed them, and only in the second year of his reign was permission finally granted to complete the building. The building was therefore delayed for about forty-two years. From this we gather that the course of the preaching of the Gospel can for a time be hindered by the sloth of believers and by the snares and tricks of unbelievers, but that it is never utterly crushed. God opens a very wide window for the Gospel at his proper time. But if we neglect the opportunities, we are made to go for a long time without many blessings.

units.la: Tertiò scriptis impedire volunt templi ædificium. Videamus quid, cui, quando, quomodo, qui nam scribant. Epistola est monitoria vel accusatoria. Scripserunt accusationem, ad verbum, odium, inimicitias, hoc est, literas quibus Iudæis odium conflarent, apud Reges & Satrapas Persicos. Scripserunt Asuero, qui mox Artaxerxes appellatur, ab alijs Cambyses, filius fuit Cyri, & vt videtur vicarius patris cū ipse bellis esset occupatus.
units.tr: Thirdly, they try to hinder the building of the temple by writing. Let us consider what was written, to whom, when, in what manner, and by whom. It was a letter of admonition or accusation. Strictly speaking, they wrote an accusation, that is, letters by which they might stir up hatred and enmity against the Jews before the Persian kings and satraps. They wrote to Ahasuerus, who is soon called Artaxerxes by others. He was the son of Cyrus, and, as it seems, the deputy of his father, since Cyrus himself was occupied with wars.

units.la: Quid scripserint. Cui.
units.tr: What they wrote. To whom.

units.la: Sciendum autem summos principes in regno Persico, Xerxes & Artaxerxes, hoc est bellatores & fortes bellatores appellari, sicut apud Ægyptios omnes reges Pharaones nominantur. Deinde habent etiam sua propria nomina.
units.tr: It should be noted that the chief princes in the Persian kingdom, Xerxes and Artaxerxes, that is, warriors and strong warriors, were so called, just as among the Egyptians all kings are named Pharaohs. Besides, they also have their own proper names.

units.la: Scripserunt ei in principio regni eius, ut statim animum eius occuparent, antequam à Iudæis cognoscere posset, quomodo res haberent. In pace.) Hoc est, nondum odio plane detecto ac patefacto, occulte, ne Iudæi rescirent.
units.tr: They wrote to him at the beginning of his reign, so that they might seize his mind at once, before he could learn from the Jews how things stood. In peace. That is, with the hatred not yet fully disclosed and revealed, secretly, lest the Jews should find out.

units.la: Scripserunt literis & verbis Syriacis. Iulius Cæsar libro I. de bello Gallico, dicit in castris Helvetiorum tabulas repertas, quæ Græcis literis fuerint scriptæ. Quidam putant quod Græcis duntaxat literis, & sermone Gallico confectæ fuerint, alijs tamen aliter videtur. Apographum epistolæ huius habetur in textu. Quidam putant duarum epistolarum hoc loco mentionem fieri. Primam viuente Cyro cum domi non esset, ad Cambysem esse scriptam: alteram postea cum Cambyses patri in regno iam successisset. Certe eos plus semel in causa tanti momenti scripsisse, non est dubitandum.
units.tr: They wrote in letters and in the Syriac language. Julius Caesar, in the first book of his Gallic War, says that tablets written in Greek letters were found in the camp of the Helvetii. Some think they were written only in Greek letters and in the Gallic language, but others think otherwise. A copy of this letter is found in the text. Some think that this passage mentions two letters: the first, written while Cyrus was still alive and not at home, to Cambyses; the second, afterwards, when Cambyses had already succeeded his father in the kingdom. Certainly there is no doubt that they wrote more than once in a matter of such importance.

units.la: Qui nam scripserint hanc epistolam, vel ei subscripserint, multis verbis indicatur. Nominatur Mithridates, Tabel & reliqui socij eius: Rehum à commentarijs, vel cancellarius eam distauit, & Simsai scriba, eam scripsit ac reliqui socij. Item Dinæi, Aphasartæi & alij populi, qui in consilium adhibiti sunt contra Iudæos. Addit, reliquos populos quos Afnappar magnus & gloriosus transtulerit in urbes Samariæ, & quotquot trans flumen, hoc est, Euphratem erant. Limes enim fuit inter regnum Babylonicum & Iudaeos. Dicuntur autem populi qui in Samaria habitabant, trans flumen habitare, respectu Babyloniorum. Cheereth, creditur nomen esse gentis vel populi: quid si fluuij vel montis nomen fit. Afanappar, ante Afaraddon distus fuit.
units.tr: Who wrote this letter, or subscribed to it, is indicated in many words. Mithridates, Tabeel and the rest of his associates are named. Rehum, the commander of the records, or the chancellor, drew it up, and Shimshai the scribe wrote it, with the rest of their associates. Likewise the Dinaeans, the Apharsathchites and other peoples who were brought in as counsellors against the Jews. It adds that the remaining peoples whom the great and glorious Osnappar transferred into the cities of Samaria, and all who were beyond the river, that is, the Euphrates, were there too. For the boundary lay between the kingdom of Babylon and the Jews. Now the peoples who lived in Samaria are said to dwell beyond the river, with respect to the Babylonians. Cheereth is thought to be the name of a tribe or people, unless it is the name of a river or a mountain. Osnappar was earlier called Asaraddon.

units.la: Quod scribæ nomen exprimitur, ideo factum puto, ut cogitemus Deum non obliuisci illorum, quæ notarij vel scribæ notant. Plerunque audaces sunt, & scribunt quæ ad impediendum cur… Euangelij pertinent, omni pudore abstersó.
units.tr: I think the name of the scribe is expressed for this reason: that we may consider that God does not forget those things which notaries or scribes record. Very often such men are bold, and they write whatever pertains to hindering the course of the Gospel, with all shame wiped away.

units.la: Tot autem subscribunt, ut rex non putet ex inuidia & odio hæc proficisci, sed ut accusatorum concordia, facilius illi persuadeat, Iudæos gentem esse malam, seditiosam, &c. Quis enim putet tot testes, illis iniuriam facere?
units.tr: So many subscribe, however, so that the king may not think that these things proceed from envy and hatred, but that, through the agreement of the accusers, he may more easily be persuaded that the Jews are a wicked and seditious nation, and so on. For who would think that so many witnesses were doing them an injustice?

units.la: Antichristus etiam hac astutia utitur, iactat quot gentes vel terrem religionem retineant unanimi consensu, quot principes & populi aduersentur nouæ doctrinæ. Sunt qui tantum respi-
units.tr: Antichrist also uses this same cunning. He boasts how many nations, or indeed the whole earth, hold to a religion by unanimous consent, and how many princes and peoples oppose a new doctrine.

units.la: ciant ad multitudinem: eam religione putantes veram esse, cui plures homines potentes & populi adhæreant. Simplices maximè multitudine decepti, dicūt, tot reges, academiæ, populi, qui sciunt, quid sequendum sit, quid minus, hoc vel illud amplectantur, &c. Tot subscripserunt huic doctrinæ, non igitur falsa esse potest. At multi sunt, qui viam ducentem ad interitum sequuntur. Videndum est, quid Deus probet, quid improbet. Nota est vox Panormitani, plus credendum esse vel simplici laico scripturam sacram afferenti, quàm toti simul concilio.
units.tr: There are those who look only to the multitude, thinking that religion is true if many powerful men and peoples adhere to it. Simple people, most of all deceived by numbers, say: so many kings, universities and peoples, who know what must be followed and what less, embrace this or that; so many have subscribed to this doctrine, so it cannot be false. Yet there are many who follow the road that leads to destruction. We must see what God approves and what he disapproves. The saying of Panormitanus is well known: that one must believe a simple layman who brings forward Holy Scripture more than the whole council together.

units.la: Vt autè Samaritani suos scribas habent, & suas literas accusatorias mittunt ad regem Persarum: Ita Antichristus suos habet conductitios: mittit suas bullas hinc inde, imò legatos suos à latere, qui Respublicas & regna turbent, & dehortentur à professione veræ doctrinæ. Conducunt etiam viros doctos, qui editis libris falsam doctrinam defendant. Neque desunt qui contra conscientiam faciant & scribant quicquid illi voluerint, ut opulenta sacerdotia posint acquirere.
units.tr: Just as the Samaritans have their own scribes and send their letters of accusation to the king of the Persians, so Antichrist has his hired men: he sends his bulls here and there, and indeed his legates from his side, who disturb commonwealths and kingdoms and dissuade them from the profession of true doctrine. They also hire learned men who, by publishing books, defend false doctrine. Nor are there lacking those who act against their conscience and write whatever those men wish, so that they may acquire wealthy benefices.

units.la: Solent adhuc viri potentes, vires suas coniungere, contra ædificium ecclesiæ. Psalmo 2.
units.tr: Powerful men still tend to join their strength together against the building of the Church. Psalm 2.

units.la: HOMILIA XIII.
units.tr: HOMILY XIII.

units.la: Exemplum literarum ad regem missarum.
units.tr: Copy of the letter sent to the king.

units.la: 11 Illud (est) exemplar epistolæ quam miserunt ad eum (nempe ad) Arthahsasthe Regem, Serui tui viri, qui sunt trans flumen, & Cheneth.
units.tr: 11 This is the copy of the letter which they sent to him, namely to Artaxerxes the king: Thy servants the men beyond the river, and Cheneth.

units.la: 12 Notum sit regi quòd Iehudæi qui ascenderunt à te ad nos, venerunt in Ierusalaim, vrbem rebellem & pessimam ædificantes, & muros fundauerunt, & parietes compposuerunt.
units.tr: 12 Let it be known to the king that the Jews who came up from thee to us are come unto Jerusalem, building the rebellious and the wicked city, and have set up the walls, and joined the foundations.

units.la: 13 Nunc notum sit Regi quod si vrbs illa ædificata fuerit, & muri fundati fuerint, tributum, vectigal, & reditum annum non dabunt, & tributum Regum ledes.
units.tr: 13 Now let it be known to the king, that if this city be builded, and the walls set up, then they will not pay toll, tribute, or custom, and thou shalt damage the revenue of kings.

units.la: 14 Præterea pro omni vicissitudine salis palatij quem comedimus, & contemtum Regis non est pulchrum nobis videre: propterea misimus & notum fecimus Regi.
units.tr: 14 Now because we eat the salt of the palace, and it is not meet for us to see the king's dishonour, therefore have we sent and certified the king.
Ve

units.la: 15 Vt quæras in libro historiarum patrum tuorũ & inuenies in libro historiarũ, ac quod urbs ista, urbs est rebellis, & nocens Regibus & principibus, & defestionem faciunt in medio eius à diebus seculi: propterea urbs hæc destructa fuit.
units.tr: 15 That search may be made in the book of the records of thy fathers: so shalt thou find in the book of the records, and know that this city is a rebellious city, and hurtful unto kings and provinces, and that they have raised sedition within the same of old time: for which cause was this city destroyed.

units.la: 16 Notum (insuper) facimus regi, quod si urbs hæc ædificata fuerit, & muri extructi fuerint, ob id portio (quæ est) transflumen, non erit tibi.
units.tr: 16 We certify the king that if this city be builded, and the walls set up, by this means thou shalt have no portion on this side the river.

units.la: QVemadmodum Samaritani, ædificatione templi varijs modis impediuerūt: ita satan, Antichristus & eius membra (spiritualis) templi extructioni, clam & aperte vehementer obsistunt. Quoties vel pauci vel plures, idololatria, superstitione & scelerib⁹ reliquis, Deo seruire volunt, & templum Dei se nihil omittunt, vt eos impediant aut reuocent vel prorsus opprimant. Vltimum quod in hoc capite audinimus, fuit quod ad Cambysem scripserunt epistolam, quæ odium & invidiā Iudæis conciliaret. Exemplum eius hoc loco recitatur. Videbimus tanquam in speculo, quomodo Antichristus variis modis, in primis verò medacijs, calumnijs, & falsis criminationibus, ecclesiā Dei oppugnet, & in odiū apud reges & principes adducat.
units.tr: As the Samaritans hindered the building of the temple in many ways, so Satan, Antichrist and his members, both secretly and openly, strenuously resist the building of the spiritual temple. Whenever few or many wish to serve God, freed from idolatry, superstition and other crimes, and the temple of God, they leave nothing undone to hinder them, to call them back, or utterly to crush them. The last thing we heard in this chapter was that they wrote a letter to Cambyses, intended to win hatred and envy for the Jews. An example of it is recited at this place. We shall see, as in a mirror, how Antichrist, in various ways, and above all by lies, calumnies and false accusations, assails the Church of God and brings it into hatred with kings and princes.

units.la: Primum significant regi, quòd Iudæi murorū Ierusalem fundamenta iecerint & muros compegerint. Vocant vrbem rebellem & pessimam. Quod domos repurgarint & ædificarint, non negari potuit, sed quòd mœnia hoc tempore fundarint, apertū fuit mendacium: toti enim erant in extructione templi. At non pudet aduersarios nostros hodie quoq; nos accusare, quod diuos & sacramenta contumeliā afficiamas, quodq; conuellamus politias, moueamus seditiones, euertamus omne ordine, laxemus frena sceleribus, vetemus bona opera, preces, eleemosynas, ieiunia, quæ accusatio est indignisima. Nam ipsi accusatores nostri, hanc ipsam præcipuè ob causam Euangelij lucè oderunt, quòd bona opera vrget, & opera tenebrarū detestatur. Apud Tertullianum legimus, veteres Christianos accusatos esse, quòd in noćturnis cœtibus, extinćtis lucernis, fœdas libidines exercuerint, occiderint infantes. Si casus aliquis tristis euenieba t, clamabant ad bestias: ad bestias, hoc est, Christianos quibus omnia mala accepta ferebant, bestijs obijciendos esse.
units.tr: First they tell the king that the Jews have laid the foundations of the walls of Jerusalem and joined the walls together. They call the city rebellious and wicked. That they had cleansed and rebuilt the houses could not be denied, but that they had laid the walls at this time was plainly a lie, for they were all engaged in building the temple. Yet our adversaries today are not ashamed to accuse us too: that we insult divine things and the sacraments, that we overturn polities, stir up seditions, subvert all order, loosen the reins to crimes, and forbid good works, prayers, almsgiving and fasting. That accusation is most unworthy. For our accusers hate the very light of the Gospel chiefly for this reason: that it urges good works and condemns the works of darkness. In Tertullian we read that the ancient Christians were accused of practising foul lusts in their nocturnal assemblies, with the lamps put out, and of killing infants. If some sad misfortune befell, they cried, "To the beasts!", that is, that the Christians, to whom they ascribed all evils, should be thrown to the beasts.

units.la: Exponunt periculum quod impendeat regi, nisi initij sobsistat. Dicunt Iudæos, si vrbis illius mœnia & propugnaculum...
units.tr: They set out the danger that threatens the king unless the beginning is resisted. They say that the Jews, if the walls and bulwarks of that city

units.la: Mendacia spargere. cula, instarata fuerint, tributum, vectigal & reditus annuos, non amplius regi persoluturos. Varia sunt nomina Pensionum & census, quae alij aliter interpretantur. His vero comprehendun tur omnia, quae principibus debentur, tributa, vectigalia, decimae, &c. Zinß/Zhenden / rendt/gült / vmbgelt / tribut/schatzung/zol/gleit/stür/brüch/tagwen/büssen/c. Haec persoluenda esse principibus, etiam natura docet. Nam quia sunt publici ministri, subditi eos alere debent. Ad Rom. 13. iubemur haec debita persoluere. Christus quoque verbo & exemplo suo, tributum esse dandum principibus docuit. Neque principes possunt ferre, vt quis annuos eorum redditus minuat. At Iudaeos dicunt sisco nociturOS, si permittatur vltra aedificare. Falsum hoc erat: nam Persicos reges, a quibus magna beneficia acceperant, coluerunt, eisq; tributa non grauatè persoluerunt.
units.tr: Spreading lies: if they are restored, they will no longer pay tribute, custom and annual revenues to the king. There are various names for rents and levies, which different people interpret differently, but under these are comprised everything owed to princes: tributes, customs, tithes, and so on. Zinß/Zhenden / rendt/gült / vmbgelt / tribut/schatzung/zol/gleit/stür/brüch/tagwen/büssen/c. That these are to be paid to princes nature itself also teaches. For since they are public servants, subjects ought to maintain them. In Romans 13 we are commanded to pay these dues. Christ too taught by word and by example that tribute must be given to princes. Nor can princes endure that anyone should diminish their annual revenues. But they say the Jews will harm the treasury if they are allowed to build further. This was false, for they had honoured the Persian kings, from whom they had received great benefits, and had paid them their tributes without grudging.

units.la: Similes accusationes postea quoque factae sunt. Christus ipse accusatur Lucae 23. capite quod author fuerit populo, ne tributum Caesari darent. Nostro quoque tempore quidam, vt principes contra nos exacuant, dicunt nos negare vectigalia, decimas & alia principibus esse pendenda, imo magistratum prorsus abolere.
units.tr: Similar accusations were made afterwards too. Christ himself is accused in Luke 23 of having urged the people not to give tribute to Caesar. In our own time too, some, to stir up princes against us, say that we deny that customs, tithes and other dues are to be paid to princes, and even that we utterly abolish the magistracy.

units.la: Haec omnia simulant Samaritani, se ratione officij sui facere. Fideles enim serui debent auertere pernitiem regni. Praeterea pro omni vicissitudine salis palatij quem comedimus. Ad verbum, quoniam sale palatij saliti sumus. Vetus translatio habet: nos autem memores salis quod in palatio comedimus. Sensus est, quia in palatio educati sumus. Apud veteres hospicij ius contrahebatur mensae & salis consortio. Sal hospitibus ante alios cibos apponi solebat. Vide proverbium Sal & mensa. Item Salem & mensam ne praetereas, id est, ne negligas amicorum consuetudines, aut ne violes amicitiae iura. Nam his rebus olim conciliabantur amici, teste Erasmo. Sal amicitiae symbolum fuit durationis gratia: corpora enim solidiora facit, & diutissime conseruat. Plura Pierius habet in suis Hierogl. Sal mutuę pacis, amoris & amicitiae signum fuisse, Guil. Stuccius in lib. de conuiuijs multis declarat folio 106. Huic phrasis illa respondet: Ich hab desse müss vnd biot nochmals buch / darumb stünd mir übel an/sc. Alij propterea quod destructionem templi destruxi mus, id est, causa sumus, vt templum quod fuit Hierosolymis, destructum fuerit. Si pro vastatione accipitur.
units.tr: The Samaritans pretend all these things as if they acted from the duty of their office, for faithful servants ought to avert the ruin of the kingdom. Moreover, for every turn of the palace salt, which we eat. Word for word: since we have been salted with the salt of the palace. The old translation has: "but we, mindful of the salt which we eat in the palace." The sense is that we were brought up in the palace. Among the ancients the right of hospitality was contracted by sharing a table and salt; salt was set before guests before the other foods. See the proverb "Salt and table." Likewise "Do not pass over salt and table", that is, do not neglect the customs of friends or violate the rights of friendship, for by these things friends were once bound together, as Erasmus testifies. Salt was a symbol of friendship because of its durability, for it makes bodies firmer and preserves them for a very long time. Pierius has more on this in his Hieroglyphics. That salt was a sign of mutual peace, love and friendship, Guil. Stuccius declares at length in his book on banquets, folio 106. That phrase corresponds to this: Ich hab desse müss vnd biot nochmals buch / darumb stünd mir übel an/sc. Others take it thus: "because we have destroyed the destruction of the temple", that is, we are the cause that the temple which was at Jerusalem was destroyed, if it is taken as devastation.

units.la: Contemtum regis non est pulchrum nobis videre.) Quia tot beneficijs affecti sumus, non decet nos contemtum & dedecus regis ferre,nos dicimus: Ἐω were nit,ḇüps wenn wir/ic. Natura docet nos gratos præbere erga illos qui nos beneficijs affecerunt,in primis vero erga principes nostros,qui nos defendunt,si præmonere à periculis eos possumus, si mala ab illis depellere,id omnino debemus facere,etiam cum vitæ nostræ periculo,sed non fingenda sunt pericula. Quot autem sunt homines ingrati,qui suos principes iniuria afficiunt: Prætexunt hodie multi suum officium,iusirandum,interim sua quærunt. Qui dam clamant,ferui Dei sumus,igitur nos asserere oportet honorem diuæ virginis,&c. Quis vero ex nobis, eam contumelia afficit: Ipsis alia cordi sunt, volunt defendere vitam suam Epicuræam,&c.
units.tr: It is not seemly for us to see the king's contempt. Since we have been bound by so many benefits, it is not fitting for us to bear the contempt and disgrace of the king. We say: [Ἐω were nit, ḇüps wenn wir/ic.] Nature teaches us to show gratitude to those who have conferred benefits upon us, and above all to our princes, who defend us. If we can warn them of dangers, and ward off evils from them, we ought certainly to do so, even at risk to our life, but dangers must not be invented. How many people, however, are ungrateful and wrong their princes! Many today pretend their duty and their oath, while meanwhile they seek their own advantage. Some cry, "We are servants of God, therefore we must assert the honour of the blessed Virgin," and so on. But who among us insults her? Others have other things at heart; they want to defend their Epicurean way of life, and so on.

units.la: Propterea misimus & notum fecimus regi, vt quæras in libro historiarum patrum tuorum,& inuenies.&c. Ne videantur malorum affectuum impulsu,odij,metus,quicquam agere:aut popu lum illum calumniari,monent vt rex, vel quispiam ex seruis eius inspiciat Chronica Persarum : in quibus inuenturus sit, quòd vrbs Hierusalem & populus Iudaicus, semper fuerit rebellis & perfidus, nocens regibus & prouincijs, & ab omni suo seditiones concitarit, eamque ob causam à Nabuchodonosore excisa sit. Quasi dicant,Non est quod nobis credas, consule tuos annales,& rem omnino ita habere videbis.
units.tr: Therefore we have sent and informed the king, that you may search in the book of the records of your fathers, and you will find, etc. Lest they seem to act from the impulse of evil feelings, hatred or fear, or to slander that people, they advise the king, or one of his servants, to consult the Chronicles of the Persians, in which he will find that Jerusalem and the Jewish people have always been rebellious and faithless, harmful to kings and provinces, that they have stirred up sedition at every turn, and that for this reason they were cut off by Nebuchadnezzar. As if they said: there is no need for you to believe us; consult your annals, and you will see that the matter stands entirely so.

units.la: Moris fuit apud Medos & Persas,vt res memoratu dignas conscriberent & legerent : id colligere possumus ex libri Hebther secundo & sexto capite. Quando Mardocheus insidias quæ regi tendebantur,per Estheram detexit,rex consignari iussit:Postea cum noctem insomnem duceret, temporis fallendi causa,Chronica proferri iussisset, & ex illis aliquid recitari,incidit in illum locum de Mardochei beneficio,&c. Hanc ipsam consuetudinem habent etiam amplissimæ Venetorum & Bernatum in Auenticis Respublicæ.Vtile autem est in literas referre res magnas,vt postea cognosci possit, quid genti alicui vtile quid pernitiosum fuerit. Si nihil annotatur, postea quisq; pro vt affectus est,res commemorat.
units.tr: It was the custom among the Medes and Persians to write down and read matters worth remembering. We can gather this from the second and sixth chapters of the book of Esther. When Mordecai disclosed through Esther the plot laid against the king, the king ordered it to be recorded. Afterwards, when he was passing a sleepless night, he ordered the Chronicles to be brought to beguile the time, and some of them to be read aloud, and he came upon that passage about Mordecai's service, and so on. The most distinguished councils of the Venetians and the Bernese have this same custom in the public archives of their commonwealth. It is useful to commit great matters to writing, so that it may afterwards be known what was useful or harmful to a people. If nothing is recorded, then afterwards each person recalls events as he has been affected by them.

units.la: Hi miscent vera falsis,vt Sinon. Defecerant Iudæi à Nabuchodonosore plus semel,ideoque pœnas dederant, at superiori bus temporibus bello lacesiti,se defenderunt,libenter de exteris regibus & regionibus bene meriti fuissent, si illi voluissent id agnoscere:falsa igitur est hæc accusatio. Neque mirum si res aliter quàm reuera habuit,in Chronica fuit relata.Solent enim victores seipsos celebrare,& victos deprimere , multaq;
units.tr: These men mix truth with falsehood, as Sinon did. The Jews had revolted from Nebuchadnezzar more than once and had paid the penalty for it. But in earlier times, when they were attacked in war, they defended themselves. They would gladly have deserved well of foreign kings and countries, if those kings had been willing to acknowledge it. This accusation is therefore false. Nor is it surprising that the matter was recorded in the Chronicles otherwise than it really happened. Victors are accustomed to glorify themselves and to belittle the vanquished, and to spread many things about them that are not true.

units.la: H de illis spargere quæ vera non sunt.
units.tr: and to spread many things about them that are not true.

units.la: Antichristus quoq; remittit principes & alios, ad decreta & acta pontificum & conciliorum, ad veteres historias. Quotiescunq; , dicit, hæc religio noua emergere voluit, oppressa fuit & excisa. Exempla proferunt de Vualdensibus, de Albigensibus, qui totum comitatum Tolosanum obtinuerint, & armis suam religionem defendere voluerint, at miserabiliter extincti sint. De aliorum etiam sanguine effuso gloriantur, &c.
units.tr: Antichrist also refers princes and others to the decrees and acts of the popes and councils, and to ancient histories. Whenever, he says, this new religion has tried to rise up, it has been crushed and cut down. They bring forward examples of the Waldensians and the Albigensians, who held the whole county of Toulouse and wanted to defend their religion by arms, but were miserably destroyed. They also boast of the blood shed from others, and so on.

units.la: Iterum hanc vrbem rebellem & seditiosam vocant. Vetus enim est hæc querela aduersariorum veritatis. Prophetæ accusati sunt seditionis, Christus ipse, Apostoli. Hodie clamant, nos magistratui adimere suam authoritatem, schismata excitare. Qui magistratus contemnunt, & seditiones concitant, ne veritatem recipete cogantur, postea omnium malorum causam in euangelij doctrinam conferunt. Ideo autem repetunt Hierusalem vrbem esse seditiosam, quia illa quæ homines maximè mouent, non semel repetimus.
units.tr: Again they call this city rebellious and seditious. This complaint of the adversaries of the truth is an old one. The prophets were accused of sedition, Christ himself, and the apostles. Today they cry out that we are taking away the authority of the magistrate and stirring up schisms. Those who despise the magistrates and stir up sedition, so that they will not be forced to receive the truth, afterwards put the blame for all evils upon the doctrine of the gospel. They repeat that the city of Jerusalem was seditious because we repeat more than once those things which most move people.

units.la: In calce epistolæ scribunt: Si vrbs hæc ædificetur, portio, quæ est transflumen non erit tibi.) Dauid ad Euphratem usque, hostibus victis terras eorum occupauerat. Late enim secundum promissionem eis factam Israelitæ dominati sunt. Nisi vero lacessiti fuissent ab hostibus, illas prouincias non occupassent. Babylonij vero & Assyrij, terras illas abductis Israelitis, cœperunt: nunc dicunt, nisi rex resistat Israelitis, illas mox iterum amissuras esse. Hodie quoque dicunt, nisi illos homines extirpaueritis, non diu rex eris in Hispania, Francia, &c. parant defectionem à rege.
units.tr: In the close of the letter they write: If this city be built, and the walls set up, then you shall have no portion on this side of the river. David had extended his rule as far as the Euphrates, conquering the enemies and occupying their lands. For, according to the promise made to them, the Israelites ruled widely. Yet unless they had been attacked by their enemies, they would not have occupied those provinces. The Babylonians and Assyrians, after carrying the Israelites away, took possession of those lands. Now they say that unless the king resists the Israelites, they will soon lose those lands again. Today too they say that unless you root out those people, you will not be king of Spain, France, and so on for long; they are preparing a revolt against the king.

units.la: Non diserte exprimunt, quod in primis cupiebant, nempe vt rex Iudæos à structura tepli prohibeat, nimirum ne videantur regi aliquid præscribere velle, aut ne ex prauis affectibus agere videantur. Neq; dicunt, cur id clam petant. Hodie Antichristus quoq; non aperte dicit, metuimus ne nos homines incipiant cognoscere, ne amittamus illam potentiam & existimationem quam hactenus habuimus: item redditus nostros ex indulgentijs &c. Omnia odiosè amplificant, vera falsis miscent, Israelitas rebellionis accusant, se commodis regni studere simulant. His regem commouere moliuntur. Hodie quoq; mendacijs & calumnijs agitur, inuocatur brachium seculare contra reformatas ecclesias.
units.tr: They do not openly state what they most desired, namely that the king should forbid the Jews to build the temple, lest they seem to want to prescribe something to the king, or lest they seem to act from wicked motives. Nor do they say why they seek this secretly. Today Antichrist too does not say openly: "We fear lest men begin to recognise us, lest we lose that power and reputation which we have had until now, and likewise our revenues from indulgences, and so on." They magnify everything odiously, they mix truth with falsehood, they accuse the Israelites of rebellion, and they pretend to care for the welfare of the kingdom. By these means they labour to stir up the king. Today too the work is done by lies and slanders, and the secular arm is invoked against the reformed churches.

units.la: Quomodo vero hæ literæ Samaritanorum à rege susceptæ sint, & quid apud regem effecerint postea videbimus.
units.tr: How these letters of the Samaritans were received by the king, and what they accomplished with him, we shall see afterwards.

units.la: HOMILIA
units.tr: HOMILY

units.la: HOMILIA XIIII.
units.tr: HOMILIA XIIII.

units.la: Rex Cambyses respondet ad epistolam Samaritanorum.
units.tr: King Cambyses replies to the letter of the Samaritans.

units.la: 17 Verbum misit rex ad Rehum à commentariis, & Simsai scribam, & reliquos socios eorum qui habitabant in Semariah, & reliquos (qui erant) trans flumen, Pacem, & Cheeth.
units.tr: 17 The king sent a word to Rehum the recorder, and Shimshai the scribe, and their other associates who lived in Samaria, and the rest beyond the river: Peace, and now.

units.la: 18 Epistola quam misistis ad nos, manifeste lecta est coram me.
units.tr: 18 The letter which you sent to us has been plainly read before me.

units.la: 19 Et à me positum est decretum, & quaesierunt, atque invenerunt quod urbs illa à diebus seculi insurgit contra Reges, & rebellat, & rebellio fit in ea.
units.tr: 19 And a decree was issued by me, and they searched and found that this city has risen against kings from ancient times, and rebels, and rebellion is made in it.

units.la: 20 Reges praeterea fortes fuerunt in Ierusalaim & Domini (fuerunt) omnium (qui erant) trans flumen, ac tributum, vectigal, & redditus annuus dabatur illis.
units.tr: 20 Moreover, mighty kings have been in Jerusalem, who ruled over all beyond the river, and tribute, customs, and an annual revenue were given to them.

units.la: 21 Nunc (ergo) ponite edictum ut cessent viri illi, & urbs illa non extruatur, donec à me praeceptum positum sit.
units.tr: 21 Now therefore issue an edict that those men cease, and that this city not be built until a command is given by me.

units.la: 22 Et cavete ut errorem faciatis in hoc: cur crescet corruptio ad nocendum Regibus?
units.tr: 22 And take care that you make no error in this: why should corruption grow to the harm of the kings?

units.la: 23 Quum primum autem exemplar epistolae Artahshasthe Regis lectum fuit coram Rehum & Simsai scriba, & socijs eorum, abierunt festinanter in Ierusalaim ad Iehudaeos, & cessare eos fecerunt brachio & robore.
units.tr: 23 As soon as a copy of the letter of King Artaxerxes had been read before Rehum and Shimshai the scribe and their associates, they hurried to Jerusalem to the Jews and made them cease by force and power.

units.la: 24 Tunc cessavit opus domus Dei quae erat in Ierusalaim, & cessavit usque ad annum secundum regni Dariaues Regis Paras.
units.tr: 24 Then the work of the house of God which was in Jerusalem ceased, and it stayed stopped until the second year of the reign of King Darius of Persia.

units.la: DIximus Samaritanos epistolàdedisse ad Cambysem regem, in qua falsò accusarint Iudaeos, quòd moenia instaurent, quibus perfectis, non amplius tributa persoluturi regionem quę trans Euphratem occupaturi sint. Simulant se ex debita obedientia hæc regi significare: & monent, ut consulat annales suos in quibus reperturus sit, hanc gentem regibus semper infestam & seditiosam fuisse, &c.
units.tr: We said that the Samaritans sent a letter to King Cambyses, in which they falsely accused the Jews that they were restoring the walls, and that once these were finished they would no longer pay tribute, and would seize the region beyond the Euphrates. They pretend that they report this to the king out of due obedience, and they advise him to consult his annals, in which he will find that this nation has always been hostile and seditious toward kings, etc.

units.la: Si res ita habuisset, recte fecissent, quod ad regem scripserunt. Debent enim subiecti quanto possunt studio promouere commoda principum suorum, & auertere mala quæ eis euenire possunt. At falsa erant quæ scribebant: nec vllum erat regi periculum à Iudæis.
units.tr: If the matter had really been so, they would have done well to write to the king. For subjects ought to promote the interests of their rulers with all the zeal they can, and to turn away the dangers that may threaten them. But what they wrote was false, and there was no danger to the king from the Jews.

units.la: Sequitur responsio regis ad cancellarium, scribam, eorumque socios, qui ad ipsum scripserant. Primo loco pacem illis exoptat, hoc est, salutem eis dicit. Deinde certiores eos facit, quod epistolam eorum acceperit, recitari curarit & statuerit, ut legerentur historiæ Persarum: in quibus inuenerint, quod vrbs illa insurrexerit contra reges, rebellarit, seditiones aluerit. Iusta bel la gesserunt Dauid, Asa, Iosaphat, Ezechias: Ioachimus autem & Zedechias, iniuste à rege Babylonio defecerant.
units.tr: There follows the king's reply to the chancellor, the scribe, and their companions who had written to him. First he wishes them peace, that is, he greets them. Then he informs them that he has received their letter, has had it read, and has ordered that the histories of the Persians be read. In these he has found that this city has risen against kings, has rebelled, and has nourished sedition. David, Asa, Jehoshaphat and Hezekiah waged just wars; but Jehoiakim and Zedekiah revolted from the king of Babylon unjustly.

units.la: Reges fortes fuerunt in Ierusalaim.) Dauid, Solomon & alij, de quibus iam diximus, longè lateque dominati sunt. De Solomone libro 3. Regum legitur, dominium eius se extendisse à fluuio magno Euphrate, usque ad riuum Ægypti. Periculum esse putat, ne vires resumant. Addit iam, quod facto opus sit. Nempe dent operam, ut cessent illi viri, ne vrbs extruatur, donec ipse aliter statuat, bis das er eines anderen Stadt werde: bis er sich eines besseren besinne. Item ne errorem faciant in hoc, id est, caueant ne sint negligentes: ne ipsorum culpa regnum detrimentum accipiat.
units.tr: Kings were mighty in Jerusalem. David, Solomon and others, of whom we have already spoken, ruled far and wide. In the third book of Kings we read that Solomon's dominion extended from the great river Euphrates to the river of Egypt. The king thinks there is a danger that they may regain their strength. He now adds what needs to be done: namely, that they should take care that these men cease, and that the city not be built until he himself decides otherwise, [German: until the city falls to another, until he comes to his senses]. Likewise, that they not make a mistake in this, that is, that they take care not to be negligent, so that the kingdom does not suffer loss through their fault.

units.la: Laudandum in hoc rege, quod non absolute & simpliciter statuit, vrbem non extruendam, sed donec aliud decernat. Non enim præcludenda est via melioribus consilijs. Prudentis viri est, si melius consilium cepit, vel ex alijs audiuit, prius emendare. Prouerbio dicitur ἄλλοτρῶν ἀμεινόνων, id est, alteris melioribus. Quo significabant, teste Erasmo Roterodamo, ea quæ prima experientia parum bene successerant, secunda nonnunquam commodius euenire, & prioris consilij erratum posteriore consilio corrigi. Imò iusiurandum quoque impium & illicitum, salubriore consilio mutandum esse, sancti patres testantur.
units.tr: In this king one should praise the fact that he did not decree absolutely and simply that the city must not be built, but only until he decided otherwise. For the way to better counsels must not be closed off. It is the mark of a wise man, if he has taken a better counsel or heard one from others, to amend his earlier decision. There is a proverb, [ἄλλοτρῶν ἀμεινόνων], that is, "of other and better things," by which, as Erasmus of Rotterdam testifies, they meant that things which had turned out poorly at first experience often turn out better the second time, and that an error of an earlier plan is corrected by a later one. Indeed the holy Fathers also testify that even an impious and unlawful oath must be changed by a wiser counsel.

units.la: Laudandum est hoc quoque, quod per scribas suos, historias crutatur. Multi nō volút vlla mora interponere, sed statim illos oppriopprimunt, qui apud eos deferuntur. Sic volo, inquiunt, sic iubeo, sit pro ratione volutas. Multi ad sola nomina, vt si aliquem audiant Lutheranum aut Caluinianum esse, statim sententiam ferunt, nihil vlterius inquirentes.
units.tr: This too is to be praised, that he examines histories through his scribes. Many do not want to interpose any delay, but at once crush those who are denounced before them. "Thus I wish, thus I command; let my will stand for reason," they say. Many, on hearing only a name, as if they had heard that someone is a Lutheran or a Calvinist, at once pass sentence, inquiring no further.

units.la: Peccat quidem in eo rex ille, quod non diligentius omnia perquisiuit, & alteram partem audiuit: sed statim accusatoribus potestatem dat agendi contra populum Dei. At nemo est tam cautus, quin à sycophantis vel calumniatoribus interdum deci piatur. Etiam bonis viris saepenumero suis criminationibus sycophantae fucum faciunt. Sibae contra herum suum Mephibosethum Dauid credidit.
units.tr: That king certainly erred in this, that he did not investigate everything more carefully and hear the other side, but at once gave the accusers power to act against the people of God. Yet no one is so cautious that he is never sometimes deceived by sycophants or slanderers. Even good men are often deceived by the false accusations of sycophants. Ziba, against his master Mephibosheth, deceived David, and David believed him.

units.la: Non statim, etiam multis & magnis viris (vt hoc loco fatum est) aliquid contra aliquem dicentibus, credendum est, audiatur semper altera pars. Multi possunt sua mendacia ornare, vt facilius alios decipiant. Per calumnias effectu est, vt Cambyses optimos suos subditos, qui salutem ipsius, precibus suis, Deo commendabant, pro inimicis habeat. Haman calumnijs à rege Assuero impetrauit, vt vno die omnes Iudaei ad internecionem deleti fuissent, nisi Deus mirabiliter eos conseruasset.
units.tr: One should not believe at once, even when many and great men say something against someone (as happens in this passage); the other side must always be heard. Many can embellish their lies so as the more easily to deceive others. Through slanders it came about that Cambyses regarded as enemies his best subjects, who commended his safety to God in their prayers. Haman, by slanders, obtained from King Ahasuerus that on one day all the Jews should have been destroyed utterly, unless God had miraculously preserved them.

units.la: Samaritani quamprimum recitatae fuerunt regiae literae, festinanter abierunt Hierosolyma & brachio & robore, hoc est, vi & armis, cum exercitu: opus templi impediuerunt. Elucet ex his ingenium impiorum. Accepta potestate, mox Hierosolyma conferunt, nulla mora interposita. Haman statim edictum quod impetrauerat, scribi iussit, & per celeres equos in omnes regni partes mitti. Quando pij affligendi sunt, idololatria aut scelera exercenda, festinant omnes: Si delenda est idololatria, si scelera punienda, res diu differtur & protrahitur.
units.tr: As soon as the royal letters were read, the Samaritans went in haste to Jerusalem "with arm and power," that is, with force and arms, with an army, and they hindered the building of the temple. The character of the impious shines forth from this. Once they have received authority, they go at once to Jerusalem, with no delay. Haman immediately ordered the edict he had obtained to be written out and sent by swift horses to all parts of the kingdom. When the godly are to be afflicted, or idolatry and crimes are to be carried out, everyone hurries; but if idolatry is to be destroyed or crimes punished, the matter is long deferred and dragged out.

units.la: Deinde plus faciunt, quàm eis iniunctum sit. De impediendo templi aedificio, ne verbum quidem ad regem scripserant, neque regis literae aliquid de illa re continebant: tamen statim illud impediunt. Moenium aedificatio nondum attentata erat à Iudaeis.
units.tr: Moreover, they do more than they were ordered. They had not even written a word to the king about hindering the building of the temple, nor did the royal letter contain anything about that matter; yet they at once hindered it. The building of the walls had not yet been attempted by the Jews.

units.la: Modus indicatur quomodo impedierint extructionem templi, nempe brachio & virtute. Non legitur quòd illis ostenderint scriptum regium, & amicè hortati sint, ne contra regis voluntatem pergant, sed vi & imperio agunt. Hodie quoque ab Antichristo brachium carnale inuocatur. Exempla manifesta sunt. Quando Concilia habentur, excitat Antichristus bella, quibus adigat homines, vt decretis Conciliorum subscribant. Post Concilium illud magnum Constantinense, in quo contra datam fidem Ioannes Hufsius crematus est, fequutum est bellum Bohemicum. Nostra memoria post Concilium Tridenti-num,arma Germaniæ illata sunt. Postea cum illud Concilium instauratum vel continuatum fuit, fequuta sunt bella ciuilia in Gallia & in inferiore Germania,quæ vario euentu multis annis gesta sunt,& adhuc geruntur. Neq; dubitandum est quin Anti-christus alijs quoq; his victis,bellum inferre moliatur. Scit fe fa-cris literis suam doctrinam confirmare nequaquam posse, con-uertitur igitur ad arma.
units.tr: The manner is indicated by which they hindered the building of the temple, namely by arm and might. It is not read that they showed the king's writing to the Jews and kindly urged them not to proceed against the king's will, but they acted by violence and command. Even today the carnal arm is invoked by Antichrist. The examples are plain. When councils are held, Antichrist stirs up wars by which he compels men to subscribe to the decrees of the councils. After that great Council of Constance, in which John Huss was burned contrary to the promised faith, the Bohemian war followed. In our own memory, after the Council of Trent, arms were brought against Germany. Afterwards, when that council was renewed or continued, civil wars followed in France and in Lower Germany, which have been waged for many years with varying outcomes, and are still being waged. Nor is there any doubt that Antichrist, having conquered others, is also striving to make war. He knows he can by no means confirm his doctrine by the sacred writings, and so he turns to arms.

units.la: Vltimo loco dicitur opus domus Domini ceffaffe, vfq; ad annum fecundum Darij, nempe Hiftafpis filij regis Persarum. Iudæi quoque videntur socordes fuisse, non statim absterreri debebant: sed metu hostium suorum fracti, opus tam diu inter-miserunt. Mittere ipsi quoq; ad regem suas literas aut nuncios debuerunt, eumq; de omnibus rebus informare. Sed fortassis factum est est idem, quod nostro tempore fit,sic circumdantur principes ab episcopis & alijs, vt literæ,libri,& etiam legati,qui causam Euangelij agu̇t,ad eos venire vix & ne vix quidem possint. Post annos, vt quidam numerant,42.demum ad intermif-sum opus redierunt. Etsi enim ad tempus Deus multa hostibus Euangelij concedat propter nostra peccata,tamen suo tempore efficit,vt templum iterum ædificetur.
units.tr: Lastly it is said that the work on the house of the Lord ceased until the second year of Darius, namely of Hystaspes' son, the king of the Persians. The Jews also seem to have been slothful; they should not have been frightened at once, but, broken by fear of their enemies, they interrupted the work for so long. They ought also to have sent their own letters or messengers to the king and informed him of all matters. But perhaps what happened is the same as what happens in our own time: princes are so surrounded by bishops and others that letters, books, and even envoys who promote the cause of the Gospel can scarcely or not even at all come to them. After some years, as certain men count, forty-two, they at last returned to the interrupted work. For although God for a time allows many things to the enemies of the Gospel because of our sins, yet in his own time he brings it about that the temple is built again.

units.la: Quantumuis autem impijs aliquando succedat , & multa contra pios impetrent: non tamen despondendus est animus, sed Deus precandus, vt principum animos flectat ad veritatis agnitionem,aut alios excitet,quibus gloria Dei curæ fit.
units.tr: However, although the impious sometimes prosper and obtain much against the godly, yet we must not lose heart; rather, we must pray to God that he may bend the minds of princes to the knowledge of the truth, or raise up others to whom the glory of God is a concern.

units.la: CAPVT V.
units.tr: CHAPTER V.

units.la: HOMILIA XV.
units.tr: HOMILY XV.

units.la: Iudæi repetunt ædificium templi.
units.tr: The Jews resume the building of the temple.

units.la: Prophetauit autem Haggai propheta, & Zacharias filius Iddo (qui fuerat) prophetæ ad Iehudæos & Ierusalaim, in nomine Dei Israelis super eos.
units.tr: Haggai the prophet prophesied, and Zechariah the son of Iddo, who was a prophet, to the Jews and to Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel over them.

units.la: 2 Tunc surrexerunt Zerubbabel filius Sealthiel, & Iefuas filius Iofadac, & cœperunt ædificare domum Dei quæ est in Ierusalaim : erant cum eis prophetæ Dei auxiliantes eis.
units.tr: 2 Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Joshua the son of Jozadak arose and began to build the house of God which is in Jerusalem. The prophets of God were with them, helping them.

units.la: NCalce superioris Capitis, diximus templi ædificationem intermissam esse, ad annum vfq; 2. Darij Persarum regis. Quibus autem artibus & technis idfaætum fit, supra explicatum est.
units.tr: At the end of the previous chapter we said that the building of the temple was interrupted until the second year of Darius, king of the Persians. The means and devices by which this came about were explained above.

units.la: Sequitur hoc 5. & sequenti Capite, quomodo populus Dei opus templi refumferit: & præfecti illud iterum impedire volue rint. Significarunt enim Dario Iudæos in ædificatione templi pergere, & consuluerunt eum numid ipsis concedere debeant? Rex iussit Iudæos pergere, sexto igitur anno regni ipsius, ædificium templi absolutum est, & dedicatio habita.
units.tr: The fifth chapter and the one that follows deal with how the people of God resumed the work on the temple, and how the officials again tried to stop it. For they reported to Darius that the Jews were going on with the building of the temple, and asked whether they ought to allow them to do so. The king ordered the Jews to go on. So in the sixth year of his reign the building of the temple was completed and its dedication held.

units.la: Ab anno fecundo Cyri quo iacta fiunt fundamenta templi, vsque ad annum Darij fecundum, numerantur circiter 40. anni. Cyrus enim regnauit annos 30. Cum autem bella gereret cu Scythis, Cambyfes filius ipsius vices videtur gessisse. Cæso Cyro à Tomyri regina, Cambyfes patri succedens regnauit annis 8. Magi duo fratres, occiso Smerde, circiter menses 7. rerum potiti, postea à coniuratis principibus cæsi sunt. Mox Darius filius Hiftapfis, qui etiam Artaxerxes dicitur, regnauit 36. annis. Secundo anno regni ipsius, opus templi haɓtenus intermissum, iterum repetitum fuit, & completum anno sexto. Hinc intelligesIudæorum verba Ioan. 2. capite, qui dicebant ad Christum 46. annis templum hoc extructum est, & tu in tribus diebus eriges illud. At ipse de templo corporis sui loquutus fuerat. Tem plum intra sexennium fuit absolutum. At illi non de continua ædificatione loquuntur: sed vt interruptum & impeditum fuit opus templi.
units.tr: From the second year of Cyrus, when the foundations of the temple were laid, to the second year of Darius, about forty years are counted. For Cyrus reigned thirty years. While he was waging war with the Scythians, his son Cambyses seems to have governed in his place. After Cyrus was slain by Queen Tomyris, Cambyses succeeded his father and reigned eight years. Then the two Magi, who were brothers, after Smerdis was killed, held power for about seven months, and afterwards they were slain by the conspiring princes. Next Darius, son of Hystaspes, who is also called Artaxerxes, reigned thirty-six years. In the second year of his reign the work on the temple, which had been stopped until then, was taken up again, and it was completed in the sixth year. From this we understand the words of the Jews in John chapter 2, who said to Christ, "This temple was built in forty-six years, and will you raise it up in three days?" But he had spoken of the temple of his body. The temple was finished within six years. Yet they are not speaking of continuous building, but of the work of the temple as it was interrupted and hindered.

units.la: 1. Quomodo autem & qua occasione tam diu intermissum opus repetunt? Adhortatione prophetarum, quos Deus excitauerat. Prophetarunt.) Id est, Vaticinati vel concionati sunt quidam prophetæ illo tempore, nempe Haggæus & Zacharias filius, id est, nepos Iddo: nam patrem habuit Barachiam. Malachiæ non fit mentio, quem quidam eundem cum Zacharia esse volunt, &c.
units.tr: 1. But how and on what occasion did they resume a work that had been left undone for so long? By the exhortation of the prophets, whom God had raised up. "They prophesied": that is, certain prophets at that time prophesied or preached, namely Haggai and Zechariah the son of Iddo, that is, his grandson, for he had Berechiah as his father. Malachi is not mentioned, whom some wish to be the same as Zechariah, and so on.

units.la: Concionati sunt Iudæis, qui fuerunt in Iudæa & Hierosolymis. Iudæi dicti sunt post relaxationem captiuitatis Babylonicæ, quotquot redierunt, etsi non ex tribu vel regno Iudæ, sed de aliis tribubus effent: sicut hodie quoq;.
units.tr: They preached to the Jews who were in Judah and at Jerusalem. The Jews were so called after the release from the Babylonian captivity, all who returned, even if they were not from the tribe or kingdom of Judah but from the other tribes, just as today also.

units.la: In nomine Domini Israel (qui fuit) super eos.) Iussu & mandato Domini prophetarunt: qui erat cum eis, cuius spiritu af- flabantur. Prophetæ non sua somnia attulerunt, sed Dei verbum.
units.tr: "In the name of the Lord, the God of Israel, who was over them." They prophesied by the command and order of the Lord, who was with them, by whose Spirit they were inspired. The prophets did not bring their own dreams, but the Word of God.

units.la: Quid prædicarint, in libris eorum propheticis, qui adhuc extant, continetur. Hortati sunt omnes, ad operis promotionem: socordia eorum in eo quod res suas conficerent, Dei vero gloriam parum curarent, reprehenderunt. Hoc est vulgare hominum vitium hodie quoque, ut suis commodis consulant, de propagatione Dei parum soliciti.
units.tr: What they preached is contained in their prophetic books, which still survive. They all urged the advancement of the work and rebuked the sloth of the people, who attended to their own affairs but cared little for the glory of God. This is a common human vice even today, to look after their own advantage and be little concerned with the spreading of God's cause.

units.la: Exemplum hoc loco habemus clementiæ diuinæ, cum enim res tantum non desperatæ essent, & templi absolutio vix & ne vix quidem sperari posset, Deus prophetas excitauit, qui populum hortarentur ad opus coeptum persequendum, eosque erigerent & consolarentur. Aliis quoque temporibus rebus afflictis, Deus suos non deseruit, sed opem eis tulit.
units.tr: Here we have an example of divine mercy. For when affairs were all but despaired of, and the completion of the temple could hardly, if at all, be hoped for, God raised up prophets who would exhort the people to pursue the work they had begun, and who would encourage and console them. At other times too, when things were in distress, God did not forsake his people, but brought them help.

units.la: Prophetæ, vt hoc obiter dicam, non tantum futura prædixerunt, sed instar ministrorum ecclesiæ populum docuerunt. Neque ex tribu tantum Leui (quam Deus exercitio religionis destinarat) sed ex omnibus delecti fuerunt, vt etiam Pontifices & Leuitas ad faciendum officium hortarentur. Multi prophetæ fuerunt omnibus temporibus, magno spiritu præditi. Quidam ex illis, suas conciones in scripta retulerunt, quorum alij nominantur maiores, quòd volumina grandiora vaticiniorum: alij minores, quòd minora conscripserint. Inter minores etiam hi duo referuntur.
units.tr: The prophets, to say this in passing, not only foretold the future but, in the manner of ministers of the Church, taught the people. They were chosen not only from the tribe of Levi (which God had appointed for the exercise of religion) but from all the tribes, so that they might also exhort the high priests and Levites to do their duty. There were many prophets in all ages, endowed with a great spirit. Some of them put their sermons into writing; of these, some are called greater, because their volumes of prophecy are larger, and others lesser, because they wrote less. Among the lesser ones these two are reckoned.

units.la: Discunt deinde qui in prophetico munere versantur, ne desperent, etsi corruptissima sunt tempora, sed subinde instent & vrgeant proceres & plebem.
units.tr: Then those who are engaged in the prophetic office learn not to despair, even if the times are most corrupt, but from time to time they should press and urge on the nobles and the common people.

units.la: Quomodo se proceres populi, audita adhortatione prophetarum gesserunt? Tunc surrexerunt Zerobabel dux & Iesus summus Pontifex, & coeperunt ædificare domum domini, non diu interrogantes, an præfecti id concederevellent, nec ne. Qui vel fragt/ derirrt vel. Cum intelligunt Deum id velle, statim ad opus se accingunt. Haggæus dicit, Dominum spiritum eorum excitasse.
units.tr: How did the nobles of the people act when they heard the exhortation of the prophets? "Then Zerubbabel the leader and Joshua the high priest arose and began to build the house of the Lord," not asking for long whether the officials would allow it or not. Those who either wavered or mocked... When they understood that God wished it, they at once set themselves to the work. Haggai says that the Lord stirred up their spirit.

units.la: Erant cum eis prophetæ Dei, corroborantes eos.) Erant ἐργοδιώκται, facile enim relabimur à bene coeptis, nisi subinde incitemur & exmulemur. Vsus huius partis.
units.tr: "The prophets of God were with them, strengthening them." They were the drivers of the work, for we easily fall back from good beginnings unless we are from time to time spurred on and stirred up. The use of this part.

units.la: 1. Quomodo audiendæ sunt sacræ conciones? Illi audita adhortatione prophetarum, statim operi accinguntur, quod metu vicinorum tam diu intermiserant: neque rem diu differunt. Potuissent dicere, nolumus absque licentia tegis hoc facere: conijceremus nos in certissimum periculum, sed cum audiunt Dei hanc esse voluntatem, manu statim admouent operi. Nihil autem temere agunt, sed ex consilio diuino. Sunt qui si in telligant concionatoribus aliquid probari, illud facere nolint, etiamsi antea eis placuit. Et quo plures conciones audiunt, eo peiores reddantur. Multi eos prorsus nolunt audire.
units.tr: 1. How are sacred sermons to be heard? Having heard the exhortation of the prophets, they at once set about the work which for fear of their neighbours they had so long left undone, and they do not put the matter off for long. They might have said, "We will not do this without the king's permission; we would be casting ourselves into the greatest danger." But when they hear that this is the will of God, they at once put their hand to the work. Nor do they act rashly, but in accordance with the divine counsel. There are some who, if they understand that something is approved by the preachers, are unwilling to do it, even though they liked it before. And the more sermons they hear, the worse they become. Many are altogether unwilling to hear them.

units.la: 2. Discevt si quando metu templum Domini ædificare no luisti, tandem animum recipias. Vt hoc loco Iudæi Iosephus Arimathensis & Nicodemus metu Iudæorum, non publicè Christum profitebantur initio, postea vero honestè eu tumularunt, sumta audacia. Apostoli quoq; qui metu fugerant, tandem Christum ad extremum vsq; spiritum profecsi sunt.
units.tr: 2. Learn that if at any time out of fear you have been unwilling to build the temple of the Lord, at last take heart. So Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus, for fear of the Jews, at first did not openly profess Christ, but afterwards, taking courage, honourably buried him. The apostles too, who had fled for fear, at last followed Christ even to the last breath.

units.la: 3. Proceres populi aliis exemplo sint, hic primi fuerunt Zerobabel & Iesue, qui opus instaurarunt: accesserunt illis prophetæ, & postea populus. Hodie templum Domini quod collapsum est, posset instaurari, hoc est, superstitiones & scelera tolli, vera religio & virtutes plantari, si proceres primi facerent officium. Puderet enim vulgus ab eis superari. Sed si illi excitari nō possint, res vel non procedit, vel saltem tarde.
units.tr: 3. Let the leaders of the people be an example to others. Here Zerubbabel and Joshua were the first, who renewed the work; the prophets joined them, and afterwards the people. Today the temple of the Lord, which has fallen into ruin, could be restored, that is, superstitions and wickedness removed, true religion and virtues planted, if the leaders first did their duty. For the common people would be ashamed to be outdone by them. But if they cannot be roused, the affair either does not go forward or at least goes slowly.

units.la: 4. Coniunguntur subinde dux & summus Pontifex. Illi enim duo ordines, ad conseruationem populi totius à Deo instituti, si concordes sint, feliciter ædificium templi promouere possunt.
units.tr: 4. The leader and the high priest are sometimes joined together. For these two orders, appointed by God for the preservation of the whole people, if they are in agreement, can happily advance the building of the temple.

units.la: HOMILIA XVI.
units.tr: HOMILY XVI.

units.la: Thatthnai conatur inhibere ædificium templi, sed frustra.
units.tr: Tattenai tries to halt the building of the temple, but in vain.

units.la: 3 In illo tempore venit adeos Thatthnai dux (eorum qui erant) trans flumen, & Setharbozenai, & socij eorum: & sic dixerunt eis, Quis posuit vobis præceptum vt domum hanc ædificaretis, & muros istos fundaretis?
units.tr: 3 At that time Tattenai, governor beyond the river, and Shethar-bozenai, with their companions, came to them and said to them: Who gave you a decree to build this house and to finish these walls?

units.la: 4 Tunc (adhuc) huiusmodi diximus eis, Quæ sunt nomina virorum qui hoc ædificium ædificant?
units.tr: 4 Then we said to them in this manner: What are the names of the men who are building this building?

units.la: 5 Oculus autem Dei eorum erat super senes Iehudæorum & non fecerunt cessare eos, donec res ad Dariaues pergeret: tunc igitur responderunt per epistolam super hís.
units.tr: 5 But the eye of their God was upon the elders of the Jews, and they did not make them cease until the matter went to Darius; then they replied by letter concerning these things.

units.la: CAP. V.
units.tr: CHAPTER 5.

units.la: INitio huius Capitis dictum est, populum Dei aedificium templi, quod multis annis vicinorum malitia intermissum fuerat, repetiuisse. Hortati enim eos sunt prophetae, vt id facerent, promittetes ejs auxilium diuinum. Sequitur Tatthnai praefectum cum socijs, iterum aedificium hoc impedire voluisse, sed frustra. Consideremus primum literam, aut sensum historicum, deinde eius vsum & fructum.
units.tr: At the beginning of this chapter it was said that the people of God resumed building the temple, a work that had been interrupted for many years by the malice of their neighbours. The prophets had urged them to do it, promising them divine help. It follows that Tattenai, the governor, with his colleagues, again tried to hinder this building, but in vain. Let us consider first the letter, or the historical sense, and then its use and fruit.

units.la: In illo tempore.) Nempe cum aedificio denuo manum admouissent, venit ad Iudaeos Tatthnai praeses vel dux eorum qui trans Euphratem erant, & Setharbozenai, qui etiam dux fuisse videtur, & socij eorum vel consiliarij, qui interrogarunt eos, cuius edicto freti, templum & muros istos, scilicet templi instaurent? Audierant fortasis quod à Cambyse decretū effet, ne aedificaretur templum antequā ipse iusisset, quodq; praeses cum vicinis, armis aedificationem prohibuissent. Mox 10. versu dicitur, eos etiam de nominibus interrogasse eorum, qui duces erant, vt ad regem scriberent. Similis fere historia Matth. 21. de Christo habetur. Qui cum in templo docerēt, venerunt ad eum pontifices & seniores populi, dicentes: ἐν ποία ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς; καὶ τίς σοί ἔδωκε τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην;
units.tr: At that time.)
