Namely, when they had again put their hands to the building, Tattenai, the governor or prefect of those beyond the Euphrates, came to the Jews, and Shethar-bozenai, who also seems to have been a leader, and their colleagues or counsellors, and asked them by whose edict they were relying when they set about restoring this temple and these walls. They had perhaps heard that Cambyses had decreed that the temple should not be built until he himself had given the order, and that the governor, with his neighbours, had forbidden the building by force of arms. Soon after, in verse 10, it is said that they also asked for the names of the men who were the leaders, so that they could write to the king. A similar story is found in Matthew 21 about Christ. When he was teaching in the temple, the chief priests and elders of the people came to him, saying: "By what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority?" [ἐν ποία ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς; καὶ τίς σοί ἔδωκε τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην;]

units.la: Nota diligenter, quod ne vnus exillis nominatur, qui antea obstiterunt, ne templum domini aedificaretur, nempe Rehum, Simsai, & aliorum. Videntur enim intra illud tempus obijsse. Quot auferuntur annis saltem viginti? Neque boni tantum, sed malìquoque, qui nescio quot annos sibi pollicentur, ex hac vita decedunt, saepe ex improuiso. Quae si diligenter homines & saepe cogitarent, non ita bonis viris aduersarentur, neque contra conscientiam sese improbis coniungerent.
units.tr: Note carefully that not one of those is named who had earlier opposed the building of the Lord's temple, namely Rehum, Shimshai, and the others. It seems they had died in the meantime. How many years are taken away, at least twenty? Not only the good but also the wicked, who promise themselves I know not how many years, depart from this life, often unexpectedly. If men thought about this carefully and often, they would not oppose good men in this way, nor join themselves to the wicked against their conscience.

units.la: Tatthnaus autem ille, eiusq; sodales, meliores fuerunt prioribus illis, non enim tanto impetu hanc causam agunt, non ad arma vertuntur, neq; falsa ad regem scribunt, aut maledictis Iudaeis inuidiam apud illum conflant: nolunt tamen aliquid contra regis decretum & voluntatem fieri.
units.tr: But that Tattenai and his companions were better than those earlier men. For they do not pursue this cause with such violence, they do not take up arms, they do not write falsehoods to the king, nor do they stir up hatred against the Jews in his eyes with slanders. Yet they do not want anything done against the king's decree and will.

units.la: Iudei non temere hoc aedificium suscēperant, sed iussu Dei per prophetas reuelato, dicunt igitur quae sint nomina virorū, qui hoc aedificium aedificet. Si verba sunt Tetthnai & sociorum eius, per interrogationem legantur.
units.tr: The Jews had not undertaken this building rashly, but at the command of God revealed through the prophets. They therefore state the names of the men who are building this structure. If these are the words of Tattenai and his companions, let them be read as a question.

units.la: Oculus autem Dei erat super senes, &c.) Prouidentia, gratia, auxilium Dei, efficiebat, vt non intermitteretur opus, tantisper dum negotium referretur ad regem. Quoties fit vt causae non fæ non ita difficiles, diu protrahantur: ita potuissetdonec per epistolam responderetur super his,instauratio templi ad annos aliquot iterum differri,nisi Deus Iudæis opem tulisset.
units.tr: But the eye of God was upon the elders, etc.) The providence, grace and help of God caused the work not to be interrupted while the matter was referred to the king. How often it happens that causes that are not so difficult are drawn out for a long time. So it could have happened that the restoration of the temple would again have been put off for some years until a reply was given by letter about these matters, had God not brought help to the Jews.

units.la: De usu & fructu huius narrationis.
units.tr: On the use and fruit of this narrative.

units.la: 1. Si ea facimus quæ Deus iubet,ideoque recta sunt,nam quam desunt homines,qui nos interpellent, interrogantes qua potestate, quo iure id faciamus? Vt illi Iudæos appellant,qua authoritate ædificent? De Christo antea diximus,de Apostolis eius idem legimus. Nostra tempestate non solum quæritur,cur à politico magistratu templa repurgentur, idolaque auferantur, altaria? &c. Sed armis hoc facere prohibentur: arcentur à sacris, qui non statim Antichristo parent. Pij in hac vita nunquam quieti erunt. Qui propter Christum nil ferre volunt, coguntur postea duriora propter diabolum perferre.
units.tr: 1. If we do the things that God commands, and therefore they are right, is it not the case that there are men who challenge us, asking by what power and by what right we do it? As they asked the Jews by what authority they were building. We have spoken earlier about Christ; we read the same of his apostles. In our own time it is asked not only why temples are cleansed by the civil magistrate, and idols and altars removed, etc.; but they are forbidden to do this by force of arms, and those who do not at once obey Antichrist are kept from the sacred things. The godly will never be at rest in this life. Those who will bear nothing for Christ are afterwards compelled to suffer harsher things for the sake of the devil.

units.la: 2. Deum aliquando in locum tyrannorum, meliores magistratus substituere. Priores illi præfecti & consiliarij, atrocissimi erant hostes populi Dei, iam meliores ipsis succedunt & humaniores. Vulgo dicitur, in magistratu raro meliores succedere. Valerius Maximus libro 6. capite 2. historiam refert de quadam vetula Syracusana, quæ quotidie Deos orabat, ut Dionysius tyrannus, cui alij exitium imprecabantur, incolumis & sibi superstes esset, ne scilicet deterior in locum eius succederet. Cæterum Deus non raro propter fideles suos, mutat mores malorum, aut bonos excitat, ne illi sub onere pereant: sed ut inducias habeant, & se colligere iterum posset. Godolias, de quo in postremis Ieremiæ Capitibus legitur, vir bonus euersa Hierosolymorum urbe, præfectus fuit reliquis populi. Nostro quoque tempore factum est interdum, ut præfecti alieni à nostra religione, melius se gesserint erga Euangelicos, quàm illi ipsi qui eandem nobiscum doctrinam profesi sunt. Patienter igitur feramus etiam dura tyrannorum imperia, ita tamen ut in terea contra Dei præcepta nihil agamus. Illi vero ingentes Deo agant gratias, pro ingenti hoc beneficio, quibus dedit magistratum bonum & amantem veræ pietatis.
units.tr: 2. God sometimes sets better magistrates in the place of tyrants. Those earlier prefects and counsellors were the most savage enemies of the people of God; now better and more humane men succeed them. It is commonly said that better men rarely succeed in public office. Valerius Maximus, book 6, chapter 2, tells the story of a certain old woman of Syracuse, who prayed every day that Dionysius the tyrant, whom others cursed to destruction, might remain unharmed and survive her, lest, of course, a worse man should succeed him in his place. But God, not rarely, for the sake of his faithful, changes the behaviour of the wicked, or raises up good men, so that the faithful do not perish under the burden, but may have a respite and be able to gather themselves again. Gedaliah, of whom we read in the last chapters of Jeremiah, a good man, after the city of Jerusalem had been overthrown, was made governor over the remnant of the people. In our own time too it has sometimes happened that prefects who are foreign to our religion have behaved better towards the evangelical folk than those who profess the same doctrine as we do. Let us therefore bear patiently even the harsh rule of tyrants, yet so that in the meantime we do nothing against the precepts of God. Let them give immense thanks to God for this great benefit, who has given them a good magistrate who loves true godliness.

units.la: 3. Quomodo præfecti & alij subditi, suis principibus fidem seruare debeant. Titthnai fidelis fuit regi suo: noluit Iudæos in ædificio templi pergere, contra regis decretum, diligenter omnia cognoscit, & tantum illa scribit, de quibus ei certo constat. Ita efficiant præfecti, ne quid contra leges & voluntatem suorum principum fiat. Hac tamen conditione, vt si sciunt Deum aliquid velle, si illi non opponant. Titthnai forte ignorabat, Iudaeos consilio Dei repetere opus templi, alioqui no se oppo-suissent. Quanquam multi sint qui ne deponantur ab officio, con tra conscientiam pijs negotium facessunt. Si fides subditorum erga suum magistratum laudatur, quanto magis fides Regi re-gum praestanda est.
units.tr: 3. How prefects and other subjects ought to keep faith with their princes. Tattenai was faithful to his king. He would not let the Jews proceed with the building of the temple against the king's decree; he examines everything carefully, and writes only those things about which he is certain. Prefects should act in such a way that nothing is done against the laws and will of their rulers. Yet on this condition: that if they know that God wills something, they should not oppose it. Perhaps Tattenai did not know that the Jews were resuming the work of the temple by the counsel of God; otherwise they would not have opposed it. Yet there are many who, so that they may not be removed from office, bring trouble upon the godly against their conscience. If the loyalty of subjects towards their magistrate is praised, how much more loyalty is owed to the King of kings.

units.la: 4. Exemplum habemus confessionis in Iudaeis. Nomina sua profitentur apud praefectos, atque ita testantur se cultum Dei Israelitici approbare. Non vacat periculo, nomina indicare, vt ad regem mittantur. Nesciebant enim fortasis quomodo rex erga Iudaicam religionem vel templum affectus esset. Factum est vetustis Christianorum temporibus, vt nomina eorum fuerint relata in catalogos, vt vel omnes vel praecipui ex illis supplicio afficerentur. Nostro tempore, multi confessionibus fidei subscripserunt, quae postea regibus oblatae sunt, non sine vitae periculo.
units.tr: 4. We have an example of confession in the Jews. They declare their names before the prefects, and so bear witness that they approve the worship of the God of Israel. It was not without danger to name themselves, so that they might be sent to the king. For perhaps they did not know how the king was disposed towards the Jewish religion or the temple. In the early times of the Christians it happened that their names were recorded in lists, so that all of them, or the principal ones among them, might be punished. In our time many have subscribed to confessions of faith, which were afterwards presented to kings, not without danger to life.

units.la: 5. Quae causa fit, quod in medio hostium ecclesia aedificetur. Oculus Dei erat super, propterea illi tantum efficere non potuerunt, vt vel tamdiu opus suspenderetur, donec sciri posset voluntas regis. Per oculum fauorem, gratiam, & auxilium Dei significari, diximus. Non tribuitur bonitati Titthnai, non sociorum eius, quod aedificium processit, sed bonitati Dei, qui veterem populum veluti agnum in medio luporum, clementer conseruauit. Hodie quoque ecclesiam contra hostium corporalium & spiritualium molitiones defendit. Nihil hic hostium clementiae, nihil nostris consilijs tribuendum. Psalmo 34. Oculi Dominae super iustos, & aures eius ad clamorem eorum. Etsi mundus fideles contemnat, tamen Deus curam eorum gerit: etsi odio sint omnibus, tamen Deus eos amat. Ab illis enim quos aspicimus, oculos non auertimus. Ein aug auff einen haben/ oculum super aliquem ponere, nostra lingua assiduam curam significat.
units.tr: 5. Why the Church is built in the midst of enemies. "The eye of God was upon them": for this reason the enemies could not achieve even this, that the work should be suspended for so long until the will of the king could be known. We have said that by "eye" is signified the favour, grace and help of God. The progress of the building is attributed not to the goodness of Tattenai or of his companions, but to the goodness of God, who mercifully preserved the ancient people as a lamb in the midst of wolves. Today too he defends the Church against the attempts of corporeal and spiritual enemies. Nothing here is to be attributed to the mercy of enemies, nothing to our own counsels. Psalm 34: "The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears are open to their cry." Even if the world despises the faithful, God nevertheless takes care of them; even if they are hated by all, God nevertheless loves them. For we do not turn our eyes away from those whom we look upon. "Ein aug auff einen haben," to set the eye upon someone, in our language signifies constant care.

units.la: Deus exaudit etiam preces eorum, qui apud mundum repulsam patiuntur. Psalmo 121. Ecce non dormitabit neque dormiet custos Israelis. Saepe cogitamus Deum nos negligere, vel dormire: reuoca igitur in metem quod perpetuas pro salute totius ecclesiae & singulis eius membris, agat excubias, prospiciat & auertat pericula. Vtitur quidem ad hanc rem opera angelorum, sed ipse est supremus excubiarum praefectus. Quia Deus tam diligenter nos custodit, nos quoq; nostros oculos ad ipsum conuertamus, vt de Dauide aliquoties legitur, ipsum adoremus, opem ab eo petamus.
units.tr: God also hears the prayers of those who suffer rejection in the world. Psalm 121: "Behold, he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep." We often think that God neglects us, or sleeps. Therefore call to mind that he keeps unceasing watch for the salvation of the whole Church and of each of its members, watches over them and averts dangers. He indeed uses the work of angels for this purpose, but he himself is the supreme commander of the watch. Since God guards us so diligently, let us also turn our eyes to him, as is read several times of David: let us worship him and seek help from him.

units.la: Videmus & experimur mundum non posse ferre aedificium templi, nos freti ope diuina non patiamur nos a sancto proposito reuocari, sed constanter in eo pergamus.
units.tr: We see and experience that the world cannot bear the building of the temple. Let us, relying on divine help, not allow ourselves to be called back from our holy purpose, but persevere constantly in it.

units.la: HOMILIA XVII.
units.tr: HOMILIA XVII.

units.la: Epistola Tatthnai & sociorum eius ad Darium, qua eum consulunt super aedificatione templi.
units.tr: The letter of Tatthnai and his associates to Darius, in which they consult him about the building of the temple.

units.la: 6 Exemplar epistolae quam miserunt Thatthenai dux (eorum qui erant) trans flumen, & Setharbozenai, & socij eius, & Apharsechaie, qui (erant) trans flumen, ad Darianes regem.
units.tr: 6 A copy of the letter which Thatthenai, governor of the (people) beyond the river, and Setharbozenai, and his associates, the Apharsechaie who (were) beyond the river, sent to King Darianes.

units.la: 7 (Verbum miserunt ad eum) Et sic scriptum erat inter eam, Darianes regi pax omnis.
units.tr: 7 (The words they sent to him.) And it was written in it thus: To King Darianes, all peace.

units.la: 8 Notum sit regi quod profecti sumus in Iehudaeam provinciam ad domum Dei maximi, & ipsa aedificatur lapide marmoreo, lignaq; ponuntur in parietibus, atq; opus illud festinanter fit, & prosperè cedit in manibus eorum.
units.tr: 8 Let it be known to the king that we went into the province of Judaea, to the house of the great God, and it is being built with marble stones, and timbers are laid in the walls, and that work is done with haste and goes forward prosperously in their hands.

units.la: 6 Tunc interrogauimus seniores illos, (atq;) sic diximus eis, Quis posuit vobis praeceptum vt domum hanc aedificaretis, & muros istos fundaretis?
units.tr: 9 Then we questioned those elders, and spoke to them thus: Who gave you the command to build this house and to lay the foundations of these walls?

units.la: 10 Et etiam de nominibus eorum interrogauimus eos, vt nota faceremus illa tibi (id est) vt scribe-remus nomina virorum (qui sunt) duces eorum.
units.tr: 10 We also asked them their names, so that we might make them known to you, that is, that we might write down the names of the men who are their leaders.

units.la: 11 Eiusmodi autem verbum responderunt nobis, dicendo, Nos sumus serui Dei caeli & terrae, & readificamus domum quae fuerat aedificata ante annis multis; quam rex Israelis magnus aedificauerat, & fundauerat eam.
units.tr: 11 They gave us this answer, saying: We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the house which was built many years ago, which a great king of Israel had built and established.

units.la: 12 Sed postquam provocauerunt patres nostri Deum caeli, tradidit eos in manum Nebuchadnesar regis Babel Chaldæi, & domum hanc destruxit, ac populum transmigrare fecit in Babel.
units.tr: 12 But after our fathers provoked the God of heaven, he gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, the Chaldean, who destroyed this house and carried the people away to Babylon.

units.la: 43 Veruntamen anno primo Chores regis Babel, Chores rex posuit edictum, ut domum Dei hanc aedificarent:
units.tr: 13 Nevertheless, in the first year of Cyrus, king of Babylon, King Cyrus issued a decree that they should build this house of God.

units.la: 14 Et etiam vasa domus Dei aurea & argentea, quæ Nebuchadnezar eduxerat è templo quod erat in Ierusalaim, & tulerat ea in templum Babel, eduxit il la Chores rex è templo Babel, & tradita fuerunt ipsi Sesbasar, quem ducem constituerat.
units.tr: 14 And also the golden and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple in Jerusalem and carried into the temple at Babylon, King Cyrus brought out of the temple at Babylon, and they were handed over to Sheshbazzar, whom he had appointed governor.

units.la: 15 Dixitq; ei, Hæc vasa tolle, abi, depone ea in templo quod est in Ierusalaim, & domus Dei aedificetur in loco suo.
units.tr: 15 And he said to him: Take these vessels, go, put them in the temple which is in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be built in its place.

units.la: 16 Tunc Sesbasar iste venit, iecit fundamenta domus Dei quæ est in Ierusalaim, et ex eo tempore usque ad hoc tempus aedificatur, & necdum perfecta est.
units.tr: 16 Then this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God which is in Jerusalem, and from that time until now it has been under construction, and it is not yet finished.

units.la: 17 Nunc ergo si regi bonum (sit), perquiratur in domo thesaurorum regis quæ est illic in Babel, anita sit quod à Chores rege positum sit edictum ut reædificarent domum Dei hanc quæ est in Ierusalaim: & voluntatem suam super hoc mittat ad nos.
units.tr: 17 Now therefore, if it pleases the king, let a search be made in the treasure house of the king which is there in Babylon, to see whether it is true that King Cyrus issued a decree that they should rebuild this house of God which is in Jerusalem; and let him send his pleasure to us concerning this matter.

units.la: HOc capite exemplum insigne & consolatione plenum nobis proponitur, quòd Deus suos qui mandata faciunt, nō deserat, sed opem eis & auxilium ferat. Mandarat Iudæis per suos prophetas, ut repeterent aedificium templi, quod multis annis intermissum erat. Id cum exequerentur, Tathnai cum suis interpellant eos: quis dederit eis potestatem reperendi aedificium templi? Deus autem corroborauit Iudæos, ut non cessarent ab opere, sed strenuè pergerent: mouit etiam cor Tithnai & aliorum, ne cogerent eos differre aedificium, tantisper dum certi aliquid à rege fuisset constitutum: item ut sincerè Iudæorum negocium apud regem agerent, & tantum non iuuarent, ut opus templi perficeretur. Apographum epistolæ ad regem, hoc loco continetur.
units.tr: In this chapter a remarkable example, full of consolation, is set before us: that God does not forsake those who do his commands, but brings them help and aid. He had commanded the Jews through his prophets to resume the building of the temple, which had been left unfinished for many years. When they carried this out, Tathnai and his men challenged them: who had given them authority to restore the building of the temple? But God strengthened the Jews so that they did not cease from the work but pressed on vigorously; he also moved the heart of Tathnai and the others, so that they did not force them to delay the building until something had been fixed by the king; and likewise so that they would deal honestly with the king on the Jews' business, and would not hinder, but rather help, the completion of the temple. A copy of the letter to the king is contained in this place.

units.la: Multum autem dissimilis est superiori epistolæ, quæ accusatione Iudaicæ gentis constat, hæc verò laude Dei & Iudæorum. Est potius epistola commendatitia quàm criminatoria. Partes eius sunt tres, nempe titulus, narratio & epilogus. Titulus continet subscriptionem: quae indicat authores huius epistolae, qui sunt Tathnai praeses, consiliarij & Apherscechael, non est nomen gentis, sed functionis, ἔπαρχοι praefecti Syriae, Sic amplitudine Superscriptione quę ostendit cui scribatur, nempe Dario: & salutationem.
units.tr: Yet it is very unlike the earlier letter, which consists of an accusation of the Jewish nation, whereas this one consists of praise of God and of the Jews. It is a letter of recommendation rather than of accusation. Its parts are three, namely the heading, the narrative, and the conclusion. The heading contains the subscription, which indicates the authors of this letter: Tathnai the governor, his counsellors, and Apherscechael. This is not the name of a people but of an office: eparchoi [ἔπαρχοι], prefects of Syria. Next comes the superscription, which shows to whom it is written, namely Darius, and then the greeting.

units.la: Pax omnis. Latini dicunt salutem plurimam. Hebraei per pacem omnia comprehendunt quae ad conseruationem animi & corporis faciunt. Haec magistratui quoque nostro imprecari debemus & alijs.
units.tr: Peace in full. The Latins say "very many greetings." The Hebrews comprehend under "peace" all things that serve the preservation of soul and body. We ought to pray these things also for our magistrate and for others.

units.la: Narratio vel expositio, constat duabus potissimum partibus. Primum dicunt se profectos esse in Iudaeam, ad templum Dei maxim (quae egregia est confessio de Deo, quanquam non plena) quod aedificetur maximis lapidibus. Santes dicit marmoreis lignaponi in muris: Sic trome lege manin die murem. Forte suspicati sunt eos aedificare velle munitionem, &c. Item aedificium hoc festinanter fieri, & feliciter procedere. Addunt se interrogasse seniores, quis ipsis hanc potestatem dederit, qui hufq; nominibus appellentur duces eorum, qui hoc opus in primis vrgeant, vt regi hoc significent.
units.tr: The narrative, or exposition, consists chiefly of two parts. First they say that they went into Judaea, to the great house of God (an excellent confession about God, though not a full one), which is being built with great stones. They say it is built with marble, and timbers are laid in the walls. Perhaps they suspected that they intended to build a fortress, etc. They also say that this building is going forward quickly and succeeding well. They add that they questioned the elders as to who had given them this authority, and named the leaders who were pressing this work forward, so that they might report it to the king.

units.la: Politica doctrina excerpenda est ex hoc loco, vt praefecti & alij, omnia diligenter inquirant quae magni sunt momenti, vt possint suos principes certiores reddere, non leues sint, & audi ta tantum referant, maximę si de hoc mandatum acceperint a suo magistratu. Ex eo quod opus tam fideliter processit, discimus Deum nobis affuturum, si monitis feruorum suorum prophetarum pareamus.
units.tr: A political lesson is to be drawn from this place: that prefects and others should carefully inquire into all matters of great importance, so that they may be able to inform their princes; that they should not be light-minded, and should report only what they have heard, especially if they have received a command on this from their magistrate. From the fact that the work went on so faithfully we learn that God will be with us if we obey the admonitions of his servants the prophets.

units.la: Secundo loco commemoratur, quid Iudaei responderint. Multa autem haec responsio continet, quae cum omnia fere supra audiuerimus, non diu illis immorabor.
units.tr: In second place, what the Jews answered is recorded. This answer contains many things, most of which we have heard almost entirely above, so I will not dwell on them long.

units.la: 1 Dicunt se esse seruos illius qui coelum & terram creauit & gubernat: sequi instaurare templum, quod ante multos annos ex tructum fuerat a rege magno, nempe Solomone, qui opibus, gloria, & potentia excelluit. 3. lib. Reg. 4. 6. Anno regni eius quarto coeptum est aedificari templum: stetit annis multis antequam a Nabuchodonosore destructum esset.
units.tr: 1 They say that they are servants of him who created and governs heaven and earth; they are seeking to restore the temple which many years earlier had been built by a great king, namely Solomon, who excelled in wealth, glory, and power. 3 Kings 4 and 6: In the fourth year of his reign the building of the temple was begun; it stood for many years before it was destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar.

units.la: 2 Postquam prouocauerunt patres nostri Deum coeli, tradidit eos in manum Nabuchodonosoris regis Babel, & domum hanc destruxit &c. Quia Deum prouocarunt ad ira suis peccatis, idololatria, cotemtu verbi, perfidia erga rege, etc. eos punien dos tradit Babylonijs: capti enim & capti sunt, templu cuerfum,
units.tr: 2 "After our fathers provoked the God of heaven, he gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and destroyed this house," etc. Because they provoked God to anger by their sins, by idolatry, by contempt of the Word, by faithlessness toward the king, etc., he handed them over to the Babylonians to be punished. For they were taken captive, the temple was overturned, the city burned.

units.la: vrbs inflammata. Non potuisset eos ante punire, quàm Deus il-los tradidisset in eorum manus. Vicinæ gentes odio quidem illos habebant, voluissentq; funditus omnes excindere, sed non potuerunt. Hæc phrasis sæpe legitur in libro Iudicum. Achior in lib. Iudith. cap. 5. idem dixit.
units.tr: God could not have punished them earlier unless he had handed them over into their hands. The neighbouring nations indeed hated them and would have wished to destroy them utterly, but they could not. This phrase is often read in the book of Judges. Achior in the book of Judith, chapter 5, said the same.

units.la: De clade Iudæorum in vltimis capitibus lib. Regum habetur: & in secundo libro Chronicorum vltimo capite, dicit Deus se mane surrexisse, prædixisse suo populo mala per prophetas, sed illos ludibrio eos habuisse. Daniel multis 9. capite in suis precibus fatetur, omnes peccauisse suisque peccatis pœnas attraxisse. Non culpam in alios homines conferunt, non in influentias cæli, non in fortunam, dicunt se peccasse. Si Deus pœnas graues nobis immittat, quis non fatebitur nos dignos esse, qui tot peccatis & sceleribus patrem clementissimum offenderimus?
units.tr: The defeat of the Jews is recorded in the last chapters of the book of Kings; and in the last chapter of the second book of Chronicles, God is said to have risen early, to have foretold to his people their misfortunes through the prophets, but that they mocked him. Daniel, in chapter 9 of his prayers, confesses that all had sinned and had brought punishments upon themselves by their sins. They do not lay the blame on other men, nor on the influences of the heavens, nor on fortune; they say that they have sinned. If God sends heavy punishments upon us, who will not confess that we deserve them, since we have offended our most merciful Father with so many sins and crimes?

units.la: Dicunt se libertatem recuperasse per regem Cyrum, qui edictum promulgarit de instaurando templo, & vasa templi dederit Sesbasar, quem ducem constituerit, vt in templum Hierolymitanum, vnde Nabuchodonosor illa transtulerat, reponeret: nempe si iterum fuisset extructum, quod iussit ædificari in loco illo in quo antea fuerat. De Sesbazaro illo dictum est in primo capite.
units.tr: They say that they recovered their freedom through King Cyrus, who published an edict concerning the restoration of the temple, and gave the vessels of the temple to Sheshbazzar, whom he had appointed governor, so that he might restore them to the temple at Jerusalem from which Nebuchadnezzar had carried them off; namely, that the temple should be built again, if it were rebuilt in the place where it had been before. Of that Sheshbazzar it was said in the first chapter.

units.la: Sesbasarum istum dicunt hi Iudæi, iecilse fundamenta tem-pli, quod est Hierosolymis, quodque ex eo tempore vsque ad hoc tempus ædificetur, & nondum perfectum fit. Non quidem continuè extructum fuit, sed interueniente longa interruptione, propter Cambysis, aut potius præfectorum eius prohibitionem.
units.tr: These Jews say that this Sheshbazzar laid the foundations of the temple which is at Jerusalem, and that it has been under construction from that time until now, and is not yet finished. It was not in fact built continuously, but with a long interruption, on account of the prohibition of Cambyses, or rather of his prefects.

units.la: Subijcit epilogum, qui continet modestam petitionem, vt rex, si molestum non sit, in domo thesaurorum iubeat perquiri & inspici annales, an res ita habeat, vt Iudæi dicunt, quòd rex Cyrus promulgarit edictum de ædificando templo: vtq; suam hac de re voluntatem eis patefacere dignetur, vt quo pacto se gerere debeant erga Iudæos, scire possint.
units.tr: He adds an epilogue, containing a modest request: that the king, if it is no trouble, would order the treasure-house to be searched and the annals inspected, to see whether the matter stands as the Jews say, namely that King Cyrus issued an edict concerning the building of the temple; and that he would deign to make his own will in this matter known to them, so that they may know how they ought to conduct themselves towards the Jews.

units.la: Vsus huius loci.
units.tr: The use of this passage.

units.la: Si quæratur cur ab ecclesia Romana defecerimus, & nouas ecclesias plantemus: respondendum est, nos à veteri Romana ecclesia, quam Paulus plantauit, non defecisse: sed à noua illa quæ verbo Dei humanas traditiones substituit: quæ idololatriam hominibus vi obtrudere conatur: quæq; iugulat eos qui puritati doctrinæ student. D. Paulus ad Galatas dicit, etiam angelum gelum de cœlo qui aliud Euangelium adferat, quàm ipse prædicarit, anathema esse. Ne igitur mirentur nos discessionem ab eis fecisse.
units.tr: If it be asked why we have departed from the Church of Rome and are planting new churches, the answer must be that we have not departed from the old Roman Church, which Paul planted, but from that new church which has put human traditions in the place of the Word of God, which tries to force idolatry upon men, and which slaughters those who strive for purity of doctrine. The apostle Paul says to the Galatians that even an angel from heaven who brings a different gospel from the one he himself preached is accursed. Let them therefore not be surprised that we have separated ourselves from them.

units.la: Iustitiæ & modestiæ exemplum habemus in Tathnai eiusque consiliarijs. Negotium Iudæorum bona fide agunt, & quodammodo iuuant eorum conatus, vt opus templi perficiatur. Non pronocant regem ad iram suis calumnijs, non falsa ei in odium gentis instillant. In testimonijs enim veritati studen dum est, recte dicta non maligne interpretanda sunt. Iubent inquirere in libris, an res ita habeant, vt Iudæi dicunt. Antichristus hodie res longe alitur aggreditur. Concitat principes contra fideles, false eos criminatur, non libros proferre iubet, sed bombardas, halabardas, hastas, enses, quo hostes ecclesiæ, vt ipse eos vocat, coherceantur.
units.tr: We have an example of justice and moderation in Tathnai and his councillors. They deal honestly with the affair of the Jews and in some measure help their efforts, so that the work of the temple may be completed. They do not provoke the king to anger with their slanders, nor do they pour false accusations into his mind against the nation. For one must be zealous for the truth in testimonies, and what has been rightly said must not be interpreted maliciously. They order the books to be searched, to see whether the matter stands as the Jews say. Antichrist today goes about things in a very different way. He stirs up princes against the faithful, accuses them falsely, and orders not books to be produced but bombards, halberds, spears and swords, by which the enemies of the Church, as he calls them, are to be restrained.

units.la: CAPVT VI.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI.

units.la: HOMILIA XVIII.
units.tr: HOMILY XVIII.

units.la: Rex iubet inquiri decretum Cyrinuentum in Media, confirmat.
units.tr: The king orders the decree of Cyrus to be searched for in Media, and confirms it.

units.la: Tunc Darius rex posuit præceptum: & quæsierunt in domo librorum thesaurorum qui positi erant in Babel.
units.tr: Then King Darius issued a command, and they searched in the house of the treasure books, which were kept in Babylon.

units.la: Inuentum est autem in scrinio (quod erat) in palatio quod (erat) in Madai prouincia, volumen vnum: & sic scriptum erat in eo memoriale:
units.tr: A single scroll was found in a chest that was in the palace in the province of Media, and a memorandum was written in it as follows:

units.la: Anno primo Chores regis, Chores rex posuit edificare domo Dei quæ erat in Ierusalaim, Domus ipsa reædificetur, quæ est locus, in quo immolant victimas, & parietes eius colligentur. Altitudo eius (sit) cubitorum sexaginta, latitudo eius, cubitorum sexaginta.
units.tr: In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus commanded that the house of God which is in Jerusalem be rebuilt, the house where they offer sacrifices, and that its walls be built up. Its height shall be sixty cubits, and its breadth sixty cubits.

units.la: Parietes, ex lapideis marmoreis tres, & parietes (vnus) è lignis nouis: & sumptus de domo regis dabitur.
units.tr: Three courses of hewn stone and one course of new timber for the walls; and the cost shall be given from the king's house.

units.la: Quin etiam vasa domus Dei aurea & argentea tea, quæ Nebuchadnesar eduxerat è templo quod erat in Ierusalaim, & detulerat in Babel, reddant, & vadant ad templum quod est in Ierusalaim ad locum suum & reponas in domo Dei.
units.tr: Moreover, let the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, be returned, and let them go to the temple in Jerusalem, each to its place, and be placed in the house of God.

units.la: 6 Nunc ergo Thatthenai dux (eorum qui sunt) trans flumen, Setharbozcalled nai, & sociii eorum, & Aphar-sechaie qui estis trans flumen, remoti estote inde.
units.tr: 6 Now therefore, Tattenai, governor beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and your companions, and Apharsechites, who are beyond the River, keep far away from there.

units.la: 7 Dimittite ut fiat domus Dei hæc, ducem Iudæorum, & seniores eorum, ut domum Dei hanc ædificent in loco suo.
units.tr: 7 Let the work on this house of God alone; let the governor of the Jews and their elders build this house of God in its place.

units.la: 8 Et a me positum est edictum de eo quod facturi estis cum senioribus Iehudæorum istis, ut ædificent domum Dei istam: nempe ut de substantia regis, quæ est tributum trans flumen, festinanter sumptus detur viris illis, ut non faciant cessare.
units.tr: 8 And I have issued a decree concerning what you are to do with these elders of the Jews, that they may build this house of God: namely, that from the king's revenue, the tribute beyond the River, the costs be promptly paid to those men, so that they are not hindered.

units.la: 6 Et id quo indiguerint, sive boues, sive arietes, sive agni in holocausta Deo cœli, frumentum, sal, vinum & oleum, iuxta verbum sacerdotum qui sunt in Ierusalaim, dentur eis per singulos dies, ut nullus sit error.
units.tr: 9 And whatever they need, whether bullocks, rams, or lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine, and oil, according to the word of the priests who are in Jerusalem, let it be given to them day by day, so that there be no failure.

units.la: 10 Ut habeant unde offerant suffimenta Dei cæli, & precentur pro vita regis, & pro filijs eius.
units.tr: 10 So that they may have what to offer sacrifices of sweet savour to the God of heaven, and may pray for the life of the king and of his sons.

units.la: Artes insigniores huius capitis, hæ possunt assignari. Primùm Darius ducum suorum rogatu, Cyri decretum de templo extruendo inquirit, quo inuento, iubet ut templum absoluant: secundo loco, obedientia ducum & præfectorum commemoratur: tertio quod ædificium templi feliciter absoluerint: quarto de dedicatione tepli: quinto de celebratione festi azymorum agitur.
units.tr: The more notable points of this chapter may be noted as follows. First, at the request of his leaders, Darius inquires into Cyrus's decree concerning the building of the temple, and when it is found, he orders that the temple be completed. Second, the obedience of the leaders and governors is recorded. Third, that they successfully finished the building of the temple. Fourth, the dedication of the temple. Fifth, the celebration of the feast of unleavened bread is treated.

units.la: Quoad primum, duces & præsides Samaritanorum scripserunt ad regem Darium, petentes ut inquirat Cyri decretum: non autem ut priores fecerant, Iudæos criminantur, sed potius pro eis intercedunt, & responsum à rege petunt. Rex iubet servos suos inquirere decretum hoc Cyri, an ita sit, ut Iudæi dicebant, an eis copiam fecerit instaurandi templum. Quæsierunt in domo librorum, hoc est, bibliotheca, ubi thesauri reponebantur in Babylone, sed inuentum non est: perquisierunt igitur in aliis regionibus, tandem inuentum est in scrinio quod erat in palatio in Media. Latina versio habet in Ecbatanis. Metropolis est in Media, Iudith oftauo capite. In illa vrbe, fuit nimirum arx vel palatium, in quo hoc decretum inuentum fuit. Daniel vt probabile est, cum Dario in Media profectus, hoc volumen conseruauit.
units.tr: As to the first point: the leaders and governors of the Samaritans wrote to King Darius, asking him to inquire into the decree of Cyrus. Unlike their predecessors, they do not accuse the Jews, but rather plead on their behalf and ask for a reply from the king. The king orders his servants to search for this decree of Cyrus, whether it is so as the Jews said, that he had granted them the right to restore the temple. They searched in the house of books, that is, the library, where treasures were kept in Babylon, but nothing was found. So they searched in other regions, and at last it was found in a chest that was in the palace in Media. The Latin version has "in Ecbatana." Ecbatana is the metropolis of Media, in Judith, chapter eight. In that city there was doubtless a citadel or palace in which this decree was found. It is probable that Daniel, who went with Darius into Media, kept this scroll.

units.la: Videmus hoc loco, quàm diligens & indefessus in rebus perquirendis rex fuerit. Non dicit, Cur diu quaererem? quaecunq; ego facere iubeo, sunt legis instar. Principes non debent praecipitanter agare, si alterius, quantumuis pauperis, honor & vita agitur: multo minus in rebus maioribus quae Rempublicam vel Ecclesiam attinet. Videndū quid verbum Dei requirat, quid ante indicatum fit. Si principes sacra biblia tanta diligentia legerent, & inquirerent quae verbo Dei consentanea essent, quae minus, non tam peruersè & corruptè de religione iudicarent. Quàm multa sunt quae cum in Papatu multi olim animaduerterint cum verbo Dei pugnare, iam acriter defenduntur, ne videantur erraffe.
units.tr: Here we see how diligent and untiring the king was in seeking out information. He does not say, "Why should I search so long? Whatever I order is law." Princes ought not to act rashly if the honour and life of another, however poor, is at stake; much less in greater matters that concern the commonwealth or the Church. One must consider what the Word of God requires and what has been decided before. If princes read the holy Bible with such diligence, and inquired what agrees with the Word of God and what does not, they would not judge so perversely and corruptly about religion. How many things there are which, though many in the Papacy once perceived to be at odds with the Word of God, are now fiercely defended, lest they seem to have been in error!

units.la: Elicimus ex hoc loco, quanti gentiles fecerint libros hifto ricos, thesauros enim suos, & libros in eodem loco repofuerút. Magni fecisse literas & literatos, amaffe scholas, collegia & Bibliothecas, Danielis primo capite Nabuchodonosoris exemplo manifestum est. De bibliothecis in genere, cofule Conradi Gesneri praefationem in suam bibliothecam.
units.tr: From this passage we gather how highly the Gentiles valued historical books, for they kept their treasures and books in the same place. That they esteemed letters and learned men, and loved schools, colleges and libraries, is clear from the example of Nebuchadnezzar in the first chapter of Daniel. On libraries in general, consult the preface of Conrad Gesner to his library.

units.la: Videmus etiam quàm vtile sit decreta iudicum, priuilegia, & alia id genus seruari, historias considgnari, vt quid faciendum sit in aliis quoq; similibus casibus, vtq; controuersiae dirimi possint, melius perspici queat.
units.tr: We also see how useful it is that the decrees of judges, privileges and other such things be preserved and that histories be recorded, so that what must be done in other similar cases may be better understood, and so that controversies may be settled.

units.la: Secundo loco inseritur Cyri edictum, cuius summa est, regem cocefsiffe Iudaeis libertatem, iufsifeq; templum illud suis impensis construi. Videamus praecipuas partes.
units.tr: Second, the edict of Cyrus is inserted, the substance of which is that the king granted the Jews liberty and ordered that the temple be built at his own expense. Let us look at its principal parts.

units.la: 1 Iubet Iudaeos aedificare, ostendens vbi aedificandum fit, & quando. Alia ratio & forma fuit templi Salomonici: Longitudo enim 60. latitudo 20. altitudo 30. cubitos habuit. Cubitus verò vsitatus, habet pedem cum dimidio. Dicunt veteres, secundum hoc templum aliter aedificatum esse, quàm hic à Cyro praescriptum fit: Illum enim postea ex consilio doctorum legis, mutasse suam sententiam. Certè non putandum est, ex suo cerebro voluisse aedificari templum.
units.tr: 1 He orders the Jews to build, showing where and when the building is to be done. The plan and shape of Solomon's temple was different: its length was sixty cubits, its breadth twenty, and its height thirty. The common cubit has a foot and a half. The ancients say that this temple was built differently from the one prescribed here by Cyrus, for Cyrus afterwards changed his opinion on the advice of the teachers of the law. Certainly we must not suppose that he wished the temple to be built according to his own imagination.

units.la: 2 Expensas dari imperat opificibus ex fisco regio, quod antea non fuit dictum.
units.tr: 2 He commands that expenses be given to the workmen from the royal treasury, which had not been mentioned before.

units.la: 3 Vasa sacra iubet illis reddi, & in templo asseruari.
units.tr: 3 He orders that the sacred vessels be returned to them and kept in the temple.

units.la: Videmus quàm pulchrum sit veritatis studium. Iudæi dixerant hæc contineri in Cyri decreto, quod cum inuenturi & lectum esset, res ita habebat, non deprehenduntur in mendacio imò plura inueniunt, quàm illi affirmarint, nempe quòd regijs impensis ædificandum sit. Non desunt doctores, qui vt suos errores coram simplicibus stabiliant, loca quidem ex sacris literis & patribus adducunt, sed non bona fide. Nam si quis inquirat, vel prorsus nihil illorum quæ dixerunt inueniet, vel rem longè secus habere. Deprehensos autem in mendacio, nihil pudet: front tem enim perfricuerunt. Quisquis à primis annis veritati afuescat, mendacium fugiat.
units.tr: We see how fine a thing is the pursuit of truth. The Jews had said that these things were contained in Cyrus's decree; when it was found and read, the matter was as they had said. They are not caught in a lie; rather they find more than they had affirmed, namely that the building is to be done at royal expense. There are no lack of teachers who, to establish their errors before simple people, cite passages from Holy Scripture and the Fathers, but not in good faith. For if anyone inquires, he will either find nothing at all of what they have said, or the matter will be quite otherwise. And when they are caught in a lie, they are not ashamed at all, for they have hardened their brow. Whoever from his earliest years grows accustomed to the truth, let him shun lying.

units.la: Tertio loco rex confirmat edictum Cyri, & certa suis dat mandata.
units.tr: Third, the king confirms the edict of Cyrus and gives definite commands to his men.

units.la: 1 Iubet Tatthnai præsidem, ducem, consiliarios & ministros suos, procul abstere, ne instauratoribus templi sint impedimento.
units.tr: 1 He orders Tattenai the governor, his colleagues, counsellors and officials to keep far away, so that they do not hinder the restorers of the temple.

units.la: 2 Decernuntur impensæ ad templi extructionem, ex tributo quod Rex habebat trans Euphratem. Mauult carere annuis redditibus, quàm ædificium illud differri. Festinanter dari iubet, vt non faciant cessare, nempe architectos, latomos: siue ne efficiant, vt instauratio intermittatur. Nam si mercedem non potuissent numerare opificibus, recessissent. Addit, quid illis dandum, quando, unde, quantum vel quomodo, quare & in quem finem. Dare illis debuerunt boues, arietes, agnos, item frumentum, sal, oleum & vinum, in singulos dies festinanter & fideliter. Ex thesauris regijs, iuxta verbum sacerdotum qui sunt in Ierusalem. Vt nullus sit error, hoc est, ne quis merito conqueri possit: non negligenter fiat. Causa indicatur, vt habeant unde offerant suffimenta Deo cœli, hoc est, vt habeant unde offerant odores suauissimos. Deo cœli, non dijs gentium. Loquitur de sacrificijs, quæ Deus si fide offerantur, odorari dicitur in scripturis, & grata habere: item de odoribus quos in aureo altari suffimenti vel thymiamatis, adolere solebant.
units.tr: 2 Money for the construction of the temple is decreed from the tribute which the king had beyond the Euphrates. He prefers to forgo his yearly revenues rather than have that building delayed. He orders that it be given promptly, so that they do not cease, that is, the architects and stonemasons, or lest the restoration be interrupted. For if they could not pay the wages to the workmen, the workmen would have withdrawn. He adds what is to be given to them, when, from where, how much, how, why and for what end. They were to give them bullocks, rams, lambs, likewise wheat, salt, oil and wine, day by day, promptly and faithfully, from the royal treasuries, according to the word of the priests who are in Jerusalem. So that there be no failure, that is, so that no one may justly complain; let it not be done carelessly. The reason is given: that they may have what to offer sacrifices of sweet savour to the God of heaven, that is, that they may have what to offer the most fragrant odours. To the God of heaven, not to the gods of the Gentiles. He speaks of sacrifices which, when offered in faith, are said in Scripture to be a sweet savour to God and to be acceptable to him; likewise of the odours which they used to burn on the golden altar of incense or thymiama.

units.la: Obseruandum est quòd hæc rex illis dari iussit, non vt heluarentur, alea luderent, aut bellum gererent ex hac pecunia, vt Romanos Pontifices fecisse constat ex illa pecunia quam ex indulgentijs corraserunt: non vt primarij ex illis multos equos alerent, & magna caterua clientum comitati incederent: sed vt Deo sacrificia ac libamina offerent, odores accenderent & ipsi quoque alimoniam necessariam haberent. Addit, Vt precentur pro vita regis, & pro filijs eius.) Rex ille non vacuus fuit pietate, alioqui preces pro se & liberis suis fieri non poftulaffet. Intercessio vtilis est, quando vnus pro alijs preca- tur. Loth eripuit Zoar suis precibus, Genef.19. Abimelech petit preces Abrahami, Gen.20. Paulus preces ecclesiarum postulat: vt subiecti preces fundat pro suo magistratu, mandatur in 1. Timoth.2. Ethnicus autem erat ille magistratus. Ierem.29. prophe ta hortatur populum sub Iechonia in Babylonem abductum, vt Deo salutem fui regis commendent suis precibus. Tertullianus in suo Apologetico testatur, hunc morem fuisse primaeuae ecclesiae, vt imperatores in precibus publicis sibi comendatos haberent, quid precati sint ostendit, quae nota sunt, &c.
units.tr: It must be observed that the king ordered these things to be given to them not so that they might gorge themselves, gamble with dice, or wage war with this money, as the Roman Pontiffs are known to have done with the money they scraped together from indulgences; nor so that the leading men might keep many horses and march about attended by a great band of clients; but so that they might offer sacrifices and drink-offerings to God, kindle incense, and also have the necessary sustenance for themselves. He adds: that they should pray for the life of the king and for his sons. That king was not devoid of piety, since otherwise he would not have asked for prayers to be made for himself and his children. Intercession is profitable when one prays for others. Lot was rescued from Zoar by the prayers of others, Gen. 19. Abimelech asks for the prayers of Abraham, Gen. 20. Paul asks for the prayers of the churches; that the subject should pour out prayers for his magistrate is commanded in 1 Tim. 2, and that magistrate was a heathen. In Jeremiah 29 the prophet exhorts the people carried away to Babylon under Jeconiah to commend the safety of their king to God in their prayers. Tertullian in his Apologeticus testifies that it was the custom of the primitive Church to have the emperors commended to them in public prayers; what they prayed for he shows in the well-known passages, etc.

units.la: Multo magis nos pro principibus Christianis, etiam non rogati, preces fundere debemus. Etsi autem alij pro nobis apud Deum intercedunt, tamen nos nostro quoque officio deesse nequaquam debemus. Legimus multos reges & principes qui tyrannice imperium gesserunt, in adulterijs volutati sunt, cedes iniustas fecerunt, &c. coduxiffe Monachos & alios, qui pro ipsis apud Deum intercederent, fiducia autem illarum precum, ipsi in suis sceleribus perrexerunt. Ita factum est vt monasteria paulatim locupletata sint. Rarus fuit princeps, qui non extruxerit monasterium, vel quae antea extrueta erant, non auxerit opibus, idem fecerunt nobiles, potentes & opulenti viri: tandem mona chi, meritaieiunia & preces suas precio vendiderunt. Multae fundationes, vt vocant monasteriorum, ita incipiunt: In Dei nomine. Perpendendum est vnicuique hominum, quam velociter tempora caduca praetereunt, & futura adpropriant. Ideo pen-set vnusquisque apud semetipsum, fi habeat vnde aliquid de facultatibus suis tribuere valeat, ad venerabilia loca pro remedio animae suae, vt in sempiterna quiete cum beato Petro & Andrea paradyfum mereatur possidere. Quia illi datis rebus suis, mercati sunt regnum coelorum. Regnum Dei tantum valet, quantum habet. Quid vilius cum emitur, vel quid carius cum possidetur? In hac igitur promissione ego. N. valde compunctus trado, &c. Ita paulatim opes monachorum in immensum creuere. Singulae fere familiae, voluerunt habere spirituales, vt vocant, personas, quae dies noctefq; pro ipsis canerent, legerent, Deum deprecarentur, ipsi interim voluptatibus & rebus mundanis fe dediderunt.
units.tr: We ought much more to pour out prayers for Christian princes, even when we are not asked to. Although others intercede for us with God, we must by no means fail in our own duty. We read that many kings and princes who ruled tyrannically, wallowed in adulteries, committed unjust murders, etc., nevertheless kept monks and others who would intercede for them with God, and on the confidence of those prayers they went on in their wickedness. Thus it came about that the monasteries were gradually enriched. Rare was the prince who did not build a monastery, or who did not increase with his wealth those already built; the nobles, powerful and wealthy men did the same. At last the monks sold their fasts and prayers for a price. Many foundations of what they call monasteries begin thus: In the name of God. Every man should consider how quickly the fleeting times pass away and draw near to the future. Therefore let each one think to himself whether he has anything from his goods which he can give to the venerable places for the remedy of his soul, so that in eternal rest with blessed Peter and Andrew he may merit to possess paradise. For those who gave up their possessions bought the kingdom of heaven. The kingdom of God is worth as much as one has; what is cheaper when it is bought, or dearer when it is possessed? In this promise, therefore, I, N., deeply moved, hand over, etc. Thus gradually the wealth of the monks grew to an immense size. Nearly every family wanted to have what they call spiritual persons, who would sing, read and beseech God day and night for them, while they themselves gave themselves over to pleasures and worldly things.

units.la: Rex Persicus petit, vt pro salute sua precentur, non autem redimit preces. Deus vult, vt quotidie vnus pro altero precemur. tur,idque gratis: non vult vt vel vendamus nostras preces, vel aliorum emamus.Quifq; vero qui beneficia ab alio accepit,gratus esse debet, suamque gratitudinem oblata occasione, rebus ipsis declarare.
units.tr: The Persian king asks that prayers be made for his safety, but he does not buy the prayers. God wills that we pray for one another daily, and that freely: he does not want us either to sell our prayers or to buy those of others. Whoever has received benefits from another ought to be grateful, and, when the occasion is offered, to declare his gratitude by deeds.

units.la: Liberalitas vel magnificentia Cyri & Darij, principibus commendatur. Est virtus egregia in ipsis. Imperatores & reges, magnas opes ecclesijs contulerunt, vt semper docti viri existerent, qui verbum Dei dextre proponere, & errores refellere possent. Abutuntur his opibus sacrificij, ad impediendum ecclesiae aedificium. Multi quoq; ecclesias spoliant suis opibus: multi quae persoluere debebant decimas & alia ecclesiarum ministris, id malignè faciunt. Tantum abest, vt liberales sint in bonarum literarum studiosos. Si quid in idololatriam, in nouos monachorum ordines, sit impendendum, in scorta, in res turpes, pleriqueque sua profundunt, sed peruersa & praepostera est illa liberalitas.
units.tr: The liberality or magnificence of Cyrus and Darius is commended to princes; it is an outstanding virtue in them. Emperors and kings have conferred great wealth on the churches, so that there might always be learned men who could set forth the Word of God rightly and refute errors. But these riches are abused by sacrificing, to hinder the building up of the Church. Many also despoil the churches of their wealth; many who ought to pay tithes and other dues to the ministers of the churches do so grudgingly. So far are they from being generous towards the students of good letters. If anything is to be spent on idolatry, on new orders of monks, on harlots, or on shameful things, most people pour out their money there, but that liberality is perverse and backward.

units.la: HOMILIA XIX.
units.tr: HOMILY XIX.

units.la: De poena qua violatores edicti regij afficiendi sint.
units.tr: On the punishment with which violators of the royal edict are to be afflicted.

units.la: 11 Praeterea a me positum est (tale) decretum, vt quicunque immutauerit verbum hoc, diruatur lignum e domo eius, & erectum suspendatur in eo, & domus eius sterquilinium fiat propter hoc.
units.tr: 11 Moreover, I have issued this decree: whoever alters this word, let a beam be torn from his house, and let him be lifted up and hanged on it, and let his house be made a dunghill because of this.

units.la: 12 Deus autem qui habitare fecit nomen suum ibi, dissipet omnem regem & populum, qui miserit manum suam vt mutet & destruat domum Dei istam quae est in Ierusalaim. Ego Darius posui decretum: fieri anter fiat.
units.tr: 12 And may God, who has caused his name to dwell there, overthrow every king and people who shall stretch out their hand to alter or destroy this house of God which is in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued a decree: let it be carried out speedily.

units.la: 13 Tunc Thatthenai dux (eorum qui erant) trans Flumen, Setharbozenai, & socij eorum, iuxta id quod miserat Darius rex, sic festinanter fecerunt.
units.tr: 13 Then Tatthenai, the governor of the region beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their companions, did this speedily, in accordance with what King Darius had sent.

units.la: Quemadmodum post assiduos & magnos imbres, sereni dies sequuntur, ita fere fit, vt tyrannis, boni & moderati principes succedant. Exemplo nobis sunt Romani imperatores, quorum multi Christianam religionem ferro & igni persquuti sunt, quibus postea alij successerunt, qui veram fidem amplexi, ChristiaChristianos defenderunt. Cambyses dissimilis patri suo Cyro, populum Dei odio habuit, ita etiam eius ferui. Sicut vulgo dicitur: Qualis rex, tales sunt eius ministri. In huius locum exalii familia Darius rex bonus venit, qui suis scripsit, vt non solum non impediant templi extructionem, sed ex suo fisco ad illam necessaria contribuant. Rebus igitur quantumuis desperatis, animus non est abijciendus, &c.
units.tr: As after constant and heavy rains come clear days, so it generally happens that tyrants give way to good and moderate princes. The Roman emperors are examples for us: many of them persecuted the Christian religion with sword and fire, and they were afterwards succeeded by others who embraced the true faith and defended the Christians. Cambyses, unlike his father Cyrus, hated the people of God, and so did his servants. As the common saying goes: What the king is, such are his ministers. In his place came Darius, a good king of another family, who wrote to his people that they should not only not hinder the building of the temple, but should contribute from his own treasury what was necessary for it. Therefore, however desperate things may seem, the spirit is not to be cast down, etc.

units.la: 3. Iam sequitur de poena illis inferenda, qui hoc decretum temerario ausu infringunt.
units.tr: 3. Next follows the punishment to be inflicted on those who break this decree with rash daring.

units.la: Rex decreuit vt quicunq; hoc verbum, id est, decretum im mutarit, domum eius demoliantur, & trabe vel tigno extracto, eum in illo suspendant: vtq; domus eius in sterquilinium, siue in latrinam conuertatur. Idem legitur Dan. 2. vbi rex Babylonicus ad sapientes Dios dicit, Nisi ostenderitis mihi somnium & interpretationem eius, efficiemini frusta, & domus vestrę ponentur in sterquilinium. In 3. cap. Rex cum videret socios Danielis, in igne a Deo serUari: Omnis, inquit, qui Deo contradixerit, redigatur in frusta, & domus eius ponatur in latrinam. 4. Reg. 10. diruerunt domū Baal, posuerunt q; eam pro latrina. Romani quoque domos eorum qui contraRempub. conspirauerunt, diruerūt. Spurius Cassius affectatę dominationis suspectus, domo eius diruta, supplicio capitali affectus est. Liuius libro 2. & Valerius Maximus lib. 6. cap. 3. de seueritate, addit cum Sp. Melio eadem auso idem factum. Area domus eius, inquit, quo iustitia suppliciij notior ad posteros peruenire, Æquimelij appellatione traxit. Quantum ergo odij aduersus hostes libertatis insitum animis antiqui haberent, parietum & tectorum in quibus versati fuerant, ruinis testabantur. Ideoq; & M. Flacci, & L. Saturnini seditiosissimorum ciuium corporibus trucidatis, penates ab imis fundamentis eruti sunt, &c. Augustus Cæsar Vidij Pollionis, crudelissimi hominis, domum funditus euertit, atq; in eo loco Liuiæ porticum ædificauit, Dion Nicæus in Augusto. In Tigurinæ vrbis vetustissimis legibus etiam habetur, vt optima domus illius, qui Rempub. grauiter læserit, diruatur. Nostris temporibus in Gallia domus aliquot illorum, qui Euangelicis ecclesijs hospitium dederunt, dirutę sunt, & à fundamentis euersę, ad perpetuam rei memoriam.
units.tr: The king decreed that whoever should change this word, that is, this decree, his house should be pulled down, and that after a beam or timber has been drawn out, he should be hanged on it; and his house should be turned into a dunghill, or a latrine. The same is read in Daniel 2, where the Babylonian king says to the wise men of the Chaldeans: "Unless you show me the dream and its interpretation, you will be made into nothing, and your houses will be turned into a dunghill." In chapter 3, when the king saw Daniel's companions preserved by God in the fire, he said: "Whoever speaks against God, let him be cut into pieces, and let his house be made a latrine." In 4 Kings 10 they pulled down the house of Baal and made it a latrine. The Romans also pulled down the houses of those who conspired against the commonwealth. Spurius Cassius, suspected of seeking tyrannical power, had his house pulled down and was put to death. Livy in book 2, and Valerius Maximus in book 6, chapter 3, on severity, add that the same was done with Spurius Melius, who had dared the same thing. The site of his house, he says, so that the punishment of justice might come more clearly to the notice of posterity, took the name of Aequimelium. How much hatred against the enemies of liberty the ancients had implanted in their hearts is witnessed by the ruins of the walls and roofs among which they had lived. And so, when the bodies of Marcus Flaccus and Lucius Saturninus, the most seditious citizens, had been slain, their household gods were torn from the very foundations, etc. Augustus Caesar utterly overthrew the house of Vedius Pollio, a most cruel man, and on that site built a portico for Livia (Dio of Nicaea, in Augustus). In the most ancient laws of the city of Zurich it is also provided that the finest house of a man who has gravely injured the commonwealth shall be pulled down. In our own times in France several houses of those who gave lodging to the evangelical churches have been pulled down and razed to the ground, as a lasting memorial of the matter.

units.la: Si tanta poena digni iudicantur, qui verbū regis mutant, quid illis expectandum qui Regis regum decreta violant, qui verbū ipsius opprimunt, aut flectunt secundum suos affectus, qui publicè per carnifices sacra Biblia comburunt, seq; Deo malitiose opponunt? Iam maledicit illis vel dira illis imprecatur, qui templum hoc euerterint. Deus qui habitare fecit nomen suum ibi, scilicet in hoc templo: qui in eo se praesentem fore promisit, se ibi invocari & celebrari iussit.
units.tr: If such great punishment is judged worthy for those who change the king's word, what is to be expected for those who violate the decrees of the King of kings, who oppress or bend his word according to their own passions, who publicly burn the holy Bibles through executioners, and who maliciously set themselves against God? Now he curses, or calls down dreadful curses upon, those who overthrow this temple. God, who has caused his name to dwell there, namely in this temple, who promised that he would be present in it, and commanded that he be invoked and celebrated there.

units.la: Dissipet omnem regem & populum qui miserit manum suam, ut mutet & destruat domum illam suam.) Perdat reges & populos, qui templum hoc destruunt. Votis regis euentus respondit: nam Romani qui euerterunt templum & urbem, grauissimas dederunt poenas Deo.
units.tr: "Let him overthrow every king and people who shall stretch out their hand to alter and destroy that house of his." He will destroy kings and peoples who demolish this temple. The outcome answered to the king's prayer: for the Romans, who overthrew the temple and the city, paid the most grievous penalties to God.

units.la: Si vero illi qui materiale templum destruxerunt, poenas merentur, quid illis expectandum erit, qui viuu Dei templum, quod non manibus hominum, no ex lignis & lapidibus factum est, destruunt. Hoc est, qui filios Dei, quos ipsi haereticos vocat, persequuntur & excruciatos necant. Profecto omnes quotquot ecclesiam Dei vexarunt, omnibus seculis poenas dederunt, exemplo nobis sunt imperatores Romani ecclesiae hostes, & multi nostro tempore. Etsi vero Deus non de omnibus suis hostibus statim poenas sumat, vel etiam in hoc seculo, tamen in altero, poenas non subterfugient.
units.tr: But if those who destroyed the material temple deserve punishment, what will be expected for those who destroy the living temple of God, which was not made by human hands nor of wood and stones? That is, those who persecute the sons of God, whom they call heretics, and torture and kill them. Surely all who have harassed the Church of God have paid penalties in every age; the Roman emperors, enemies of the Church, are examples for us, and many in our own time. And although God does not at once exact punishment from all his enemies, or even in this age, yet they will not escape punishment in the next.

units.la: Ethnicus ille rex, ultimo die multos reges & principes iudicabit. Etsi enim non plenam habaret Dei notitiam: tamen eius gloriam ardentius vindicat, quam hodie multi ex illis principibus faciant, qui Christianae religionis periti & defensores videri volunt, cum interim tyrannice dominentur, cultus pro suo arbitrio constituentes, Antichristum defendant, & veram Christi membra acerrime persequantur.
units.tr: That heathen king will judge many kings and princes on the last day. For although he did not have full knowledge of God, he nevertheless avenged his glory more ardently than many of those princes do today, who wish to be seen as skilled in and defenders of the Christian religion, while meanwhile they rule tyrannically, setting up worship at their own pleasure, defend Antichrist, and most fiercely persecute the true members of Christ.

units.la: 4. Ego Darius posui decretum: festinanter fiat. Clausula est huius decreti. Vult ut statim expediatur. Non enim satis est fere bonas leges, & bona decreta facere, nisi defendantur. Leges sunt anima ciuitatis, sublatis vel euersis illis, perit corpus rei publicae. Athenienses suos habuerunt νομοφύλακας quos legibus seruandis praeposuerunt: Illi ipsos magistratus legibus uti cogebant: & ne quid contra leges & Rempublicam in comitijs, suffragijs populi scisceretur, studiose cauebant.
units.tr: 4. I, Darius, have issued a decree: let it be carried out speedily. This is the closing clause of this decree. He wants it to be carried out at once. For it is not enough to make good laws and good decrees, unless they are defended. Laws are the soul of a state; when they are removed or overthrown, the body of the commonwealth perishes. The Athenians had their guardians of the laws [νομοφύλακας], whom they set over the keeping of the laws. These compelled the magistrates themselves to observe the laws, and they took careful precautions that nothing be enacted in the assemblies or by the votes of the people contrary to the laws and the commonwealth.

units.la: Ex eo quod Darius decretum Cyri confirmat, discunt principes & magistratus, ut praedecessorum suorum priuilegia, decreta, tabulas sigillo eorum munitas, ratas habeant. Cum enim illa infringunt, aut rabulis forensibus concedunt, ut contra illa agant, actum est de ipsorum dignitate. Porro si priuilegia, item gentium consuetudines, mores & instituta verbo Dei aduersan tur, non sunt obseruanda. Qui mordicus illa retinere volunt, satis ostendunt, fe non recte in fide institutos esse. Ita plerique asse-cti sunt, vt maiorum decreta & instituta, si mala sint defen-dant, dicant eos non stultos fuisse, si bona sint, securè con-temnant.
units.tr: From the fact that Darius confirms the decree of Cyrus, princes and magistrates learn that they should hold valid the privileges, decrees and documents of their predecessors, sealed with their seal. For when they break these, or allow pettifogging lawyers to act against them, their own dignity is at stake. Further, if privileges, likewise the customs, manners and institutions of peoples, are opposed to the word of God, they are not to be observed. Those who want to hold on to them stubbornly show well enough that they have not been rightly instructed in the faith. Many are so disposed that they defend the decrees and institutions of their forefathers if they are bad, saying that the forefathers were not fools; if they are good, they despise them with impunity.

units.la: Secunda pars Capitis, continet executionē huius decre-ti. His literis recitatis, Tatthenai & consiliarij ipsius, mox impe-rata fecerunt. Unde colligimus eos, Deo ita mouente cordai-porum, Iudaeos non odio habuisse. Si literae illae ipsis fuissent in gratae, potuissent varias habere exceptiones, & rem in aliud tem-pus reijcere, potuissent etiam simulare se imperata fecisse, sed id non faciunt.
units.tr: The second part of the chapter contains the execution of this decree. Once these letters had been read, Tatthenai and his councillors straightway did what was commanded. From this we gather that, God so moving the hearts of these men, they did not hold the Jews in hatred. If those letters had been unwelcome to them, they could have raised various objections and deferred the matter to another time; they could even have pretended that they had done what was commanded, but they did not do this.

units.la: Discant subditi, suis dominis parere. Multa obedientiae subditorum erga magistratum exempla, hinc inde in sacris scri- pturis leguntur, inter quae velut gemma lucet, Christi obedi-entia quam Romanis, sub quorum imperio editus est in hanc lu-cem, praestitit. Bis enim legitur tributum eis dedisse, & alios quoque cohortatus esse, vt dent Caesari, quae Caesaris sunt, & Deo, quae Dei sunt. Imprimis vero ministri, ... cipum, qui de-fensores legum esse debent, cito faciant quod iussi sunt, & vt iuf si sunt. Obedientia subiectorum imperia stabiliuntur.
units.tr: Let subjects learn to obey their lords. Many examples of the obedience of subjects toward the magistrate are read in the sacred Scriptures on every side, among which shines like a jewel the obedience of Christ, which he rendered to the Romans, under whose rule he was brought into this light. For it is read that he twice gave tribute to them, and also exhorted others to give to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's. Above all, ministers ... princes, who ought to be defenders of the laws, should quickly do what they are ordered, and as they are ordered. The empires of subjects' obedience are made stable.

units.la: HOMILIA XX.
units.tr: HOMILIA XX.

units.la: Templum feliciter absoluitur.
units.tr: The temple is successfully completed.

units.la: 14 Seniores itaque Iehudaeorum aedificabant, & prosperè cedebat secundum prophetiam Haggai prophetae, & Zechariah filij Addo: & aedificauerunt, ac perfecerunt ex praecepto Dei Israelis, & ex praecepto Chores & Dariaues, & Arthahsasthe regis Paras.
units.tr: 14 So the elders of the Jews built, and it went well for them, according to the prophecy of the prophet Haggai and of Zechariah the son of Iddo. They built and finished it by the command of the God of Israel, and by the command of Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes king of Persia.

units.la: 15 Perfecta est ergo domus haec vsque ad diem tertium mensis Adar, qui erat annus sextus regni Da-riaues regis.
units.tr: 15 So this house was finished by the third day of the month Adar, which was the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.

units.la: IN tertia parte huius Capitis, agitur de profectu & perfectio-ne operis. Seniores dicuntur aedificasse templum: Iuniores quoque suo officio non defuisse, credendum est. Illi vero nomi-nantur, quia magna eorum fuit authoritas, & reliqui oculos in illos conuerterunt. Prosperè autem eis successit, secundū prophetiam Haggæi & Zachariæ. Per hos enim iussit Deus eos tem plum instaurare, quod illi fecerunt, & institerunt etiam & vrse runt eos, ne cessarent. Vel, secundum prophetiam: promiserant enim eis, euentum fore felicem. Deus igitur reipsa ostendit, se constantem esse in suis promisisis.
units.tr: In the third part of this chapter, the progress and completion of the work is described. The elders are said to have built the temple; we may believe that the younger men did not fail in their duty either. But the elders are named because their authority was great, and the rest turned their eyes to them. It went well for them, however, according to the prophecy of Haggai and Zechariah. For God, through these prophets, had ordered them to restore the temple. They did this, and they also persisted and urged them not to cease. Or, "according to the prophecy": the prophets had promised them that the outcome would be happy. So God in fact showed that he is constant in his promises.

units.la: Ædificarunt, & perfecerunt. Scilicet templum ex præcepto Dei & Cyri, Darij & Artaxerxis. Quidam coniunctionem vaf accipiunt ἐνλοτικῶς per expositionem, Darij qui & Artaxerxes, alij quia coniunctio illa interponitur, per Artaxerxem intelligunt filium Darij, cuius tempore absoluta sint, quæ ad or natum templi faciebant.
units.tr: They built and finished it. Namely the temple, by the command of God and of Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes. Some take the conjunction vav in a unifying sense [ἐνωτικῶς] by way of explanation, so that Darius is also Artaxerxes. Others, because the conjunction is inserted, understand by Artaxerxes the son of Darius, in whose time the works that pertained to the adornment of the temple were completed.

units.la: Absolutum est ædificium templi tertio die mensis Adar, qui partim Februario nostro, partim Martio respondit. 6. anno regni Darij.
units.tr: The building of the temple was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which partly corresponds to our February and partly to March, in the sixth year of Darius.

units.la: Ex his doctrinam consolatione plenam eruimus: nempe quòd si illa faciamus quæ Deus iussit, etsi magnam habeant difficultatem, tamen ipse nobis non defuturus sit conatibus nostris. Iudæi iussu ... volüntate Dei, templum extruxerunt: magna, vt Cap. 4. audiuimus, obiecta eis fuerunt impedimenta, quæ Deus omnia sustulit. Successit in impij Cambysis locum, Darius rex bonus, is satrapas etiam bonos habuit, qui humanos & beneuolos se Iudæis præbuerunt: hæc autem Deo tribuenda est, in calce Capitis indicatur.
units.tr: From these facts we draw a doctrine full of comfort: namely, that if we do what God has commanded, even though it presents great difficulty, he will not fail our efforts. The Jews built the temple by the command and will of God. Great hindrances were placed in their way, as we heard in chapter 4, but God removed them all. In place of the wicked Cambyses came Darius, a good king, who also had good satraps, who showed themselves kind and friendly to the Jews. This, however, must be attributed to God, as is indicated at the end of the chapter.

units.la: Nobis quoque Deus præcipit, vt templum spirituale ædificemus, hoc fit, si abnegatis erroribus, per fidem Christo insecuramur, sanctè & iustè viuamus, & alios quoque ad veram pœnitentiam adducamus. Hoc difficile quidem est: nam Satanas, Antichristus, mundus, caro nostra, nobis impedimento sunt. At si quisque ope Dei fretus, in sua vocatione faciat quod debet, nostris quoque laboribus benedicit. Ministri ecclesiæ, Haggæi & Zachariæ exemplo instent hominibus eosque vrgeant: præcepta & exempla in scripturis ob oculos habentes. Principes edictis, vt Darius, ædificium illud spirituale promouent, illosque defendant, qui propter veritatem in periculum veniunt: dent operam, vt Euangelium illis, qui adhuc in erroribus versantur, prædicetur: patresfamilias suos ita instituant, vt domus ipsorum infar ecclesiæ sint. Singuli dent operam, vt ipsi sint templum, in quo Spiritus sanctus habitare velit: non hara sint diaboli.
units.tr: God commands us too to build a spiritual temple. This is done if, renouncing errors, we cling to Christ by faith, live holily and righteously, and bring others also to true repentance. This is indeed difficult, for Satan, the Antichrist, the world and our own flesh are obstacles to us. But if each person, trusting in the help of God, does in his own calling what he ought, he also blesses our labours. Let the ministers of the Church, after the example of Haggai and Zechariah, press upon people and urge them, keeping the precepts and examples of Scripture before their eyes. Let the princes, by edicts as Darius did, advance that spiritual building and defend those who come into danger for the truth. Let them take care that the Gospel is preached to those who are still caught in errors. Let heads of households so instruct their families that their houses may be like a church. Let each person take pains to be a temple in which the Holy Spirit wishes to dwell, and not a sty of the devil.

units.la: Deus bone quot possemus lucrifacere, si digne Euangelio viueremus? Nemo desperet aut in latebras se abdat, aut clauum
units.tr: Good God, how many we could win, if we lived worthy of the Gospel! Let no one despair or hide himself in hiding places, or give up the helm.

units.la: Templum spirituale quomodo ædificetur. num abijciant, quasi rem tentet, quae fieri non po‐terum si non statim extructio templi absoluatur, tamen in tempore fiet, si diligentes & seduli fuerimus. Hoc quoq; templum, non uno anno extructum fuit. Vulgo dicitur, Romam non uno die conditam esse. Alijs quoq; exemplis docemur, Deum fideliter laboratibus, & ipsum respicientibus, successum dare. Temporibus Apostolorum totus mundus idololatriae deditus erat, sed pauculi magno & incredibili successu, passim in toto orbe collegerunt Christo insignes ecclesias. Quot unicus Paulus instituit. Paulo ante nostram aetatem, pauci viri, & paruq apud homines existimationis, Antichristi fraudes detexerunt contra hominum expectationem, qui putabant mox opprimendos: sed Deus eis felicem successum dedit.
units.tr: How the spiritual temple is to be built. Though the thing may seem to be attempted as if it could not be done unless the building of the temple were completed at once, it will nevertheless be done in time, if we are diligent and earnest. This temple too was not built in one year. As the common saying goes, Rome was not founded in a single day. We are taught by other examples too that God gives success to those who labour faithfully and look to him. In the times of the Apostles the whole world was given over to idolatry, yet a few men, with great and incredible success, gathered notable churches for Christ throughout the whole world. How many did the single Paul establish!
