Shortly before our own age, a few men of little repute among people uncovered the frauds of the Antichrist, contrary to the expectation of men who thought they would soon be crushed. But God gave them a happy success.

units.la: Quot vero interea, inquis, miserè interierunt? quot oppida capta, quoties infeliciter pugnatum est, ab illis, qui fiducia promissionum Dei, ecclesias plantarunt? Respondeo, Promissiones corporales cum exceptione crucis intelligendas esse. Multos quoq; non Dei gloriam: sed suam potius & priuatam utilitatem sequutos esse, hostes contemsisse, seipsos mutuo prodidisse, postea in Euangelium omnem culpam relatam. Deus adhaec varijs aerumnis fidem & patientiam suorum fidelium exercet.
units.tr: But, you will say, how many in the meantime have miserably perished? How many towns have been taken, how often has fighting gone badly for those who, trusting in the promises of God, planted churches? I answer: the promises are to be understood as bodily promises with the exception of the cross. Many also, not seeking the glory of God but rather their own private advantage, have despised enemies, betrayed one another, and afterwards laid all the blame on the Gospel. Besides, God exercises the faith and patience of his faithful people with various troubles.

units.la: Illi qui spirituale templum, ecclesiam Dei, non plantant, sed funditus excindere conantur, ad tempus quidem feliciter degunt, tandem vero aeternis malis inuoluentur. Pij qui cum Christo afflictiones sustinent, tandem cum eo gloria afficientur. Quæruntur multi Deum non defendere ecclesiam, cum ipsi nihil faciant.
units.tr: Those who do not plant the spiritual temple, the Church of God, but seek to tear it up from the foundations, indeed live happily for a time, but at last they will be entangled in eternal evils. The godly who endure afflictions with Christ will at last be honoured with him in glory. Many complain that God does not defend the Church, when they themselves do nothing.

units.la: Vt vero illis qui ecclesiam aedificant, Deus successum dat, eisque benedicit: ita aliis quoque qui res à Deo praescriptas ordiuntur, prosperè cedit. Qui Deo inuocato discunt literas, artificia, qui coniugium contrahunt, benedictionem ab eo accipiunt. Petri labores Lucae 5. cap. irriti fuerunt, donec rete in lacum proiecit, iubente Domino. Similis historia Ioannis 21. capite exstat.
units.tr: Just as God gives success to those who build the Church and blesses them, so too it goes well for others who undertake the things prescribed by God. Those who learn letters and crafts calling on God, those who enter marriage, receive a blessing from him. Peter's labours in Luke chapter 5 were in vain, until at the Lord's command he cast the net into the lake. A similar story is found in John chapter 21.

units.la: Priuatim igitur & publicè illa facienda sunt, quae Deus praecipit, vt ut cum periculo videantur coniuncta: potest enim & vult, rebus bonum euentum dare.
units.tr: Therefore those things which God commands are to be done both privately and publicly, even though they may seem bound up with danger. For he is able, and he is willing, to give a good outcome to our undertakings.

units.la: HOMILIA XXI.
units.tr: HOMILY XXI.

units.la: Dedicatio templi.
units.tr: The dedication of the temple.

units.la: 16 Fecerunt q; filij Israel is sacerdotes & Leuitæ, ac reliqui filij transmigrationis, dedicationem domus Dei huius cum gaudio.
units.tr: 16 And the children of Israel, the priests and the Levites, and the rest of the children of the captivity, kept the dedication of this house of God with joy.

units.la: 17 Et obtulerunt in dedicatione domus Dei huius, vitulos centum, arietes ducentos, agnos quadringentos, & hircos caprarum in sacrificium pro peccato, pro toto Israel duodecim, secundum numerum tribuum Israelis.
units.tr: 17 And they offered at the dedication of this house of God a hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and for a sin offering for all Israel twelve he-goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.

units.la: 18 Constituerunt q; sacerdotes in divisionibus suis, & Leuitas in distinctionibus suis, super opus Dei quod faciendum erat in Ierusalaim, sicut scriptum est in libro Moisis.
units.tr: 18 And they set the priests in their divisions, and the Levites in their courses, for the service of God, which is at Jerusalem, as it is written in the book of Moses.

units.la: AB initio tertij Capitis, vsque ad versum huius 16. dictum est quomodo altari extrucĭo, & iactis templi fundamentis, hoc ædificium impeditum multis annis, postea prophetarum hortatu, iterum repetitum & feliciter tandem absolutum fit. Ex quibus colligimus quàm ægrè procedat templi spiritualis ædificium, miris technis satana & impijs illud remorantibus.Si aliquot ex nobis tam essent seduli in negotijs quæ Dei gloriam spectant, quàm sunt in illis quæ ad priuatum quæstum suum faciunt, summa festinatione hoc spirituale ædificium procederet.
units.tr: From the beginning of the third chapter up to verse 16 of this passage it has been related how the altar was erected and the foundations of the temple were laid; this building, hindered for many years, was afterwards taken up again at the urging of the prophets and at length happily completed. From these things we gather how slowly the building of the spiritual temple proceeds, while Satan and the wicked hinder it by wonderful devices. If some of us were as diligent in those affairs which concern God's glory as we are in those which bring us private gain, this spiritual building would advance with the greatest speed.

units.la: Videamus nunc de dedicatione vel consecratione huius templi, nempe à quibus & quomodo facta sit. Scribitur Sacerdotes, Leuitas, & filios migrationis, hoc est, illos qui ab exilio redierunt, templum Domini dedicasse cum gaudio. Lætati enim sunt, quòd hoc ædificium tandem ad finem optatum perductum esset, & vera religio publicè exerceri posset. Attulerunt vel obtulerunt (קרב karaf est in textu) boues centum, arietes ducentos, agnos quadrigentos, itē hircos duodecim piaculares, secundum tribus Israelis, ex omnibus enim tribubus aliqui redierant. Non quòd holocaustis peccata expientur: sed quia fuerūt typi remissionis peccatorum, quam Christus nobis suo sanguine acquisiuit.
units.tr: Let us now consider the dedication or consecration of this temple: namely, by whom and in what manner it was done. It is written that the priests, the Levites, and the children of the captivity, that is, those who had returned from exile, dedicated the temple of the Lord with joy. For they rejoiced that this building had at last been brought to its desired end, and that true religion could be practised publicly. They brought or offered (the text has קרב, karaf) a hundred oxen, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and likewise twelve he-goats for sin, according to the tribes of Israel, for some had returned from all the tribes. Not that sins were expiated by the burnt offerings, but because they were types of the remission of sins, which Christ has won for us by his blood.

units.la: Statuerunt autem Sacerdotes & Leuitas, secun-diui- siones vel classes suas, iuxta quas sacris operari, & per vices Deo ministrare debuerunt. Erat inter Leuitas ordo certus, & quaedam distributio in certas partes. Leuitica tribus in tres familias fuit distributa, in Cahatitas, Gersonitas & Meraritas: hi rursus diducebantur in ordines quatuor. Quid singulorum fuerit officium, fuse in Leuitico & libro Numerorum exponitur. Postea Dauid quoq; in classes eosdistinxit, vt per vices Deo seruirent. Multum enim refert, vt ordo seruetur: In bello, in magnis familijs, si bene institutae sint, singuli norunt suum officium.
units.tr: Moreover, the priests and the Levites appointed their divisions or classes, according to which they were to perform the sacred duties and minister to God in turn. Among the Levites there was a fixed order and a certain distribution into set parts. The tribe of Levi was divided into three families, the Kohathites, the Gershonites and the Merarites; these in turn were subdivided into four orders. What the duty of each was is set out at length in Leviticus and in the book of Numbers. Afterwards David also divided them into classes, so that they might serve God in turn. For it matters greatly that order be kept: in war, and in large households, if they are well ordered, each man knows his own duty.

units.la: DEDICATIO TEMPLORVM.
units.tr: THE DEDICATION OF TEMPLES.

units.la: Hoc loco de dedicatione templi externi, veteris & noui populi, & spiritualis quoque, paucula quaedam annotanda sunt. Exodi 40. legimus tabernaculum quod Dei iussu erectum erat, à Mose initiatum esse vel consecratum. Chamah consecrare significat, visibus sacris dicare, primum visurpare. Oleo autem peculiari & certis ceremonijs tabernaculum, item sacerdotes, vestes & vasa tabernaculi consecrata sunt. Numeri 7. capite, principes obtulerunt in dedicatione sua, donaria ad dedicationem tabernaculi. Postea Solomonis templum ingenti cum gaudio, clamore, iubilatione, tubis & reliquis instrumentis musicis fuit dedicatum. Preces publicas in eo habuit, oblata sunt magna & varia sacrificia. De oleo nihil dicitur, at probabile est, & templum illud, & vasa eius omnia fuisse vncta. Domos etiam priuatas dedicarunt. Deuteronomij 20. capite iubetur ille qui suam domum nondum dedicauit, ex militia reuerti, eamq; dedicare, ne forte occumbat in bello, & alius dedicet eam. Dauid psalmum 50. conscripsit quando domum suam quam sibi construxerat, dedicare voluit. Cum primum aedes inhabitare incipimus, eas dedicamus.
units.tr: Here a few brief remarks are needed on the dedication of the outward temple of the old and new people, and of the spiritual temple as well. In Exodus 40 we read that the tabernacle, which was erected by God's command, was initiated, or consecrated, by Moses. Chamah means to consecrate, to dedicate to sacred use, to take into use for the first time. The tabernacle, and likewise the priests, the garments and the vessels of the tabernacle, were consecrated with special oil and fixed ceremonies. In Numbers chapter 7 the princes offered gifts at the dedication of the tabernacle. Afterwards Solomon's temple was dedicated with great joy, shouting, rejoicing, trumpets and other musical instruments. Public prayers were offered in it, and many and varied sacrifices. Nothing is said about oil, but it is probable that both the temple and all its vessels were anointed. They also dedicated private houses. Deuteronomy 20 orders that the man who has not yet dedicated his house should return from military service and dedicate it, lest perhaps he die in battle and another dedicate it. David wrote Psalm 50 when he wished to dedicate the house he had built for himself. As soon as we begin to live in a house, we dedicate it.

units.la: Secundi templi initiatio vel dedicatio hoc loco describitur. Postea cum contaminatum esset ab Antiochi Epiphanis mi-litibus, Iudas Machabaeus recepta vrbe, illud repurgauit, & tunc encaenia fuerunt instituta, quae quottannis celebrantur. 1. Machabaeorum quarto capite. Ioannis 10. capite, Christus etiam ad Encaenia venisse legitur. Solomonis templum semel dedicatum est, neq; fuit anniuersaria festiuitas.
units.tr: Here is described the initiation, or dedication, of the second temple. Later, when it had been defiled by the soldiers of Antiochus Epiphanes, Judas Maccabeus, after recovering the city, cleansed it, and then the feast of the Encaenia was instituted, which is celebrated every year (1 Maccabees 4). In John 10 we read that Christ also came to the Encaenia. Solomon's temple was dedicated once, and there was no yearly festival of it.

units.la: Ceremoniae autem quibus veteres dedicarunt sacra loca, personas, vasa, tunc habuerunt verbum Dei, non autem diutius debu{-}durare, quàm ad tempora Christi: vmbrae enim fuerunt & typi rerum futurarum.
units.tr: The ceremonies by which the ancients dedicated holy places, persons and vessels had the Word of God with them, but they were not meant to last longer than the time of Christ, for they were shadows and types of things to come.

units.la: Christiani annos à natali Christi circiter 300. nulla habuerunt templa, sed metu tyrannorum in locis occultis congregati sunt, ad verae religionis exercitium. Hinc in maioribus & vetustioribus ecclesijs cryptas extruxerunt, vt conditionem veterem Christianorum, memoriae imprimerent: tandem cum pax data esseт ecclesijs sub Constantino magno, ille Hierosolymis, vt historia testatur, Christo templum egregium extruxit, donis exornauit, atque ad eius dedicationem Episcopos vocauit, qui illo tempore Tyri concilium celebrabant. Dedicatio verò illa, teste Eusebio, Euangelicis sermonibus, precationibus & laudibus Dei constabat: non aqua, sale, cinere, oleo, & alijs rebus quas hodie adhibent.
units.tr: For about three hundred years after the birth of Christ, Christians had no temples; for fear of the tyrants they gathered in hidden places to practise the true religion. Hence in the larger and older churches they built crypts, so as to keep the old condition of the Christians in memory. At last, when peace was given to the churches under Constantine the Great, he built at Jerusalem, as history bears witness, a splendid temple to Christ, adorned it with gifts, and summoned the bishops, who at that time were holding a council at Tyre, to its dedication. That dedication, according to Eusebius, consisted of gospel sermons, prayers and praises of God, not of water, salt, ashes, oil and other things which they use today.

units.la: Veram consecrationem templorum non reijcimus. Vera autem est, quando illa in eis exercentur, propter quae extruenda sunt, quando agnoscimus dona Dei, & rectum vsum petimus, gratias agimus quod conuenire tuto possumus. Omnia quae primum vsurpare incipimus, precibus & gratiarum actione dedicanda vel consecranda sunt.
units.tr: We do not reject the true consecration of temples. It is true when those things are carried out in them for which they are to be built; when we acknowledge the gifts of God, ask for their right use, and give thanks that we can meet there safely. Everything that we begin to use for the first time must be dedicated or consecrated with prayers and thanksgiving.

units.la: Christus liberos nos fecit à ceremonijs Iudaicis, Antichristus non contentus illas reduxisse & ecclesijs obtrusisse, insuper ex gentilismo multas adiecit, ita vt falsi cultus, paulatim aucti & cumulati sint. Vtq; niues in alpibus verno tempore ex tenui initio, veluti repercussione vocis, aut auiculae volatu, motae, conglobari incipiunt, & tandem longe lateq; omnia prosternunt & implent: ita idololatria ex paruis initijs creuit, & tandem in immensum aucta, ecclesiam ferè obruit.
units.tr: Christ has freed us from Jewish ceremonies. Antichrist, not content to have brought them back and forced them upon the churches, has in addition added many from paganism, so that false worship, gradually increased and heaped up, has grown. And just as snows in the Alps in spring, starting from a small beginning, are set in motion as if by the echo of a voice or the flight of a little bird, and then begin to gather into a mass and at last lay low and fill everything far and wide, so idolatry grew from small beginnings, and at last, increasing without measure, has almost overwhelmed the Church.

units.la: Dicamus autem nunc tantum de consecratione aedium sacrarum, sacellorum, altarium, coemeteriorum, & aliorum id genus. Suffraganeis episcopis ferè id committitur. Illi à papa praeficiuntur ecclesijs, quas nunquam viderunt, neq; visuri sunt, vt Antiochenae, Tyriae, &c. quia vero inde reditus nullos habent, huiusmodi pecuniae aucupijs, sese alunt. De templo, de singulis aris, de coemiterio, certam summam pecuniae illis numerare oportuit. Factum est in agro Tigurino, vt suffraganeus quidam totum coemeterium lustrarit, postea cum pauperculi agricolae inter rogaret, vbi sepeliendi essent infantes qui absq; baptismo decederent: mox angulum quendam coemiterij iusit non esse sacrum, vel prophanauit, sed neq; hoc gratis, denuo enim pecunias ei numerari oportuit. Quando templum vel coemiterium prophanatum fuit tum fuit per cædes, libidines, aut si sepultus aliqui fuitâ pontifice excommunicatus, denuo lustrare & expiare illud oportuit, vel reconciliare, sic enim vocant, & iterum numerare pecuniam, alioqui missæ non fuerunt in illo templo celebratæ, sed ostia templi occlusa, & intermissus Dei cultus. Talis quidá episcopus accepta pecunia in agro quoq; nostro, duo templa consecrauit, sacerdote verò quodam eum Simoniacum esse dicente, quòd dona spiritus venderet. Ille respondit, se non paciscicum rusticis, ut Simon fecit cum Petro, sed ne hoc scelus in currat, se ipsis diserté præcipere, ut tantum sibi pro illa luftratio ne numerent.
units.tr: Now let us speak only of the consecration of sacred buildings, chapels, altars, cemeteries and things of that kind. This is mostly committed to suffragan bishops. They are appointed by the pope over churches which they have never seen and never will see, such as those at Antioch, Tyre, and so on. Since they have no income from these, they support themselves by such money-catching. For the temple, for each altar and for the cemetery, a fixed sum of money had to be paid to them. It happened in the Zurich territory that a certain suffragan bishop purified the whole cemetery; afterwards, when a poor farmer asked him where infants who died without baptism were to be buried, he at once ordered a certain corner of the cemetery not to be holy, or defiled it. But not even this was done for nothing: once again money had to be counted out to him. When a temple or cemetery had been defiled, which happened through murders, lusts, or if anyone had been buried there who had been excommunicated by the bishop, it had to be purified and expiated again, or reconciled (for so they call it), and the money counted out again. Otherwise Masses were not celebrated in that temple, but its doors were shut and the worship of God was suspended. Such a bishop, having received money, also consecrated two temples in our country, although a certain priest said that he was a Simoniac, because he sold the gifts of the Spirit. He replied that he did not bargain with the peasants, as Simon did with Peter, but so that this crime should not occur he himself expressly ordered them to count out only so much money to him for that purification.

units.la: Loca sepulturæ apud veteres consecrata non fuerunt, nam cadauera extra vrbes sepeliebant, & multi in suis agris vel hortis sepulturam delegerunt. Tandé sepulturæ cum templis coniungi ceperunt.
units.tr: Among the ancients, places of burial were not consecrated, for they buried corpses outside the cities, and many chose a burial place in their own fields or gardens. Eventually burial places began to be joined to temples.

units.la: Adhæc templa non soli Deo dedicantur, sed apostolis, sanctę virgini, martyribus, confessoribus, & ipsis etiam angelis. D. Augustinus negat fas esse, creaturis templa condere. Lib. 1. contra Maximinum Arrianorum episcopum: Nonne, inquit, si templū alicui sancto angelo excellentissimo delignis & lapidibus facemus, anathematizaremur à veritate Christi & ecclesia Dei? Quia creaturæ exhiberemus eam seruitutem, quæ vni tantum Deo debetur. &c. Vide etiam de Ciuitate Dei libro 22. capite 10. De vera religione capite vltimo. Templa ab illis quibus dedicata sunt, nomen acceperunt, vt templum D. Petri, Andreæ, Sebaldi, &c.
units.tr: Moreover, temples are dedicated not only to God, but to the apostles, the holy Virgin, martyrs, confessors, and even to angels themselves. St Augustine denies that it is lawful to build temples to creatures. In Book 1 against Maximinus, the Arian bishop: "Would we not," he says, "if we made a temple of wood and stone to some most excellent holy angel, be cut off from the truth of Christ and the Church of God? Because we would be giving to a creature that service which is owed to the one God alone, etc." See also The City of God, book 22, chapter 10, and On True Religion, last chapter. Temples have taken their names from those to whom they were dedicated, such as the temple of St Peter, St Andrew, St Sebald, etc.

units.la: Templis non contenti, sacella extruxerunt hinc inde, in quibus missas celebrarent, quæ etiam suas dedicationes & patronos habuerunt.
units.tr: Not content with temples, they built chapels here and there, in which they celebrated Masses; these also had their own dedications and patrons.

units.la: Varios autem & multiplices ritus adhibent suffraganei templum initiaturi, caligantes in foleaccendunt cereos, aquam benedictam in parietes intus & extra spargunt, oleo parietes inungunt, cruces consignant, suffitum faciunt, alphabetha Græca & Hebraica pauimento inscribūt. Hęc pluris ab illis fiunt, quàm quæ Deus ipse instituit. Denunciant vt populus illo die quotannis coueniat, cum dedicatio templi Solomonis toto orbe celeberrimi semel facta, repetita amplius non fit: dantur largæ indulgentiæ aduentantibus. Luxu, libidinibus, saltationibus, in dedicationibus illis, omnia diffluunt, vt Lupercalia & Bacchanalia potiusquàm feriæ Christianorum censeri debeant. Loco verbi Dei missæ habentur. In cœcionibus suis, si quæ sunt, inuehuntur in pura & veram doctrinam. Quibus ceremonijs templum maius Basileae ab episcopo, Heinrici Imperatoris temporibus consecratum fit, vide Basilicnsia Chronica Christiani Vrftifij.
units.tr: The suffragan bishops, when they are about to initiate a temple, use various and manifold rites: they light candles while the place is in darkness, sprinkle holy water on the walls within and without, anoint the walls with oil, make the sign of the cross, perform fumigation, and write the Greek and Hebrew alphabets on the pavement. They make far more of these things than of those which God himself instituted. They proclaim that the people should gather every year on that day, though the dedication of Solomon's temple, most celebrated throughout the world, was done once and is not repeated. Large indulgences are granted to those who come. At these dedications everything runs to luxury, lusts and dancing, so that they should be counted rather as the Lupercalia and Bacchanalia than as Christian holy days. In place of the Word of God, Masses are held. In their sermons, if there are any, they rail against pure and true doctrine. With such ceremonies the larger temple at Basel was consecrated by the bishop in the time of the Emperor Henry; see the Basel Chronicles of Christian Urstisius.

units.la: De quibusdam sacellis, veluti de sacello D.Michaelis in monte Gargano, dicitur, quod ab angelis consecrata sint, ideoq; plurimi certis annorum recursibus ad illa confluunt. Rem ita habere firmiter se dicunt credere, & gloriantur de papae bullis quibus id confirmetur: interim miseri scire nolunt, haec facile fingi posse ab otiosis ventribus. Deus bone quam varias Dianae virginis apparitiones monachi praedicatori Bernae Auenticorum confinxerunt? Sed esto haec vel illa visa & audita sint, ut referunt, tamen certum est ad confirmandam superstitionem, permissu Dei, satanam miranda facere. Potest etiam, Paulo teste, se in angelum lucis transformare. De templo Ephesino res maior scribitur. Nam, teste Plinio, operi praefuit Ctesiphon architectus. Is cum anxius esset quomodo in limine ipso epistylion molem maximam attollere posset, & manum sibi inferre cogitaret, noctürno tempore in quiete vidit praesente Deam cui templum fiebat, hortantem ne hoc faceret, se compositilTe lapidem: atq; ita postero die apparuit, &c.
units.tr: Of certain chapels, for example the chapel of St Michael on Monte Gargano, it is said that they were consecrated by angels, and so very many flock to them at fixed intervals of years. They say they firmly believe that the matter is so, and they boast of the papal bulls by which it is confirmed; meanwhile the wretched people refuse to know that such things can easily be invented by idle bellies. Good God, what a variety of apparitions of the Virgin Diana did the monks invent for the preacher at Bern of the Aventicenses! But granted that these or those things were seen and heard, as they report, it is nevertheless certain that Satan, by God's permission, performs marvels to confirm superstition. He can also, as Paul bears witness, transform himself into an angel of light. A greater matter is written about the temple at Ephesus: for, according to Pliny, the architect Ctesiphon was in charge of the work. When he was anxious how he could raise the huge architrave over the very threshold, and was thinking of laying hands on himself, one night in sleep he saw the goddess to whom the temple was being built, present, urging him not to do this, since she herself had set the stone in place; and so on the next day it appeared, etc.

units.la: Neq; solum templa superstitiosi homines, verum alia multa confecrarunt. Vnde facile colligi potest, quam necessaria sit emendatio doctrinae & rituum, in ecclesia.
units.tr: Nor have superstitious men consecrated only temples, but many other things besides. From this it can easily be gathered how necessary is the reform of doctrine and of rites in the Church.

units.la: Addenda iam sunt paucula, de dedicatione spiritualis templi. D.Paulus dicit 1.Corinth.3, An nescitis quod corpora vestra templum sunt spiritus sancti, & quod spiritus sanctus habitat in vobis? In 2.ad Corinth.6.capite, templum estis viuentis Dei. Homines consecrantur Deo, quando per baptismum recipiuntur visibiliter in populi Dei consortium. Cauendum igitur, ne hoc templum Baccho, Veneri, Mercurio dedicemus: sed impollutum custodiamus. Qui materiale templum polluit, graviter peccat, quanto magis peccant illi, qui templum spiritus sancti prophanant.
units.tr: There are now a few things to be added concerning the dedication of the spiritual temple. St Paul says, 1 Corinthians 3: "Know ye not that your bodies are the temple of the Holy Ghost, and that the Holy Ghost dwelleth in you?" In 2 Corinthians 6: "Ye are the temple of the living God." Men are consecrated to God when, through baptism, they are visibly received into the fellowship of the people of God. We must take care, therefore, that we do not dedicate this temple to Bacchus, Venus or Mercury, but keep it undefiled. If he who defiles a material temple sins grievously, how much more do those sin who profane the temple of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: HOMILIA XXII.
units.tr: HOMILIA XXII.

units.la: De celebrata solennitate paschali à Iudaeis Hierosolymis.
units.tr: On the Passover celebrated by the Jews at Jerusalem.

units.la: 19 Fecerunt praeterea filij transmigrationis Pascha quartadecima mensis primi. (Purificati enim erat Sacerdotes & Leuitæ, tanquam vnus, omnes mundi erant) immolauerunt in quam Pesah pro omnibus filijs transmigrationis, & pro fratribus suis sacerdotibus, & pro seipsis. Comederunt itaque filij Israelis qui reuersi erant de transmigratione, & omnis qui subduxerat se à coinquinatione gentium terræ ad eos, vt requireret Iehovam Deum Israelis. Fecerunt & solennitatem infermentatorum septem diebus cum lætitia, quod exhilarasset eos Iehovah, & converrisset cor regis Assur ad eos, ad confortandum eos in opere domus Dei, Dei (inquam) Israelis.
units.tr: 19 The children of the captivity also kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month. (For the priests and Levites were purified, all of them together as one man, all were clean.) They slew the passover for all the children of the captivity, for their brethren the priests, and for themselves. So the children of Israel who had returned from the captivity ate it, and every one who had separated himself from the filthiness of the nations of the land to seek the LORD God of Israel. They also kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy, for the LORD had made them joyful, and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of God, the God (I say) of Israel.

units.la: IN calce huius capitis, commemoratur, qui, quando, quomodo & vbi pascha celebrarint. Dicit noster author, filios transmigrationis pasah fecisse, die 14. primi mensis, nempe Nisan vel Abib, qui partim Martio, partim Aprili respondet. Annus fuit mutatus in liberatione populi ex Ægypto. Primus enim mensis Nisan deinceps fuit, quia in hoc libertate Israelitæ adepti sunt. 14 die mactatus agnus post occasum solis, à quo 15. inchoabant, & pascha edebant. Purificati enim erant sacerdotes & Leuitæ, tanquam vnus, omnes mundi erant. (Deus Num. 9. cap. dispensauit de tempore paschæ. Impediti vel immunditia aliqua, aut peregrinatione, secundo mense pascha facere potuerunt. Cæteris omnibus obseruatis, quæ primo lex præscribit. Ezechias rex pascha fecit secundo mense: cumq; plurimi ob breuitatem temporis, sanctificari non possent, precibus ipsius & Leuitarum expiati, postea pascha fecerunt. Purgabantur autem per orationes, ablutiones, & continentiam ab vxoribus & immunditijs legis. Si qui ad honesti viri mensam accedunt, se præparant, multò magis in paschali epulo id faciendum erat.
units.tr: AT the end of this chapter, the author recalls who, when, how and where they celebrated the passover. Our author says that the children of the captivity kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, namely Nisan or Abib, which falls partly in March and partly in April. The year was changed at the deliverance of the people from Egypt, for Nisan became the first month from then on, because in it the Israelites obtained their freedom. On the fourteenth day the lamb was slain after sunset, and from the fifteenth they began and ate the passover. For the priests and Levites were purified, all of them together as one, all were clean. (God, in Numbers chapter 9, provided for the time of the passover: those who were prevented by some uncleanness, or by a journey, could keep the passover in the second month, all the other things being observed which the law first prescribes. King Hezekiah kept the passover in the second month; and since very many, because of the shortness of the time, could not be sanctified, they were cleansed by his prayers and those of the Levites, and afterwards kept the passover. They were purified by prayers, washings, and abstinence from wives and from the uncleannesses of the law. If people who approach the table of an honourable man prepare themselves, how much more should this be done at the paschal feast.)

units.la: Immolarunt vel mactarunt omnibus filijs transmigrationis & fratribus suis sacerdotibus, & sibi ipsis.) Leuitæ qui quasi lanij erant, videntur mactasse omnes paschales agnos, sicut annotaui in 2. Paralipomenon capite 30. folio 197. item capite 35. sol. 216. Nolo tamen dissimulare, quod Philo lib. 3. de vita Mosis scribit: tempore paschæ non vt alias plebeos homines victimas adducere ad altare, sed iubente lege totam gentem sacrificare, dum
units.tr: They slew or killed it for all the children of the captivity, and for their brethren the priests, and for themselves.) The Levites, who were as it were the butchers, seem to have slain all the paschal lambs, as I noted on 2 Chronicles chapter 30, page 197, and likewise chapter 35, page 216. I do not wish, however, to conceal what Philo writes in the third book of On the Life of Moses: at the time of the passover, not as at other times, when the common people brought victims to the altar, but by command of the law the whole nation sacrificed, while ... if anyone should act as priest, etc.

units.la: M se quis[?] gerat pro sacerdote,&c.
units.tr: M ... if someone acts for a priest, etc.

units.la: Comederunt itaq; Israelitæ reuersi de exilio,& qui conuersi erant ad fidem Iudæorum, quos proselytas vocant. Græci à προσῆλυθω venio: quod ex Ethnica religione in Iudaicam venirent, circumcidebantur enim, & legi Dei se obstringebant. Hebræi gerim eos vocant. Periphrasis vel descriptio eorum hoc loco habetur: omnis qui subduxerat se ab inquinatione gentium terræ ad eos, vt requireret Iehouam Deum Israelis.
units.tr: So the Israelites who returned from exile ate it, and those who had been converted to the faith of the Jews, whom they call proselytes. The Greeks [προσῆλυθω] derive this from coming (to), because they passed from the heathen religion into the Jewish one; for they were circumcised and bound themselves to the law of God. The Hebrews call them gerim. A periphrasis or description of them is given in this place: every one who had separated himself from the filthiness of the nations of the land to seek the LORD God of Israel.

units.la: Fecerunt & solennitatem infermentatorum septem diebus. Festum paschæ etiam festum azymorum dicitur, quia per septem dies infermentatis panibus vescebantur. Prima dies quæ est 15. & 21 fuerunt festi. Cum lætitia.) Deus enim in solennibus illis fe stis, lætos esse iusit. Vide Neh. 8. ca. quod exhilarasset eos Deus.) Deus eos hilares reddidit.
units.tr: They also kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days. The feast of the passover is also called the feast of unleavened bread, because for seven days they ate bread without leaven. The first day, which is the fifteenth, and the twenty-first, were festal days. With joy. For God commanded them to be glad at those solemn feasts; see Nehemiah chapter 8. For the LORD had made them joyful. God made them cheerful.

units.la: Et conuertisset cor regis Assur ad eos, ad confortandum eos in opere domus Dei, Dei inquam Israelis.) Deus regem Assur, qui etiam Persarum rex fuit, reddidit Iudæis propitium. Mirabilis fuit reuersio. Assyrij antea infesto animo erat in Iudeos, nunc adiuuant eos in opere domini. In Proverbijs dicit Salomon cor regis esse in manu Domini. Si nos conuertamur ad Deum feria pœnitentia, tyranni fient nobis amici & benevoli. Ex hostibus Deus facile amicos facere potest. Quare si vis habere propitios principes, vicinos, precare Dominum vt corda eorum emolliat, &c.
units.tr: And had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of God, the God, I say, of Israel. God made the king of Assyria, who was also king of the Persians, favourable to the Jews. The change was remarkable. The Assyrians had earlier been hostile to the Jews; now they help them in the work of the Lord. In the Proverbs Solomon says that the heart of the king is in the hand of the Lord. If we turn to God in a time of repentance, tyrants will become our friends and well-wishers. God can easily make friends out of enemies. Therefore, if you want to have favourable princes and neighbours, pray the Lord that he soften their hearts, etc.

units.la: Dicendum est hoc loco, de institutione vel de ritu paschæ, de quo Exodi 12. cap. fusè agitur: Deinde quæ sit eius significatio. Deus præcepit populo suo, vt mense primo qui Nisan dicitur, vnaquæque domus 10. die ex grege Sæh, hoc est, agnum vel hædum deligat, qui sit perfectus, vel sine macula, anniculus, masculus. Hunc seruent ad diem decimum quartum, & sub vespere diei, vniuersa multitudo illum mactet. Sanguinem eius excipiat, & fasciculo hyssopi, superliminare & postes domus in qua edebatur pascha, aspergant, ne primogeniti ab angelo vastatore occidantur. Assare eum iubet, non elixare, neque crudum edere. Idque illi tantum facere debebant, qui Israelitæ & circumcisi erant. Excludebantur ab hoc epulo, extranei, qui non habitabant cum ipsis: Aduenæ, qui habitare coeperant cum Israelitis: sed nondum circumcisi fuerant: Item serui emptitij non circumcisi ac mercenarij. In domo vna totum edere debuerunt, caput, pedes, intestina, vt nihil relinquerent. Si nimis pauci erant, vicinos sibi adiungere iusi sunt. Iosephus dicit aliquando vido vicenos, plerunque denos simul pafchah edifle. Reliquum, vt olla quæ non debuerunt frangi, nerui & alia non apta esui, comburenda erant. Quomodo edendus fuerit agnus ille annotatur: more peregrinantium, debuerunt enim accincti esse, calceati, baculos tenere in manibus, & festinanter eum comedere, cum herbis amaris, azymis item vesci septem diebus, & à fermentatis abstinere debuerunt, sub pœna capitis. Hoc autem festum quotannis celebrandum fuit, inque illum finem, vt partim specialis illius redemptionis ex Ægypto, partim futuræ & generalis illius redemptionis in Christo factæ, admonerentur. Filijs etiam suis inculcare debuerunt, quid sibi hic ritus vellet.
units.tr: Here we must speak of the institution and the rite of the passover, which is treated at length in Exodus chapter 12, and then of its meaning. God commanded his people that in the first month, which is called Nisan, each household should on the tenth day take from the flock a seh, that is, a lamb or kid, which should be perfect, without blemish, a yearling, male. They were to keep it until the fourteenth day, and toward evening the whole assembly was to slay it. They were to catch its blood, and with a bundle of hyssop sprinkle the lintel and the doorposts of the house in which the passover was eaten, so that the firstborn should not be killed by the destroying angel. He commanded that it be roasted, not boiled, nor eaten raw. And this only those were to do who were Israelites and circumcised. Excluded from this feast were foreigners who did not dwell with them; sojourners who had begun to live with the Israelites but had not yet been circumcised; likewise bought servants who were not circumcised, and hired servants. They had to eat the whole of it in one house, the head, feet and entrails, so that they left nothing. If the households were too few, they were ordered to join their neighbours to themselves. Josephus says that sometimes they ate the passover in companies of twenty, and most often of ten together. What was left over, such as the pot, which they were not to break, the sinews, and other things unfit for food, had to be burned. The manner in which that lamb was to be eaten is recorded: in the manner of travellers, for they had to be girded, shod, to hold staves in their hands, and to eat it hastily, with bitter herbs; likewise for seven days they were to eat unleavened bread and abstain from leavened things, under penalty of death. This feast was to be celebrated every year, for the purpose that they might be reminded partly of that special redemption from Egypt, and partly of the future and general redemption made in Christ. They were also to impress on their sons what this rite meant.

units.la: Quid singula significent audiemus. Proponuntur enim nobis mysteria magnarum rerum, nempe quis sit Christus & qualis, quid conferat pijs, & quomodo participes ipsius reddamur.
units.tr: Let us hear what each element signifies. For the mysteries of great things are set before us, namely who Christ is and what sort of person he is, what he confers on the godly, and how we are made partakers of him.

units.la: 1 Ouem deligebant: animal, vt poeta dicit, sine fraude doloqi. Significatur Christus non solum propter innocentiam & patientiam, sed quia oblatus est. Ioannis primo capite, Ecce agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi. 1. Petri 1. cap. Redempti sumus sanguine, &c.
units.tr: 1. They chose a sheep or a goat. As the poet says, the animal is without guile. Christ is signified not only by his innocence and patience, but because he was offered. John chapter 1: Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world. 1 Peter 1: We were redeemed with blood, etc.

units.la: 2 Ex ouibus & hœdis. Hœdi in sacris literis impios significant, Christus ex pijs & impijs secundum carnem natus est. Matth. 1. capite.
units.tr: 2. From the sheep and the goats. In Holy Scripture goats signify the ungodly; Christ was born according to the flesh of the godly and the ungodly. Matthew chapter 1.

units.la: 3 Agnus debuit esse integer vel perfectus, qui careret corporis vitio, non mancus nec claudus esset. Christi integritas & innocentia significatur. Conceptus est de spiritu sancto, natus ex virgine. 1. Pet. 2. Dolus non est inventus in ore eius: talem esse decebat illum, qui nos à peccatis redemit. Anniculus esse debuit vt esset confirmatis viribus. Masculus quia mares sunt robustiores. Christus virili robore præditus est: vicit diabolum, mortem peccatum.
units.tr: 3. The lamb had to be whole or perfect, having no bodily defect, not maimed nor lame. The integrity and innocence of Christ are signified. He was conceived of the Holy Spirit, born of a virgin. 1 Peter 2: Guile was not found in his mouth. Such a one it was fitting to be, who redeemed us from sins. It had to be a yearling, so that its strength would be established. Male, because males are stronger. Christ is endowed with manly vigour: he overcame the devil, death, and sin.

units.la: 4 Agnus ille seruabatur quatriduo. Deligendus enim erat 10. die mensis, & mactandus ad vesperam 14. Christus enim non statim cum in hanc terram venit, crucifixus fuit. Deinde vt conspectu agni admoniti, cogitarent de promissionibus sibi factis.
units.tr: 4. That lamb was kept for four days. For it had to be chosen on the tenth day of the month, and slain toward evening on the fourteenth. For Christ, when he came into this world, was not crucified at once. Then, that being admonished by the sight of the lamb, they might think on the promises made to them.

units.la: 5 Mactatur sub vesperam. Christus enim in vltima mundi ætate, crucis supplicio affectus est.
units.tr: 5. It was slain toward evening. For Christ, in the last age of the world, was subjected to the punishment of the cross.

units.la: 6 Ab omni cœtu mactandus fuit. Nam omnes sumus causa mortis eius: neque propter unum & alterum obijt, sed propter totam ecclesiam.
units.tr: 6. It had to be slain by the whole assembly. For we are all the cause of his death: he did not die for one or another, but for the whole Church.

units.la: 7 Sanguinem agni excipere debuerunt in peluim vel phialâ. Preciosus enim est sanguis Christi, & non calcandus pedibus. ad Hebr.10.cap.
units.tr: 7 They were to catch the blood of the lamb in a basin or a bowl, for the blood of Christ is precious and not to be trampled underfoot. Heb. 10.

units.la: Hoc sanguine postes & superliminare notabant, vt percusis Ægyptijs, se saluos euasisse recordarentur, & sanguine Christi se protegendos scirent. Aspergebantur autem postes fasciculo hyssopi, quæ humilis est herba & contemta: sed vim habet purgandi. Prædicatio Euangelij de Christo crucifixo stulta quoq; vide tur, at per eam aspergi nobis oportet, hoc est, fide recipi sangui nem Christi, qui malos angelos arcet à nobis.
units.tr: With this blood they marked the doorposts and the lintel, so that, after the Egyptians were struck, they would remember that they had escaped and would know that they were protected by the blood of Christ. The doorposts were sprinkled with a bundle of hyssop, a humble and despised herb, yet one with the power to cleanse. The preaching of the gospel about the crucified Christ also seems foolish, but we must be sprinkled with it, that is, receive the blood of Christ by faith, which keeps the evil angels away from us.

units.la: 8 Non satis erat illum mactare, sed assum non elixum edere eum debuerunt. De manducatione carnis Christi, qui noster est agnus. Ioan.6.cap. fusè agitur. Assæ carnes significant ardentem amorem Christi erga genus humanum, & cruciatus quos nostra causa pertulit: item fide veluti igni probata & sancto spiritu feruente comedendū esse. Non crudum edere debuerunt. Crudum edunt, qui eius morte offenduntur, vt Petrus: qui dicunt, an nō alia potuit salutis ratio inueniri quàm supplicū, filij Dei?
units.tr: 8 It was not enough to slay the lamb; they were to eat it roasted, not boiled. The eating of the flesh of Christ, who is our lamb, is treated at length in John 6. The roasted flesh signifies the burning love of Christ toward the human race and the sufferings he endured for our sake; it also signifies that we must eat him by faith, tested as if by fire, and burning with the Holy Spirit. They were not to eat it raw. Those eat it raw who are offended by his death, like Peter, and who say: could no other way of salvation have been found than the punishment of the Son of God?

units.la: 9 Omnes Israelitæ & circumcisi, hunc agnum edebant. Beneficiorum enim Christi participes sunt, qui per fidem circumciduntur in cordibus suis, & ad populum Dei pertinent. Excluduntur ab hoc epulo extranei, hoc est illi qui alieni sunt ab ecclesia, quos pudet Euangelij, & qui illud persequuntur, agni, hoc est, Christi non fiunt participes. Serui emptitij, hoc est servi flagitiorum. Aduenæ, hoc est, qui tantum simulant se ecclesiæ membra esse. Mercenarij, qui quærunt suum commodum: qui ditescere volunt ex Euangelio. Quamdiu tales sunt exclu- duntur.
units.tr: 9 All the Israelites, and the circumcised, ate this lamb. For those who are circumcised in their hearts through faith, and belong to the people of God, are partakers of the benefits of Christ. Outsiders are excluded from this feast, that is, those who are alien to the Church, who are ashamed of the gospel, who persecute it, and so do not become partakers of the lamb, that is, of Christ. Bought servants, that is, slaves of wickedness. Sojourners, that is, those who only pretend to be members of the Church. Hired servants, who seek their own advantage, who want to grow rich from the gospel. As long as they are such, they are excluded.

units.la: 10 In domo vna celebranda erat pascha, neque efferendum aliquid de carne agni. Per hoc vnitas Ecclesiæ fuit significata.
units.tr: 10 The Passover was to be eaten in one house, and nothing of the lamb's flesh was to be carried out of it. By this the unity of the Church was signified.

units.la: 11 Totum agnum edere debebant, caput, pedes, intestina, nihil ex eo relinquere, totus enim Christus noster est: eumq; integra fide amplecti debemus. Caput nō edunt, qui Deū esse non credunt: pedes, qui hominem: intestina, qui non credunt omnia in ipso nobis data esse à patre. Si nimis pauci in domo aliqua essent, vicini vocandi erant ad hoc epulum, quo commendabatur eis mutuus amor.
units.tr: 11 They had to eat the whole lamb, the head, the feet and the entrails, leaving nothing of it, for whole Christ is ours, and we ought to embrace him with a whole faith. They do not eat the head who do not believe that he is God; they do not eat the feet who do not believe that he is man; they do not eat the entrails who do not believe that all things have been given to us in him by the Father. If there were too few people in a house, neighbours were to be invited to this feast, by which mutual love was commended to them.

units.la: 12 Quæ supererant, scilicet non apta in cibum, erant combu- renda, ne colerentur ab ipsis.
units.tr: 12 Whatever was left over, namely the parts not fit for food, was to be burned, so that they would not be worshipped by them.

units.la: 13 Ossa nō frangenda erant: significatur robur Christi nemo te quidem infringi.
units.tr: 13 The bones were not to be broken: this signifies the strength of Christ, which no one can break.

units.la: 14. Edentes instructi erant ad iter: quia illa nocte iter ingressi sunt. Nos quoque locum manentem non habemus: spiritualis Ægyptus deserenda est. Accincti esse debebant. Lucæ ii. Præcincti sitis lumbis vestris.
units.tr: 14. Those eating were to be equipped for the journey, because they were going to set out that night. We too have no lasting place to dwell: spiritual Egypt must be left behind. They were to be girded up. Luke ii.: "Let your loins be girded."

units.la: 15. Baculum habere in manibus suis, calceati qui habitus est iter facientium. Festinanter ederunt: ardentissima enim cupiditate edendus Christus. Præter agnum, alia quoque apposita fuerunt, nempe herbæ amaræ, quæ significant dolorem ex peccatorum recordatione suscepțum, & duram seruitutem, quam pertulerunt in Ægypto, eo was jnen ein Bitter Frut Azymos iusi sunt edere in memoriam liberationis: non enim potuerunt præ festinatione massam fermentare: deinde illi panes sunt insuauiores. Azymi etiam significant sinceritatem, & animi innocentiam. Fermentum expurgarunt ex ædibus, sub pœna capitis. Fermentum notat doctrinam falsam & corruptos mores. 1 ad Corinth. 5. cap. Hæc ceremonia durare debuit ad Christi usque tempora, & liberis interrogantibus, quare hoc facerent, recitanda erat à suis parentibus tota historia. In paschatis agni locum, novû Sacramentum successit, nempe Eucharistia.
units.tr: 15. They were to have a staff in their hands and shoes on their feet, the dress of those who travel. They ate in haste, for Christ is to be eaten with the most ardent desire. Besides the lamb, other things were also set out, namely bitter herbs, which signify the grief taken up from remembering sins, and the harsh bondage they had endured in Egypt, which was a bitter fruit for them. They were ordered to eat unleavened bread in memory of their deliverance; for in their haste they could not leaven the dough, and moreover those loaves are less pleasant. Unleavened bread also signifies sincerity and innocence of mind. They removed leaven from their houses under penalty of death. Leaven signifies false teaching and corrupt morals. 1 Cor. 5. This ceremony was to last until the times of Christ, and when children asked why they did this, the whole history was to be recited by their parents. In place of the paschal lamb, a new sacrament succeeded, namely the Eucharist.

units.la: CAPVT VII. HOMILIA XXIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VII. HOMILY XXIII.

units.la: Quis & qualis fuerit Esdras.
units.tr: Who Ezra was and what kind of man he was.

units.la: Post hæc autem in regno Arthahshasthe regis Persarum (erat) Ezra filius Seraiah, filij Azariah, filij Hilcijah, 2 Filij Sallum, filij Sadoc, filij Ahitub, 3 Filij Amariah, filij Azariah, filij Meraioth, 4 Filij Zeraihiah, filij Vzzi, filij Bucci, 5 Filij Abisua, filij Pinhas, filij Elazar, filij Aaron sacerdotis primi.
units.tr: Now after these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of the Persians, there was Ezra, son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah, 2 son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub, 3 son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth, 4 son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki, 5 son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the first priest.

units.la: 6 Is Ezra ascendit è Babel, & erat scriba velox in Lege Mosis, quam dedit Iehouah Deus Israelis: & dedit ei rex iuxta manu Iehouæ Dei sui super ipsum, omnem petitionem eius.
units.tr: 6 This Ezra went up from Babylon. He was a scribe quick in the Law of Moses, which the LORD God of Israel had given. The king granted him all that he asked, because the hand of the LORD his God was upon him.

units.la: SICVT Iudæi non vno anno, neque sub vno rege in captiuitatem Babylonicam abducti sunt, sed multi primum cum Ioachimo rege, & mox illo ipso anno, cum Iechonia, tandem reliqui cum Zedechia rege: ita etiam non simul vno anno, & sub vno rege ex captiuitate redierunt: sed primum regnante Cyro cum Zerobabele & Iesu summo sacerdote, multi in patriam redierunt, postea elapsis circiter 46. annis regnante Artaxerxe, hoc est, Dario Histaspis, multi sub duce Esdra, qua de re agitur in secunda parte huius libri, quæ hoc loco incipit. Illi ædificarunt templum materiale, hic ædificauit populum, quod opus est præstantius. Vitia enim quæ in hunc populum irrepserant, correxit, præcipue vero matrimonia, &c.
units.tr: Just as the Jews were not led into Babylonian captivity in one year or under one king, but many first went with King Jehoiakim, soon after in the same year with Jeconiah, and at last the rest with King Zedekiah, so they did not return from captivity together in one year or under one king. Rather, first in the reign of Cyrus, many returned to their homeland with Zerubbabel and Jeshua the high priest. Then, about forty-six years later, in the reign of Artaxerxes (that is, Darius son of Hystaspes), many returned under the leadership of Ezra. This is the matter treated in the second part of this book, which begins at this point. Those men built a material temple; this man built up the people, and that work is the more excellent. For he corrected the vices that had crept into this people, above all the marriages, and so on.

units.la: Partes verò 7. huius Capitis, sunt tres. In prima commemoratur, quis fuerit Esdras, quando & cū quibus ascenderit ex Babylone, item quodnam eius fuerit institutum: In altera ponitur diploma Persici regis, vel priuilegium quod Esdras impetrauit: In tertia Esdras gratias agit Deo, quod regis animum flexerit ad tuendos & iuuandos Iudæos.
units.tr: The seven parts of this chapter are three. In the first, it is recounted who Ezra was, when and with whom he went up from Babylon, and also what his office was. In the second, the decree of the Persian king, or the privilege that Ezra obtained, is set out. In the third, Ezra gives thanks to God that He turned the king's heart to protect and help the Jews.

units.la: In tota autem illa narratione multa commemorantur, quæ ad laudes Esdræ faciunt. Audiamus igitur quare & ille & alij amici Dei, seipsos interdum commendent. Cum Solomon in Prouerbijs suis vigesimo septimo capite, & sapientes etiam gentilium vetent, ne quis seipsum vel laudet vel vituperet. Vulgo dicunt, Illos vicinos malos habere, qui seipsos laudant. Si illi hominibus non probantur, qui suas laudes ab adulatoribus libenter audiunt, quanto minus probandi sunt, qui suarum met laudum sunt præcones? Nemo testis esse potest in sua causa. Quisque ita se gerat, vt alij ipsum, non immerito laudibus celebrent.
units.tr: Throughout that whole narrative, many things are recorded that serve to praise Ezra. Let us hear, then, why he and other friends of God sometimes commend themselves. Solomon in Proverbs, chapter 27, forbids anyone to praise or blame himself, and the wise men of the Gentiles also forbid it. People commonly say that those who praise themselves have bad neighbours. If men do not approve of those who gladly hear their own praises from flatterers, how much less should those be approved who are the heralds of their own praises? No one can be a witness in his own cause. Let each person so conduct himself that others rightly celebrate him with praise.

units.la: Alios quoque sanctos homines seipsos laudasse, constat ex sacris literis. Iob. 12. & 31. suas virtutes prædicat. Moses Numeri 12. capite se mitissimum omnium hominum vocat. Samuel in primo libro capite 12, in publicis comitijs magnificè de seipso loquitur, ostendens quando magistratum gesserit, neminem offenderit, potestate sua non sit abusus. D. Paulus in 2. ad Corint. capite tertio & vndecimo, suas laudes, labores & pericula, quæ Christi causa suscepepit, prolixè commemorat. At non ex leuitate quadam & ambitione hoc fecerunt, sed propter Dei gloriam & vtilitatem proximi. Iobum amici accusabant hypocritas & impietatis, recitat igitur, quibus rebus deditus, & à quibus bus alienus fuerit. Mosi omnes aduersantur, suspicari igitur aliquis potuisset, morosum & crudelem fuisse, proinde fe excnfat. Samuel dicit fe recte functum esse suo munere, vt populus fe regem petendo peccasse intelligat, nulla enim in re Samuelem accusare potuerunt : simul nouum quoque regem fui officij obliquè voluit admonere. D.Paulus suas afflictiones,quas Euangelij causa sustinuit, multis prædicat, quia accusabatur ab aduersarijs suis, quòd nihil veræ religionis causa perpessus esset, quibus os obturare voluit. Esdras sua encomia propter seriem historiæ recitat. Nam quia pars magna illarum rerum fuit, quas narrat, necessitas coegit eum de seipso quædam inserere.
units.tr: It is clear from the sacred letters that other holy men too have praised themselves. In Job 12 and 31 he proclaims his own virtues. Moses, in Numbers 12, calls himself the meekest of all men. Samuel, in the first book, chapter 12, speaks magnificently of himself before the public assembly, showing how he discharged his office, that he offended no one, and that he did not abuse his power. St Paul, in 2 Corinthians chapters 3 and 11, fully recounts his praises, labours and dangers which he undertook for Christ's sake. But they did this not out of any levity or ambition, but for the glory of God and the benefit of their neighbour. Job's friends accused him of hypocrisy and impiety, so he recounts the things to which he was devoted and those from which he was free. All men opposed Moses, so someone might have suspected him of being morose and cruel; therefore he excuses himself. Samuel says he has performed his duty rightly, so that the people may understand that they sinned in asking for a king; for they could accuse Samuel in nothing. At the same time he wished to admonish the new king obliquely about his office. St Paul proclaims his many afflictions which he endured for the sake of the gospel, because his adversaries accused him of having suffered nothing for the sake of true religion; he wished to stop their mouths. Ezra recounts his own commendations on account of the sequence of the history. For since he was a large part of those events that he narrates, necessity compelled him to insert some things about himself.

units.la: Neque solum sanctì Dei homines suarum virtutum mentionem faciunt, sed etiam vitiorum. Exemplo nobis sunt Moses, Ionas, Matthæus, Paulus. Vnde discimus vigilandum esse, ne incidamus in scelera: si lapsi fuerimus,non desperandum,neque alios reijciendos,quibus idem accidit.Quod si vere loquendum sit, Spiritus sanctus sacras literas dictauit secundum illud: Matth.10. Vos non estis qui loquimini,sed,&c.His præmissis venimus ad textum.
units.tr: Nor do the holy men of God mention only their virtues but also their vices. Moses, Jonah, Matthew and Paul are examples for us. From this we learn that we must be watchful lest we fall into sins; if we have fallen, we must not despair, nor reject others to whom the same has happened. But if one must speak truly, the Holy Spirit dictated the sacred letters, according to that saying in Matthew 10: "It is not you who speak, but," etc. With these things premised, we come to the text.

units.la: Post hæc verba.)Id est,res gestas,absoluto templo,dedicato, post celebratum festum paschale,&c.ascendit populus.
units.tr: After these words.) That is, the events after the temple was finished and dedicated, after the Passover feast had been celebrated, etc., when the people went up.

units.la: Esdras genealogiam suam contexens,per 17. gradus ad Aaronem vsque primum Pontificem maximum, à Deo in deserto ad hoc munus designatum,refert. Antea primogeniti sacerdotes fuerunt in vnaquaq; familia. 1.Paralip.5. cap. gradus 23. numerâtur.In hoc catalogo sextus est Vzi,7. Zerahia.8.Maraioth, post hunc sex intermissi sunt, nempe Amarias,Achitob,Zadoc, Achimaas, Asarias, Ioannan,forsan ad vitandum fastidium: vt sæpe fit in genealogijs, alibi diligenter conscriptis. Post Vzi sextum ordine, summus Pontificatus translatus est in familiam Ithamari fratris Eleazari, ex qua Heli septimus ordine summus Pontifex fuit.Achitob 8.Abimelech 9.Abiathar 10. Postea Pontificatus redijt in priorem familiam,temporibus Dauidis,& plenius Solomonis, eiecto Abiathare, & Zadoco præfecto, qui 11. est in ordine summorum Pontificum, & etiam in serie prosapiæ Efdræ. Qui post Vzi fuerunt,nempe Zerahia, Maraioth,Amarias,Achitob,non gesserunt summum Pontificatum: sed priuatim vixerunt. Seraiæ quem Nabuchodonosor obtruncauit,filij fuerunt Iofedec, qui ductus est in Babylonem, & Esdras scriba. Iosedeehi filius, etiam summo Pontificatu functus est. Hæc omnia in tabulam retuli, libro 1. Paralipom. vnde qui volunt petere possunt.
units.tr: Ezra, tracing his genealogy through seventeen generations back to Aaron, the first high priest, whom God in the wilderness had designated for this office, sets it out. Previously the firstborn were priests in each family. In 1 Chronicles 5 the count runs to twenty-three generations. In this list Uzzi is the sixth, Zerahiah the seventh, Meraioth the eighth. After this, six are omitted, namely Amariah, Ahitub, Zadok, Ahimaaz, Azariah and Johanan, perhaps to avoid tedium, as often happens in genealogies, which are diligently recorded elsewhere. After Uzzi, in the sixth place in order, the supreme priesthood was transferred to the family of Ithamar, brother of Eleazar, from which Eli was the seventh in order to be high priest. Ahitub was the eighth, Abimelech the ninth, Abiathar the tenth. Afterwards the priesthood returned to the former family in the time of David, and more fully in the time of Solomon, when Abiathar was expelled and Zadok was put in charge, who is the eleventh in the order of high priests, and also in the line of Ezra's descent. Those who came after Uzzi, namely Zerahiah, Meraioth, Amariah and Ahitub, did not hold the supreme priesthood, but lived as private persons. The sons of Seraiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar put to death, were Jehozadak, who was carried into Babylon, and Ezra the scribe. Jehozadak's son, Jeshua, also held the high priesthood. I have set all these things in a table in the first book of Chronicles, so whoever wishes can look there.

units.la: Sacerdotes autem, præcipuè summi Pontifices, in magno precio, non solùm apud Iudæos, sed gentes quoque fuisse constat. Imperatores etiam summi Pontifices esse voluerunt. Leuitici stirpi honoris causa mandata est cura religionis, de qua re alibi. Quod sacerdotes hodieferè contemptui sunt, partim propterea quòd reprehensione scelerum & idololatriæ sibi inuidiam conflant, partim quòd & ipsi scelerate interdum viuunt. Qui suo munere funguntur, & recte viuunt, hodie quoque apud viros pios maximo sunt in precio, vt ministri & legati Dei.
units.tr: It is clear that priests, especially the high priests, were held in great esteem, not only among the Jews but also among the nations. Emperors even wished to be high priests. The care of religion was entrusted to the tribe of Levi for the sake of honour, a matter discussed elsewhere. That priests today are almost held in contempt is partly because by rebuking sins and idolatry they stir up hatred against themselves, and partly because they themselves sometimes live wickedly. Those who discharge their office and live rightly are, even today, held in the highest esteem among godly men, as ministers and ambassadors of God.

units.la: Porrò qui præclaro genere nati sunt, caueant sibi ne illi sint macula. Qui nullos præclaros habuerunt maiores, & obscuris sunt natalibus, operam dent vt suam familiam virtutibus, & rebus præclarè gestis, ornent & illustrem faciant.
units.tr: Moreover, those who were born of an illustrious family should take care lest they be a stain upon it. Those who had no distinguished ancestors and were born in obscurity should work to adorn and make illustrious their family by virtues and noble deeds.

units.la: Vocat se scribam velocem in lege, quam Deus dedit suo populo, in monte Sinai, tonitruis, fulmine & igne, ei terrorem incutiens, vt ad legis reuerentiam eum excitaret. De qua re Exodi 20. capite. Sensus est Esdram optimè fuisse versatum in Lege Dei.
units.tr: He calls himself a quick scribe in the law which God gave to his people on Mount Sinai, striking them with thunder, lightning and fire, so as to arouse in them reverence for the law. Concerning this, see Exodus chapter 20. The sense is that Ezra was thoroughly versed in the Law of God.

units.la: Scribæ erant legisperiti vel legisdoctores. Omnis eorum opera, in Lege rectè intelligenda, populoque explicanda, insumebatur. Qui Matthæi 22. & Lucæ 10. legisperitus dicitur vel doctor, Marci 12. capite appellatur scriba. Scribas dictas volunt, eò quod officium eorum esset describere leges. סופרים sophe-rim dicuntur apud Hebræos à ספר sophar recensendo, nunciando, exponendo, vel à ספר sæpher libro, quasi librarij abeuoluendis, exponendis & custodiendis libris sacris. Scriba velox in lege Domini.) Id est, exercitatissimus, & promptissimus qui in numerato habet sacras legis quæstiones, & illis motis feliciter potest respondere. Psalmo 45. Lingua mea, dicit prophe ta, est veluti stylus scribæ expediti. Referunt Hebræi Esdram literas reperisse nouas, ad scribendum faciliores. Temporibus Christi multi erant scribæ (γραμματεῖς) in populo, qui falsas interpretationes afferebant.
units.tr: The scribes were men learned in the law, or teachers of the law. All their work was spent in rightly understanding the Law and explaining it to the people. The one called a lawyer or teacher in Matthew 22 and Luke 10 is named a scribe in Mark chapter 12. They are said to be called scribes because their office was to write out the laws. Among the Hebrews they are called sophērim [סופרים] from sāphar [ספר], to recount, announce, expound, or from sēpher [ספר], a book, as if to say librarians, who unroll, expound and guard the sacred books. "A quick scribe in the law of the LORD": that is, most practised and ready, who has at hand the questions of the sacred law and can answer well when they are raised. In Psalm 45 the prophet says: "My tongue is like the pen of a ready scribe." The Hebrews report that Ezra invented new letters, easier for writing. In the time of Christ there were many scribes (grammateis [γραμματεῖς]) among the people, who put forward false interpretations.

units.la: Ordo scribarum apud Romanos fuit honestus. Festus hos definit librarios, qui rationes publicas scribunt in tabulis. Aparuerunt singulis magistratibus eo nomine, vt rationes publicas in tabulas referrent, & leges atque omnia perscriberent. Cicero in Verrem scribit, illorum hominum fidei tabulas publicas commissas fuisse, & magistratibus ius suggesisse. Hodie quoq; scribarū ordo honestus est: multumq;.possunt prodesse Reipub.si boni sint. Contemnuntur à multis eò quòd multi ex illis, malis artibus vtuntur ad comparandas opes, & res bonas interdum impediūt,&c. Vide Sigonij libros de antiquo iure Italiæ,in quibus caput extat describis.
units.tr: The order of scribes among the Romans was honourable. Festus defines them as clerks who write up the public accounts in tables. They were appointed to each of the magistrates under that name, to enter the public accounts in the registers and to record laws and all other matters. Cicero, in his speech against Verres, writes that the public records were entrusted to the good faith of these men, and that they gave advice to the magistrates on the law. Today too the order of scribes is honourable, and it can be of great service to the commonwealth if its members are good men. Many despise them because many of them use wicked arts to acquire wealth and sometimes hinder good measures, and so on. See Sigonius's books on the ancient law of Italy, where a chapter on this subject is to be found.

units.la: Addit, in magna gratia apud regem fuisse. Dedit ei omnia, quæ petijt.) Petijt autem præcipuè, vt sibi liceret cum residuis Iudæis patriam repetere. Iuxta manum Dei super ipsum.) Id est, iuxta magnam illam gratiam, vt Vatablus exponit, vel pro magno illo fauore,quo Deus prosequebatur Esdrā. Causa cur gratus fuerit,est fauor Dei. Deinde in eo conspicuæ erant multæ virtutes. Si gratus esse vis hominibus,& imprimis magnis principibus,multum retulerit,vt Deus sit tecum. Is verò tecum erit,si munus tuum sedulò obeas. Si diuersum fiat, hoc est,si nihilominus ingratus fis,Deus in bonum hoc tibi facit. Multi putant quiduis cōcedendo impijs, gratiam eorum comparari, sed res ipsa docet eos ferociores reddi. Etsi agni lupos demulceat, tamen non ponunt suum ingenium.
units.tr: He adds that Ezra was in great favour with the king. He gave him all that he asked. But what he asked for above all was that he might be allowed to lead the remaining Jews back to their homeland. According to the hand of the Lord upon him. That is, according to that great favour, as Vatablus explains it, or because of that great goodwill with which God regarded Ezra. The cause of his being welcomed was the favour of God. Moreover, many virtues were conspicuous in him. If you wish to be pleasing to men, and above all to great princes, it will matter much that God be with you. And he will be with you if you carry out your task diligently. If it turns out otherwise, that is, if you are nevertheless ungrateful, God is doing this to you for your good. Many think that by granting whatever they like to the wicked they win their favour, but the thing itself teaches that they are made fiercer. Even if lambs soothe wolves, the wolves do not put off their nature.

units.la: Quidam hunc Esdram cum Zerobabele volunt Hierosolyma venisse, sed postea iterum reuertisse in Babylonem, vt Iudæos illos, qui remanserant, etiam reduceret, quòd ideo mihi non probabile fit, quia antea eius nomen non fuit expressum.
units.tr: Some hold that this Ezra came to Jerusalem together with Zerubbabel, but afterwards returned again to Babylon in order to lead back also those Jews who had remained there. This seems to me improbable, because his name was not mentioned before.

units.la: Rex ille amat Esdram, qui peregrinus fuit, nimirum propter sapientiam & pietatem: paratus fuit quiduis in eius gratiam facere. Principes coniungant sibi pios homines, quorum consuetudine meliores efficiantur: non magos, mimos, parasytos,tricongios,&c.
units.tr: That king loved Ezra, who was a foreigner, no doubt on account of his wisdom and piety; he was ready to do whatever he could for Ezra's sake. Princes should attach to themselves godly men, by whose company they may become better: not magicians, mimes, parasites, flatterers, and so on.

units.la: Quotsunt hodie inter literatos, qui magnis donis prædītos, vel hoc ipso nomine, oderunt, metuentes ne ipsorum luminibus officiant?
units.tr: How many today among the learned hate those who are endowed with great gifts, or hate them for this very reason, fearing that they may overshadow their own lights?

units.la: HOMILIA XXIIII.
units.tr: HOMILIA XXIIII.

units.la: Cum quibus & quando Esdras ex Babylone Hierosolyma venerit,& quodnam eius institutum fuerit.
units.tr: With whom and when Ezra came from Babylon to Jerusalem, and what his purpose was.

units.la: 7 Ascenderunt autem de filijs Israelis, & de Sacerdotibus & Leuitis, & cantoribus, & ianitoribus, & Nethinæis in Ierusalaim anno septimo Artxerxis regis.
units.tr: 7 And there went up some of the children of Israel, and of the priests, and the Levites, and the singers, and the porters, and the Nethinim, to Jerusalem in the seventh year of king Artaxerxes.

units.la: 8 Et peruenit in Ierusalaim quinto mense, ipse est annus septimus regis.
units.tr: 8 And he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which is the seventh year of the king.

units.la: 9 Nam in prima (die) mensis primi fuit initium ascensus de Babel, & prima (die) mensis quinti venit in Ierusalaim iuxta manum Dei sui bonam super eum.
units.tr: 9 For on the first day of the first month was the beginning of the going up from Babel, and on the first day of the fifth month he came to Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God upon him.

units.la: 10 Ezra enim parauerat cor suum ut requireret legem Iehouæ, ac faceret, & doceret Israelem præceptum & iudicium.
units.tr: 10 For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of Jehovah, and to do it, and to teach Israel statute and judgment.

units.la: IN hoc & sequente Capite, describitur secundus ascensus populi Dei ex Babylone in Hierusalem & Iudæam, duce Esdra.
units.tr: In this and the following chapter is described the second going up of the people of God from Babylon to Jerusalem and Judea, under the leadership of Ezra.

units.la: In prima profectione non omnes Babylonem reliquerunt, nolue runt enim nidos suos deserere, pericula & labores itineris perferre, & denuo magnis sumptibus & laboribus ædes extruere, agros purgare. Post multos igitur annos, Esdra colligit populi reliquos, eisque persuasit, ut in patriam redirent. Quis & qualis Esdras illefuerit dictum est. Sequitur cum quibus & quando ascenderit, & quodnam eius consilium fuerit.
units.tr: In the first departure, not all left Babylon; for they were unwilling to abandon their nests, to endure the dangers and labours of the journey, and to build houses again at great expense and toil, and to clear the fields. So after many years Ezra gathered the remnant of the people and persuaded them to return to their homeland. What sort of man Ezra was has already been said. What follows is with whom and when he went up, and what his purpose was.

units.la: 1. Qui nam cum eo ascenderint, indicatur, aliqui filij Israel, nimirum aliquot ex omnibus tribubus, Sacerdotes, Leuitæ, cantores & Nethinim. Horum alibi quoq; fit mentio. Iosue 9. capite, Hiuæos Iosue & seniores receperunt in fœdus, qui simulabant se ex disitis locis venire, tertio die Israelitæ viderunt se deceptos, cum venirent ad vrbes eorum, Gibea, Ciriathlearim & alias. Populus omnes occidere volebat, & vrbes diripere. Senio res nolebant, ne Deum cotra se prouocarent per cuius nomen iusiurandum fecerant. Illi regerebat, illos mentitos esse: sed tandem placuit senioribus, ut propter interpositam sacramenti religionem, eis parceretur, & quasi ciuiliter mortui essent, hoc est, in nullo precio, ut ligna secaret & gestarent, item aquam; Nethinim autem dicti sunt, de quibus supra.
units.tr: 1. Who went up with him is indicated: some of the children of Israel, namely some from all the tribes, priests, Levites, singers and Nethinim. Mention of these is made elsewhere too. In Joshua chapter 9, the Hivites who pretended to come from distant places were received by Joshua and the elders into a covenant. On the third day the Israelites saw that they had been deceived, when they came to their cities, Gibeon, Kiriath-jearim and others. The people wanted to kill them all and plunder the cities. The elders were unwilling, lest they provoke God against themselves, by whose name they had sworn. The people replied that those men had lied; but at last the elders decided that, on account of the sanctity of the oath they had given, they should be spared, and that they should be as if civilly dead, that is, of no account, to cut wood and carry water. They were called Nethinim, as mentioned above.

units.la: Ex eo autè quòdhoc loco inter reduces, eorum fit mentio, discimus, Deum illorū quoq; rationem habere, qui in nullo nu mero sunt apud homines. Deus enim non respicit personas.
units.tr: From the fact that in this passage mention is made of them among those who returned, we learn that God also takes account of those who are of no number among men. For God does not regard persons.

units.la: 2 Tempus ascensus annotatur. Calendis primi mensis Nisan qui Aprili fere respondet, agitauit Esdras consilium de Babylone deferenda. Calendis quinti mensis Ab, qui Augusto respondet, vedet, venerunt Hierosolyma. An vero primo statim mense iter in gresi sint, non exprimitur. Certe no tantum distat Hierusalem a Babylone, vt homini expedito, quinque vel quatuor mensibus ad hoc iter conficiendum opus sit: sed si quis magnum exercitum ducat, & in illo mulieres, pueros, pecora, illi longa mora opus est.
units.tr: 2. The time of the going up is noted. On the first day of the first month, Nisan, which roughly corresponds to April, Ezra set about the plan of leaving Babylon. On the first day of the fifth month, Ab, which corresponds to August, he came to Jerusalem. Whether they set out in the first month itself is not stated. Certainly Jerusalem is not so far from Babylon that a man travelling light needs four or five months for this journey; but if someone leads a great army, with women, children and cattle, a long delay is needed.

units.la: Fuit hic annus septimus Artaxerxis. Commune fuit hoc nomen omnium regum Persicorum. Quidam igitur volunt hunc ascensum fuisse sub Artaxerxe Dario Hystaspis filio, sub quo & templum perfectum fuit: quidam sub filio ipsius Xerxe: quidam sub Artaxerxe qui μακρόχειρ dicitur, quam sententiam Theodorus Bibliander (qui in Chronologia diligentissime versatus est) reiicit. Hunc enim vt intelligamus, tum alia, tum aetate Ezrę non pati, &c. Proinde vanum esse quod Iulius Africanus tradiderit, quem postea alij secuti sunt, sub eo Ierusalem esse restitutam, quod factum sit sub Dario.
units.tr: This was the seventh year of Artaxerxes. This name was common to all the Persian kings. Some therefore hold that this going up took place under Artaxerxes Darius, son of Hystaspes, under whom the temple was also completed; others under his son Xerxes; others under Artaxerxes who is called Longimanus (Macrocheir). Theodore Bibliander, who was most diligently versed in chronology, rejects this last opinion. For to understand this, both other things and the age of Ezra do not allow it, etc. Therefore, what Julius Africanus handed down, which others afterwards followed, that Jerusalem was restored under this king, is empty, because it was done under Darius.

units.la: Quicquid sit, Darius Hystaspis & Artaxerxes longimanus, optimi principes fuerunt. Esdras igitur natus occasionem, puta fauorem & gratiam regis, ea vtitur. Docens & nos occasione ad res bonas esse vtendū. Sub pijs principibus, potes religionem discere, & alios docere, ea vtitor. Occasiones vero ad res malas, ne arripias. Hac de re alibi saepe diximus.
units.tr: Whatever the case, Darius son of Hystaspes and Artaxerxes Longimanus were excellent princes. Ezra, therefore, made use of the opportunity that arose, namely the favour and grace of the king. This teaches us too that opportunities must be used for good things. Under godly princes you may learn religion and teach others; use these opportunities. But do not seize opportunities for evil things. We have often spoken about this matter elsewhere.

units.la: Deinde exemplum habemus fidei in Esdra, & alijs quoque, qui cum abundarent omnibus bonis in Babylone, se itineri comiserunt. Esdras potuisset splendide apud regem Persicum, a quo amabatur, viuere, sed mauult cum populo Dei pericula subire. Hoc quoq; nomine Moses ad Heb. 11. cap. laudatur: Fide, inquit, Moses cum grandis esset, renuit vocari filius filiae Pharaonis: potius eligens malis affici cum populo Dei, quàm temporales habere mundi delitias: maiores existimás diuitias probrū Christi, quàm Ægypti thesauros. Intuebatur enim in remunerationem. Fide relinquit Ægyptum, nec timuit furorem regis. Quasi enim visibilem vidisset, obduruerat. Nostro quoq; tempore multi in mundo magni esse potuissent, si errores manifestos defendere, aut saltem eos dissimulare voluissent, sed maluerunt esse pauperes, quàm Deum offendere, sua vocatione omissa.
units.tr: Next we have an example of faith in Ezra, and in others also, who, though they abounded in all good things in Babylon, committed themselves to the journey. Ezra could have lived splendidly at the court of the Persian king, by whom he was loved, but he preferred to undergo dangers with the people of God. For this reason Moses too is praised in Hebrews chapter 11: "By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the temporal pleasures of sin, esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt; for he had regard to the recompense of reward. By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king; for he endured as seeing him who is invisible." Many in our own time could have been great in the world, if they had been willing to defend manifest errors, or at least to dissemble them, but they preferred to be poor rather than offend God and abandon their calling.

units.la: Venit in Ierusalem iuxta manum Dei sui bonam super se.) Quod salui & incolumes Hierosolyma peruenerunt, tribuit diuinae misericordiae, qui sua manu eos conseruarit. Iter ingressi Deum precemur, vt nos deducat & reducat. Alij etiam suis precibus, iter facientes Deo commendent, & Dei beneficium agnoscant, si res suas feliciter conficiant.
