Multi also quaeruntur se infelices esse, cum in suis rebus Deum non curent.
units.tr: "He came to Jerusalem according to the good hand of his God upon him." That they arrived safe and sound at Jerusalem he ascribes to the divine mercy, which preserved them by his hand. Having set out on the journey, let us pray to God that he may lead us and bring us back. Others too, while travelling, should commend themselves to God by their prayers and acknowledge God's benefit if they carry out their affairs successfully. Many, however, complain that they are unhappy when they do not care for God in their affairs.

units.la: III. Quod nam institutum Esdrae fuit? Direxit cor suum ad quaerendum legem Domini, & ad faciendum, & ad docendum in Israel mandata & iura. Appositum animum ut inquireret vel peruestigaret, hoc est, discere legem Dei. Illam postea in mandata & iura vel statuta & iudicia distinguit. Comprehendit autem omnes legis partes, moralem, ceremonialem & iudicialem. Alij intelligunt quod inuestigarit, hoc est, legis libros amissos reparavit. Iudaeorum sententiam hac de re supra refutauimus.
units.tr: III. What was Ezra's purpose? "He set his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments." He applied his mind to inquire into and investigate, that is, to learn the law of God. Afterwards he distinguishes it into statutes and judgments, or ordinances and decisions. He comprehends indeed all parts of the law: moral, ceremonial and judicial. Others understand that he investigated, that is, that he restored the lost books of the law. We have already refuted the opinion of the Jews on this matter above.

units.la: 2. Vt faceret eam. Non enim satis est legem Dei scire, sed facere eam debemus, hoc est, quantum in hac corruptione carnis fieri potest, moribus exprimere. Debebat autem Ezdras ceremoniales quoque & iudiciales leges illo tempore seruare, non-dum enim erant abrogatae.
units.tr: 2. "To do it." For it is not enough to know the law of God, but we must do it, that is, express it in our conduct as far as is possible in this corruption of the flesh. Ezra was bound also to observe the ceremonial and judicial laws at that time, for they had not yet been abrogated.

units.la: 3. Vt eam alijs traderet. Continetur his verbis, veri episcopi officium. Primo debet discere legem, id est, verbum & voluntatem Dei, veram doctrinam. D. Paulus in 1. Timoth. 3. vult vt pastor sit διδακτικὸς, hoc est, vt possit commode & methodice docere. Quomodo autem docebit alios scripturarum imperitus? Deinde debet docere alios, sub doctrina comprehendit consolationes, adhortationem, castigationem, &c. Item facere, debent enim specula & exemplum esse commisi sibi gregis, ne eis obijci possit, quod Christus Pharisaeis & scribit obiecit: quod magna onera alijs imponant, quae ipsi ne digito quidem attingunt. Mat. 7. agitur de illis qui faciunt verbum, id est, fide ample ctuntur, & vitam ei accommodant.
units.tr: 3. "To teach it to others." The office of a true bishop is contained in these words. First he must learn the law, that is, the Word and will of God, the true doctrine. St Paul in 1 Timothy 3 wants the minister to be διδακτικὸς [didaktikos], that is, able to teach fittingly and methodically. But how will one who is unskilled in the Scriptures teach others? Next he must teach others; under doctrine he includes consolations, exhortation, rebuke, etc. Likewise he must do the things he teaches, for they ought to be a mirror and example to the flock committed to them, lest it can be objected to them what Christ objected to the Pharisees and scribes: that they laid heavy burdens on others which they themselves would not touch even with a finger. Matthew 7 speaks of those who do the word, that is, who embrace it with faith and accommodate their life to it.

units.la: Si cum his conferamus Episcopos & Praelatos, vt vocantur, nostri seculi: quotusquisque quaesto est, qui velit sacras literas discere? aut eas alios docere? multi incedunt militum more, belluantur, ludunt, scortantur. Si qui sunt ex eis, qui volunt docere, tam ineptè hoc faciunt, vt longè praestaret eos à docendo prorsus abstinere. Non enim Christi meritum vrgent, non vitae puritatem, sed friuolas ceremonias, oppignorantes interdum animas suas, se vera dicere. Etiam qui veri ministri ecclesiarum videri volunt, negligenter suum munus interdum obeunt. Quod si recte doceant, tamen vitae turpitudine omnia destruunt.
units.tr: If we compare with these the bishops and prelates, as they are called, of our age: how few are there who want to learn the sacred letters, or to teach them to others? Many march about like soldiers, revel, play, and fornicate. If there are some among them who want to teach, they do it so clumsily that it would be far better for them to abstain altogether from teaching. For they press not the merit of Christ, nor the purity of life, but frivolous ceremonies, sometimes pledging their souls that they speak the truth. Even those who wish to be seen as the true ministers of the churches sometimes carry out their office negligently. And even if they teach correctly, they destroy everything by the foulness of their lives.

units.la: Quamuis autem ministri ecclesiarum, peculiariter ad hoc vocati sunt, vt literas sacras discant, alijs interpretentur, & sanctè viuant: tamen ab omnibus etiā Christianis postulatur (sunt enim {c}nim reges & sacerdotes) vt legem Dei intelligant, secundum am viuant, eamq; suo modo doceant, Deumq; celebrent.
units.tr: Although ministers of the churches are called specially for this, that they should learn the sacred letters, interpret them to others, and live holily, yet it is required of all Christians also (for they are kings and priests) that they understand the law of God, live according to it, teach it in their own way, and praise God.

units.la: HOMILIA XXV.
units.tr: HOMILIA XXV.

units.la: Diploma regis Artaxerxis inseritur.
units.tr: The king's decree is inserted.

units.la: 11 Iflud autem est exemplar epistolæ quam tra didit rex Arthasasthe Ezræ Sacerdoti, scribæ (inquâ) verborum præceptorum Iehouæ, & statutorum eius su per Israelem.
units.tr: 11 This is a copy of the letter which King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe (I say) of the words of the commandments of Jehovah and his statutes over Israel.

units.la: 12 Arthasasthe rex regum Ezræ Sacerdoti, scribæ legis Dei cœli consummato, & ipsi Cheeneih.
units.tr: 12 Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of the God of heaven, perfect, and so forth (Cheeneih).

units.la: 13 Ame positum est decretum quod quicunq; spô taneus est in regno meo de populo Israelis, & sacerdo tibus, & leuitis, vt eat in Ierusalaim tecum, vadat.
units.tr: 13 I have issued a decree that whoever in my kingdom is willing, from the people of Israel, and from the priests and Levites, may go with you to Jerusalem.

units.la: 14 Quemadmodum à conspestu regis, & septem consiliariorum eius missus es, vt inquiras in Iebudæam & Ierusalaim propter legem Dei tui, quæ est in manu tua.
units.tr: 14 Since you are sent from the presence of the king and his seven counsellors, to inquire into Judea and Jerusalem concerning the law of your God, which is in your hand.

units.la: 15 Et vt deferas argentum & aurum quod rex & consiliarij eius sponte obtulerunt Deo Israelis, cuius tabernaculum (est) in Ierusalaim.
units.tr: 15 And to carry the silver and gold which the king and his counsellors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose tabernacle is in Jerusalem.

units.la: 16 Et omne argentum & aurum quod inueneris in tota prouincia Babel, cum spontaneis populi, & sacerdotibus qui sponte obtulerint domui Dei sui quæ est in Ierusalaim.
units.tr: 16 And all the silver and gold that you find in the whole province of Babylon, together with the freewill offerings of the people and of the priests, who have given willingly to the house of their God which is in Jerusalem.

units.la: 17 Vt celeriter emas argento hoc vitulos, arietes, agnos, & minham eorum, & libamina eorum, & oferas ea super altare domus Dei vestri quæ est in Ierusalaim: (ita facito).
units.tr: 17 That you may quickly buy with this silver bullocks, rams, lambs, with their meal offerings and drink offerings, and offer them upon the altar of the house of your God which is in Jerusalem (so do).

units.la: 18 Quod autem tibi & fratribus tuis placuerit de reliquo argento & auro facere, secundum voluntatem Dei vestri facite.
units.tr: 18 As for whatever seems good to you and your brothers to do with the rest of the silver and gold, do it according to the will of your God.

units.la: 19 Porrò vasa quæ tradita sunt tibi in ministerium domus Dei tui, redde coram Deo in Ierusalaim.
units.tr: 19 Moreover, the vessels delivered to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver before God in Jerusalem.

units.la: 20 Et catera quæ fuerint necessaria pro domo Dei tui, quæ connenerit te dare, dabis è domo thesaurorum regis.
units.tr: 20 And whatever else is needed for the house of your God, which it falls to you to provide, you shall give from the king's treasury.

units.la: 21 Et à me Arthasasthe positum est decretum omnibus thesaurarijs quisunt trans Flumen, ut omnia quæ petierit à vobis Ezra sacerdos, & scriba legis Dei, cito fiat.
units.tr: 21 And I, Artaxerxes, have issued a decree to all the treasurers who are beyond the River, that whatever Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of God, asks of you, be done quickly.

units.la: 22 Vsque ad argenti talenta centum, & vsque ad tritici, coros centum, & vsque ad vini batos centum, & vsque ad batos olei centum, & sal quod non scriptum est.
units.tr: 22 Up to a hundred talents of silver, and up to a hundred cors of wheat, and up to a hundred baths of wine, and up to a hundred baths of oil, and salt without stated measure.

units.la: 23 Quicquid fuerit ex decreto Dei cæli, fiat fest-inanter domui Dei cæli, cuius ut quid futura est ira contra regnum regis & filiorum eius?
units.tr: 23 Whatever is commanded by the decree of the God of heaven, let it be done diligently for the house of the God of heaven; for why should there be wrath against the kingdom of the king and his sons?

units.la: ALtera pars huius capitis, complectitur diploma regis Artaxerxis (siue Darius Hystaspis, siue eius filius Xerxes, siue, ut quidam volunt, Artaxerxes μακρόχειρ nepos eius, fuerit) quod Esdras Ierusalem profecturus ab eo impetrauit.
units.tr: The second part of this chapter contains the decree of King Artaxerxes (whether this was Darius Hystaspis, or his son Xerxes, or, as some wish, Artaxerxes Longimanus, his grandson), which Ezra obtained from him when about to set out for Jerusalem.

units.la: Quatuor autem potissimum hoc diploma continet. Primum quod rex omnibus qui vellent, reditum in patriam cum Esdra concesserit. Alterum est de bonis ecclesiasticis, quæ illis rex principes & populus dederunt. Tertium est de immunitate sacerdotum & leuitarum. Quartum quod rex Esdræ potestatem facit, ordinandi Rempublicam, & simul iudicibus præscribit suum officium. Duo priora capita iam explicabimus, si prius ritu lum vel summam huius decreti, & salutationem, quæ præfigitur, audiuerimus.
units.tr: This decree contains chiefly four things. First, that the king granted to all who wished to return to their homeland with Ezra. Second, concerning the church property, which the king, the princes and the people gave to them. Third, concerning the immunity of the priests and Levites. Fourth, that the king gives Ezra authority to set in order the commonwealth, and at the same time prescribes to the judges their duty. We shall now explain the first two points, if first we have heard the summary of this decree and the greeting which precedes it.

units.la: Primo loco dicitur, hoc exemplar esse vel apographum, vulgò copiam vocant, epistolæ vel decreti aut priuilegij, quod rex Esdræ sacerdoti & scribæ verborum domini præceptorum & institutorum (omnes partes legis comprehendit) concesserit.
units.tr: In the first place it is said that this is a copy, or transcript (commonly called a copy), of a letter or decree or privilege which the king granted to Ezra the priest and scribe of the words of the Lord's commandments and ordinances (it comprises all parts of the law).

units.la: Deinde rex Artaxerxes, Esdræ salutem imprecatur. Alij legunt scribæ consummato & absoluto. Se regem regum, id est, regem maximum nominat: multis enim regibus imperauit. Monarcha fuit. In libro Esther Assuerus (quidam hunc ipsum volunt fuisse) 127 prouincias sub se habuit. Simplicitatem & modestiam in titulis vides. Nostro tempore totas paginas implent principrincipes suis titulis. Esdrae quoq; plus semel honorificum dat titulum, vocans eum sacerdotem & scribam in lege Dei caeli.
units.tr: Then King Artaxerxes sends greetings to Ezra. Others read "scribe, perfected and complete." He names himself king of kings, that is, the greatest king, for he ruled over many kings. He was a monarch. In the book of Esther, Ahasuerus (some think this is the same man) had 127 provinces under him. You see simplicity and modesty in his titles. In our time princes fill whole pages with their titles. He also gives Ezra an honourable title more than once, calling him priest and scribe in the law of the God of heaven.

units.la: Ex quo colligimus, honorandos esse viros primarios, tam ec clesiasti cos quàm politicos. Paulus hoc à nobis exigit ad Romanos 12.13. item in 1. ad Timoth. 5. Presbyteri duplici honore digni sunt. 1. Pet. 2. cap. Omnes honorate, fraternitatem diligite, Deum timete, regem honorate, &c. Deus in Leuitico per Mosem dicit: coram cano capite assurge, &c. Sunt qui ministros ecclesiae vel hoc nomine appernentur, quòd Dei serui sunt.
units.tr: From this we gather that leading men are to be honoured, both ecclesiastical and civil. Paul requires this of us, Rom. 12.13, and likewise in 1 Tim. 5: "Elders who rule well are worthy of double honour" (1 Tim. 5.17). 1 Pet. 2: "Honour all men, love the brotherhood, fear God, honour the king." God says in Leviticus through Moses: "Rise up before the hoary head," etc. There are some who take the name of ministers of the Church for this reason too, that they are servants of God.

units.la: Deo etiam honorificum titulum tribuit. Non simpliciter Deum nominat, sed Deum caeli, quod postea aliquoties repetit. Item Deum Israelis, cuius habitatio sit Hierosolymis. Commonefaciens nos, ut reuerenter de Deo loquamur. Horrendum est quod multi nomen Domini non tantum vanè, sed etiam contumeliose vsurpant.
units.tr: He also gives an honourable title to God. He does not simply name God, but "the God of heaven," which he repeats several times afterwards; likewise "the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem." He reminds us that we ought to speak of God reverently. It is dreadful that many use the name of the Lord not only in vain but even reproachfully.

units.la: Iam sequitur prima pars huius narrationis vel expositionis, quòd Artaxerxes rex, exemplo Cyri concesserit omnibus Iudeis qui voluntarij erant (neminem enim voluit cogere) ut cum Esdra in patriam redirent. Additur, Esdram missum esse ab ipso, & à septem consiliarijs, ut visitet: vel, ut inquirat in Iudaeam &Ierusalem, in veluxta legem Dei, quae in manu eius sit, id est, ut in statuat eos in lege, & omnia ad illam reuocet. Coneeffa est eis libertas certa conditione, ut sequantur praescriptum legis. Non est libertas, sed diabolica potius seruitus, si quis facit quicquid ei suadent praui affectus.
units.tr: Now follows the first part of this narrative or exposition: that King Artaxerxes, following the example of Cyrus, granted to all Jews who were willing (for he did not wish to compel anyone) that they should return to their homeland with Ezra. It is added that Ezra was sent by him and by the seven counsellors to visit, or to inquire into, Judea and Jerusalem, according to the law of God which is in his hand, that is, that he should establish them in the law and bring everything back to it. Liberty is granted to them on a certain condition, that they follow what the law prescribes. It is not liberty, but rather a diabolical slavery, when someone does whatever his wicked desires urge him to do.

units.la: Persae septem principes habebant à consiliis, quorum in libro Esther etiam fit mentio. Sic Germania habet senatum septem electorum.
units.tr: The Persians had seven princes as counsellors, and mention of them is also made in the book of Esther. Thus Germany has a senate of seven electors.

units.la: Optima haec est forma visitationis, ut omnia secundum verbum Dei fiant.
units.tr: This is the best form of visitation: that everything be done according to the word of God.

units.la: Secundo loco ostenditur quod rex cos non vacuis manibus sed muneribus amplissimis donatos, à fe dimiserit. Attinguntur circumstantiae, quis, quid dederit, quantum, cui, quomodo & in quem finem. Nos verborum ordinem sequemur.
units.tr: Second, it is shown that the king dismissed them from his presence not empty-handed but furnished with very ample gifts. The circumstances are touched upon: who gave, what, how much, to whom, how, and to what end. We shall follow the order of the words.

units.la: 1 Rex iubet Esdram secum exportare aurum & argentum, ab ipso & consiliarijs suis sponte Deo Israelis datum. Deinde omne aurum & argentum, quod in Babylone Esdras collegerat quodq; populus, nimirū Babylonicus, Persicus & Iudaeus, qui in Babylone remanserat, item sacerdotes sponte sua ad templum Hierosolymitanum contulerant. De his donarijs inferius capite octauo agitur. Pauci sunt principes, qui opibus suorum subiectorum non inhient, tantum abest, vt abituris multa largiantur.
units.tr: 1 The king orders Ezra to take with him the gold and silver given freely to the God of Israel by himself and his counsellors. Then all the gold and silver which Ezra had collected in Babylon, and which the people (namely the Babylonians, Persians and Jews who had remained in Babylon) and likewise the priests had of their own accord contributed to the temple at Jerusalem. These gifts are treated below in chapter eight. There are few princes who do not covet the wealth of their subjects; so far is it from them to lavish much on those who are leaving.

units.la: 2 Iubet Esdram illam pecuniam accipere, & pro illa singulari cura & studio statim emere quae ad sacrificiorum apparatu spectabant: opes illas non in alios vsus, saltem ad tempus, conferre debuit, ied emere pecudes, oblationes & libationes, vt offerrentur non in excelsis, sed in altari templi Dei Israelis. Incredibiles sumptus ad sacrificiorum ministerium requiruntur.
units.tr: 2 He orders Ezra to receive that money and, with singular care and zeal, to buy at once what pertains to the equipment of the sacrifices. He ought not to put those resources to other uses, at least for the time being, but to buy cattle, oblations and libations, so that they might be offered not on the high places but on the altar of the temple of the God of Israel. Incredible expense is required for the ministry of sacrifices.

units.la: 3 De pecuniis abundantibus post peracta sacrificia, permittit vt quicquid Esdras & fratres eius Iudaei, faciendum statuant, id fiat: non pro ipsorum libidine, sed secundum voluntatem Dei ipsorum, sicut ipse praecepit. Haec est regula recte dispensandi bona ecclesiastica.
units.tr: 3 Concerning the surplus money after the sacrifices are completed, he permits that whatever Ezra and his Jewish brothers decide to do, let it be done: not according to their own lust, but according to the will of their God, as he himself has commanded. This is the rule for rightly dispensing ecclesiastical goods.

units.la: 4 Iubet rex, vt Esdras vasa quae fidei eius concredita erant, & ad ministerium templi cedebant, reddat coram Deo in Ierusalem, scilicet rerum sacrarum custodibus. Coram Deo dicit, cogi tet igitur quisquis, se coram Deo stare, & ipsi quoq; rationem esse reddendam.
units.tr: 4 The king orders that Ezra restore before God in Jerusalem the vessels which were entrusted to his faith and belonged to the service of the temple, that is, to the keepers of the sacred things. He says "before God," so let whoever considers that he stands before God also consider that he must render an account.

units.la: 5 Addit se mandasse suis thesaurarijs vel quaestoribus trans Euphratem, vt quicquid Esdras ab ipsis postulauerit, id omne sine recusatione faciant. Definitur autem certus modus, intra quem se Esdras contineat, ne studio nimio maiora petat. Iubet dari illis ad centum talenta argenti. Talentum varium fuisse, ab illis fuse exponitur, qui de ponderibus & mensuris scripserunt. Ad centum Choros tritici, & centum batos olei, & salem, non ad mensuram, sed quantum Esdras petat. Corus est mensura aridorum, capit medimnos Atticos 41. teste Iosepho Antiquitatum libro decimoquinto, capite duodecimo. Batus mensura est liquidorum, capit sextarios, si Iosepho creditur 72. Harum mensurarum fit etiam in Euangelio mentio Lucae decimo sexto, vbi iniquus dispensator conuocatis singulis debitoribus domini sui, interrogauit primum, quantum debes domino meo? is respondit centum batos olei: tum ille dixit ei, accipe tabulas, dein scribe 50. Deinde illum qui centum coros tritici debebat, iussit 80. scribere. Difficile est has mensuras ad nostras redigere, sed multum fuit quod rex concesit. Corus enim est amplissima aridorum mensura apud Hebraeos. Germanus interpres batos olei tonen conuertit. Potest etiam reddi centner, quia oleum ponderatur, Coros frumenti malter forn. Salem fine mensura illis dare debuerunt : nemo enim immodicè illo vtitur.
units.tr: 5 He adds that he has instructed his treasurers or quaestors beyond the Euphrates that whatever Ezra asks of them, they should do without refusal. A certain fixed measure is defined within which Ezra is to keep himself, lest by excessive zeal he ask for more. He orders that up to a hundred talents of silver be given to them. That the talent varied is explained at length by those who wrote on weights and measures. Up to a hundred cors of wheat, and a hundred baths of oil, and salt, not by measure but as much as Ezra asks. The cor is a measure of dry goods, holding 41 Attic medimni, according to Josephus, Antiquities, book fifteen, chapter twelve. The bath is a measure of liquids, holding 72 sextarii, if Josephus is to be believed. Mention of these measures is also made in the Gospel of Luke, chapter sixteen, where the unjust steward, having summoned each of his lord's debtors, asked the first, "How much do you owe my lord?" He answered, "A hundred baths of oil." Then he said to him, "Take your bill and write fifty." Then he ordered the one who owed a hundred cors of wheat to write eighty. It is difficult to reduce these measures to ours, but what the king granted was a great deal. For the cor is a very ample measure of dry goods among the Hebrews. The German translator renders "baths of oil" as "Tonnen." It can also be rendered "Centner," since oil is weighed, and "cors of wheat" as "Malter." They ought to have given salt without measure, for no one uses it immoderately.

units.la: 6 Rex mandat vt omnia quæ ad Dei legem pertinent,accuratè & festinanter in templo eius administrentur, ne ira veniat contra regis regnum & filios eius. Quàm infeliciter cecidit Achani,quod Deo consecrata surripuit, ex libro Iosue notum est. Balthasar qui sacris vasis in prophano conuiuio abusus fuit, statim audit regnum suum diuidendum. Ananias & Saphyra subita morte perierunt, propter sacrilegium suum. Filijs malè consulunt,qui auro illo Tholosano eos locupletare volunt,vltionem enim diuinam contra se prouocant.
units.tr: 6 The king orders that everything that pertains to God's law be administered accurately and diligently in his temple, lest wrath come upon the king's realm and his sons. How unhappily Achan fell, because he stole what was consecrated to God, is known from the book of Joshua. Belshazzar, who abused the sacred vessels at a profane banquet, immediately hears that his kingdom is to be divided. Ananias and Sapphira perished by sudden death on account of their sacrilege. They ill serve their sons who want to enrich them with that Tolosan gold, for they provoke divine vengeance against themselves.

units.la: Vsus.
units.tr: Use.

units.la: 1 In hac narrationis parte,primùm exemplum magnę clemen-tiæ in hoc rege nobis proponitur.Nam Iudæis propter diuersam religionem non est molestus.Amat Esdram,redire cupientibus in suam patriam, dat potestatem. Nostro tempore tanta est sæuitia multorum principum, qui Christiani videri volunt, vt cum Iudæos,qui desierunt Dei populus esse,foueant,euangelium tamen amplexis,qui vni Christo suam salutem acceptam referunt, nullum cedant locum.
units.tr: 1 In this part of the narrative, first, an example of great clemency in this king is set before us. For he is not troublesome to the Jews on account of their different religion. He loves Ezra and gives permission to those who wish to return to their homeland. In our own time there is such savagery among many princes, who wish to seem Christian, that while they cherish the Jews, who have ceased to be God's people, they show no mercy at all to those who have embraced the gospel and ascribe their salvation to Christ alone.

units.la: 2 Deinde regiæ munificentiæ insigne exemplum hoc loco habemus, sicut supra in Cyro, & in eodem, vt quidam volunt, Dario priuati quoque multa contribuerunt. Carolus Magnus & alij principes Christiani,multas ecclesias fiue basilicas extruxerunt,sacris vasis & vestibus eas ornarunt. Et quanquam multis persuasum fuerit, quòd hac ratione peccata sua expiarent,tamen multi contulerunt opes ad conseruationem ministerij, ædificiorum,scholarum,& etiam pauperum. Multis quidem in locis,fatis prospectum est ecclesijs,non igitur postulatur à prin-cipibus,vt sua liberalitate illas iuuent : sed vt quæ ab aliis data sunt,non in prophanos vsus conferant:non indignentur, si necessaria ministri petant,procurationem illorum bonorum committant viris bonis & pijs.
units.tr: 2 Next, we have here a notable example of royal generosity, as above in Cyrus, and in the same Darius, as some hold; private persons also contributed much. Charlemagne and other Christian princes built many churches or basilicas and adorned them with sacred vessels and vestments. And although many were persuaded that by this means they would expiate their sins, nevertheless many contributed wealth for the support of the ministry, of buildings, of schools, and also of the poor. Indeed in many places provision has been made for the churches, so it is not demanded of princes that they help them by their liberality; rather, that what has been given by others should not be turned to profane uses, and that they should not be indignant if the ministers ask for what is necessary, but should entrust the administration of those goods to good and pious men.

units.la: Quod priuatos attinet,vbi non est necessarium vt ad conseruationem ministerij aliquid conferatur, liberalitatem suam exercere debent erga pauperes,qui sunt viuum templum Dei viua eius simulachra. Semper habebunt quod conferant, vestes,esculenta,poculenta,&c.Idq; cito & sponte faciendum est, ne offensam Dei incurramus.
units.tr: As for private persons, where it is not necessary that anything be contributed for the support of the ministry, they ought to exercise their liberality towards the poor, who are the living temple of God and his living images. They will always have something to give: clothing, food, drink, and so on. And this must be done promptly and willingly, lest we incur the offence of God.

units.la: Nemo est qui sacris opibus magis abutatur, quàm ipsi Papistæ, nam suum luxum & fastum ex illis alunt, idololatriam propagant, bella aliis inferunt, verum Dei cultum impediunt.
units.tr: There is no one who abuses sacred wealth more than the Papists themselves; for they feed their luxury and pride from it, they propagate idolatry, they wage wars on others, and they hinder the true worship of God.

units.la: Pia illa solicitudo regis Persici, vt Deo secundum legem suam seruiant, recteque omnia curet, excitare nos debet ad diligentiam, qua quisque in sua vocatione vti debet, præcipuè autem in exercendo Dei cultu, ne Dei offensam incurramus. Non mirum si hodie multæ Respublicæ, multæ familiæ, infelices sint, cum multis gloria Dei curæ non sit, neque persoluant sacra vectigalia vt debebant, neque recte illis vtantur, aut alios abstentes coerceant cum possent ac deberent.
units.tr: That devout solicitude of the Persian king, that they should serve God according to his law and that everything be rightly ordered, ought to stir us to the diligence with which each person should act in his own calling, and especially in exercising the worship of God, lest we incur God's offence. It is no wonder if today many commonwealths and many families are unhappy, since with many the glory of God is no concern, and they neither pay the sacred taxes as they ought, nor use them rightly, nor restrain others who stand aloof, though they could and should.

units.la: HOMILIA XXVI.
units.tr: HOMILIA XXVI.

units.la: De immunitate ministrorum Dei, ordinatione Reipublicæ & pœnis: item de gratiarumactione Esdræ.
units.tr: Concerning the immunity of God's ministers, the ordering of the commonwealth and its punishments; also concerning Ezra's thanksgiving.

units.la: 24. Vobis autem notum facimus, quod omnibus Sacerdotibus, & Leuitis cantoribus, ianitoribus, Nethinæis, & ministris domus Dei huius, tributum, vectigal, & reditum annuum præfectus nullus imponet.
units.tr: 24. And we make known to you that no governor shall impose any tribute, tax, or annual revenue upon the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, the Nethinim, or the ministers of this house of God.

units.la: 25. Tu autem Ezra secundum sapientiam legis Dei tui, quæ (est) in manu tua, constitue iudices, & causidicos, qui iudicent vniuersum populum, qui est trans flumen, omnes qui norunt leges Dei tui: & eum qui non nouerit, docebitis.
units.tr: 25. And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of the law of your God, which is in your hand, appoint judges and advocates who may judge all the people beyond the river, all who know the laws of your God; and whoever does not know them, you shall teach.

units.la: 26 Omnem autem qui non fecerit legem Dei tui, & legem regis, celeriter iudicium fiat de eo siue ad mortem, siue ad eradicationem eius, siue ad condemnationem substantiæ, & ad vinciendum.
units.tr: 26. Let judgment be swiftly executed on everyone who does not keep the law of your God and the law of the king, whether by death, or by banishment, or by confiscation of goods, or by imprisonment.

units.la: 27 Benedictus Iehouah Deus patrum nostrorum, qui dedit tale quidpiam in corde regis, vt glorificaret domum Iehouæ quæ (est) in Ierusalaim.
units.tr: 27. Blessed be Jehovah, the God of our fathers, who put such a purpose into the heart of the king, to glorify the house of Jehovah which is in Jerusalem.

units.la: 28 Et super me inclinauit misericordiam coram rege, & consiliarijs eius, & omnibus principibus regis potentibus: & ego confortatus manu Dei mei super me, congregaui de Israele principes, vt ascenderent mecum.
units.tr: 28. And he extended mercy to me before the king, his counsellors, and all the king's mighty princes. And I, strengthened by the hand of my God upon me, gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me.

units.la: HOMILIA XXVI.
units.tr: HOMILY XXVI.

units.la: EX decreti siue epistolæ regis, quam Esdræ sacerdoti in patriam proficiscenti dedit, quatuor præcipuis capitibus duo iam ante exposuimus: sequitur tertiū quòd sacrorum minorum fros donauit immunitate à tributis, vectigalibus & annuis reditibus.
units.tr: We have already explained two of the four main points of the decree, or letter, which the king gave to Ezra the priest as he set out for his homeland. The third point follows: the king granted the lesser sacred officials immunity from tributes, customs duties and annual dues.

units.la: Tributa, vectigalia, & alij reditus, iure penduntur principibus. Magnos enim sumptus eos facere oportet. Christus ipse tributum imperatori Rom. persoluit. Paulus dicit: Reddite omnibus quod debetur, cui tributum: tributum: cui vectigal, vectigal, &c. Possunt aut principes, quibus volut, propter merita, vel alijs de causis, illa remittere. Rex Persicus suis præfectis mandauit, vt ipsi tributa & alia à populo exigerent, ministri domus Dei cuiusque ordinis, immunes effent, nempe sacerdotes, Leuitæ, cantores, ianitores, Nethinæi & alij. Sicut ecclesiæ maiores suas habuerunt classes, quidam fuerunt sacerdotes, quidam diaconi, quidam acoluthi. By den stiffelichen ist die abteilung gsin / etliche sind priester/die anderen Euangelier / die dritten Epistler genennt worden: Ita in veteri testamento, ministri tempori fuerunt in suos ordines distributi.
units.tr: Tributes, customs duties and other dues are rightly paid to rulers, for they must bear great expenses. Christ himself paid tribute to the Roman emperor. Paul says: "Render to all what is owed: tribute to whom tribute is due, customs to whom customs are due," and so on. Rulers may, for merit or other reasons, remit these dues as they wish. The Persian king ordered his governors to collect taxes and other levies from the people, but to exempt the ministers of God's house, of every rank: the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, the Nethinim and others. Just as the Church has had its greater and lesser orders, some priests, some deacons, some acolytes, (by the old custom the division was of this kind: some were called priests, others evangelists, and the third kind epistlers), so in the Old Testament the ministers of the temple were distributed into their own orders.

units.la: Tributa sunt quæ ex agris & prædijs: vectigalia quæ ex mercibus, & ex ijs rebus quæ importantur & exportantur, soluimus. Ideo autem hæc onera rex illis remisit, vt legi diuinæ suoq; ministerio diligentius incumberent. Cæterum illi nihilominus regibus & satrapis eorum, subiecti erant, bonisq; legibus parebant.
units.tr: Tributes are what we pay on fields and estates; customs duties are what we pay on goods and on things imported and exported. The king remitted these burdens to them so that they might devote themselves more diligently to the divine law and their ministry. Nevertheless they remained subject to the kings and their satraps, and obeyed good laws.

units.la: Aliarum quoq; gentium sacerdotes, immunes fuerunt à publicis oneribus. Apud Ægyptios, Gen.47. apud Athenienses, Diodorus Siculus lib.2. Apud Gallos Druides, Cæsar lib.6. de bello Gallico. Romani quoq; veteres teste Appiano lib.4. multa hac in refuis sacerdotibus concesserunt. Christiani imperatores hos imitati, voluerunt vt ecclesiarum ministri, à personalibus, vt vocat, muneribus liberi essent, ne à suo ministerio abducerentur, & distraherentur. Tametsi vero nobis liberalitate & priuilegijs principum frui liceat: debemus tamen ad conseruandā charitate, in terdu de nostro iure aliquid remittere, neq; illo striste vti, etc.
units.tr: The priests of other nations too were exempt from public burdens: among the Egyptians (Gen. 47), among the Athenians (Diodorus Siculus, book 2), and among the Gauls the Druids (Caesar, book 6 of the Gallic War). The ancient Romans too, according to Appian, book 4, granted many such privileges to their priests. Christian emperors, imitating them, wished that the ministers of the churches be free from so-called personal duties, so that they would not be drawn away and distracted from their ministry. Although we may enjoy the generosity and privileges of princes, we ought nevertheless, for the sake of preserving charity, at times to remit something of our right and not to use it too strictly.

units.la: Progressu temporis pontifices, episcopi, sacerdotes & monachi non solū ab exactionibus, & omnibus alijs publicis oneribus, liberi esse voluerunt, sed se ab omni magistratuum iurisdictione & obedientia exemerunt, ac iugo prorsus excusso, sceleratum impunitatem captarunt, suumque regnum stabiliuerunt: Magistratus enim non potestatem habuerunt, vt eis quicquam præciperent, vetaret, imponerent, aut etiā eos punirent. Causæ enim ad episcopos referebantur.Hoc vero pugnat cum verbo Dei.Nam D.Paulus ad Romanos 13.Omnis ,inquit, anima potestatibus supereminentibus subdita sit, hoc est, omnis homo pareat magistratibus , qui reliquos homines excellunt. Chrysostomus hunc locum exponens,dicit, siue sit Propheta, siue Euangelista.
units.tr: As time went on, the pontiffs, bishops, priests and monks wished to be free not only from levies and all other public burdens, but they also exempted themselves from all jurisdiction and obedience to the magistrates. Having thrown off the yoke altogether, they sought out wicked impunity and established their own kingdom. For the magistrates had no power to command them, forbid them, impose anything on them, or even punish them; causes were referred to the bishops. But this conflicts with the word of God. For the apostle Paul, in Romans 13, says: "Let every soul be subject to the higher powers," that is, let every man obey the magistrates who excel the rest of men. Chrysostom, expounding this passage, says: whether it be a prophet or an evangelist.

units.la: Quanta audacia Romani pontifices contra legitimum magistratum insurrexerint,eumq; contemserint secundum vaticinium D.Petri 2.capite 2.locupletissimè testantur historiæ. Olim Romani imperatores eligebant & confirmabant episcopos Romanos,eosq; iureiurando adstringebant. Postea res mutata est.Pontifices enim nullum agnoscunt imperatorem, qui ab ipsis coronam acceperit.Ipsi depositis imperatoribus, alios in eorum locum substituunt.
units.tr: How great the audacity with which the Roman pontiffs rose up against the lawful magistrate and despised him, according to the prophecy of St Peter in 2 Peter 2, the histories bear abundant witness. Once the Roman emperors elected and confirmed the Roman bishops, and bound them by oath. Later the situation changed. For the pontiffs acknowledge no emperor who has received the crown from them. They depose emperors and put others in their place.

units.la: Neque solum principum præpostera liberalitate,magnam licentiam consequuti sunt , qui serpentes in sinu suo nutrierunt, sed ipsi fere eam sibi illis inutis vendicarunt. In Concilio Lateranensi quod anno Domini 1215. sub Innocentio Papa III. celebratum est, interalia decretum fuisse legitur: Neconstitutiones principum Ecclesijs præiudicent : vt ab omni cotributione ecclesiastici sint immunes:ne tributa soluantur ante decimas. Constituerunt etiam in hoc Concilio, vt omnes qui à spiritualibus pro hæreticis habeantur & condemnentur,per seculares magistratu puniantur quoad facultates & vitam.Iтe,vt omnes seculares potestates,publicè iuret,quod de terris suæ iurisdictionis subiectis,omnes hæreticos bona fide exterminare velint,& nemini parcere. Qui hoc facere negle xerint, excommunicandos esse,& omnes subditos ipsorum,à iureiurando illis præstito,à Papa absoluendos. Alios vero Catholicos,excomunicatis bellum inferre debere,terram eorum occupare & possidere,sine vlla contradictione extirpatis hæreticis,&c.Excomunicatos vero & hæreticos,omnes illos esse scribitur lib.5.de hæreticis, Titulo 7.ad abolendâ, in Decretalibus Gregorij 9. quotquot non per omnia de sacramentis sentiant cum ecclesiaRomana:vel quotquot à Romana ecclesia,aut eius Episcopis,tales iudicentur. His iactis fundamentis , pontifices Romani mox persecuti sunt fideles , & inprimis Romanos imperatores,Fridericum 1.Fridericum 2.Ludouicū 4.sub quibus Tigurini quoq; excomunicati fuerunt. Et quanquâ plures videret imperatorib.magnâ iniuriâ fieri:tamè excomunicationis telo,interdicto, vt vocant, alijsq; nefarijs pontificum artibus, princi-
units.tr: Not only through the preposterous generosity of princes did they obtain great licence, they who nourished serpents in their bosom, but they almost claimed that licence for themselves against those same princes. In the Lateran Council, which was held in the year of the Lord 1215 under Pope Innocent III, it is read that among other things a decree was made that the constitutions of princes should not prejudice the churches, that the clergy should be immune from every contribution, and that tributes should not be paid before tithes. In this Council they also established that all who are regarded and condemned as heretics by the spiritual authorities should be punished by the secular magistrate with respect to their goods and their life. Likewise that all secular powers should publicly swear that they will in good faith exterminate all heretics from the lands subject to their jurisdiction, and spare no one. Those who neglected to do this were to be excommunicated, and all their subjects were to be absolved by the Pope from the oath they had sworn to them. Other Catholics were to make war on the excommunicated, occupy and possess their land, and, with the heretics exterminated, without any opposition, and so on. It is written that the excommunicated and heretics are all those (book 5, On Heretics, title 7, Ad abolendam, in the Decretals of Gregory IX) who do not in all things think with the Roman Church about the sacraments, or who are judged such by the Roman Church or its bishops. With these foundations laid, the Roman pontiffs soon persecuted the faithful, and above all the Roman emperors: Frederick I, Frederick II, Louis IV; under whom the Zurich people too were excommunicated. And although many saw that great injury was being done to the emperors, nevertheless by the weapon of excommunication, by interdict, as they call it, and by other wicked arts of the pontiffs,

units.la: Hæretici. principes fuerunt à iure suo depulsi & oppref i.Nulla enim vin cula aut fœdera illos reprimunt. Helueticum fœdus hac quoq; occasione cœpit. Nam cum tres pagi Heluetiorum Ludouico adhærerent contra Fridericum Auftriacum, Auftriaci maiorem sæuitiam ceperunt exercere contra tres illos pagos,qu̇e res eos perpulit,vt fœdus intær fe inirent,ad conseruationem suæ libertatis. Ludouicus 4. probauit & confirmauit eorum priuilegia & fœdera,&c
units.tr: Heretics. The princes were driven from their right and oppressed. For no bonds or covenants restrain them. The Swiss covenant too began on this occasion. For when three Swiss districts adhered to Louis against Frederick of Austria, the Austrians began to exercise greater cruelty against those three districts, which drove them to make a covenant among themselves for the preservation of their liberty. Louis IV approved and confirmed their privileges and covenants, and so on.

units.la: Res verò à pontificibus Romanis eò deducta est, vt non pudeat pòtificem 40.capite Si papa,scribere, Si Papa suæ & fraternæ salutis negligens deprehendatur, inutilis & remissus in suis operibus,& insuper à bono taciturnus, quod magis sibi officit & omnibus, nihilominus innumerabiles populos caterua-tim secum ducit primo mancipio gehennæ cum ipso plagis multis vapulaturus: huius culpas ilthic redarguere præsumit mortali im nullus, quia cunctos ipse iudicaturus, à nemine est iudicandus, nisi deprehendatur à fide deuius. Illi tamen homines, audent Euangelium hac ratione infamare, quòd magistratus tollat, cum detecta Antichristi malitia, magistratum à Deo ordinatum defendat.
units.tr: But matters have been brought by the Roman pontiffs to such a point that the pontiff is not ashamed to write (40 distinction, canon "If the Pope") that "if the Pope is found negligent of his own and his brothers' salvation, useless and slack in his works, and moreover silent about the good, which harms himself and everyone more, he nevertheless leads countless peoples in troops with him to the first slavery of hell, to be beaten with many blows. He presumes that no mortal may rebuke his faults there, since he himself is to judge everyone and is to be judged by no one, unless he is found to have strayed from the faith." Yet these men dare to defame the Gospel on this ground: that it removes the magistrate, whereas, once the malice of the Antichrist has been exposed, it defends the magistrate ordained by God.

units.la: Dolendum est quòd cum in tanta olim authoritate ministri ecclesiæ fuerint, hodie feré contemnantur: à multis onerentur potius,quàm vt immunitate donentur,&c.
units.tr: It is to be lamented that, although the ministers of the Church once had such great authority, today they are for the most part despised; they are burdened by many rather than granted immunity, and so on.

units.la: Quarto loco dicitur regem dedisse potestatem Efdræ,vt e-ligat iudices & præsides(arbitros Munsterus vertit) qui popu-lum gubernent. Magnum autem hoc est Dei beneficium,si homine non certis familijs alligati sunt, sed deligere ex toto Reipublicæ corpore possunt,quibus gubernacula committant. Iubet autem eos non ex prauis affectibus eligere,sed pro sapientia Dei tui quæ est in manu tua.) Hoc est,secundum legem vel verbum Dei, quod verè sapientes reddit, teste Paulo, & quod in promptu habes. Habebat enim codices sac̃ os,& in eis erat ver satissimus. Etsi autem multi sint loci scripturæ, qui ostendant qualis esse debeat magistratus, valde insignis est qui Exodi 18. capite extat, vbi Iethro dicit de electione iudicum ad Mosem generum suum (Deut.1. Deo tribuitur quod hic Iethroni tribuitur, Dominus enim per illum loquutus est) tu autem deliges ex toto populo, viros strenuos, timentes Deum, amantes veritatem,& odio habentes auaritiam: præficiesq; eis tribunos & centuriones,&c.
units.tr: In the fourth place it is said that the king gave Ezra the power to choose judges and governors (Münster translates "arbiters") who would govern the people. This is a great blessing of God, if they are not bound to certain families, but can choose from the whole body of the commonwealth those to whom they entrust the helm. He orders them to choose not out of wicked desires, but according to the wisdom of your God, which is in your hand. That is, according to the law or word of God, which truly makes men wise, as Paul witnesses, and which lies ready to hand. For he had the sacred books, and was very learned in them. Although there are many passages of Scripture that show what a magistrate ought to be, that in Exodus 18 is especially notable, where Jethro, speaking to his son-in-law Moses about the choice of judges (Deut. 1: what is here attributed to Jethro is attributed to God, for the Lord spoke through him), says: "You shall choose from all the people strenuous men, fearing God, loving truth, and hating avarice; and you shall set over them tribunes and centurions," and so on.

units.la: Officium iudicum est,iudicare, id est, causas audire,difcutere,auditis causis ferre sententiam, & inter litigantes discerne re,bonos defendere,malos punire. Ostendit quos iudicare debeant, nempe totum populum, qui est vltra fluuium, scilicet Euphratem. Omnes,nempe peritos in lege Dei: illos vero qui ignorant Legem, doceri iubet, multi Iudæi reuersi ex longo exilio, Legem & mores patrios obliti erant. Iudices non debebant iudicare ex affectibus, sed pronunciare fecundum æquum & iustum, ex Dei legibus. Magna autem inter illos est differentia,qui Legem norunt,ac scientes & volentes illam violant,& inter illos qui Legem ignorant.His ignoscendum est,vel poena mitiganda,illis vero nequaquam.
units.tr: The office of judges is to judge, that is, to hear causes, examine them, once the causes have been heard pronounce sentence, distinguish between litigants, defend the good and punish the wicked. He indicates whom they ought to judge, namely the whole people who are beyond the river, that is, the Euphrates. All, that is, those skilled in the law of God; but those who are ignorant of the law he orders to be taught, since many Jews returning from long exile had forgotten the law and their ancestral customs. Judges ought not to judge out of their emotions, but to pronounce according to what is equitable and just, from the laws of God. There is, however, a great difference between those who know the law and knowingly and willingly violate it, and those who are ignorant of the law. The latter must be forgiven, or their punishment lessened; the former by no means.

units.la: Alterum eorum officium est, poenis afficere transgressores legum. Rex enim de omnibus illis qui Dei & suas leges violant, iubet poenas sumere, de diuitibus pariter & pauperibus: ne de illis dici posit illud Satyricum:
units.tr: The second duty of the magistrate is to inflict punishments on those who break the laws. The king orders that penalties be exacted from all who violate God's laws and his own, rich and poor alike, so that the satirist's words cannot be applied to him:

units.la: Dat veniam corvis, vexat censura columbas.
units.tr: He grants pardon to the crows, while the censor harasses the doves.

units.la: Item,leges aranearum telis similis esse, in quibus hæreant muscæ, crabrones vero perrumpant. Vult etiam sine mora, vel studiose, poenas de illis sumant. Hoc dolendum si res eo veniunt, vt qui legem obseruant, aut qui violatores increpant ex officio, ad poenas postulentur. Quatuor autem supplicium genera constituit.
units.tr: Likewise, the laws are like spiders' webs, in which the flies stick while the hornets break through. He wants the penalties exacted from such offenders without delay and with diligence. It is a sad thing when matters reach the point where those who keep the law, or those who rebuke its violators, are called to account for their office. He lays down four kinds of punishment.

units.la: 1. Est capitale supplicium. In Lege Dei tria mortis genera contra sceleratos sancita sunt, suspensio, lapidatio, combustio,quidam addunt,gladij animaduersionem,quæ tamen ordinaria non fuit.
units.tr: (1) The first is capital punishment. God's Law sanctioned three kinds of death against criminals: hanging, stoning and burning. Some add the punishment of the sword, though this was not the ordinary one.

units.la: 2. Eradicatio. Per quem intelligunt exilium vel proscriptionem. Exules dicuntur relegati & deportati,inter quos hæc est differentia, quod relegatis vti licebat bonis proprijs in exilio: Deportatis vero non licebat quicquam ex suis bonis possidere. Deinde quidam ad certum tempus, alij perpetuo exulare iubentur.
units.tr: (2) Banishment. By this they understand exile or outlawry. Exiles are those who are relegated and those who are deported, and the difference between them is this: those relegated could use their own goods while in exile, but those deported could possess nothing of their goods. Further, some are ordered to exile for a fixed time, others for life.

units.la: 3. Est multa pecuniaria,vel priuatio possessionis,aliquando totius,aliquando partis.
units.tr: (3) A fine, or the deprivation of property, sometimes of all of it, sometimes of part.

units.la: 4. Est carcer, vel vincula, quo nomine compedes, pedicas, manicas, cathenas, neruos, intelligunt. Sub his alia quoque poenarum vel suppliciorum genera comprehendit: vt sunt mutilatio corporis, amputatio manuum, fustigatio, &c.
units.tr: (4) Imprisonment or chains, under which name they understand fetters, stocks, manacles, chains and bonds. Under these they include also other kinds of penalties and punishments, such as mutilation of the body, cutting off of hands, flogging, and so on.

units.la: Non vni poenæ omnes subijcit. Quia peccata non sunt paria, vt Stoici finxerunt. In eodem genere alij plus peccant, alij minus.
units.tr: He does not subject everyone to the same penalty, because sins are not equal, as the Stoics pretended. Within the same kind, some sin more and others less.

units.la: Supplicia-rum genera. minus. Circumstantiæ peccata graviora vel leviora efficiunt. Quidam peccant ex ignorantia: quidam ex humana imbecillitate quidam maiorem peccandi occasionem habent, & maiores impulsus: quidam tantum non perpelluntur ad peccandū: quidam ex mera malitia peccant. Iudicum æquitati permittitur, vt diligenter examinatis circumstantijs, pro modo vel pondere criminum, modum statuant supplicij.
units.tr: Circumstances make sins more or less grave. Some sin through ignorance, some through human weakness; some have a greater occasion for sinning and stronger impulses; some are barely pushed to sin; some sin from sheer malice. The fairness of judges is entrusted with examining the circumstances carefully and, according to the measure and weight of the crimes, fixing the measure of the punishment.

units.la: Necessarium autem est, vt crimina his pœnis vendicentur. Sunt enim qui virtutis amore à peccatis retrahantur: sunt rursus qui pœnę formidine coercentur. In magna familia, liberi in officio non possunt contineri, nisi virgis castigentur. Magistratus qui non puniunt sceleratos, parum memores sunt sui officij. In Proverbijs Salomonis cap. 17. verf. 15. Qui improbum absoluit, & qui iustum condemnat, vtrunque Deus detestatur. Magistratus gladium accepit diuinitus, ad bonorum defensionem, & malorum oppressionem, ad Roman. 13. cap. Sæpe etiam fit, vt si magistratus recusét punire sceleratos, ipsi tandem ab illis puniantur.
units.tr: It is also necessary that crimes be avenged by these punishments. For some are restrained from sin by the love of virtue, while others are restrained by the fear of punishment. In a large household, children cannot be kept in obedience unless they are chastised with the rod. Magistrates who do not punish the wicked are little mindful of their office. In Proverbs 17:15 of Solomon: "He that justifies the wicked, and he that condemns the just, both are an abomination to God." The magistrate has received the sword from God, for the defence of the good and the suppression of the wicked (Rom. 13). It often happens too that, if magistrates refuse to punish the wicked, they themselves are at last punished by them.

units.la: Ex hoc edicto intelligitur, Deum etiam extra Israelem suos cultores habuisse, qualis hic Artaxerxes fuit, & alij. De hoc Dario, Nicolaus Lyranus in capite sexto huius libri annotat: ex eo quòd Deo cœli eos iusit sacrificia offerre, elucere quòd iste rex habuerit fidem vnius veri Dei: nec scribit, tenebatur ad legem Mosaicam, cum esset gentilis: vt frequenter dictum est. Sufficiebat enim gentilibus ad salutem, credere vnum Deum prouidentem saluti hominum per modum sibi congruum: & in hoc articulo prouidentiæ continetur totum mysterium Christi implicitè, &c.
units.tr: From this edict it is understood that God also had worshippers outside Israel, such as this Artaxerxes and others. Concerning this Darius, Nicholas of Lyra, in his note on the sixth chapter of this book, observes that from the fact that he ordered sacrifices to be offered to the God of heaven, it is clear that this king had faith in the one true God. He does not write that he was bound to the Mosaic law, since he was a Gentile, as has often been said. For it was enough for Gentiles to salvation to believe in one God who provides for the salvation of men in a manner suited to them; and in this article of providence the whole mystery of Christ is contained implicitly, and so on.

units.la: In tertia parte huius Capitis, recitatur quomodo se Esdras gesserit impetrato regis decreto. Primum gratias Deo agit, pro beneficijs ab eo acceptis. Deinde dicit se congregasse capita, vt in patriam redirent. Singula verba ponderabimus. Benedictus Deus patrum nostrorum. Hoc est, laudetur ab omnibus, gratiæ ei agantur. Cuius Deo patrum nostrorum, hoc est, Deo Israelis. Distinguit eum à Dijs gentilium. Propterea autem celebrandum dicit: quia mouerit animum regis Artaxerxis, ad ornandum & promouendum templum Hierosolymitanum: De regis munificentia supra dictum est. Nisi Deus cor eius flexisset, maluisset opes suas, vt alij principes, effundere in ædificia insana, epulas, bella, &, vt quidam solent, in artem alcumisticam. Deinde, quòd se gratiosum fecerit apud Regem, consiliarios eius, aliosque mnes proceres regis.Demosthenes dixit,vt est apud Stobæum, πάντων ἐστὶ δυσχερέστατον τὸ πολλοῖς ἀρέσκειν, hoc est, omnium difficillimum esse, multis placere. Alij principibus viris placere,putant rem arduam esse. Pauperes & exules fere ab aliquibus eorum contemnuntur, imo odio habentur:suos subiectos temere in bellis obiectant periculis:non pluris facere videntur, quàm si ranæ esse. At Deus, in cuius manu sunt corda regum, nullo negotio flectere potest eorum animos, vt pauperes,egenos,exules,beneuolè complectantur,exemplo nobis est Iosephus,Hester,&c.
units.tr: In the third part of this chapter it is recounted how Ezra conducted himself once the king's decree had been obtained. First he gives thanks to God for the benefits received from him. Then he says that he gathered the heads of the people so that they might return to their homeland. We shall weigh each word. Blessed be the God of our fathers. That is, let him be praised by all, and thanks be given to him. "The God of our fathers," that is, the God of Israel. He distinguishes him from the gods of the Gentiles. He says that he is to be celebrated for this reason: that he moved the heart of King Artaxerxes to adorn and advance the temple at Jerusalem. The king's generosity was mentioned above. Unless God had bent his heart, he would rather have poured out his wealth, as other princes do, on mad buildings, feasts, wars, and, as some are wont to do, on alchemy. Next, that he made himself acceptable to the king, his counsellors, and all the other nobles of the king. Demosthenes said, as recorded by Stobaeus, "Of all things it is most difficult to please many" [πάντων ἐστὶ δυσχερέστατον τὸ πολλοῖς ἀρέσκειν], that is, that of all things it is most difficult to please many. Others think it a hard thing to please princely men. The poor and exiles are almost despised by some of them, indeed held in hatred; they carelessly expose their subjects to dangers in wars, and they seem to think them no more worth than frogs. But God, in whose hand are the hearts of kings, can with no trouble bend their minds so that they embrace the poor, the needy and the exiles with kindness. Joseph, Esther, and others are examples to us.

units.la: Esdras ascribit diuinæ bonitati,quòd gratus fuit regi & proceribus eius, scit Deum esse bonorum omnium fontem, a quo omnia habemus.Docens nos suo exemplo,ne quod hypocritæ solent, nostris meritis, dignitati, prudentiæ, illa bona tribuamus : sed grato animo, Dei beneficium agnoscamus & prædicemus. Gratiarum autem actio, non in verbis tantum est posita,sed in hoc,vt caveamus nobis a malo,& faciamus bonum.
units.tr: Ezra ascribes to divine goodness that he was acceptable to the king and his nobles, knowing that God is the fountain of all good things, from whom we have everything. He teaches us by his example not to attribute these blessings to our merits, dignity or prudence, as hypocrites are wont to do, but with a grateful heart to acknowledge and proclaim God's benefit. Thanksgiving, however, consists not in words alone, but in this: that we take care to refrain from evil and do good.

units.la: Solomon Prouerbiorum 16. verf. 7. Cum placuerint Domino viæ alicuius, etiam inimicos eius conciliat ei. Potest illo articulo, quo nobis agendum est cum illis, qui infesto in nos sunt animo,eos mutare. Esdras dicit,se magno animo fuisse,pro gratia & fauore a Deo accepto, & congregasse capita Israelis,vt secum ascenderent Hierosolyma. Remisi & socordes sumus tantisper,donec spiritu diuino corroboremur,qui idoneos nos facit ad res bonas.
units.tr: Solomon, Proverbs 16:7: "When a man's ways please the Lord, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him." Thus, by the same method by which we must deal with those who are hostile to us, he can change them. Ezra says that he was of great courage, relying on the grace and favour received from God, and that he gathered the heads of Israel so that they might go up with him to Jerusalem. We are also remiss and slothful for so long, until we are strengthened by the divine Spirit, who makes us fit for good things.

units.la: Quæ remorari residuos in Babylone potuerint,quo minus patriæ desiderio tenerentur,supra recitauimus. Cæterum Esdram nō parum profecisse,sequens caput ostendet. Deus enim non vult nostros labores secundum verbum suum susceptos, superuacaneos & irritos esse.
units.tr: What might have hindered the rest from remaining in Babylon, so that they would not be held by longing for their homeland, we have related above. Moreover, the following chapter will show that Ezra made no little progress. For God does not wish our labours undertaken according to his word to be vain and fruitless.

units.la: Discimus exemplo huius viri, homines solicitare,vt relicta spirituali Babylone, patriam repetant. Per Babylonem significatur mundus & regnum Antichristi : qui sedem suam Romæ habet,quæ Babylon a veteribus nominatur.Nam sicut Babylon idololatriam prouexit, Dei populum afflixit, moribus corruptissimis fuit:ita etiam Roma. In 1.Pet.5.cap.verba hæc, Salutat vos in Babylone ecclesia,quidam ex vetustis patribus de Roma intelligunt,quòd moribus Assyriæ Babyloni respondeat. Quam interpretationem ipsi Papistæ nil il infamia nominis deterriti, libenter agnoscunt, modo concedatur Petrum Romæ fuisse. Vix quidem persuaderi hominibus potest,vt Babylonem omni bus delitijs affluentcm deferant, tamen non deesse debemus no ftro officio. Proponendi illis sunt loci scripturæ, qualis ille est locus in Apocalypsi 18 capite,&c. Vbi Dominus dehortatur omnes fideles à consortio Romanæ ecclesiæ, Exite,inquiens, ex ea populi mi,ne participes fitis peccatorum eius,& de plagis eius ne participetis,&c.Recedimus morum & religionis difsimi litudine. Deinde vitæ integritate etiam multos lucrifaciemus. Breuiter,fi diligentes fuerimus,nó perdemus operam. Qui nó statim Babylonem relinquent,saltem post annos aliquot,vt hoc loco, in nouam Hierosolymam proficiscentur, hoc est, adiungent fe ecclesiæ,& tandem cœlestem patriam incolent. Non omnes eodem tempore in vineam Domini venire, Matth.20.ca. parabola docetur.
units.tr: From the example of this man we learn to urge men to leave spiritual Babylon and return to their homeland. By Babylon is signified the world and the kingdom of Antichrist, who has his seat at Rome, which is called Babylon by the ancients. For just as Babylon promoted idolatry, afflicted God's people, and was most corrupt in its morals, so too has Rome. In 1 Pet. 5, the words "The church that is in Babylon salutes you," some of the ancient fathers understand of Rome, because its morals correspond to those of Assyrian Babylon. The Papists themselves, not deterred at all by the infamy of the name, gladly acknowledge this interpretation, provided it is granted that Peter was at Rome. It can hardly be persuaded to men that they should leave Babylon, which abounds in every kind of luxury; yet we must not fail in our duty. Passages of Scripture must be set before them, such as that passage in the eighteenth chapter of the Apocalypse, and so on, where the Lord exhorts all the faithful to withdraw from fellowship with the Roman church: "Come out of her, my people," he says, "that you be not partakers of her sins, and that you receive not of her plagues," and so on. We withdraw because of the dissimilarity of morals and religion. Then, by the integrity of our life we shall win many too. In short, if we are diligent, we shall not lose our labour. Those who do not leave Babylon at once will, after some years, as in this place, set out for the new Jerusalem; that is, they will join themselves to the church, and at last dwell in the heavenly homeland. That not all come into the Lord's vineyard at the same time is taught in the parable of Matthew 20.

units.la: Deum precabimur vt suo spiritu nos corroboret, quo & ipsi Babylonem relinquere, & alios quoq; exipfa extrahere possimus,eosq; Hierosolyma reducere: vt semel abAntichrifti iugo liberatos,non amplius illud nobis imponi patiamur.
units.tr: We shall pray to God that he strengthen us by his Spirit, so that we may both leave Babylon ourselves and be able to draw others out of it too, and lead them back to Jerusalem; so that, once freed from the yoke of Antichrist, we may not suffer that yoke to be laid upon us again.

units.la: CAPVT VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: HOMILIA XXVII.
units.tr: HOMILY XXVII.

units.la: Catalogus illorum qui cum Esdra Hierosolyma venerunt.
units.tr: A catalogue of those who came up with Ezra to Jerusalem.

units.la: Isti autem sunt principes patrum eorum, & genealogia ipsorum qui ascenderunt mecum in regno Arthahsasthe regis, de Babel.
units.tr: These are the chief men of their fathers' houses, and the genealogy of those who went up with me from Babylon in the reign of King Artaxerxes.

units.la: 2 De filijs Pinhas, Gersum : de filijs Ithamar, Daniel: de filijs Dauidis, Hattus,
units.tr: 2 Of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom; of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel; of the sons of David, Hattush.

units.la: 3 De filijs Secheniah, (qui erat) de filijs Paros, Zechariah, & cum eo genealogia masculorum, centum & quinquaginta.
units.tr: 3 Of the sons of Shecaniah, who was of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah; and with him were reckoned males of his line, one hundred and fifty.

units.la: 4 De filijs Pahathmoab, Elioenai filius Zerahiah, & cum eo (erant) ducenti masculi.
units.tr: 4 Of the sons of Pahath-moab, Elihoenai son of Zerahiah; and with him were two hundred males.

units.la: 5 De filijs Sechaniah, filius Iahaziel, & cum eo trecenti masculi.
units.tr: 5 Of the sons of Shecaniah, Jahaziel son of Jahaziel; and with him three hundred males.

units.la: 6 De filijs Adin, Ebed filius Ionathan, & cum eo quinquaginta masculi.
units.tr: 6 Of the sons of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan; and with him fifty males.

units.la: 7 De filijs autem Elam, Iesaiah filius Athaliah, & cum eo septuaginta masculi.
units.tr: 7 Of the sons of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah; and with him seventy males.

units.la: 8 Et de filijs Sephatiah, Zebadiah filius Michael, & cum eo octoginta masculi,
units.tr: 8 And of the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael; and with him eighty males.

units.la: 9 De filijs Ioab, Obadiah filius Iehiel, & cum eo ducenti & octodecim masculi.
units.tr: 9 Of the sons of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel; and with him two hundred and eighteen males.

units.la: 10 De filijs Selomith filius Iosaphiah, & cum eo centum & sexaginta masculi.
units.tr: 10 Of the sons of Shelomith, son of Josiphiah; and with him one hundred and sixty males.

units.la: 11 De filijs vero Bebai, Zechariah filius Bebai, & cum eo viginti & octo masculi,
units.tr: 11 Of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai; and with him twenty-eight males.

units.la: 12 Et de filijs Azgad, Iohanan filius Haccathan, & cum eo centum & decem masculi.
units.tr: 12 And of the sons of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan; and with him one hundred and ten males.

units.la: 13 Et de filijs Adonicam nouissimi, quorum nomina haec sunt, Eliphelet, Ieiel, & Semaaiah, & cum eis sexaginta masculi.
units.tr: 13 And of the sons of Adonikam, the last ones, whose names are these: Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah; and with them sixty males.

units.la: 14 De filijs vero Biguai, Vthai, & Zabud, & cum eo septuaginta masculi.
units.tr: 14 Of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zabbud; and with them seventy males.

units.la: 15 Congregaui autem eos ad fluuium qui venit in Ahaua, & mansimus ibi diebus tribus: postquam consideraui populum, & Sacerdotes, & de filijs Leui non inueni ibi.
units.tr: 15 I gathered them together at the river that flows to Ahava, and we camped there for three days. When I had looked over the people and the priests, I found there none of the sons of Levi.

units.la: 16 Misi itaque ad Eliezer, ad Ariel, ad Semaaiah, & ad Elnathan, & ad Iarib, & ad Elnathan, & ad Nathan, & ad Zechariah, & Mesullam principes, & ad Ioiarib, & ad Elnathan, peritos.
units.tr: 16 So I sent for Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah and Meshullam, leaders, and for Joiarib and Elnathan, men of understanding.

units.la: 17 Et praecepi eis de Iddo duce in Chasiphiah loco, posuique in ore eorum verba quae loquerentur ad Iddo & fratrem eius Nethinim in Chasiphiah loco, ut adducerent nobis ministros pro domo Dei nostri.
units.tr: 17 And I charged them to go to Iddo, the leader at the place Casiphia, and I put into their mouths the words they were to speak to Iddo and his brothers the Nethinim at the place Casiphia, that they might bring us ministers for the house of our God.

units.la: 18 Adduxerunt ergo nobis iuxta manum Dei nostri bonam super nos, virum intelligentem de filijs Mahali filij Leui, filij Israel: & Serebiah, & filios eius, & fratres eius, octodecim.
units.tr: 18 So, by the good hand of our God upon us, they brought us a man of understanding, of the sons of Mahli son of Levi, son of Israel; and Sherebiah with his sons and brothers, eighteen.

units.la: 19 Et Hasabiah, & cum eo Iesaiah de filijs Merari, fratres eius, & filios eorum viginti.
units.tr: 19 And Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, with his brothers and their sons, twenty.

units.la: 20 De
units.tr: 20 Of

units.la: HOMILIA XXVII.
units.tr: HOMILIA XXVII.

units.la: De Nethinæis vero, quos posuerat Dauid, & principes ad ministerium Leuitarum, Nethinæos, ducentos & viginti: omnes hi expositi fuerunt nominibus.
units.tr: Of the Nethinim, whom David and the princes had appointed for the service of the Levites: two hundred and twenty, all of them named by name.

units.la: NTER maxima beneficia, quibus Deus populum suum affecit, merito numerari debet eductio ex Babylonica captiuitate, de qua in hoc libro fusè scribitur.
units.tr: Among the greatest benefits with which God favoured his people, the deliverance from the Babylonian captivity rightly deserves to be counted; it is described at length in this book.

units.la: Superiore Capite audiuimus Esdram impetrata à rege Persico facultate redeundi in patriam, ascendisse Hierosolymam. Literæ regis vel diploma ad Iudææ satrapas, insertum est huic narrationi.
units.tr: In the previous chapter we heard that Ezra, having obtained from the Persian king permission to return to his homeland, went up to Jerusalem. The king's letter, or decree, to the governors of Judea is inserted into this narrative.

units.la: Quemadmodum vero 2. cap. catalogus illorum contexitur qui in primo ascensu fuerunt: ita in hoc 8. cap. principum, id est, patrum, vel ducum, qui cum Esdra Hierosolyma ascenderunt. Seruatur autem hic ordo. Primo in genere illorum qui volentes profecti sunt, nomina ponuntur: Deinde speciatim Leuitarum quos accersiuerunt.
units.tr: Just as in the second chapter a list is woven together of those who were in the first going up, so in this eighth chapter there is a list of the leaders, that is, of the heads of families or chiefs, who went up to Jerusalem with Ezra. The order here is kept as follows. First, the names of those who went willingly are set down in general; then, specifically, the Levites whom they summoned.

units.la: Tres familiæ principio attinguntur: duæ Aaronitarum & Sacerdotum de linea Eleazar, & de linea Ithamar, tertia è tribu Iuda & prosapia regia. Illarum proceres & duces peregrinationis, fuerunt Phinees, Daniel, Hattus. Inde recensentur capita cum numero contributorum, ex quibus etiam ante aliqui ascenderunt. Numerantur 1496 mares, præter fœminas & liberos. Nolui nomina quæ in hoc catalogo ponuntur, recitare, quia molestum esset: Si quis velit, domi legat.
units.tr: Three families are mentioned at the outset: two of the Aaronites and priests, one from the line of Eleazar and one from the line of Ithamar, and a third from the tribe of Judah and the royal lineage. The chiefs and leaders of their journey were Phinehas, Daniel and Hattush. Then the heads of families are enumerated with the number of those contributing, some of whom had also gone up earlier. There are counted 1,496 males, besides women and children. I have not wished to recite the names set down in this list, since it would be tedious; if anyone wishes, let him read them at home.

units.la: Dicit se congregasse eos ad fluuium, qui venit in Achaia, scilicet oppidum, vel fluuium etiam hoc nomine intelligit. In Babylone enim multos fluuios esse, ex Psal. 137. intelligitur: Super flumina Babylonis, illic sedimus, etiam fleuimus. Iosephus Euphrate hoc loco intelligit, forte fuit aliquis riu² eius. Tota enim regio irrigua fuit, propter plures alueos ex fluuio deductos.
units.tr: He says that he gathered them at the river that flows into Ahava, meaning either the town or the river of that name. For that there were many rivers in Babylon is clear from Psalm 137: "By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept." Josephus understands the Euphrates here; perhaps it was some branch of it. For the whole region was well watered, on account of the many channels drawn off from the river.

units.la: Ibi triduum commorati sunt, partim ut quiescerent: partim ut expectarent, an forte Leuitæ, vel alij plures essent adventuri.
units.tr: There they stayed for three days, partly to rest, and partly to wait and see whether perhaps Levites or more others would come.

units.la: Ex hoc loco misit Esdras legationem, cuius hæ circumstantiæ annotantur. Quis eos miserit, unde, quando, quare, quot, ad quos, quomodo, & quid effecerint.
units.tr: From this place Ezra sent an embassy, and the circumstances of it are noted: who sent them, whence, when, why, how many, to whom, in what manner, and what they accomplished.

units.la: Cum Esdras seruasset populum & sacerdotes, hoc est, cum eos recensuisset, nullas ibi Leuitas inuenit. At cap. 7. diserte legitur, ascendisse aliquot filios Israelis, sacerdotes, Leuitas, cantores, ianitores, Nathinim, in Ierusalem. Ad quod sic respondeo. Supra in genere dixit, Israelitas ascendisse è Babylone Hierosolyma: iam hoc Capite speciatim explicat quomodo id factum sit, quid eis in itinere acciderit, priusquam Hierosolyma pervenirent. Leuitas non sponte adfuisse, sed vocatos. Solet autem scriptura summam alicuius rei paucis proponere, quam postea per partes explicat. Sic Moses Genesis 1. capite in genere proponit, Deum in principio creasse cœlum & terram, quod postea speciatim explicat.
units.tr: When Ezra had reviewed the people and the priests, that is, had enrolled them, he found no Levites there. But in chapter 7 it is clearly read that some sons of Israel, priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers and Nethinim, went up to Jerusalem. To this I answer as follows. Above, in general terms, he said that the Israelites went up from Babylon to Jerusalem; now in this chapter he explains in particular how this was done, and what befell them on the way before they reached Jerusalem. The Levites were present not of their own accord but were summoned. Now Scripture is accustomed to set out the sum of a matter briefly, and afterwards to explain it part by part. So Moses in the first chapter of Genesis states in general that God created heaven and earth in the beginning, which he afterwards explains in particular.

units.la: Cum igitur nullos Leuitas inueniret, misit vndecim viros, nouem primarios, duos sapientia, eloquentia & prudentia reliquis præstantiores. Plures ideo videtur mittere, quod res esset grauior. Ad grauiora enim negotia, plures legati decernuntur. Illi duo inter multos illos videntur principes legationis fuisse constituti.
units.tr: Since, therefore, he found no Levites, he sent eleven men: nine leaders, and two who excelled the rest in wisdom, eloquence and prudence. He seems to have sent more because the matter was more serious; for more envoys are appointed for weightier business. Those two among the many seem to have been appointed as the chiefs of the embassy.

units.la: Misit eos ad Iddo principem Casphiae. Quidam locum esse dicunt in Assyria, vicinum Caspiae. Lyranus putat locum esse in Babylone. Sunt qui ad Iudaeos missos dicant, qui fuerint vltra Caspios montes, tunc enim nondum fuisse reclusos, quod ab Alexandro magno factum, scribit Iosephus. Haec sententia refellitur duobus argumentis. Primum est, quod Iudaei illi ab Assyrijs abducti fuerint, non à Nabuchodonosore. Paucos autem ex 10. tribubus Hierosolymam redijsse. Alterum, quod tam paucis diebus, longum illud iter non potuisset confici. Ad quae respondetur, intra 70. annos captiuitatis, plures ex regno Iuda potuisse ad illos transfire. Deinde non procul ab illo loco, fuisse Iudeos collectos ad profectionem.
units.tr: He sent them to Iddo, the chief of Casiphia. Some say the place is in Assyria, near the Caspian. Lyra thinks the place is in Babylon. There are those who say that they were sent to Jews who lived beyond the Caspian mountains, for those had not yet been opened, which Josephus writes was done by Alexander the Great. This view is refuted by two arguments. The first is that those Jews had been led away by the Assyrians, not by Nebuchadnezzar, and only a few of the ten tribes returned to Jerusalem. The second is that in so few days so long a journey could not have been completed. To these it is answered that within the seventy years of captivity, many from the kingdom of Judah could have passed over to them; and moreover, that Jews had been gathered for the departure not far from that place.

units.la: Tradunt Iudaei 10. tribus adhuc in montibus (nimirum Caspijs) vltra flumen quem ipsi Sabbaticum vocant, inclusos detineri, quos tandem erupturos, & se per illos ex præsenti captiuitate redimendos stultè credut. Vulgo illos Iudaeos rufos appellant, de quibus multa in suis precibus iactant & cantat, vide Paulum Fagium in paraphrasi Chaldaica super Deut. 30. cap.
units.tr: The Jews relate that the ten tribes are still detained in the mountains (namely the Caspian ones), shut in beyond the river which they themselves call the Sabbatical, and they foolishly believe that these will at last break out and be redeemed through them from the present captivity. Commonly they call those Jews the Red Jews, about whom they boast and sing much in their prayers. See Paul Fagius on the Chaldee paraphrase of Deuteronomy 30.

units.la: Misit eos vt peterent Leuitas ministros templi. Scire enim poterat, numerum Leuitarum qui Hierosolymis iam erant, non sufficere ad exercitium religionis. Quoto die misi sint, non exprimitur. Dedit eis formulam verborum quibus vterentur, instructionem vt vulgo dicimus.
units.tr: He sent them to ask for Levites, ministers of the temple. For he could know that the number of Levites who were already in Jerusalem was not sufficient for the exercise of religion. On what day they were sent is not stated. He gave them a form of words to use, an instruction, as we commonly say.

units.la: Posui verba in ore eorum.) Mandaui quid dicerent. Prophetæ quoq; dicunt: Deus posuit verba mea in ore meo: dictauit mihi quæ sint dicenda.
units.tr: I have put the words in their mouth. I commanded what they should say. The prophets also say: "God has put my words in my mouth"; he dictated to me what was to be said.

units.la: Iudæi rufi. Quid impetrarint legati, adduxerunt iuxta manum bonam Domini super eos, virum prudentem Serebiam, & alios Leuitas, item Nethinim, numero 258. Nethinim dicit noster author, quos dederunt Dauid & principes vt seruirent Leuitis, &c. Gibeonitæ sic dictifunt, quos ob dolum quo vsi fuerunt, Iosue destinauit seruitio templi. Numerus illorum diminutus fuit, Saul multos extirpauerat. Bibliander dicit necessarium fuisse, vt aliunde legerentur. Proinde Dauidem & alios principes alios dedisse, ex quorum posteris hi fuerint. Superioribus quoq; seculis principes ecclesijs & monasterijs mancipia dederunt.
