units.tr: The Red Jews. As to what the envoys obtained, they brought, "according to the good hand of the Lord upon them," a prudent man, Sherebiah, and other Levites, also Nethinim, numbering 258. Our author says the Nethinim are those whom David and the princes gave to serve the Levites, and so on. The Gibeonites were so called, whom Joshua appointed to the service of the temple on account of the deceit they had used. Their number was diminished, since Saul had destroyed many of them. Bibliander says it was necessary that they be gathered from elsewhere. Therefore David and the other princes gave others, from whose posterity these were. In earlier centuries too, princes gave slaves to churches and monasteries.

units.la: Vsus huius loci.
units.tr: The use of this passage.

units.la: 1 Præter illa quæ secundo capite annotauimus, discimus ex hoc loco, quod pauci res magnas posse efficere, si serio agant. Vulgo dicitur, vnus vir, nullus vir. Sensus est, nihil egregium præstari posse ab vno homine, omnium auxilio destituto. Plerunque vero Deus excitat, qui sequantur fortes duces. Esdras magnam multitudinem excitauit (nam si colligas illos numeros, inuenies 1754. præter fœminas & pueros) quæ religionis suis possessionibus, iter quantumuis periculosum ingressa est. Si multi essent Esdræ, hoc est, ministri ecclesiæ zelo magno prædicti, plures ex Babylone, hoc est, ex idololatria & spirituali seruitute peccati & mortis æternæ educerentur. Sed quia zelus nullus est, non hortamur alios, vt deserant peccata & idololatriam imo cum verbis, tum vita nostra offendimus alios, neque est mirum, tam paucos ex seruitute diaboli emergere, vel semel liberatos iterum deficere. Homines ignaui, mille fingunt pericula, vbi nulla sunt.
units.tr: 1 Besides what we noted in the second chapter, we learn from this passage that a few men can accomplish great things if they act in earnest. The saying goes, "one man is no man." The meaning is that nothing outstanding can be done by one man if he is left without help from others. Yet God usually raises up brave leaders for others to follow. Ezra gathered a great multitude (if you add up those numbers you will find 1,754, not counting women and children), who undertook a journey however dangerous it was, for the sake of their religion and their possessions. If there were many Ezras, that is, ministers of the Church endowed with great zeal, more people would be led out of Babylon, that is, out of idolatry and the spiritual slavery of sin and eternal death. But since there is no such zeal, we do not urge others to forsake their sins and idolatry. Indeed, by both our words and our lives we give offence to others. It is no wonder that so few emerge from the slavery of the devil, or that those who have once been set free fall back again. Lazy men invent a thousand dangers where there are none.

units.la: 2 Exemplo Esdræ discunt omnes proceres ecclesiæ & Rei publicæ, vt dent operam ne ecclesiæ destituantur idoneis ministris: sed vt scholæ recte instituta sint, ex quibus prodeant litterati homines, qui præfecti ecclesijs, puram & incorruptam doctrinam recte tradant. Esdras scire potuit, quomodo res Hierosolymis haberent, quod & ministris necessarijs carerent. Matthæi 9. capite in fine legitur, Cum Iesus vidisset turbas, affectu misericordiæ tactum esse erga illos, quod essent destituti ac dispersi, velut oues non habentes pastorem. Tunc dixisse discipulis suis: Ipsa quidem messis copiosa, cæterum operarij pauci. Rogate igitur dominum messis, vt extrudat operarios in messem suam. Paulus ad Titum 1. cap. dicit inter alia, se Titum propterea in Creta reliquisse, vt constituat oppidatim presbyteros sicut ipse sibi ordinarit. Docet etiā quales illi esse debeant etc.
units.tr: 2 From Ezra's example, all the leaders of the Church and the commonwealth learn to take care that the Church is not left without suitable ministers, but that the schools are rightly ordered so that learned men may come forth, set over the churches, and faithfully teach pure and uncorrupted doctrine. Ezra could have known how matters stood at Jerusalem, and that they lacked necessary ministers. At the end of Matthew 9 we read that when Jesus saw the crowds, he was moved with compassion for them, because they were distressed and scattered like sheep without a shepherd. Then he said to his disciples: "The harvest is indeed plentiful, but the labourers are few. Therefore pray the Lord of the harvest to send out labourers into his harvest." Paul, in Titus 1, says among other things that he left Titus in Crete so that he might appoint elders in every town, as he himself had directed him. He also teaches what kind of men these should be, and so on.

units.la: 3 Quod numerum Nethinæorum colligit, & omnes suis nominibus appellatos dicit, ostendit homines illos qui nullo numero sunt in mundo, apud Deum, qui non accipit personas, in magno esse precio. Ad Ephesios 6. cap. hortatur apostolus dominos ad officium suum ergaseruos, addens: Scientes quod & vester ipsorum Dominus est in cœlis, nec personæ respectus est apud illum, &c. Item ad Galat. 2. & 3. cap.
units.tr: 3 That Ezra counts the Nethinim and says that all of them are called by their names shows that those men, who count for nothing in the world, are held in great esteem before God, who does not regard persons. In Ephesians 6 the apostle exhorts masters to do their duty towards their servants, adding: "Knowing that your own Master also is in heaven, and there is no respect of persons with him." Likewise in Galatians 2 and 3.

units.la: 4 Exemplum legatorum fidelium. Sæpe mittendi sunt legati, qui nomine ecclesiæ vel Reipublicæ aliquid agant, illis certa dantur mandata, quæ diligenter bona, fide perficere debent. Iosue & Calebus legati vel exploratores, quæ in mandatis habebant, fideliter exequuti sunt. De bonis & malis legatis, aliquot extant sententiæ apud Solomonem: Istos mandata sua fideliter exposuisse, & rectè suo functos esse officio, vel ex hoc liquet, quod tot Leuitas collegerunt.
units.tr: 4 The example of faithful envoys. Often envoys must be sent who act in the name of the Church or the commonwealth, and they are given definite instructions, which they must carry out diligently and faithfully. Joshua and Caleb, sent as envoys or spies, faithfully carried out what they had been commissioned to do. There are several sayings in Solomon about good and bad envoys. That those men faithfully set out their instructions and rightly performed their office is clear from this alone: they gathered so many Levites.

units.la: HOMILIA XXVIII.
units.tr: HOMILIA XXVIII.

units.la: Iudæi ieiunio & precibus profectionem inchoantes, exauditi sunt.
units.tr: The Jews, beginning their journey with fasting and prayer, were heard.

units.la: 21 Tunc indixi ibi ieiunium iuxta fluuium Ahaua, vt affligeremus nos coram Deo nostro, vt quæreremus ab eo viam rectam nobis, & paruulis nostris, ac vniuersa substantia nostra.
units.tr: 21 Then I proclaimed a fast there by the river Ahava, that we might humble ourselves before our God, to seek from him a straight way for us, for our little ones, and for all our substance.

units.la: 22 Erubui enim petere a rege exercitum & equites vt tuerentur nos ab inimico in via: dixeramus enim ad regem, dicendo: Manus Dei nostri (est) super omnes requirentes eum in bonitate: fortitudo vero & furor eius super omnes qui derelinquunt eum.
units.tr: 22 For I was ashamed to ask the king for an army and horsemen to protect us from the enemy on the road; for we had said to the king: "The hand of our God is upon all who seek him in goodness, but his strength and his wrath are upon all who forsake him."

units.la: 23 Ieiunauimus itaque, & petiimus a Deo nostro propter hoc, & placatus est nobis.
units.tr: 23 So we fasted and besought our God for this, and he was appeased toward us.

units.la: QVod Esdras præcedenti capite generatim dixit, se cum populo Hierosolyma venisse, in hoc capite per partes explicat. Recensetenim nomina illorum & numerum, qui secum ex Babylone ascenderunt: deinde vbi congregati sint, often dicitur quomodo Leuitæ vocati aduenerint. Cumq; iam omnes congregati essent, non statim mouerunt castra, sed priusquam fauorem Dei ambiuerunt.Esdras enim indixit ieiunium & publicas preces.Sic enim facere solebant reges & sacerdotes periculosis temporibus.2. Paralipomenon vigesimo capite Iosaphatus rex,quando Moabitae, Ammonitae,Syri & Idumaei,regnum Iuda magnis viribus inuaserunt, ieiunium indixit & ad preces se conuertit,&c.Estherae quarto capite populus Dei captiuus tribus diebus & totidem noctibus ieiunauit. Ionae tertio capite de rege Niniuitarum idem legitur. Ieiunabant, vt in precibus ardentiores essent, nam plenus venter ad preces feriās non est idoneus. Hinc est quod scriptura preces & ieiunia ferè coniungit.Matthaei 17.Lucae 2.Actorum 14.1. ad Corinth. 7.capite.
units.tr: What Ezra said in general in the previous chapter, that he came to Jerusalem with the people, he now explains in detail. For he lists the names and number of those who came up with him from Babylon; then he tells how the Levites were summoned and came, once they had gathered. When all had assembled, they did not set out at once, but before they sought the favour of God. For Ezra proclaimed a fast and public prayers. Kings and priests were accustomed to do this in dangerous times. In 2 Chronicles chapter 20, King Jehoshaphat, when the Moabites, Ammonites, Syrians and Idumaeans invaded the kingdom of Judah with great forces, proclaimed a fast and turned himself to prayer, and so on. In Esther chapter 4, the captive people of God fasted for three days and as many nights. In Jonah chapter 3 the same is read of the king of the Ninevites. They fasted so that they might be more fervent in prayer, for a full belly is not fit for prayer on working days. Hence Scripture commonly joins prayers and fasts: Matthew 17, Luke 2, Acts 14, 1 Corinthians chapter 7.

units.la: Hoc loco ieiunarunt & Esdras & populus, vt humiliarent vel affligerent se coram Deo suo, ficq; testarentur sepeccatores esse, & ab eo petierent vt ipse esset eorum dux viae, quo cum vxoribus,liberis & ingentibus opibus, Hierosolyma tuti & incolumes peruenirent.Potuisset quidem Esdras a rege, apud quem in magna erat gratia,impetrare equites,à quibus in itinere contra praedones fuissent defensi, sed pudebat eum petere.Metuebat enim,ne rex vel alij offenderentur, si qui antea tam magnificè loquuti erant de Deo Israelis, quod tueatur & protegat quotquot eum requirunt: robur atq; indignationem suam ostendat contra omnes quotq; ipsum deserunt.iam carnalem brachium peterent:& quaerendo humanum auxilium,diuino viderentur diffidere.Proinde diuino fretus auxilio, iter ingressi sunt.Deus autem exaudiuit eos:& rei felicem dedit euentum.
units.tr: Here both Ezra and the people fasted, to humble and afflict themselves before their God, and so to bear witness that they were sinners, and to ask him to be their guide on the way, so that they might reach Jerusalem safely and unharmed, with their wives, children and great wealth. Ezra could indeed have obtained from the king, in whose great favour he stood, horsemen to defend them against robbers on the journey; but he was ashamed to ask. For he feared that the king and others might take offence, since they had earlier spoken so magnificently of the God of Israel, that he protects and shields all who seek him, and shows his strength and indignation against all who forsake him. They would now be seen to distrust God's help and to seek a carnal arm, and by seeking human aid they would seem to distrust divine aid. Therefore, relying on divine help, they set out on their journey. And God heard them and gave a happy outcome to the matter.

units.la: Pauca haec verba,plena sunt dulci consolatione & doctrina.
units.tr: These few words are full of sweet consolation and teaching.

units.la: Primum discimus peregrinationes,praesertim periculosas,à precibus inchoandas esse,quas fundere debent se ad iter accingentes, & alij quoq; pro illis,vt sospites incolumes sint & reuertantur.Difficile & periculosum erat, cum vxoribus,liberis & impedimentis, tantisq; opibus,tam procul proficisci:Precan tur igitur Deum, vt ipse dignetur eos conseruare. Si profici ceris in peregrina loca atque regiones,vt ibi habites, vel discendarum literarum, linguarum, artium liberalium & mechanicarum, aut mercaturae gratia, aut etiam publicas ob causas, memor huius exempli,committe te Deo, petens & expectans ab eo auxilium. Plura enim in itinere nobis aliquando eueniunt, quae nos non prospicere, neque cauere possumus. Possumus incidere in latrones, in bestias. Euentus non sunt in nostra potestate.Ideo Paulus 1. Corinth. quarto capite. Veniam, inquit, breui ad vos, si dominus voluerit. Iacobi 4. capite docemur cum conditione dicendum, huc illuc proficiscar nempe si Deus voluerit. Psalmo 37. A Domino gressus hominis firmantur, & viam eius dirigit. Prouerbiorum 3. versu 6. In omnibus vijs tuis cogita vel cognosce eum (Dominum) ipse diriget gressus tuos: capite 6. versu 9. Cor hominis cogitabit viam suam, & Dominus dirigetgressum eius. Capite 20. versu 24. A Domino sunt gressus viri, homo autem quomodo intelliget viam suam vel eius? Ieremiae 10. Scio Domine quod non est hominis via eius, nec viri vt dirigat gressus suos: & quomodo disponet homo viam? Per viam metaphoricè institura hominis intelligit, quicquid instituit, feliciter procedit, & secundum literam, ipsam viam. Si quis iter instituit, nō succedit nisi Deus fortunauerit. Accinēti ad iter, interdum coguntur mutare consilium, aberrant à via, aliquando vt redire in viam vix possint. Genesis 21. Agar cum Ismaele errat in deserto, in quo perijsset, nisi à Deo per angelum in viam fuisset reducta, qui fontem ei ostendit, ex quo hauriens aquam, filium recreauit. Augustinus in Enchiridio ad Laurentium: Nobis ipsis, inquit, accidit, vt in biuio falleremur, & non iremus per illum locum, vbi operiens transitum nostrum Donatistarum manus armata subsederat, atque ita factum est, vt quo tendebamus, per deuium circuitum veniremus, atque inde gratias ageremus Deo, &c.
units.tr: First, we learn that journeys, especially dangerous ones, should begin with prayers, which those who prepare for the road ought to pour out, and others too should pray for them, that they may be safe and return unharmed. The journey was difficult and dangerous, with wives, children, baggage and such great wealth to go so far. They therefore prayed God that he would deign to preserve them. If you set out for foreign lands and regions, to live there, or for the sake of learning languages, the liberal and mechanical arts, or for trade, or even for public business, remember this example, commit yourself to God, asking for and expecting help from him. For on the journey many things sometimes happen to us which we can neither foresee nor guard against. We may fall among robbers or wild beasts. Events are not in our power. Therefore Paul says in 1 Corinthians chapter 4: "I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills." James chapter 4 teaches us to speak with this condition: "I will go here or there, if God wills." Psalm 37: "The steps of a man are established by the Lord, and he directs his way." Proverbs 3:6: "In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will direct your steps." Chapter 16, verse 9: "A man's heart devises his way, but the Lord directs his steps." Chapter 20, verse 24: "A man's steps are from the Lord; but how can a man understand his own way?" Jeremiah 10: "I know, O Lord, that the way of man is not in himself; it is not in man to direct his steps. How can man order his way?" By "way," in a metaphorical sense, is meant whatever a man undertakes; whatever he undertakes proceeds happily. Literally, it means the road itself. If someone plans a journey, it does not succeed unless God grants good fortune. Those setting out on a journey are sometimes forced to change their plans; they wander from the road, and sometimes can hardly find their way back onto it. Genesis 21: Hagar wandered in the wilderness with Ishmael, where they would have perished, unless God had led her back onto the way through an angel, who showed her a well, from which she drew water and revived her son. Augustine in the Enchiridion to Laurentius: "It happened to us ourselves," he says, "that we were misled at a fork in the road, and did not go by the place where an armed band of Donatists had lain in wait to ambush our passage; and so it came about that by a roundabout detour we reached where we were heading, and then we gave thanks to God," and so on.

units.la: Apud Ethnicos quoque peregrinationis ergo sacrificia simul & vota fiebant Herculi & Sango. Dij quos peregrè profecturi, inuocare solebant, à Graecis ἐνοδίοι dicti sunt. Vide Stuc cij Antiquitatum conuiuialium commentarios, folio 101.
units.tr: Among the heathen too, sacrifices and vows were made for the sake of a journey, to Hercules and Sancus together. The gods whom those about to travel abroad were accustomed to invoke were called by the Greeks Enodian gods [ἐνοδίοι]. See the commentaries of Stucius on the Antiquities of Banquets, folio 101.

units.la: Aliae quoque res arduae, cum religione inchoandae sunt, vt si matrimonium contrahas, foedera pangas, concionatores, magistratus deligas, bella geras, &c. Hodie vulgò res omnes à poculis & conuiuijs ordimur: non à precibus & ieiunijs. Gentiles quoque alia grauianegotia à religione vel potius superstitione auspicati sunt. Si vero à Deo petendum est, vt iter terrestre non bis ostendat, quanto magis vt nobis iter caeleste ostendat, & si ab illo aberrauerimus, nos in illud reducat?
units.tr: Other difficult matters too must be begun with religion: if you contract marriage, make covenants, choose sermon-givers or magistrates, wage wars, and so on. Today nearly everything we begin is started with cups and feasts, not with prayers and fasts. The Gentiles too began other weighty affairs with religion, or rather superstition. If we must ask God that he show us the way on land so that we do not go astray, how much more should we ask that he show us the heavenly way, and, if we wander from it, lead us back into it?

units.la: Secundo loco vides quanto studio scandala vitanda sint. Per se malum non erat, petere defensores, & se contra vim munire. Deus enim tentandus non est. At si hoc tempore Esdras à rege petijsset praesidium, ortum fuisset scandalum. Rex aut alij infirmi, dicere aut minimum cogitare potuissent, vt paulo ante diximus, isti qui tam praeclarè & magnificè de Deo suo loquuti sunt,
units.tr: Secondly, you see with what great care scandals are to be avoided. In itself it was not wrong to ask for defenders and to protect oneself against violence. For God is not to be tempted. But if at this time Ezra had asked the king for protection, a scandal would have arisen. The king and others who were weak could have said, or at least thought, as we said a little earlier, about those who had spoken so splendidly and magnificently of their God:

units.la: Scandala vitanda. sunt, nunc diffisi eius auxilio, petunt brachium carnale ad fui defensionem. Vana igitur eorum sunt verba: Id quod sycophantæ exaggerarent. Ad hoc igitur scandalum vitandum, se credut diuino auxilio.
units.tr: Scandals must be avoided. "Now that they distrust his help, they seek a carnal arm for their own defence." Their words would therefore be empty, which slanderers would exaggerate. To avoid this scandal, then, they trusted in divine help.

units.la: Caueamus igitur nobis quoq; à scandalis. Sunt autem scandala quædam, vt vocant in scholis, accepta, quædam data. Accepta vocamus cum homines immeritò offenduntur, vt cum impios & hypocritas offendit vera doctrina de iustificatione hominis, de bonis operibus, cum nolunt taxari errores, & cultus idolorum. Facta quoq; recta eos offendunt, vt cum sacerdos pius vxorem honestam ducit. Hæc offendicula non sunt curanda. Data vero sunt, cum homines falsa doctrina, aut malis exemplis alios in erroribus confirmant: & ad imitationem excitat, &c. De huiusmodi scandalis Matth. 18. dicitur. Væ homini per quem venit scandalum &c. Magnopere dolendum est, tot reperiri, qui nullam neq; hominum neq; nominis diuini rationem habeant, sed temere faciunt quicquid collibitum est, neq; vllius rei eos pudet.
units.tr: Let us therefore also take care to avoid scandals. Some scandals, as the schools call them, are taken, and some are given. We speak of scandal taken when men are offended without good reason, as when the impious and hypocrites are offended by true teaching on the justification of man and on good works, when they will not allow their errors and the worship of idols to be censured. Even right deeds offend them, as when a godly minister takes an honest wife. Such stumbling-blocks are not to be heeded. But scandal is given when men by false teaching or bad examples confirm others in their errors, and stir them up to imitate them, and so on. Of such scandals it is said in Matthew 18: "Woe to the man by whom the scandal comes," etc. It is greatly to be lamented that there are so many who have no regard either for men or for the divine name, but rashly do whatever pleases them, and are not ashamed of anything.

units.la: Tertio consideranda est aurea hæc sententia: Manus Dei nostri est super omnes requirentes eum in bonitate: robur vero & indignatio eius, super omnes qui derelinquunt eum.) Breue quidem est hoc dictum, sed si euoluamus & explicemus, videbimus amplitudinem rerum, quæ in eo continentur. Singula verba suam habent emphasim. Manus Dei est eius potentia & defensio. Addit, nostri Dei, qui promissiones eis insignes fecerat, & plura beneficia in eos contulerat. Est super omnes requirentes eum. Non paucos tantum, ne igitur deterreris tua indignitate aut infirmitate. Requirere Deum, in scriptura significat veram pœnitentiam ad eum couerti, eum colere, spem in eo collocare, eum inuocare, obtemperare eius mandatis. In bonitate, quidam iungunt cum manu Dei, vt idem sit quod manus eius bona: quidam ad quærentes Deum. Addit Antithesin, robur autem & ira, super omnes qui derelinquunt eum. Potentiam & iram suam declarat contra illos, qui ad eum non confugiunt vera fide & inuocatione, vel ab eo deficiunt, vt apostatæ quique respiciunt ad humana tantum prædidia, &c.
units.tr: Thirdly, this golden saying is to be considered: The hand of our God is upon all who seek him in goodness; but his strength and indignation are upon all who forsake him.) This saying is indeed brief, but if we unfold and explain it, we shall see the breadth of the matters contained in it. Each word has its own emphasis. "The hand of God" is his power and defence. He adds "of our God," who had made outstanding promises to them and had bestowed many benefits upon them. Is upon all who seek him. Not just a few; so do not let yourself be deterred by your unworthiness or weakness. To seek God, in Scripture, means to turn to him in true repentance, to worship him, to place hope in him, to call upon him, to obey his commandments. "In goodness": some join this with the hand of God, so that it means his good hand; others with those who seek God. He adds an antithesis: "but his strength and wrath are upon all who forsake him." He declares his power and his wrath against those who do not flee to him in true faith and invocation, or who fall away from him, such as apostates who look only to human props, and so on.

units.la: Similes sententiæ alibi quoque extant, vt Psalmo 37. Improbi excindentur, sed expectantes Iehouam hæreditate possidebunt terram. Psalmo 9. Non deseris quærentes te Iehoua, &c. Deuteronomio quarto capite, Cum quæsieris Deum tuum, inuenies eum, si tamen toto corde quæsieris, &c. Isaias 55.capite, Quærite Deum dum inueniri potest.Ieremiæ 29.cap. Quæretis me, & non inuenietis, nempe si animo hypocritico quæratis non vera fide. Quomodo aliquid quæramus, Lucæ decimoquinto ostenditur.In prouerbijs, Qui me quærunt vt argentum & aurum,me inuenient. Hæc sententia non tantum de singulis hominibus,sed de totis populis,regnis, vrbibus accipienda est. Etsi verò contrarium potius sæpenumero fieri videatur,vt cum impij florent:tamen cogitandum est,nondum vt prouerbio dicitur,omnium dierum soles occidisse.
units.tr: Similar sayings also appear elsewhere, as in Psalm 37: "The wicked shall be cut off, but those who wait upon Jehovah shall possess the land as an inheritance." Psalm 9: "Thou dost not forsake those who seek thee, O Jehovah," etc. Deuteronomy chapter 4: "When you seek your God, you will find him, if indeed you seek him with your whole heart," etc. Isaiah chapter 55: "Seek God while he may be found." Jeremiah chapter 29: "You will seek me and will not find me," namely if you seek with a hypocritical mind and not with true faith. How we ought to seek something is shown in Luke chapter 15. In Proverbs: "Those who seek me as silver and gold will find me." This saying is to be understood not only of single persons but of whole peoples, kingdoms and cities. Although the opposite often seems to happen, as when the wicked flourish, we must nevertheless consider that, as the proverb says, the suns of all days have not yet set.

units.la: Quarto loco, Deus preces eorum dicitur exaudiuisse, quod ex sequentibus fiet planius. Nostras quoque preces exaudiri certum est. Esaiæ 65. cap. promittit Deus suis:adhuc illis loquentibus exaudiam eos. Si non statim accipias quòd petis,accipies suo tempore. Deus enim certas habet causas, ob quas non statim mala à nobis depellat, aut bona quæ petimus conferat. Si dicas, sæpe nobis prorsus non dari quod petimus, respondeo,hoc ideo accidere, quod vel non petamus quæ petenda sunt,vel non eo modo quo petenda erant. Vitium non hæret in Deo,sed in nobis.De quo alibi plura diximus. Quod recte inchoamus & instituimus,feliciter succedit.
units.tr: In the fourth place, God is said to have heard their prayers, which will become clearer from what follows. That our prayers too are heard is certain. In Isaiah chapter 65 God promises his people: "While they are still speaking, I will hear them." If you do not receive immediately what you ask, you will receive it in its own time. For God has certain reasons why he does not at once drive evils away from us or bestow the goods we seek. If you say that often what we ask is not given to us at all, I answer that this happens either because we do not ask for the things that ought to be asked, or because we do not ask in the manner in which they ought to be asked. The fault does not cling to God but to us. We have said more about this elsewhere. What we rightly begin and undertake succeeds happily.

units.la: HOMILIA XXIX.
units.tr: HOMILY XXIX.

units.la: Deliguntur viri egregij qui donaria Hierosolyma deferant.
units.tr: Distinguished men are chosen to carry the gifts to Jerusalem.

units.la: 24 Separaui autem de principibus Sacerdotum duodecim, Serebiah, Hasabiah, & cum eis ex fratribus eorum decem.
units.tr: 24 And I set apart twelve of the chief priests, Serebiah, Hasabiah, and with them ten of their brothers.

units.la: 25 Et appendi eis argentum & aurum, & vasa illa, oblationem domus Dei nostri, quam obtulerant rex & consiliarij eius, & principes eius, & vniuersus Israel qui reperti fuerant.
units.tr: 25 And I weighed out to them the silver and the gold, and those vessels, the offering to the house of our God, which the king and his counsellors, and his princes, and all Israel who were present had offered.

units.la: 26 Appendi inquam in manibus eorum argenti talenta-sexcenta & quinquaginta, & vasa argentea centum talentorum, & auri centum talenta,
units.tr: 26 I weighed out, I say, into their hands six hundred and fifty talents of silver, and silver vessels of a hundred talents, and a hundred talents of gold,

units.la: 27 Et crateres aureos viginti, drachmarum mille: & le: & vasa area aurei coloris boni, duo, desiderabilia vt aurum.
units.tr: 27 And twenty golden bowls worth a thousand drachmas; and two vessels of fine bronze, as precious as gold.

units.la: 28 Postea dixi eis: Vos estis sanctitas Iehouæ, & vasa sanctitas: & argentum illud & aurum (estoblatio sponte facta Iehouæ Deo patrum nostrorum.
units.tr: 28 Then I said to them: You are holy to the LORD, and the vessels are holy; and the silver and the gold is a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of our fathers.

units.la: 29 Vigilate, et custodite, donec appendatis coram principibus Sacerdotum, & Leuitarum, & principibus familiarum Israelis in Ierusalaim in cubiculis domus Iehouæ.
units.tr: 29 Watch and keep them, until you weigh them before the chief priests and the Levites and the heads of the families of Israel in Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of the LORD.

units.la: 30 Susceperunt ergo Sacerdotes illi & Leuitæ pondus argenti, & auri, & vasorum, vt adducerent in Ierusalaim ad domum Dei nostri.
units.tr: 30 So the priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver and the gold and the vessels, to bring them to Jerusalem, to the house of our God.

units.la: QVanquam Esdras, populo iam ad fluuium congregato, neminem amplius expectaret: tamen iter non statim ingressus est, sed ieiunium ante indixit, vt ardentius iter faustum & felix à Deo precarentur. Sequitur Esdram quosdam delegisse, quibus donaria, de quibus supra diximus, commisserit: Deinde eos adhortatum esse, vt bona fide ea custodirent. Tertio quomodo illa donaria, vt Hierosolyma perferrent, acceperint.
units.tr: Although Ezra, now that the people had gathered by the river, expected no one else, he did not set out at once, but first proclaimed a fast, so that they might pray more earnestly to God for a safe and prosperous journey. The passage goes on to say that Ezra chose certain men and entrusted to them the gifts mentioned above; then that he exhorted them to guard these faithfully; and third, how they received those gifts to carry them to Jerusalem.

units.la: 1 Delegit duodecim de principibus sacerdotum & de Leuitis, vt postea dicitur, nempe Serebiam & Hasabiam, & cum illis fratres, id est, cognatos eorum decem, ex eadem enim stirpe orti erant. Illos ipsos voluit fuisse, quorum supra in hoc capite, facta est mentio. At Maheli a quo Serebias descendit, ipsius Leui nepos fuit, ex Merari filio. Hasabias quoque ex filijs Merari diserte fuisse dicitur: Quomodo ergo potuerunt principes esse sacerdotum, cum hæc familia tantum habuerit Leuitas? Potest ergo fieri, vt alij potius fuerint ex familia Aaronis, quæ sola sacerdotes dedit, ijsdem nominibus appellati.
units.tr: 1 He chose twelve of the chief priests and of the Levites, as is said afterwards, namely Serebiah and Hasabiah, and with them their brothers, that is, their kinsmen, ten in number, for they had sprung from the same stock. He meant them to be those whose names were mentioned above in this chapter. But Mahli, from whom Serebiah descended, was a grandson of Levi himself, through his son Merari. Hasabiah too is expressly said to have been of the sons of Merari. How, then, could they be chief priests, when this family had only Levites? It may be that others, rather from the family of Aaron, which alone furnished priests, were called by the same names.

units.la: Illis appendit ad libram (nimirum ponderibus Hebraicis) aurum, argentum, & vasa, quæ rex, principes, & populus, qui in Babylone erat, magno numero contulerant ad visum templi. Speciatim recensetilla donaria, 650. talenta argenti, & vasa argentea centum talentorum. Auri centum talenta: crateras, pelues vel phialas aureos 20. habentes solidos vel drachmas mille. Et duo vasa aerea magni precij, non dissimilia auro.) Apud veteres teste Plinio libro 34 capite 1.2. aes tanto fuit in precio, vt argenti quoque atque auri precium aequarit. Corinthium aes ex omnibus maximè laudatur. Vergilius quoque libro 2. Geor gicorum inter res in maximo precio habitas numerat Ephyraea aera, id est, Corinthia. Prius enim haec vrbs Ephyra dicta fuit. Postea omnia vasa ex aere elegantia, Corinthia sunt appellata.
units.tr: He weighed out to them, by the balance (that is, by Hebrew weights), the gold, the silver and the vessels which the king, the princes and the people who were in Babylon had contributed in great numbers for the adornment of the temple. The gifts are listed one by one: 650 talents of silver, and silver vessels of a hundred talents; a hundred talents of gold; twenty golden bowls, cups or phials, of a thousand solidi or drachmas; and two bronze vessels of great value, not unlike gold. (Among the ancients, according to Pliny, book 34, chapters 1 and 2, bronze was held in such esteem that its price equalled that of silver and gold. Corinthian bronze is praised above all others. Virgil too, in book 2 of the Georgics, counts Ephyrean bronze, that is, Corinthian, among the things held in the highest value. For this city was formerly called Ephyra. Afterwards all fine vessels of bronze were called Corinthian.)

units.la: Talentum non est vnius generis. Si ad nostra tempora deducatur, maxima fuerunt illa donaria. Aliquot vt vocamus, tonnæ auri & argenti facti & infecti, &c. Non autem loquitur scriptura de vasis quæ Babylonem translata fuerant à Nabuchodonosore, sed de nouis quæ Deo dedicarant. Posteris quoq; temporibus, ad templum Hierosolymitanum non tantū Iudæi hinc inde dispersi, sed etiam gentiles dona miserunt. Augustum Cæsarem, scribit Iosephus, absentem templum soluisse, & eximijs donarijs ornasse.
units.tr: A talent is not of one kind. If it is reckoned in our own money, those gifts were very great: some, as we would say, tuns of gold and silver, both wrought and unwrought, and so on. But Scripture does not speak of the vessels which Nebuchadnezzar had carried off to Babylon, but of new ones which they had dedicated to God. In later times too, not only Jews scattered here and there but also Gentiles sent gifts to the temple at Jerusalem. Josephus writes that Augustus Caesar, though absent, paid for the temple and adorned it with splendid gifts.

units.la: Cur autem nec plures nec pauciores quàm duodecim delegerit, non constat. Forte propter 12. patriarchas, à quibus totidem tribus nomen habebant, id factum est. Christus quoque eandem ob causam duodecim apostolos creditur elegisse.
units.tr: Why he chose neither more nor fewer than twelve is not clear. Perhaps it was done on account of the twelve patriarchs, from whom the twelve tribes had their names. Christ too is believed to have chosen twelve apostles for the same reason.

units.la: Curæ & diligentiæ horum virorum, committit hæc donaria, principum & aliorum liberalitate ad vsum sacrum collata, vt per totum iter diligenter curent, dum imponuntur iumentis vel carris, & deponuntur. Dicit enim eos esse sanctuarium Domini, hoc est, consecratos Domino, & vasa quoq; Domino dedicata esse, & sponte oblata. Quare eos hæc diligenter custodire debere, donec Hierosolyma perferentes, principibus sacerdotum & præcipuis patribus Israelis, ea tradant in gazophylacijs vel exedris templi.
units.tr: He entrusts these gifts, collected for sacred use from the generosity of the princes and others, to the care and diligence of these men, so that they look after them carefully throughout the whole journey, while they are loaded onto beasts or wagons and unloaded again. For he says that they are the sanctuary of the LORD, that is, consecrated to the LORD, and that the vessels too are dedicated to the LORD and were offered freely. Therefore they ought to guard these things diligently until, carrying them to Jerusalem, they hand them over to the chief priests and the leading fathers of Israel, to be placed in the treasuries or exedrae of the temple.

units.la: Illi verò pondus auri & argenti atq; vasorum acceperunt, vt ad templum deferrent. Postea eos eodem numero & pondere principibus sacerdotum & senioribus illa dedisse narratur.
units.tr: They received the weight of the gold, the silver and the vessels, to carry them to the temple. Afterwards it is related that they handed them over to the chief priests and elders, in the same number and by the same weight.

units.la: Vsus.
units.tr: Use.

units.la: 1 Disce quales deligendi sint procuratores bonorum ecclesiæ. Esdras enim hæc donaria non cuiuis obuio committit, sed viris præstantibus, de quibus spes erat, quòd bona fide essent acturi. In nouo Testamento apostoli primum opes Ecclesiæ procurarunt, postea crescente ecclesia, Actorum capite 6. couocarunt discipulos, dixerunq; ad eos: Dispicite ex vobis viros septe idoneo testimonio ornatos, plenos spiritu S. & sapientes, quos
units.tr: 1 Learn what kind of men should be chosen as stewards of the Church's goods. Ezra does not entrust these gifts to just anyone who comes along, but to outstanding men from whom there was hope that they would act in good faith. In the New Testament the apostles first looked after the Church's resources. Later, when the Church had grown, they called the disciples together, as recorded in Acts chapter 6, and said to them: "Look out among you for seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, whom

units.la: Ass. Quibus bo na ecclesiæ committenda. quos præficiamus huic negotio. Hoc consilium placuit fidelibus, delegerunt Stephanum plenum fide & Spiritu sancto, & alios, &c. In 1. ad Timoth. 2. quales diaconi, & etiam ipsorum uxores esse debeant, ostenditur. Postea temporibus Laurentius diaconus, maluit vstulari, quàm ecclesiæ thesauros tyranno tradere vel prodere. Si procuratio bonorum ecclesiæ malis committatur, pauperes fraudantur: magistratus malè audit.
units.tr: Marginal note: To whom the goods of the church are to be committed. Whom we may appoint to this business. "This saying pleased the whole multitude, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, and others, etc." In 1 Tim. 2 it is shown what kind of deacons they should be, and also what their wives should be like. Later, in the time of Laurence the deacon, he preferred to be roasted rather than hand over or betray the Church's treasures to a tyrant. If the management of the Church's goods is entrusted to bad men, the poor are defrauded and the magistrate is ill spoken of.

units.la: 2. Quod nam sit officium, vel quomodo se gerere debeat, procuratores thesaurorum ecclesiæ. Vigilare, custodire opes sacras, & in vsus legitimos distribuere debent, semperque cogitare quòd thesauri illi Dei sint, quodq; magnum sit scelus rem Deo consecratam in vsum prophanum convertere. Non solùm hominibus accepti & expensi danda erit ratio, sed etiam Deo, quem nemo potest fallere. Si officium suum diligenter exequuti fuerint, premium ferent, sin minus pœnas dabunt & graues quidem. Exempla habes in rege Balthasare apud Danielem: in Achane in libro Iosue, in Ananía & Saphyra. Etiam in sacrilegis apud Ethnicos.
units.tr: 2. What the duty of the stewards of the Church's treasures is, and how they should conduct themselves. They ought to watch over and guard the sacred resources and distribute them for lawful uses, and they should always keep in mind that these treasures belong to God, and that it is a great wickedness to turn a thing consecrated to God to profane use. An account must be given not only to men, of what has been received and spent, but also to God, whom no one can deceive. If they carry out their duty diligently, they will receive a reward; if not, they will pay penalties, and severe ones indeed. You have examples in King Belshazzar in Daniel, in Achan in the book of Joshua, in Ananias and Sapphira, and also in sacrilegious men among the heathen.

units.la: Quod si Esdras tam diligenter curauit, vt vasa hæc, aurea, argentea & ærea, idoneis hominibus committerentur, qui illa ex Babylone Hierosolymam transferrent, quanto magis curandum, vt viua Dei vasa fidis hominibus committantur, à quibus ex hoc mundo, in cœlestem Hierosolymam perducantur? Homines vasis comparat scriptura. Paulus Act. 9. σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς, hoc est, vas electum dicitur, quo Christus vsus est ad conuertendas gentes. Apostolus ad Romanos 9. scribit de vasis iræ & gloriæ. 1. Petri 3. mulier dicitur vas infirmius. Vasa fictilia & vitrea, fragilia sunt, cauendum igitur ne ea confringantur. 1. Thes. 4. 4. Sciat vestrum vnusquisq; suum vas (σκεῦος) possidere cum sanctificatione & honore, vbi vas corpus significat. Accipitur etiam pro anima. Ministri ecclesiæ, quorum fidei committa sunt illa vasa, cogitent se consecratos esse Christo Domino, & vasa illa sanguine eius purgata esse, ideo omni studio, cura atq; diligentia cauendum, ne illa pereant aut frangantur sua negligentia aut perfidia. Reposcet Dominus rationem de illis, quos sanguine suo mercatus est. Parentes quoque quibus Deus liberos dedit, pædagogi, magistri, hospites quibus liberi committuntur, cogitent illos quasi depositum esse, quod custodiendum eis datum sit, fideiq; eorum commissum. Proinde fideles sint depositarij.
units.tr: If Ezra took such care that these vessels, of gold, silver and bronze, were committed to suitable men who would carry them from Babylon to Jerusalem, how much more ought we to take care that the living vessels of God are committed to faithful men, by whom they may be led out of this world into the heavenly Jerusalem? Scripture compares men to vessels. Paul in Acts 9 is called a chosen vessel [σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς], that is, a vessel of election, which Christ used to convert the Gentiles. The apostle in Romans 9 writes of vessels of wrath and of glory. In 1 Peter 3 a wife is called the weaker vessel. Earthen and glass vessels are fragile, so care must be taken that they are not broken. In 1 Thess. 4:4: "Let each one of you know how to possess his own vessel [σκεῦος] in sanctification and honour," where vessel signifies the body. It is also taken for the soul. The ministers of the Church, to whose faith those vessels are committed, should consider that they have been consecrated to Christ the Lord, and that those vessels have been cleansed by his blood. Therefore with all zeal, care and diligence they must take heed that those vessels do not perish or get broken through their negligence or faithlessness. The Lord will require an account of those whom he has purchased with his own blood. Parents also, to whom God has given children, and tutors, teachers, and the hosts to whom children are entrusted, should consider that they are like a deposit, given to them to keep and committed to their faithfulness. Therefore let the faithful be trustworthy keepers.

units.la: 3. Exemplum obedientiæ, superioribus ab inferioribus præstandæ, hoc loco insigne habemus.12.illi viri, onus illud custodiæ, in se recipiunt absq; recusatione. Non dicunt, cur illud ad libram appendis, ac si nobis non sit fidendum? Quantus labor erit subinde onerare & exonerare asinos, camelos, hoc argento & auro? Conijcis nos in certissimum vitæ periculum, latrones nobis insidiantur, si sciant nos thesauris præfectos esse? Quam vtilitatem habebimus ex nostris laboribus? Potuissent hæc & alia afferre ad inobedientiam suam excusandam, sed quia vera fide præditi sunt, statim obediunt Esdræ. Idem nos faciamus erga magistratus, ministros ecclesiæ, parentes, heros nostros, nisi præcipiant nobis, quæ verbo Dei è diametro repugnant.
units.tr: 3. Here we have a notable example of the obedience which inferiors owe to their superiors. 12. Those men took upon themselves that burden of guarding without refusal. They do not say, "Why do you weigh this out by the pound, as if we were not to be trusted? How great a labour it will be to load and unload asses and camels again and again with this silver and gold! You are throwing us into the most certain danger of our lives; robbers will lie in wait for us if they know we are in charge of the treasures! What benefit will we get from our labours?" They could have brought these and other such arguments to excuse their disobedience, but because they were endowed with true faith, they at once obey Ezra. Let us do the same towards magistrates, ministers of the Church, parents and our masters, unless they command us things which flatly contradict the Word of God.

units.la: HOMILIA XXX.
units.tr: HOMILY XXX.

units.la: Esdras cum populo venit Hierosolymam.
units.tr: Ezra comes with the people to Jerusalem.

units.la: 31 Profecti autem sumus à flumine Ahava duodecima (die) mensis primi, vt iremus in Ierusalaim: & manus Dei nostri fuit super nos, eruitq; nos de manu inimici & insidiatoris in via.
units.tr: 31 We set out from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month, to go to Jerusalem. The hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from the hand of the enemy and of the ambusher on the way.

units.la: 32 Tandem peruenimus Ierusalaim, & mansimus ibi tribus diebus.
units.tr: 32 At last we came to Jerusalem and stayed there three days.

units.la: 33 Die autem quarta appensum est argentum, & aurum, & vasa (illa) in domo Dei nostri, per manum Meremoth filij Vrijah sacerdotis, & cum eo (erant) Elazar filius Pinhas: cum illis vero (erat) Iozabad filius Iesua, & Noadiah filius Bimmi Leuitæ.
units.tr: 33 On the fourth day the silver, the gold and the vessels were weighed out in the house of our God, by the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest. With him was Eleazar the son of Phinehas, and with them Jozabad the son of Jeshua and Noadiah the son of Binnui the Levite.

units.la: 34 In numero & pondere per omnia: & descriptum est vniuersum illud pondus tempore illo.
units.tr: 34 Everything was counted by number and weight, and the whole weight was recorded at that time.

units.la: 35 (Porro) qui venerant de captiuitate, filij transmigrationis, obtulerunt holocausta Deo Israelis, vitulos duodecim pro toto Israele, arietes nonaginta sex, agnos septuaginta septem, hircos (sacrificij pro) peccato duodecim, omnia in holocaustum Iehouæ.
units.tr: 35 Moreover, those who had come out of captivity, the children of the exile, offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bullocks for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve he-goats as a sin offering, all as a burnt offering to the LORD (Iehovah).

units.la: 36 Et tradiderunt leges regis satrapis eius, & ducibus cibus (qui erant) trans Flumen: & exaltauerunt populum, & domum Dei.
units.tr: 36 They also delivered the king's commissions to his satraps and to the governors beyond the River; and they furthered the people and the house of God.

units.la: QVomodo Esdras cum suo populo, se ad profectionem compararit, supra explicatum est: sequitur quomodo Hierosolyma peruenerint, quid ibi fecerint, & quomodo satrapæ regis se erga illos gesserint.
units.tr: Above it was explained how Ezra and his people made ready for the journey. What follows is how they reached Jerusalem, what they did there, and how the king's satraps behaved toward them.

units.la: Esdras commemorat quomodo iter institutum feliciter confecerint. Domini enim manum, hoc est, gratiam & auxilium super eos fuisse, eosque eripuisse ex manibus, id est, poteestate hostium, & eorum qui in via eis insidiati sunt. Profectio illa trium mensium fuit. Primo mense, hoc est, Nisan, egressi sunt, & quinto mense appulerunt Hierosolymis, supra 7. cap. Non autem defuisse prædones, qui in eos irruissent, nisi Deus suum populum protexisset, eosque ab eis liberasset, ex his verbis intelligitur. In magnis eum illis solitudinibus Arabes, instar Ziganorum incertis sedibus vagantur: non habent proprias regiones: figunt tabernacula in desertis, vbi aquam & pascua inueniunt, postea quæruntalia loca. Nihil habent nisi quod rapto acquirunt. Nullus magistratus potest illos in ordinem redigere, omnes eos timentes ex improuiso irruentes in pagos, oppida, ea diripiunt, &c. Hi faciè extremum agmen carpere potuissent, vt Amalechitæ fecerunt Israelitis in deserto.
units.tr: Ezra recounts how they happily completed the journey they had undertaken. The hand of the Lord, that is, his grace and help, was upon them, and it rescued them from the hands, that is, the power, of their enemies and of those who lay in wait for them on the way. That journey lasted three months. They set out in the first month, that is Nisan, and in the fifth month they arrived at Jerusalem, as stated above in chapter 7. That robbers did not attack them, however, unless God had protected his people and freed them from these men, is understood from these words. In those great deserts the Arabs wander like Gypsies with no fixed abode. They have no territories of their own. They pitch their tents in the wilderness where they find water and pasture, and afterwards they seek other such places. They have nothing except what they acquire by plunder. No magistrate can bring them into order. Everyone fears them, since they fall without warning upon villages and towns and sack them, and so on. They could easily have fallen upon the rear of the column, as the Amalekites did to the Israelites in the wilderness.

units.la: Profectionem illam paucis complectitur Esdras, facile enim quisque potest cogitare, quàm laboriosum & molestum sit, tam longum iter cum pueris, mulieribus & impedimentis conficere: quàm varia quotidie accidant in itinere, illa baiulat infan tem, hic trahit ægrum, sæpe sub diuo pernoctandum est, &c.
units.tr: Ezra sums up that journey in a few words, for anyone can easily imagine how laborious and troublesome it is to complete so long a journey with children, women and baggage: how many different things happen on the road every day; one carries an infant, another drags a sick man, and often one must spend the night under the open sky, and so on.

units.la: Discimus ex hoc loco, neminem illos lædere posse, siue priuatim, siue publicè, qui Deum habent auxiliatorem & protectorem. Si Deus pro nobis, exclamat Apostolus ad Romanos 8. capite, quis contra nos? Vellet multi nos opprelfos, sed Deus non vult. E contra si Deus manu suam ab aliquo subtrahit, non potest à quoquam defendi, & ex malis liberari.
units.tr: From this passage we learn that no one can harm those who have God as their helper and protector, whether privately or publicly. "If God is for us," the Apostle cries out in the eighth chapter of Romans, "who can be against us?" Many might wish to oppress us, but God does not wish it. On the other hand, if God withdraws his hand from someone, that person cannot be defended by anyone nor freed from evils.

units.la: Videmus etiam preces nostras, non esse fruftraneas & inutiles, sed à Deo exaudiri. Precati erant, vt in via à Deo custodirentur, hoc factum esse, ex hoc loco apparet.
units.tr: We also see that our prayers are not vain and useless, but are heard by God. They had prayed that they might be kept safe by God on the way, and that this was granted is clear from this passage.

units.la: Quid fecerunt postquam Hierosolyma peruenerunt?
units.tr: What did they do after they reached Jerusalem?

units.la: 1. Postquam commorati sunt ibi tribus diebus, quos respirationi dederunt. Defatigati enim erant ex itinere. Ouidius dicit:
units.tr: 1. After they had stayed there three days, they gave themselves to rest, for they were worn out from the journey. Ovid says:

units.la: Quod caret alterna requie durabile non est.
units.tr: What lacks alternating rest is not lasting.

units.la: 2. Quarto die vt reuersi sunt, tradiderunt thesauros. Circumstantiæ attingûtur, qui, quádo, quid, vbi, cui, quomodo red diderint. Sacerdotes illi & Leuitæ 12. appenderunt donaria sibi commissa, aurum, argentum & vasa, nimirum ponderibus Hebræorum, in templo, per manum Meremoth, præsentibus tribus Leuitis. Cur quarto demum die illa donaria reddiderint, scire non possum. Forte nō tantum fuit periculum à furibus & sacrilegis, vt nostro tempore. Negligentiæ certè hoc non debet ascribi. Appenderút autem omnia, iuxta numerum & pondus. Atq; illo tempore pondus illud vniuersum est descriptum, & in rationes relatum. Quàm feliciter & diligenter commissum sibi munus exequuti sint, testatur hæc historia. Si hodie exacta ratio ab illis qui pecuniam publicam tractát, exigeretur, quis similem fidem & diligentiam se reperturum speraret?
units.tr: 2. On the fourth day, when they had returned, they handed over the treasures. The circumstances are touched upon: who, when, what, where, to whom and how they delivered them. Those priests and Levites weighed out the gifts entrusted to them, the gold, silver and vessels, by the weights of the Hebrews, in the temple, through the hand of Meremoth, in the presence of three Levites. I cannot know why they delivered those gifts only on the fourth day. Perhaps there was not as much danger from thieves and sacrilegious men as there is in our time. This certainly should not be ascribed to negligence. They weighed everything according to number and weight. And at that time the whole weight was recorded and entered in the accounts. How happily and diligently they carried out the duty entrusted to them, this history bears witness. If today an exact account were demanded from those who handle public money, who would hope to find similar faithfulness and diligence?

units.la: 3. Sacrificasse quoq; leguntur. Exprimûtur autem hæcir cumstantiæ, quis sacrificarit, quid, cui, pro quibus, quare. Filij captiuitatis, qui ex captiuitate redierunt, sacrificia retulerút, nempe holocausta 12. iuuencos vel vitulos, & totidem hircos peccati, id est, in sacrificiû pro peccato. 96. arietes, 77. agnos, omnia in holocaustum Domino.
units.tr: 3. They are also read to have offered sacrifices. The circumstances are expressed: who sacrificed, what, to whom, for whom, and why. The children of the captivity, who had returned from captivity, brought offerings: namely, burnt offerings of twelve young bulls or calves, and as many he-goats of sin, that is, for a sin offering; ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, all as a burnt offering to the Lord.

units.la: Holocaustum fuit sacrificij genus, quod totum igne consumebatur, ita vt nihil præter pellem sacerdoti cederet. Hoc constabat iuuenco vel vitulo, item agno vel capro, propter pauper tatem, etiam turtures vel columbas sacrificare licebat. Ritus holocaustorum continetur in libro Mosis. Offerebatur pro peccatis singulorum & totius populi. Non quòd holocaustum per se vim haberet expiandi peccata, sed quod typus esset sacrificij tandem in ara crucis peragendi, quo peccatis deletis, Deus nobis placandus esset. Pro toto Israele.) Non pro seipsis tantum, sed reliquis quoq; fratribus, etiam illis, qui in Babylone & Media permanserant, fortasis propter 12. tribus Israelis, totidem tauros & hircos immolarunt.
units.tr: The burnt offering was a kind of sacrifice that was wholly consumed by fire, so that nothing went to the priest except the hide. It consisted of a young bull or calf, likewise of a lamb or a goat; on account of poverty it was also permitted to sacrifice turtledoves or pigeons. The rite of the burnt offerings is contained in the book of Moses. It was offered for the sins of individuals and of the whole people. Not that the burnt offering in itself had the power to expiate sins, but because it was a type of the sacrifice that was at last to be completed on the altar of the cross, by which, with sins blotted out, God is to be appeased for us. For all Israel. Not only for themselves, but also for their fellow brethren, even those who had remained in Babylon and Media, perhaps on account of the twelve tribes of Israel, they sacrificed as many bullocks and he-goats.

units.la: Videntur etiam his sacrificijs, Deo gratias agere voluisse, quòd respondentem votis suis successum dedisset. Ethnici quoque liberati ex magnis malis, vel cum vias suas ad optatum exitum perduxerunt, sacrificia sua laudis habuerunt.
units.tr: By these sacrifices they seem also to have wished to give thanks to God, because he had granted success that answered their prayers. Heathens too, when they were freed from great evils, or when they brought their ways to the desired end, held sacrifices of praise.

units.la: Non satis est incipere res arduas, cum invocatione auxilij diuini: sed si feliciter cadunt, gratos nos debemus Deo exhibere. Si Deus vel te, vel alios eripit ex Babylonica captiuitate, si ex aliis malis liberat, puta bello, fame, malorum insidijs, si bona tibi confert, sacrificium laudis illi offerte, corpus & animam tuam illi consecrato, pauperibus eleemosynas largas distribuito, peccata agnosce, & veniam precare.
units.tr: It is not enough to begin difficult undertakings with the invocation of divine help; if they turn out happily, we ought to show ourselves grateful to God. If God delivers you or others from Babylonian captivity, if he frees you from other evils, such as war, famine, or the snares of the wicked, if he bestows good things upon you, offer to him a sacrifice of praise, consecrate to him your body and soul, distribute generous alms to the poor, acknowledge your sins, and pray for pardon.

units.la: 4. Adhaec regis epistolam vel diploma dederunt eius satrapis vel praefectis atque ducibus, qui trans fluuium erant. Res potuit dilationem pati. Alias si literae alicui committuntur ad aliquem perferendae, statim curandae sunt, non diu detinendae.
units.tr: 4. In addition they gave the king's letter, or decree, to his satraps and prefects and governors who were beyond the river. The matter could have suffered delay. Otherwise, if letters are entrusted to someone to be delivered to another, they must be attended to at once, not kept back for long.

units.la: 5. Matrimonia correxisse, infra audiemus.
units.tr: 5. We shall hear later how they corrected the marriages.

units.la: Vltimo loco habetur, Satrapas regis atque duces, populi Iudaici & templi curam & patrocinium suscepisse. Obseruantiam eorum vides erga regem. Qui pridem volebant impedire templum, nunc exaltant, hoc est, magnificiunt: prosequuntur & populum & templum fauore, eosque iuuant & promouent, postquam id suo regi gratum esse intelligunt. Multi maiore odio & inuidia exarsisent & licet hoc rex decreuisset: tamen ipsi noluissent illud exequi. Vnicum scriptum regis illos monuit, vt quod gratum illi fuit fecerint: merito igitur tot scripta Regis regum nos commouere debent, vt in ipsum credamus, & fideles suos nobis commendatos habeamus. Hoc enim ipsi placere, illa locupletissime testantur.
units.tr: Lastly, it is noted that the king's satraps and governors took up the care and protection of the Jewish people and of the temple. You see their deference toward the king. Those who had formerly wished to hinder the temple now exalt it, that is, they magnify it; they favour both the people and the temple with goodwill, and they help and promote them, once they understood that this was pleasing to their king. Many would have blazed with greater hatred and envy, and even though the king had decreed this, they themselves would not have wanted to carry it out. A single written command of the king admonished them to do what was pleasing to him. Therefore the many writings of the King of kings ought to move us to believe in him, and to hold his faithful servants commended to us. For these writings most abundantly attest that this is pleasing to him.

units.la: CAPVT IX.
units.tr: CHAPTER IX.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXI. Querela de peccato Iudaeorum ad Esdram delato.
units.tr: HOMILY XXXI. A complaint about the sin of the Jews, brought to Ezra.

units.la: Quumá perfecissent haec, accesserunt ad me principes, dicendo, Non seperauit se populus Israelis, & Sacerdotes, & Leuitae a populis terrarum: in abominationibus illorum Chenaanaeorum, Hittheorum, Perizaeorum, Iebusaeorum, Ammonitarum, & Moabitarum, Misritarum & Emoraeorum, (sunt abominationes eorum.)
units.tr: When they had finished these things, the leaders came to me, saying: "The people of Israel, the priests and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands, with their abominations, those of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians and Amorites (for these are their abominations)."

units.la: 2 Quia sulerunt de filiabus eorum sibi & filijs suis: miscuméque semen sanctum cum populis terrarum: & manus principum & magistratuum fuit in prævari-catione ista, prima.
units.tr: "For they have taken some of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, and the holy seed has been mingled with the peoples of the lands; and the hand of the princes and magistrates has been first in this trespass."

units.la: HOC & sequenti Capite, causa matrimonialis describitur, vel factum singularis fortitudinis, iustitiæ, fidei, prudentiæ : Ideoque diligenter cognoscendum erit. Summa hæc est: Cum Esdras Hierosolyma peruenisset, significatum ei est, quod quidam præcipui nominis, duͤctis alienigenis vxoribus, priores eiecerint. Quibus auditis Esdras reipsa dolorem suum testatus, preces effudit, petens à Deo, vt populo sit propitius. Suo autem exemplo fecit, vt multi virtriusque sexus accurrerent, & in lachrymas effunderentur. Sachanias vero hortatur eum, vt surgat, & ei spem facit, quòd alienigenas vxores dimissuri sint. Esdras iureiurando adegit principes sacerdotum & Leuitarum, totumque populum, vt hoc facerent. Indicitur coetus in urbe Hierosolymorum, graui poena constituta, propter illud negotium. Esdras ostendit quàm graviter peccarint, hortatur eos ad pœnitentiam. Illi fatentur se peccasse, & obedientiam promittunt. In calce Capitis, nomina iudicum, & illorum qui alienigenas dimiserunt, recitantur.
units.tr: This chapter and the next describe a matter of marriage, or a deed of singular courage, justice, faith and prudence, and so it must be studied carefully. The gist is this: when Ezra had arrived at Jerusalem, he was told that certain men of note had taken foreign wives and had put away the earlier ones. On hearing this, Ezra showed his grief by his deeds, and poured out prayers, asking God to be merciful to the people. By his example, many of both sexes ran together and dissolved in tears. Shechaniah urges him to rise and gives him hope that the men will dismiss the foreign wives. Ezra binds the chief priests and Levites and the whole people by oath to do this. An assembly is called in the city of Jerusalem, with a severe penalty set for those who did not attend, because of this business. Ezra shows how gravely they have sinned and exhorts them to repentance. They confess that they have sinned and promise obedience. At the end of the chapter, the names of the judges and of those who dismissed the foreign wives are recorded.

units.la: Hæc historia multiplicem habet vtilitatem. Discimus ex ea, quo pacto magistratus & priuati se gerere debeant, quando aperta scelera in populo grassantur, nempe non esse dissimulanda, &c. Deinde quàm religiosè matrimonium colendum sit, &c. Item alia de quibus suo loco.
units.tr: This history has many uses. From it we learn how magistrates and private persons ought to conduct themselves when open crimes spread among the people: namely, that they must not be overlooked, and so on. Then, how religiously marriage must be honoured, and so on. Likewise other matters, which will be dealt with in their place.

units.la: Quo ad hoc nonum caput, duo potissimum in eo tractantur. Primum est querela delata ad Esdram, de peccato Israelitarum. Alterum quomodo Esdras se gesserit. Reipsa dolorem suum testatus est, & preces ardentes ad Deum effudit.
units.tr: As for this ninth chapter, two main things are treated in it. The first is the complaint brought to Ezra about the sin of the Israelites. The second is how Ezra conducted himself. He showed his grief by his deeds, and poured out fervent prayers to God.

units.la: Videamus iam primam partem, nempe querelam quæ peruenit ad Esdram à viris primarijs, de alienis vxoribus. Quuḿ perfecissent hæc.) Quæ in fine præcedentis Capitis commemorantur, cum thesauros sacros appendissent, sacrificia obtulissent, & regijs præfectis diploma regis tradidissent, accesserunt ad Esdram viri primarij & boni, quibus salus populi curæ erat, dicentes, Populum Israelis, Sacerdotes & Leuitas, non separasse à populis terrarum, hoc est, quæ in his terris vel regionibus fuerant, Chananæorum, &c. vel etiam vicinarum, quæ idololatræ & gentiles erant, nominantur enim Ægyptij.
units.tr: Let us now look at the first part, namely the complaint that reached Ezra from the leading men about the foreign wives. When they had finished these things. The things recorded at the end of the previous chapter, when they had weighed out the sacred treasures, offered sacrifices, and handed the king's decree to the royal officials, the leading and good men came to Ezra, to whom the welfare of the people was a concern, saying that the people of Israel, the priests and the Levites, had not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands; that is, those who were in these lands or regions, the Canaanites, and so on; or even neighbouring ones, who were idolaters and Gentiles, for the Egyptians are named.

units.la: Accusatio populi. Populus terrarum. In abominationibus eorum.) Hoc est, moribus illos referre, eadem facere, quæ faciebant proscripti illi populi. Numeri 20. Deut.12.18. & multis alijs locis, de eorum sceleribus legitur. Seipsum mox explicans, dicit: Eos sibi & filijs suis accepisse de filiabus illorum vxores, quæ eos ad cultum deorum alienorum pel lexerunt. Mistumq; est semen sanctum cum populis terrarum.) Qui sanctus populus esse debuerunt, se miscentes cum Ethnicis vxoribus polluti sunt. Et manus principum & magistratuum fuit in prævaricatione ista, prima.) Hoc est, principes & magistratus, qui prohibere alios debuerunt, omnium primi ceperunt hoc pacto violare legem Dei, quæ extat Deut.7. & ab Ioel.2.3. cap. repetitur, suoq; exemplo alios permouerunt vt idem facerent.
units.tr: The accusation of the people. The peoples of the lands. In their abominations. That is, that they imitated them in manners and did the same things as those condemned peoples did. Numbers 20; Deut. 12 and 18, and many other places, tell of their crimes. Soon explaining himself, he says that they had taken for themselves and their sons wives from their daughters, who had enticed them to the worship of foreign gods. And the holy seed has been mingled with the peoples of the lands. Those who ought to have been a holy people were defiled by mixing themselves with heathen wives. And the hand of the princes and magistrates has been first in this trespass. That is, the princes and magistrates, who ought to have restrained others, were the first of all to begin to break God's law in this way, which stands in Deut. 7 and is repeated in Joel 2:3, and by their example moved others to do the same.

units.la: Res, vt planius intelligas, ita habet. Multi qui primo ascenderunt Hierosolyma venerunt cum Zerobabele, iamque 45. annum agebant in patria, spretis vxoribus suis senio confectis, contra fidem matrimonij eas dimiserunt, & iuniores alienigenas duxerunt, vt ex 2. Malachiæ intelligitur, qui hoc nomine eos corripit. Dupliciter peccarunt. Primum enim, repudiatio illa per se vitiosa erat: Deinde vetita fuerunt connubiacum gentilibus. Venerunt igitur viri pij & boni ad Esdram, metuentes ne denuo à Deo punirentur, & expositi sunt illi quomodo res habeant, vt de remedio maturè cogitaret, & Dei iram ab eis auerteret.
units.tr: So that you may understand it more clearly, the matter stands thus. Many who first went up to Jerusalem came with Zerubbabel, and by now they had been in their homeland for forty-five years. Having scorned their wives, worn out with age, they put them away against the marriage covenant and took younger foreign women, as is understood from Malachi 2, where he rebukes them for this. They sinned in two ways. First, the repudiation was itself sinful; second, they were forbidden to marry Gentiles. Therefore godly and good men came to Ezra, fearing that they would again be punished by God, and they explained to him how matters stood, so that he might think early about a remedy and turn God's wrath away from them.

units.la: Vsus huius loci.
units.tr: The use of this passage.

units.la: 1. Discimus semper fore homines, quibus sceleria diffliciant, & sibi à ventura ira diuina metuant, &c.
units.tr: 1. We learn that there will always be men whom wickedness displeases, who fear the divine wrath to come, and so on.

units.la: 2. Magistratui & & ministris ecclesiæ, illa indicanda esse, quæ contra bonas leges committuntur, ne Dei offensam incurramus. Audis enim viros magnos hoc fecisse, qui nequaquam accusandi sunt, quòd iniustè fecerint, quodq; fuerint sycophantæ. Nemo enim tacere aut dissimulare debet, si quid cōtra verbum Dei agitur. Iosephus hoc nomine laudatur, quòd fratrum suorū peccata patri retulit: non ex inuidia, odio, ambitione, auaritia, (vt quadruplatores qui ex accusatione quadruplum lucrifacie bant) sed vt illa emendaret. Multum igitur refert quo impulsu & quâ ob finem, quis deferat peccata ad magistratū, an impulsu, gloriæ Dei, salutis proximi id faciat, vtq; malū auferatur, an verò ex prauis affectibus. Detractio & calumnia mala est, cum nō aut heri, aut alijs quibus debebamus, peccata aliorum detegimus. Dan.3.cap. Chaldæi socios Danielis ex odio & inuidia apud regem accusant, quòd legè eius violarint. Dan. 6. diligenter irueftigarunt,vt aliquod crimen aduersus Danielem inuenirent in regis negotijs, tandem efficiût vt rex legem ferat,ne quis intra {}30.dies aliquid petat nisi à rege,quòd cum Daniel non faceret, mox eum accusarunt.Ecclesia Dei nunquam caruit huiuscemo di accusatoribus & delatoribus,imò proditoribus. Quid Paulo acciderit,testantur Acta Apostolica. Quid primæuæ ecclesiæ,ex Apologijs Christianorum colligere promptum est. Hodie clan cularijs testimonijs multi boni viri exagitar tur. Hi principes vl trò & sua sponte venerût ad Esdrâ,multò magis à magistratu ac cerfiti,& sacramento rogati, dicant quòd verum esse sciunt,ne-mini parcentes, vt malis obsistant. Nisi enim hoc fiat,tandem ira Dei contra nos inflammatur.
units.tr: 2. It is for the magistrate and the ministers of the Church to disclose those things which are committed against good laws, lest we incur the offence of God. For you hear that great men did this, who by no means deserve to be accused of acting unjustly, or of being informers. For no one ought to keep silent or overlook it if anything is done against the Word of God. Joseph is praised for this, that he reported his brothers' sins to their father: not out of envy, hatred, ambition or greed (like the quadruplators, who gained fourfold from accusations), but so that they might be amended. Therefore it matters much by what impulse and for what end someone reports sins to the magistrate: whether he does it from zeal for the glory of God and the salvation of his neighbour, so that the evil may be removed, or from corrupt affections. Slander and calumny are evil when we disclose the sins of others not for the sake of the ones we ought to serve. In Dan. 3, the Chaldeans accuse Daniel's companions before the king out of hatred and envy, because they had violated his law. In Dan. 6, they diligently searched for some crime against Daniel in the king's affairs; at last they brought it about that the king enacted a law that no one should ask anything for thirty days except from the king, and when Daniel did not obey it, they at once accused him. The Church of God has never lacked such accusers and informers, indeed betrayers. What happened to Paul is attested by the Acts of the Apostles. What happened to the primitive Church may readily be gathered from the Apologies of the Christians. Today many good men are harassed by secret testimonies. These leaders came to Ezra of their own accord and of their own will; how much more, then, ought those who are asked by the magistrate and bound by oath to say what they know to be true, sparing no one, so that they may withstand evils. For unless this is done, at last the wrath of God will be kindled against us.

units.la: 3. Separemus nos ab illis qui mala patrant, quibuscunque modis nobis iuncti sint. Act.2.de Petro scribitur,quòd pluribus sermonibus populum testificatus sit,exhortatus dicens:Seruemini à generatione hac praua. Admonens de salutis eorum periculo agi, quam nisi ab his separentur, retinere nequaquam possint. Hodie multi clamant,nolumus separari ab alijs,vicinis,foederatis,cognatis. At quædam separatio est necessaria. Si ab hominibus impijs, qui tibi arctè coniuncti sunt, separari aliter non potes aut diuelli corpore,separato te saltem morum dissimilitudine,hoc est,ne sis illis similis. Nisi enim hoc feceris, Christus nouissimo die te separabit à suis. Peccant Anabaptistæ,qui se ab illis separant,qui puram doctrinam retinent,&c.
units.tr: 3. Let us separate ourselves from those who commit evil, by whatever bonds we are joined to them. In Acts 2 it is written of Peter that he testified to the people with many words, exhorting them, saying: "Save yourselves from this crooked generation." He warned that their salvation was in danger, which they could by no means keep unless they were separated from these. Today many cry out: "We do not want to be separated from others, neighbours, allies, kinsfolk." But some separation is necessary. If you cannot be separated from impious men, who are closely joined to you, or torn away from their body, at least separate yourself by a difference of morals, that is, do not be like them. For unless you do this, Christ on the last day will separate you from his own. The Anabaptists sin, who separate themselves from those who hold pure doctrine, and so on.

units.la: 4. Conspicitur hic imbecillitas carnis quæ manet in sanctis, in hac vita. A captiuitate reuersi,in qua tot annis quasi in fornace excocti fuerunt,iterum corrumpuntur,vitijs succrescentibus. Cogitare debuerunt,quàm male eis cessisset, quòd mores gentium à Deo proscriptarum imitatæ essent. Nunquam igitur satis cauti esse possumus. Assiduè vigilandum est,ac ferò & absque mora obsistendum malis. Stultum est,quod quidam vociferantur, quomodo in ecclesia tam multi errores nasci potuissent? Quomodo nascuntur in agro vel horto zizaniæ?
units.tr: 4. Here we see the weakness of the flesh which remains in the saints in this life. Having returned from captivity, in which for so many years they had been refined as in a furnace, they are corrupted again, as vices grow up. They ought to have considered how badly it had gone for them, because they imitated the customs of the peoples whom God had condemned. We can therefore never be cautious enough. We must watch constantly, and resist evils early and without delay. It is foolish when some shout: how could so many errors have arisen in the Church? How do tares arise in a field or a garden?

units.la: 5. Quàm perniciosum sit,proceres ecclesiasticos & politicos,in errores & flagitia incidere. Sacerdotes,Leuitæ,principes & magistratus, duxerunt alienigenas,mox alij eorum exemplû sequuti sunt. Vulgo dicunt,abbatë si proferat cubos,Monachis ludendi copiam facere. Debebât quidè homines legibus viuere non exēplis:At hoc non fit,experimur enim vitia latissimè spargi in aliquo populo,si principes illis sint obnoxij. Quæ enim magnorum virorum exemplo fiunt,plerunq; rectè fierividentur. Au-reafuntilla carmina Claudij in Consulatu Honorij.
units.tr: 5. How harmful it is when the leaders of the Church and of the state fall into errors and disgraceful acts. Priests, Levites, princes and magistrates took foreign wives, and soon others followed their example. People commonly say that if an abbot plays at dice, he gives the monks licence to gamble. Men ought to live by laws, not by examples; but this does not happen, for we find that vices spread very widely among any people if the princes are guilty of them. For what is done by the example of great men generally seems to be done rightly. Those verses of Claudian in the consulship of Honorius are golden:

units.la: In commune iubes si quid censesq; tenendum Primus inffafubi,tune obferuantior æqui Fit popnlus,nec ferre vetat quum viderit ipsum Auctorem parere sibi. Componitur orbis Regis ad exemplum,nec sic inflectere sensus Humanos edicta valent,quàm vita regentis. Mobile mutatur semper cum principe vulgus.
units.tr: If you command anything to be held in common, and you, the first in the state, are more observant of what is fair, the people becomes more so too, nor does it forbid what it sees its own author obeying himself. The world is formed by the king's example, and edicts cannot bend human minds so much as the life of the ruler does. The fickle crowd always changes with the prince.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXII.
units.tr: HOMILY XXXII.

units.la: Esdras testatur dolorem quem ex leuitate Iudæorum conceperit.
units.tr: Ezra testifies to the grief he felt at the levity of the Jews.

units.la: 3 Quod verbum cum audissem, scidi vestimentum meum, & tunicam meam, & euulsi capillos capitis mei, & barbam meam, ac sedi stupens.
units.tr: 3 When I heard this word, I rent my garment and my mantle, and plucked off the hair of my head and of my beard, and sat astonied.

units.la: 4 Congregati sunt ad me omnes pauidi in verbis Dei Israelis ob præuaricationem (filiorum) transmigrationis: ego autem sedebam stupens vsque ad sacrificium vespertinum.
units.tr: 4 Then were assembled unto me every one that trembled at the words of the God of Israel, because of the transgression of those that had been carried away; and I sat astonied until the evening sacrifice.

units.la: 5 At in sacrificio vespertino surrexi de afflictione mea: quumq; scidissem vestimentum meum & tunicam meam, curuaui me super genua mea, atq; expandi palmas meas ad Iehouam Deum meum.
units.tr: 5 And at the evening sacrifice I arose up from my heaviness; and having rent my garment and my mantle, I fell upon my knees, and spread out my hands unto the LORD my God.

units.la: DIximus à primarijs viris querelam esse delatam ad Esdram, de illis Iudæis qui primo ascensu Hierosolyma peruenerant, quod cum in aliis proscriptarum gentium mores imitarentur, tum in eo quod matrimonij dignitate contempta, primas vxores repulerant, ac nouas & alienigenas contra legem Dei duxerant, idq; non plebei tantum, sed & proceres populi fecerant: Iam sequitur quomodo Esdras his cognitis, se gesserit.
units.tr: We said that a complaint had been brought to Ezra by the leading men concerning those Jews who had come up to Jerusalem in the first return: that while they imitated the customs of the peoples who had been cast out, they had also, having despised the dignity of marriage, put away their first wives and taken new foreign wives contrary to the law of God; and this was done not only by the common people but by the nobles of the nation as well. Now follows how Ezra behaved when he had learned of these things.

units.la: Scidit vestes suas & pallium, vestem interiorem & exteriorem, nos dicimus rocf vnb mantel: deinde euulsit comam & barbam: item sedit solus, vel mœrens, attonitus, turbatus, cogitans nimirum quomodo corrigi hæc possent. Capite 10. addet humi procubuisse, & in lachrymas solutus esse. Externis verò illis rebus vel symbolis, testatus est magnum animi sui dolorem. Mos enim fuit gentium Orientalium, vt in summo dolore scinderent vestes, capillos evellerent, & in terram sederent: plærunque se puluere vel cinere asperserunt.
units.tr: He tore his clothes and his cloak, both the inner and the outer garment (we call it the mantle); then he tore out his hair and beard. Likewise he sat alone, either in mourning, dumbfounded and troubled, no doubt considering how these things could be put right. Chapter 10 adds that he threw himself down on the ground and dissolved in tears. By those outward acts, or symbols, however, he showed the great grief of his mind. For it was the custom of the peoples of the East that in extreme sorrow they tore their garments, pulled out their hair, and sat on the ground; most often they sprinkled themselves with dust or ashes.

units.la: De scisione vestium, multa exempla extant. Numeri 14. de Iosue & Caleb dicitur, quod vestes sciderint, propter speculatorum perfidiam.
