Iosue 17. cum ciues in oppido Hai eruptione facta, de monte deturbassent Israelitas, & aliquot interfecissent. In nouo Testamento Caiaphas scribitur vestes scidisse, de quo nihil dicam quia hypocrita fuit. Actorum 14. Paulus & Barnabas cum a Lystrensibus diuinis honoribus afficerentur, vestes sciderunt, significantes hanc rem ita ipsis dolere, vt mirum non esset, corda eorum rumpi.
units.tr: There are many examples of the tearing of garments. Numbers 14 says of Joshua and Caleb that they rent their clothes because of the faithlessness of the spies. Joshua 17, when the men of the town of Ai, after making a sally, drove the Israelites down from the mountain and killed some of them. In the New Testament Caiaphas is written of as having rent his clothes, but I will say nothing of him, since he was a hypocrite. Acts 14: when Paul and Barnabas were honoured with divine worship by the Lystrans, they rent their garments, signifying that the matter grieved them so deeply that it would be no wonder if their hearts broke.

units.la: Isaias 15. de Moabitarum excidio, in omnibus capitibus eius dicit, est calvitium, & omnis barba est detonsa. Ieremiae 48. de ijsdem scribens, omne caput, inquit, est caluum, & omnis barba attonsa. In luctu enim comam evellebant, abradebant barbam, nos contra facimus.
units.tr: Isaiah 15, on the destruction of Moab, says of all its heads: there is baldness, and every beard is cut off. Jeremiah 48, writing of the same people, says: every head is bald, and every beard is shaved. In mourning they plucked out their hair and shaved off their beards; we, on the contrary, do the opposite.

units.la: Isaiae 47. dicit: Descende & sede in puluere virgo filia Babel &c. Iob. 2. sedit in sterquilinio. Ezechielis 26. Sedebunt in terra, de mercatoribus. Ionae 3. rex Niniuitarum sedit in puluere. Ieremiae 13. Dic regi & reginae: humiliate vos & sedete (in terra) quoniam descendit dignitas vestra, & corona magnificentiae vestrae, &c. In Threnis Ieremiae 2. Sederunt in terra, conticuerunt senes filiae Sion: impossuerunt puluerem super caput suum & accincti sunt saccis, &c.
units.tr: Isaiah 47 says: Come down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon, etc. Job 2 sat in the dunghill. Ezekiel 26 (of the merchants): they shall sit upon the earth. Jonah 3: the king of Nineveh sat in the dust. Jeremiah 13: Say to the king and the queen: humble yourselves and sit down (on the ground), for your dignity has come down, and the crown of your glory, etc. Lamentations 2: The elders of the daughter of Zion sit upon the ground and keep silence; they have cast dust upon their heads and girded themselves with sackcloth, etc.

units.la: Quid effecit Esdras his symbolis? Cum initio solus esset, postea multi ad eum venerunt, de quo plenius initio capitis 10. sequetur: Nempe omnes timentes verbum Dei, propter transgressionem. Hoc est, qui metuebant ne eis accideret quod Deus comminatus est transgressoribus legis, quodque antea eis accidera t. De causis cogitabant ob quas prius electi erant in exilium. Prophetae commemorant in suis concionibus, contemtum dominae coelestis, & contumaciam in atrocibus delictis: similes poenas hoc quoque tempore videbant imminere. Haec phrasis in sequenti etiam capite repetitur.
units.tr: What did Ezra achieve by these symbols? At first he was alone, but afterwards many came to him, as will be told more fully at the beginning of chapter 10: namely, all who feared the word of God because of the transgression. That is, those who feared that what God threatened to transgressors of the law would befall them, and what had befallen them before. They considered the causes for which they had earlier been chosen for exile. The prophets recall in their sermons the contempt of the heavenly Lady and the obstinacy in atrocious sins; at this time too the people saw similar punishments hanging over them. This phrase is repeated in the following chapter also.

units.la: Trepidantes in verbis Dei Israelis, est piorum periphrasis, im pij verbum Dei, minas & promissiones sufq; deq; ferunt. Pijs dolet Deo offendi. Isaiae vltimo dicit Deus: ad quem respiciam nisi ad contritum spiritu, & trementem sermones meos?
units.tr: "Trembling at the words of the God of Israel" is a periphrasis for the pious; the impious treat the word of God, its threats and its promises, with contempt. The pious grieve to offend God. In the last chapter of Isaiah God says: To whom shall I look, but to him who is contrite in spirit and trembles at my words?

units.la: Sedit autem perturbatus & afflictus, vsq; ad oblationem vespervespertinam. Singulis diebus mane & vespéri agnus immola-batur,quod sacrificium iuge vocatur,de quo Exodi 29. & Le-uitici 6.Ad illud sacrificium multos venisse probabile est.
units.tr: He sat, however, troubled and afflicted, until the evening offering. Every day, morning and evening, a lamb was sacrificed; this sacrifice is called the continual offering, concerning which see Exodus 29 and Leviticus 6. It is probable that many came to that sacrifice.

units.la: Quid praeterea fecit Esdras : tempore vespertinæ oblatio-nis,surrexit ex afflictione sua,& laceratis vestibus procumbens in genua sua, expandit manus suas ad dominum Deum suum, non ad creaturas quantumuis excellentes : & ardentes preces effudit paras extendere,expandere,leuare. Eleuatio manuum est gestus orantium,& gestus vetustus. Moses enim vi-storiam petens contra Amelechitas,attollit manus. Isaiæ cum leuaueritis manus,non exaudiam vos.In Psalmis aliquoties te-statur Dauid,se manus sustulisse ad Deum. Symbolum est deditionis & deiectionis.Dedentes se victori, qui ius necis in eos habet,manus protendunt:Item luto aut aquis immersi,manus protendunt,vt apprehensos extrahamus. Significatur hoc gestu, nos versantes in interitu, opem ac liberationem petere à Deo,cui totos nos dedimus.Manus in precibus sustollendi morem,Vergilius quoq; attingit,Æneid.2. At pater Anchises oculos ad sydera laetus Extulit, & caelo palmas cum voce tetendit. Iupiter omnipotens, &c. Æneid.5.lib. Et fors æquatis cepisset praemia rostris: Ni palmas ponto tendens vtrafq; Cloanthus, Fudisset preces, diuosq; in vota vocasset, &c. Item, Æneid.10. de Turno. Et dublices cum voce manus ad sydera tendit, Omnipotens genitor, &c.
units.tr: What else did Ezra do? At the time of the evening offering he rose from his affliction, and, with his garments torn, fell upon his knees and spread out his hands to the Lord his God, not to creatures however excellent; and he poured out ardent prayers. To stretch out, to spread, to lift up (the hands): lifting up the hands is the gesture of those who pray, and an ancient one. For Moses, seeking victory against the Amalekites, lifted up his hands. Isaiah: When you lift up your hands, I will not hear you. In the Psalms David several times testifies that he raised his hands to God. It is a symbol of surrender and of dejection: those who give themselves up to a victor, who has the power of life and death over them, stretch out their hands; likewise those sunk in mud or water stretch out their hands so that they may be drawn out when grasped. By this gesture is signified that we, placed in peril of destruction, seek help and deliverance from God, to whom we have given ourselves wholly. Virgil also touches on the custom of raising the hands in prayer. Aeneid 2: But father Anchises, joyful, lifted his eyes to the stars and stretched out his palms to heaven with a voice: Almighty Jupiter, etc. Aeneid 5: And perhaps the prize would have been won with the oars evenly matched, had not Cloanthus, stretching both palms out over the sea, poured forth prayers and called upon the gods in vows, etc. Likewise, Aeneid 10, of Turnus: And with a voice he stretches both hands to the stars: Almighty Father, etc.

units.la: Aristoteles in libro de mundo. Omnes scribit Deo summum locum attribuere,subijciens: πάντες ὁ ἄνθρωποι ἀνατείνοντες ταῖς χεῖρας εἰς τὸν ὑψηλὸν εὐχὰς ποιούμενοι, id est, omnes enim deprecaturi ad caelum manus tollimus. Apud Homerum saepe legitur ... Sublatas in caelum manus, indicium esse adorationis. Pierius quoq; in suis hieroglyphicis annotauit.
units.tr: Aristotle, in his book On the World, writes that all men attribute the highest place to God, adding: all men, lifting their hands to the heights, make their prayers [πάντες οἱ ἄνθρωποι ἀνατείνοντες ταῖς χεῖρας εἰς τὸν ὑψηλὸν εὐχὰς ποιούμενοι], that is, we all raise our hands to heaven when we are about to pray. In Homer one often reads ... that hands lifted up to heaven are a sign of adoration. Pierius also noted this in his Hieroglyphics.

units.la: Quando vero & vbi orandum sit,quæritur. Esdras vespéri cum populus frequentior confluere ad sacrificium, precatus est, vt alios ad poenitentiam accenderet,non vt se ostentaret. Matth.6. Psal.55.versu 17.Ego ad dominum clamabo,& Iehoua seruabit me. Vespere & mane & meridie(hoc est,indesinenter) orabo & tumultuabor,& audiet vocem meam,&c. Precatus est ante templum,multis praesentibus,&c.
units.tr: The question is when and where one ought to pray. Ezra prayed in the evening, when the people were gathering in larger numbers for the sacrifice, to kindle others to repentance, not to make a show of himself. Matthew 6. Psalm 55, verse 17: As for me, I will call upon God, and the LORD shall save me. Evening and morning and at noon (that is, without ceasing) I will pray and make my lament, and he shall hear my voice, etc. He prayed before the temple, with many present, etc.

units.la: Vsus huius loci.
units.tr: The use of this passage.

units.la: 1. Discunt fideles, & in primis ministri ecclesiae, exemplo Esdrae qui sacerdos fuit, quid sit agendum, vel quomodo affecti esse debeamus, si leges diuinae violentur. Esdras hoc facto Iudaeorum grauiter afficitur, & reipsa testatur, sibi non probari. Non extenuat eorum scelus, neque dicit, nimis late nunc sparsum est, obstandum fuerat initijs. Minimum dolorem nostrum tenari debemus, neque statim emendationem desperare. Cum nostro tempore omnes fere leges conculcentur, & poenae pro foribus sint, tamen rarus est qui moueatur, vel cui lachrymula excidat. Vel si sint aliqui, quibus scelera serio diuplicent, & putant cohercenda, abusus corrigendos, tamen exosi sunt aliis omnibus.
units.tr: 1. Believers learn, and above all the ministers of the Church, from the example of Ezra, who was a priest, what ought to be done, and how we ought to be moved, if the divine laws are violated. Ezra is gravely affected by this deed of the Jews, and by his actions he shows that he does not approve of it. He does not minimise their crime, nor say, "It has spread too widely now; it should have been resisted at the beginning." We ought to feel our sorrow in full and not despair of amendment at once. In our own time almost all laws are trampled underfoot, and punishments are at the door, yet there are few who are moved, or from whose eyes a tear falls. Or if there are some who take the sins seriously, and think that they must be restrained and the abuses corrected, nevertheless they are hated by all the others.

units.la: 2 Si vel paucis dolat corruptus status populi, & de emenda tione serio cogitant, Deus alios quoque excitat, qui eis sint auxilio. Cum dolorem suum Esdras externis signis testaretur, statim se coniungunt illi, qui timebant iram Dei, ob contemptum verbi ipsius. Postea Sachanias opem illi promittit, qui etiam Ethnicam duxerat. Si tantus zelus esset in proceribus ecclesiae & Reipublicae, corrigendi ac emendandi mores corruptos, fem per adhuc plures reperirentur, quibus hoc curae esset. Quoties illi a quibus minime expectatis, Euangelij negotium promouent? Sed si ipsis ministris coniugia cum idololatris non disiplicent, si fcortationem, vsuras immodicas, militiam mercenariam, & alia id genus vel extenuant vel defendunt, mirum non est, si alij quoque remissi sint & negligentes.
units.tr: 2. If even a few grieve over the corrupted state of the people and think seriously about amendment, God also raises up others who will be their help. When Ezra showed his grief by outward signs, at once those joined him who feared the wrath of God because of contempt for the Word itself. Afterwards Shechaniah promised him help, the one who had also married a foreign wife. If there were such great zeal among the leaders of the Church and the commonwealth to correct and amend corrupt morals, many more would still be found who would take this to heart. How often do those from whom we least expect it advance the cause of the gospel? But if the ministers themselves do not object to marriages with idolaters, and if they either make light of or defend fornication, excessive usury, mercenary soldiering and other things of this kind, it is no wonder if others too become lax and negligent.

units.la: 3 Quomodo nos ad preces componere debeamus: vel quis habitus precantium esse debeat. Quo ad vestes, placet Deo, si humiles simus. Esdras scissa vel lacerata veste preces fundit, in genua demittit, manus in coelum porrigit, vel expandit. Veteres serio precaturi, saccos fere induerunt. Videretur iudices contumelia affecisse, qui delicti veniam petiturus, non cultu solito reorum: sed vestibus sumptuosis in confessum eorum prodiret. Apud Romanos rei ad iudicium vocati, mutata veste, foridati ac capillo & barba promissa, debitam poenam deprecabantur. Quomodo Deo placeremus, si deprecaturi poenas, immoderato corporis cultu, in templum veniamus? Paulus 1. ad Timoth. 2. capite de coetibus sacris agens, praescribit feminis ne cultu corporis sumptuoso & luxurioso vtantur. Quod vero corporis constitutionem in precibus attinet, dicendum est, eas vel priuatas esse, vel publicas. In priuatis quisque suo arbitratu potest agere : in publicis sequatur quifq; suæ ecclesiæ morem fi non fit superstitiosus. Apud veteres vulgaris fuit genuflectio & extensio vel expansio manuum. Ad Ephesios 3. capite dicit apostolus, fe flectere genua ad patre domini nostri Iesu Christi, vt ipsi fortitudine roborentur. Metuebat enim ne propter suas afflictiones, à fide resilirent. 1. Timoth. 2. Volo viros vbiq; orare, manus extendentes puras, abfq; ira & hæsitatione. D. Augustinus libro 2. ad Simplicianum, quæstione 4. Non refert, inquit, quomodo corpus constituatur, dummodo animus Deo præfens, peragat intentionem suam. Nam & stantes oramus, sicut scriptum est, publicanus de longinquo stabat: & fixis genubus, sicut in Actis Apostolicis legimus: & sedentes, sicut Dauid & Helias. Nisi autem & iacentes oraremus, non scriptum effet in psalmis, Lauabo per singulas noctes lectum meum. Cum enim quisq; orationem quærit, collocat membra sicut ei occurrerit accommodata pro tempore positi corporis ad mouendum affectum, &c.
units.tr: 3. How we ought to prepare ourselves for prayer, or what posture those who pray should have. As to clothing, it pleases God if we are humble. Ezra pours out his prayers with his garment torn or rent, he sinks to his knees, and he stretches out or spreads his hands towards heaven. The ancients, when they were about to pray seriously, generally put on sackcloth. A judge would seem to have been treated with contumely if a man seeking pardon for a fault came before the court not in the usual dress of the accused, but in costly garments. Among the Romans, accused persons summoned to judgement changed their clothes, went about in mourning dress, and let their hair and beard grow, and so begged for the punishment due to them. How could we please God if, coming into the temple to beg for relief from punishments, we came with immoderate adornment of the body? Paul, in 1 Timothy 2, speaking of the sacred assemblies, prescribes that women should not use costly and luxurious adornment of the body. As for the posture of the body in prayer, it must be said that prayers are either private or public. In private prayer each may act as he pleases; in public prayer let each follow the custom of his own congregation, provided it is not superstitious. Among the ancients kneeling and the stretching out or spreading of the hands were common. In Ephesians 3 the apostle says that he bows his knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, that they may be strengthened with might; for he feared lest, because of his afflictions, they would fall away from the faith. 1 Timothy 2: "I desire that men pray everywhere, lifting up pure hands, without wrath and doubting." Augustine, in the second book to Simplicianus, question 4: "It does not matter," he says, "how the body is posed, provided the mind, present to God, carries out its intention. For we pray standing, as it is written, 'The publican stood afar off'; and with knees bent, as we read in the Acts of the Apostles; and sitting, as David and Elijah did. Indeed, unless we also prayed lying down, it would not have been written in the Psalms, 'I will wash my bed every night.' For when anyone seeks prayer, he places his limbs as they suit him, in the position of the body that is appropriate at the time for stirring the feeling," etc.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXIII.
units.tr: HOMILIA XXXIII.

units.la: Precatio Efdræ, in qua confitetur peccata sua & populi.
units.tr: The prayer of Ezra, in which he confesses his own sins and those of the people.

units.la: 6 Ac dixi, Deus mi, pudet me & erubesco attollere Deus mi faciem meam ad te: quoniam iniquitates nostræ multiplicatæ sunt super caput, & delicta nostra creuerunt vfq; ad cælum.
units.tr: 6 And I said, "My God, I am ashamed and blush to lift up my face to you, my God, because our iniquities have multiplied over our heads, and our sins have grown up to heaven."

units.la: 7 A diebus patrum nostrorum fuimus in delicto magno vfq; ad diem hanc, ac propter iniquitates nostras traditi fumus nos, reges nostri, & sacerdotes nostri in manum regum terrarum, in gladium, in captiuitatem, & in rapinam, & in pudorem vultus, fecundum diem hanc.
units.tr: 7 "From the days of our fathers we have been in great guilt, even to this day, and for our iniquities we, our kings and our priests, have been handed over into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to shame of face, as on this day."

units.la: 8 Nunc autem modico momento fuit misericordia à Iehoua Deo nostro (ita) vt relinqueret nobis (homines) ienafionis, & daret nobis clauum in loco sancto suo, vt illuminaret oculos nostros Deus noster, & daret nobis vitam modicam in seruitute nostra:
units.tr: 8 "But now, for a brief moment, mercy has come from the LORD our God, so that he left us a remnant (of men) that escaped, and gave us a peg in his holy place, so that our God might enlighten our eyes, and give us a little life in our servitude."

units.la: 9 Quia fer ui eramus, & in seruitute nostra non dereliquit nos Deus noster, sed inclinavit super nos misericordiam coram rege Paras, ut daret nobis vitam, ut exaltaret domum Dei nostri, & instauraret solitudines eius, & daret nobis sepem in Iehudah & in Ierusalaim.
units.tr: 9 "For we were slaves, and in our servitude our God did not forsake us, but inclined mercy toward us in the sight of the king of Persia, so that he would give us life, so that he would raise up the house of our God, restore its ruins, and give us a hedge in Judah and in Jerusalem."

units.la: SAncti homines à rerum origine, in suis afflictionibus à Deo opem petierunt: vtq; liberi filiæ dantur ad parentes suos rectà confugiunt: ita filij Dei, hoc est fideles ad patre suum cœlestem statim per preces fe conferunt. Exemplum hoc loco insigne habemus in Esdra, qui cum intellexisset Iudæos male se gerere, maximè circa matrimonium, ad preces se converterit, quarum formula hoc loco proponitur.
units.tr: Holy men, from the beginning of things, sought help from God in their afflictions, just as children who are given to their parents flee straight to them; so the sons of God, that is, the faithful, at once betake themselves to their heavenly Father through prayers. We have a notable example here in Ezra, who, when he understood that the Jews were behaving badly, especially in the matter of marriage, turned to prayer, and the form of that prayer is set out here.

units.la: Confessus est publicè & sua & populi peccata, præcipuè vero ostendit quàm graue sit scelus, quòd Ethnicas uxores duxerint, & quid mali allaturum sit, nisi corrigatur. Etsi hæc oratio ad Deum dirigatur, tamen spectat populum, ut agnoscat peccata & supplicia.
units.tr: He confessed publicly both his own sins and those of the people, and above all he showed how grave a crime it was that they had taken foreign wives, and what evil would follow unless it were corrected. Although this prayer is addressed to God, it nonetheless concerns the people, so that they may acknowledge their sins and punishments.

units.la: Pudet me, et erubescō attollere, Deus mi, faciem meam ad te.) Luc.18. publicanus procul stans, nec oculos volebat ad cœlum attollere, sed percutiebat pectus suum, dicens: Deus propitius esto mihi peccatori, &c.
units.tr: "I am ashamed and blush to lift up my face to you, my God." (Luke 18.) The tax collector, standing afar off, would not even lift his eyes to heaven, but struck his breast, saying, "God, be merciful to me, a sinner," etc.

units.la: Causam subijcit: Quoniam iniquitates nostræ multiplicatæ sunt super caput.) Metaphora petita ab aquis. Peccata excedunt vel superant capita nostra, nos dicimus, wir steckend in den sünden über die ozen.
units.tr: He gives the cause: "Because our iniquities have multiplied over our heads." This is a metaphor taken from waters. Sins exceed or overtop our heads; we say, "wir steckend in den sünden über die ozen" (we are sunk in sins up over the ears).

units.la: Et delicta nostra creuerunt usq; in cœlum.) Magna sunt & multa. Hyperbole est, adeo creuerunt, ut cœlum ipsum attingere videantur, Vatablus. Filius Acolastus Lucæ 15. Pater, inquit, ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, peccavi in cœlum, id est graviter: καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου, & coram te, hoc est, impudenter, neque sum amplius dignus vocari filius tuus.
units.tr: "And our sins have grown up to heaven." They are great and many. It is a hyperbole: they have grown so much that they seem to reach heaven itself (Vatablus). The prodigal son in Luke 15 says, "Father, I have sinned against heaven" [ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν], that is, grievously; "and before you" [καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου], that is, shamelessly; "and I am no longer worthy to be called your son."

units.la: Omnia quidem peccata perveniunt ad cœlos, sed de maximis dicitur quòd ascendant ad cœlum, ut de cæde Abelis, & Sodomitarum sceleribus. 2. Paralipomenon 28. occidit eos in ira, quæ pervenit ad cœlos, &c.
units.tr: All sins indeed reach the heavens, but of the greatest it is said that they ascend to heaven, as of the murder of Abel and the wickedness of the Sodomites. 2 Chronicles 28: "He slew them in wrath, which reached to heaven," etc.

units.la: Ex his verbis nemo colligat, propter peccatorum magnitudinem, refugiendum à conspectu Dei, & abstinendum esse à precibus. Quo enim peccata nostra maiora sunt, tanto magis ad animarum medicum confugiendum est. Esdras nos monet ut attrocitatem peccatorū intelligamus, & humiles simus, &c.
units.tr: Let no one gather from these words that, because of the greatness of sins, one must flee from the sight of God and abstain from prayer. For the greater our sins are, the more we must flee to the physician of souls. Ezra warns us that we should understand the atrocity of sins, and be humble, etc.

units.la: Addit, eos non nuper demum peccare cepisse, sed maiores quoque ipsorum peccasse, ideoque saepe a Deo afflicti sunt per varios tyrannos, ut ex Iudicum & Regum libris perspici potest. Multae fuerunt captiuitates illius populi, quibus posteri nihilo facti cautiores, peccata peccatis cumularunt, ideoque traditi sunt in manum regum terrarum. Non tantum vulgares, sed & reges & sacerdotes, qui fere impunitatem sperant, poenas dederunt. Ingladium.) Plures enim bello caesi sunt.
units.tr: He adds that these people had not only lately begun to sin, but that their forefathers had sinned as well, and therefore they were often afflicted by God through various tyrants, as can be seen from the books of Judges and Kings. That people suffered many captivities, and their descendants, made no wiser by them, heaped sins upon sins, and so were handed over into the hand of the kings of the lands. Not only the common people but also kings and priests, who for the most part hope for impunity, paid the penalties. "To the sword." For more were slain in war.

units.la: In captiuitatem.) Hostis illos qui caesi non sunt, in captiuitatem traxit: & in rapinam.) Direpta sunt eorum opppida, castella, vici, detractae sunt vestes viris & mulieribus.
units.tr: "Into captivity." He drew into captivity those enemies who were not slain; and "into plunder." Their towns, fortresses and villages were plundered, and clothing was stripped from men and women.

units.la: Et in pudorem vultus.) Fabula enim facti sunt hostium suorum: saepe erubuerunt quando hostium sannas audire cogebantur: an Deus suum illum populum non afferat? &c. Vide Psalmum 44. 79. &c.
units.tr: "And to shame of face." For they became a laughing-stock to their enemies; often they blushed when they were forced to hear the jeers of their foes. Does God not bring his own people to this? Etc. See Psalms 44 and 79, etc.

units.la: Secundum diem hanc.) Vt videre est, wie offenlich am tag ligt/ wie yederman weyst. Hinc colligitur, Deum peccatis ferio irasci. Duo verba ponuntur quae peccatum significant, nempe onan & afcham. Complectuntur autem omnia peccata, quae contra primam & secundam tabulam committuntur.
units.tr: "As on this day." As is plain to see, "wie offenlich am tag ligt, wie yederman weyst" (as is plain in broad daylight, as everyone knows). Hence it is gathered that God is angered by sins. Two words are used which signify sin, namely onan and afcham. They comprehend all the sins that are committed against the first and the second table.

units.la: Nunc autem modico momento, &c.) Sensus est: Cum multa & magna essent peccata nostra, Dominus subito & repente misertus est sui populi: recenset quomodo id factum sit. Vt relinqueret nobis homines emastionis.) Potuisset omnes delere, etiam in Babylone, sed seruauit reliquias.
units.tr: "But now, for a brief moment, etc." The sense is: although our sins were many and great, the Lord suddenly and unexpectedly had mercy on his people; he recounts how this came about. "So that he left us a remnant of men." He could have destroyed all of them, even in Babylon, but he preserved a remnant.

units.la: Et daret nobis iattad clauum vel paxillum in loco sacro suo.) Hoc est, sedes certas, firmas & fixas. Metaphora sumpta ab illis, qui clauum figunt, e quo vestes, & alia suspendant. Isaiae 22. capite de Eliacim qui Sobnae proditori succesit: & figam eum veluti clauum in loco fideli, & erit in folium gloriae patris sui. Et suspendent super ipsum gloriam omnem domus patris sui, stirpes & posteritates, omnia vasa minora, &c.
units.tr: "And gave us a peg [iattad] or stake in his holy place." That is, certain, firm and fixed seats. The metaphor is taken from those who fix a peg or nail on which they hang garments and other things. In Isaiah 22, concerning Eliakim, who succeeded the traitor Shebna: "I will fix him like a nail in a sure place, and he shall be a throne of glory to his father's house. And they shall hang upon him all the glory of his father's house, offspring and descendants, all the lesser vessels," etc.

units.la: Vt illuminaret oculos nostros.) Oculos mentis nostrae illustrauit. Erbat vnno vn ere augen vffgerhon. Vt ostendere nobis peccata nostra, suam iustitiam, & etiam clementiam, vt saltem idi saperemus. Vel illuminare oculos significat vitam & laetitiam reddere. In magnis doloribus caligant oculi, in laetitia restituitur eis sua vis, &c.
units.tr: "So that he might enlighten our eyes." He enlightened the eyes of our mind. "Erbat vnno vn ere augen vffgerhon" (the eyes were raised up). So that he might show us our sins, his righteousness, and also his clemency, so that at least we might come to our senses. Or, to enlighten the eyes signifies giving life and gladness: in great sorrows the eyes grow dim, and in joy their strength is restored to them, etc.

units.la: Es daret nobis vitam modicam in seruitute nostra.) Per vitam respirationem & consolationem intelligit. Nos dicimus dedit nobis,das wir vns ein wenig widerumb erholet haben. Quod mox explicat,fatetur enim quod sint serui,quodq; Deus eos in seruitute non deseruerit. Addit,Deum ipsos gratos effecisse regi Persico, qui vitam eis concesserit,vt extruerent templum quod iacebat in ruinis.
units.tr: "And gave us a little life in our servitude." By "life" he means respite and consolation. We say, "He gave us", "das wir vns ein wenig widerumb erholet haben" (that we have recovered ourselves a little again). He immediately explains this: he confesses that they are slaves, and that God did not forsake them in servitude. He adds that God made them acceptable to the Persian king, who granted them life so that they might build the temple, which lay in ruins.

units.la: Et daret eis sepem in Iuda & Ierusalem.) Hoc est,eos defender et contra hostium iniurias,ne expositi essent omnium incursibus & libidini. Moenia vrbis Hierosolymorum,hoc tempore nondum instaurata erant. Metaphora ducta ab illis,qui sepibus muniunt hortos & agros suos, vt homines & feras ab eis arceant. Satan fatetur Deum quasi sepi quadam domum Iobi, & omnia quae habet,circumdedisse,&c. Postea inferet, Vos autem spreta illa bonitate, violastis legem Dei, & poenas attrahitis,&c.
units.tr: "And gave them a hedge in Judah and Jerusalem." That is, he defended them against the injuries of their enemies, so that they would not be exposed to the attacks and lust of all. The walls of the city of Jerusalem had not yet been restored at this time. It is a metaphor drawn from those who protect their gardens and fields with hedges, to keep men and wild beasts away from them. Satan acknowledges that God had, as it were, surrounded Job's house and all that he had with a hedge, etc. Afterwards he will add: "But you, having scorned that goodness, have violated the law of God and draw punishments upon yourselves," etc.

units.la: Theodorus Bibliander paulo aliter haec verba interpretatus est, nempe quod Deus reduxerit reliquias in patriam, & aliquousque produxerit iam res Iudae, suisseque inchoata beneficia Dei quae feliciter potuerint prouehi ad pristinam gentis amplitudinem. Deum reliquias seruasse, voluisseque dare clauum,id est, solidam sedem, & illuminari oculos ipsorum,vt ruinae Ierusalem excitarentur ac sepes vrbi & regioni circumducerentur, daturumque fuisse plenam libertatem: nisi ipsi obstitissent suae felicitati, gloriae & amplitudini gentis, qui sic prouocarint Dominum, vt vniuersos posset extirpare. Lo hat vns erst Gott ein wenig ghulffen / vnnd möcht alles gût werden mit der zyt/als sich die sach nun wol hat angleffen / so gond wir hin vnnd verschüttendo alls mit vnserem schandtlichen låben.
units.tr: Theodore Bibliander interpreted these words somewhat differently: namely, that God had brought the remnant back to their homeland and had already advanced the affairs of Judah to some extent, and that the beginnings of God's blessings could be carried forward successfully to the former greatness of the nation. God had preserved the remnant and was willing to give them the peg, that is, a firm seat, and to enlighten their eyes, so that the ruins of Jerusalem would be raised up, a hedge would be drawn around the city and the land, and he would have granted them full liberty, had they not themselves stood in the way of their own happiness, the glory and greatness of their nation, provoking the Lord so that he could have destroyed them all. Bibliander's German runs: "Look, God has first helped us a little, and everything might become good in time, since the matter has now begun to go well; yet we go on and squander everything with our shameful way of living."

units.la: Quaeri hoc loco potest, cur Esdras alijs se connumeret, eum alienus fuerit a peccato ipsorum? Item Isaias, Ieremias, Daniel & alij quoque Prophetae qui sancte vixerunt, annumerant se alijs peccatoribus. Respondeo, hoc ideo ab eis factum, quod scirent se natura peccatores esse. Omnes homines sunt peccatores: nemo est qui suos naevos non habeat. Illi qui manifestis quidem flagitijs non sunt obnoxij, peccatis aliorum non obstiunt vt debebant & poterant,quia neminem volunt offendere, obstringunt se reatu alienorum peccatorum.
units.tr: One may ask at this point why Ezra counts himself among the others, since he was not guilty of their sins. Likewise Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel and the other prophets, who lived holy lives, number themselves among the other sinners. I answer that they did this because they knew that by nature they were sinners. All men are sinners; there is no one who does not have his own blemishes. Those who are not bound by open crimes nevertheless do not oppose the sins of others as they ought and could, because they do not want to offend anyone; so they make themselves liable for the guilt of others' sins.

units.la: Vsus huius precationis.
units.tr: The use of this prayer.

units.la: 1 Quid faciendum sit si peccauimus. Esdras cofitetur & sua populi peccata. Ingenuè igitur corâ Deo fateamur nos pecca- tores esse,non negemus, non elevemus aut defendamus nostra peccata, aut in alios conferamus, sed ea detestemur & damne- mus. Prouerbiorum 28. Qui abscondit scelera sua,non dirige- tur: qui autem confessus fuerit & reliquerit ea, misericordiam consequetur. 1. Iohan. 1. Si confiteamur peccata nostra,fidelis & iustus est, vt remittet nobis peccata nostra, &c. Exempla habe- mus in Dauide, Daniele & aliis. Confessi sunt Deo sua peccata contra quem peccarunt, & qui solus potest remittere. Imposto- res docent peccata non remitti, nisi sacrificulis etiam sigillatim recitentur. Qui non agnoscunt peccata sua, præcludunt sibi ia- nuam gratiæ Dei.
units.tr: 1. What must be done if we have sinned. Ezra confesses also the sins of the people. Let us therefore frankly acknowledge before God that we are sinners; let us not deny it, nor excuse or defend our sins, nor shift them onto others, but let us detest and condemn them. Proverbs 28: "He who conceals his crimes will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy." 1 John 1: "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins," etc. We have examples in David, Daniel and others. They confessed their sins to God, against whom they had sinned, and who alone can forgive them. Impostors teach that sins are not forgiven unless they are also recited one by one to the priests. Those who do not acknowledge their sins shut against themselves the door of the grace of God.

units.la: 2. Vnde bella, seruitus, contemtus oriantur. Ex contemtu verbi Dei & flagitijs, vt hoc loco dicitur, & Deut. 28. Deus mi- natur. Hodie plurimis persuasum est, ex obseruatione mandatorum & verbi Dei, bella, seditiones, & alia id genus oriri. Proinde contra præcepta Dei multa faciunt, vt pacem & tranquillitatem conseruent.
units.tr: 2. Whence wars, slavery and contempt arise. From contempt of the Word of God and from crimes, as is said in this place, and Deut. 28, God threatens. Today most people are persuaded that wars, seditions and other things of this kind arise from the observance of the commandments and the Word of God. Accordingly, they do many things against the precepts of God in order to preserve peace and tranquillity.

units.la: 3. Clementiæ diuinæ illustre hoc loco exemplum habemus. In medijs afflictionibus non obliuiscitur suorum. Cum Iudæi in deformi seruitute viuerent, eorum non est oblitus. Dein de flexit animos regum, vt Iudæos amarent. Ipse enim, vt sæpius in hoc libro annotauimus, regit regum corda. Hodie quoq; ergo suos sic animatus est.
units.tr: 3. We have here a notable example of the divine clemency. In the midst of afflictions he does not forget his own. Although the Jews lived in shameful servitude, he did not forget them. Then he turned the hearts of kings so that they loved the Jews. For he, as we have often noted in this book, rules the hearts of kings. So today also he cares for his own in the same way.

units.la: 4. Rebus quantumuis desperatis, Deus (vt hoc loco fecisse dicitur) repente potest suos liberare. Immensa enim eius est potentia.
units.tr: 4. However desperate things may be, God (as is said to have happened in this place) can suddenly deliver his own. For his power is immeasurable.

units.la: 5. Calamitas exilij non tantum profecit, quin patrum exemplo delinquerent. Vnde colligitur carnis nostræ infirmitas, de qua supra.
units.tr: 5. The calamity of the exile did not so much improve them that they did not sin as their fathers had. From this we gather the weakness of our flesh, of which we have spoken above.

units.la: 6. Officium regum indicatur exemplo Darij, nempe vt suos subiectos defendant ab iniuria, eos in vita conseruent, & templi Domini ruinas instaurent. Vtq; hoc facere possint, preces pro ipsis fundendæ sunt à subiectis ipsorum.
units.tr: 6. The duty of kings is shown by the example of Darius, namely that they defend their subjects from injury, keep them alive, and restore the ruins of the Lord's temple. And so that they may be able to do this, prayers must be poured out for them by their subjects.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXIIII.
units.tr: HOMILY XXXIV.

units.la: Exponit in specie, quomodo violarint legem de coniugio cum exteris.
units.tr: He explains in particular how they broke the law concerning marriage with foreigners.

units.la: 10 Nunc ergo quid dicemus, o Deus noster, post hæc? nam dereliquimus præcepta tua,
units.tr: 10 And now, what shall we say, O our God, after this? For we have forsaken thy commandments,

units.la: 11 Quæ præcepisti per manum seruorum tuorum prophetarum, dicendo, Terra ad quam ingredimini, vt possideatis eam, terra immunda est ob immunditiā populorum terrarum, propter abominationes quibus repleuerunt eam ab ore ad os immunditia sua.
units.tr: 11 Which thou hast commanded by the hand of thy servants the prophets, saying: The land which you enter to possess is an unclean land, because of the filthiness of the peoples of the lands, with the abominations with which they have filled it from one end to the other with their uncleanness.

units.la: 12 Idcirco nunc filias vestras ne detis filijs eorum, & filias eorum ne accipiatis filijs vestris, neque quaeratis pacem eorum & bonum eorum vsque in seculum: vt confortemini, & comedatis bonum terræ, & iure hereditario (eam) possidendam tradatis filijs vestris vsque in seculum.
units.tr: 12 Therefore now give not your daughters to their sons, neither take their daughters for your sons, nor seek their peace or their prosperity for ever: that you may be strong, and eat the good of the land, and leave it by hereditary right to your children for ever.

units.la: 13 Post omnia vero quæ euenerunt nobis propter opera nostra mala, & propter delictū nostrum magnum, cum tu Deus noster prohibueris ne essemus deorsum propter iniquitates nostras, & dederis nobis euasionem talem.
units.tr: 13 And after all that has come upon us for our evil deeds and our great trespass, seeing that thou, our God, hast held us back from being brought low because of our iniquities, and hast given us such a deliverance as this,

units.la: 14 Nunquid reuertemur ad dissipandum præcepta tua, & ad affinitatem contrahendam cum populis abominationum istarum? nunquid non irasceris contra nos vsque ad consumptionem, ita vt non sit residuum & euasio?
units.tr: 14 Shall we again break thy commandments and enter into marriage ties with the peoples of these abominations? Wouldest thou not be angry with us until we were consumed, so that there should be no remnant and no escape?

units.la: 15 Iehouah Deus Israelis, tu es iustus, quoniam residui sumus filij euasionis secundum diem hanc: en ad sumus nos coram te in delictis nostris, neque enim licet nobis consistere coram te propter hoc.
units.tr: 15 O LORD God of Israel, thou art righteous, for we are left as an escaped remnant, as on this day: behold, we stand before thee in our trespasses, for none can stand before thee because of this.

units.la: INardente illa & feria precatione, quam Esdras præsente populo ad Deū effudit, principio sua & populi peccata palàm confessus est, propter quæ poenis affecti sint. Deum autem misericordiam illis tribuisse, eosque multis & magnis beneficijs affecisse: quibus neglectis Deum iterum offenderint.
units.tr: In that fervent and solemn prayer, which Ezra poured out to God in the presence of the people, he first openly confessed his own sins and those of the people, for which they had been punished. But God had shown them mercy and bestowed on them many great benefits, and when they neglected these, they offended God once more.

units.la: Iam propius accedit exponendo quomodo contra legem de nuptijs cum proscriptis populis non contrahendis peccarint, ob quam causam metuendum sit, ne nouas poenas attrahant. Nunc ergo quid dicemus post hæc?) Quod post hæc omnia quæ nobis euenerunt, nempe post peccatorum castigationem, & multiplicia beneficia à Deo accepta, tantum scelus impuden ter patrauimus ? Quando quis ea flagitia repetit, propter quæ castigatus est, vtq; prouerbio dicitur, Iterum eundem ad lapidem offendit, non potest excusari: item, quando quis illos à qui bus multis & magnis beneficijs affectos est, offendit. Dicit eos dereliquisse mandata, quæ per suos seruos prophetas præcepe-rit. Prophetæ non sua somnia tulerunt, sed illa quæ Deus ipsis instillauit, inculcarunt populo.
units.tr: Now he draws closer, explaining how they sinned against the law forbidding marriage with the banned peoples, and for this reason they must fear lest they bring new punishments upon themselves. "And now, what shall we say after this?" That after all these things that have befallen us, namely the chastisement of our sins and the many benefits received from God, we have committed so shameless a crime? When someone repeats the sins for which he was punished, and, as the proverb says, stumbles again over the same stone, he cannot be excused; likewise when someone offends those by whom he has been loaded with many great benefits. He says that they have abandoned the commandments which God delivered through his servants the prophets. The prophets did not bring forth their own dreams, but urged upon the people what God had instilled into them.

units.la: Terra in quam ingredimini, terra immunda est, &c.) Proscri-ptæ iliæ gentes, suis flagitijs terram suam polluerunt. Leuit.18. incestis libidinibus, item vt pasim apud prophetas legitur, auaritia, idololatria, magicis artibus, iniustis cædibus, & alijs id genus. De moribus illarum gentium Leuit.20. Num.33. Deut.9. 2.Reg.17. Ezech.16. Psal.100. Repleuerunt eum ore ad os immundi-tia sua.) Id est, vsq; ad summum. Metaphora sumpta à vasis, quæ ad labra vsq; plena sunt, Vatablus. Hæc phrasis 4.Reg.21. legitur de Manasse, quòd vrbem ab ore ad os sanguine impleuerit. Id-circo nunc filias vestras ne detis filijs eorum, & filias eorum ne acci-piatis filijs vestris.) Non dicit, Filiæ veστræ non nubant filijs eo-rum, aut filij non ducant vxores eorum filias. Non enim licebat olim liberis, inscijs & incofultis suis parentibus, aut qui eorum loco essent, matrimonium contrahere. Irrita erant coiugia, quæ absque parentum consensu fiebant. Quem morem vtile esset reuocari. Lex hæc extat Deut.7. causa additur: auocabit enim filium tuum, ne eat post me, & colent Deos alienos: propterea irascetur furor Iehouæ in nos, & disperdet vos cito, &c. Neq; quæratis pacem eorum, & bonum eorum vsq; in seculum.) Hoc est, ne curetis salutem & incolumitatem eorum: nil commune cum illis habeatis, imo interfici illos iussit. Annon hostes quoq; diligendos lex Dei præcipit? Respondendum est, hos declaratos fuisse hostes, & à Deo ipso proscriptos. Adijcitur promissio, qua Israelitæ ad obedientiam inuitantur: Vt confortemini.) Vt fortiores facti, illis possitis resistere. Et comedatis bonum terræ.) Ne alij fructus & fruges terræ, quæ fecunda fuit, absumant.
units.tr: "The land into which you enter is an unclean land, etc." Those banned nations polluted their land with their crimes: incestuous lusts (Lev. 18.), and, as is read everywhere in the prophets, avarice, idolatry, magical arts, unjust murders, and things of that kind. On the customs of those nations see Lev. 20., Num. 33., Deut. 9., 2 Kings 17., Ezek. 16., Ps. 100. "They have filled it from mouth to mouth with their uncleanness." That is, to the very brim. The metaphor is taken from vessels filled right up to the lips, Vatablus. This phrase is read in 4 Kings 21 of Manasseh, that he filled the city with blood from mouth to mouth. "Therefore now give not your daughters to their sons, and take not their daughters for your sons." He does not say, "Let your daughters not marry their sons, or your sons not take their daughters as wives." For formerly it was not lawful for children to contract marriage without the knowledge and counsel of their parents or those who stood in their place; marriages made without parental consent were void. It would be useful for that custom to be revived. This law stands in Deut. 7., and a reason is added there: "for he will turn your son away from following me, and they will serve other gods; so the anger of the LORD will be kindled against you, and he will destroy you quickly, etc." "Nor seek their peace and their prosperity for ever." That is, do not care for their welfare and safety; have nothing in common with them. Indeed he commanded that they be put to death. Does not the law of God also command us to love our enemies? It must be answered that these had been declared enemies and proscribed by God himself. A promise is added by which the Israelites are invited to obedience: "that you may be strong." That, having become stronger, you may be able to resist them. "And eat the good of the land." So that others may not consume the fruits and produce of a land that was fertile.

units.la: Vtq; iure hæreditario hanc terram tradere filijs & posteris veστris possitis. Magni beneficij loco habetur, si quis opes suas quantumuis modicas, iustis hæredibus relinquat. Cum tamen gra-ues pœnas dederimus propter ingentia nostra peccata, non ta-men vt illis meremur, funditus fumus extincti, & prorsus op-presi. Deus enim aliquas reliquias superesse voluit.
units.tr: "And that you may hand this land down by hereditary right to your sons and posterity." It is counted a great benefit if someone leaves his wealth, however modest, to rightful heirs. Yet although we have been given heavy punishments for our enormous sins, and not as we deserve, we have not been utterly uprooted and entirely crushed. For God wished some remnants to survive.

units.la: Verba illa, Quum tu prohibueris ne effemus deorsum, hunc habent sensum. Tu cohibuisti teipsum, ne propter iniquitates nostras, nos opprimeres. Vel, ne prorsus inferiores essemus inimicis nostris, vt resurgere nobis non liceret. Nam mox subijcit, Et dederis euasionem talem. Sic Deut. 28. Ponetque te Iehouah in caput, & non in caudam: erisque duntaxat sursum & non deorsum, &c. Vatablus. Nunquid reuertemur ad dissipandum praecepta tua? Cum pro tuis illis beneficijs, nos gratos praebere debeTemus, iterum violauimus praecepta tua, o Deus, & affinitatem cum proscriptis gentibus contraximus. Nunquid non irasceris contra nos vsq; ad consumtionem? Iustum quidem esset, vt nos omnes prorsus deleres propter peccata nostra, sed esto nobis propitius.
units.tr: "Since thou hast restrained us that we should not be brought low" has this sense: you restrained yourself, so that you would not crush us because of our iniquities. Or: that we would not be utterly inferior to our enemies, so that it would not be permitted us to rise again. For he soon adds, "and hast given such an escape." So Deut. 28.: "The LORD will set you on top and not at the tail; you shall be only above and not beneath," etc., Vatablus. "Shall we again break thy commandments?" Since we ought to show ourselves grateful for your benefits, we have again violated your commandments, O God, and contracted affinity with the banned nations. "Wouldest thou not be angry with us even to consumption?" It would indeed be just for you to wipe us all out utterly on account of our sins, but be propitious to us.

units.la: Tu es iustus. Irasceris peccatis. Nos qui euasimus vt palàm omnes vident, Adsumus coram te in delictis nostris, neq; consistere possumus coram te propter hæc. Nos graviter peccasse non audemus negare: confiteri quoq; nos oportet, quòd poena digni sumus, sed ne agas nobiscum secundum nostra merita.
units.tr: "Thou art righteous." You are angry at sins. We who have escaped, as all plainly see, "stand before you in our trespasses, and cannot stand before you because of these." We dare not deny that we have sinned grievously; we ought also to confess that we deserve punishment, but do not deal with us according to our merits.

units.la: Discimus ex hac parte precationis.
units.tr: We learn from this part of the prayer.

units.la: 1. Regiones propter incolarum scelera foedar & pollui: Deus autem eas purgat, eijciendo veteres colonos, &c.
units.tr: 1. Regions are defiled and polluted because of the sins of their inhabitants, but God cleanses them by casting out the old settlers, and so on.

units.la: 2. Illos graviter peccare, qui in contrahendo matrimonio verae religionis rationem non habent. Deus noluit vt Israelitae connubia cum proscriptis gentibus, & alijs quoque iungerent, quod ex subiecta ratione intelligitur. Abraam obstringit iureiurando seruum suum, ne apud idololatras Isaaco vxorem quaerat. Parentes Esau graviter offensi sunt, quòd inscijs ipsis, Ethnicas vxores duxisset. Si periculum non erat, quo ad religionem, licuit alienigenas ducere. Moses filiam Iethronis Madianitae, Salmon Rahabam, Booz Rutham, & alij Ethnicas duxerunt, sed ad fidem veram conuersas. Peccant adhuc graviter, qui idololatras vxores, filijs suis iungunt propter opes, familiam, &c. Gravius peccant, qui filias suas infidelibus elocant: maxima enim incurrunt pericula, adiguntur ad superstitiones à maritis, liberi in falsa religione educantur, &c.
units.tr: 2. Those who do not regard true religion when they contract marriage sin grievously. God did not wish the Israelites to join themselves in marriage with the condemned nations or with others, as is understood from the reason given below. Abraham bound his servant by oath not to seek a wife for Isaac among idolaters. Esau's parents were gravely offended that he had taken heathen wives without their knowledge. If there was no danger to religion, it was permitted to take foreign wives. Moses took the daughter of Jethro the Midianite, Salmon took Rahab, Boaz took Ruth, and others took heathen women, but these women had been converted to the true faith. Those who still join their sons to idolatrous wives for the sake of wealth, family, and so on, sin grievously. They sin even more gravely who give their daughters in marriage to unbelievers, for they incur the greatest dangers: they are driven into superstitions by their husbands, and their children are brought up in false religion, and so on.

units.la: 3. Iudaei propter sua peccata in magna mala inciderant: & metuit Esdras, ne iterum propter violatam legem poenas incurrant. Peccata verò sunt nostri fundi calamitas. De hoc supra quoq; dictum est.
units.tr: 3. Because of their sins the Jews had fallen into great calamities, and Ezra fears that they will again incur punishment for the violation of the law. Sins, moreover, are the cause of the calamity of our land. This has also been said above.

units.la: 4. Iterum quoq; discimus, Deum suu populum non prorsus excindere propter peccata, vt posset. Habac. 3. cap. Cum irasceris fceris,misericordiæ recordaris.
units.tr: 4. Again we learn that God does not utterly destroy his people on account of their sins, although he could. Habakkuk 3. "When you are angry, you remember mercy."

units.la: 5. Imbecillitatis humanæ magnum hoc est argumentum, quòd Iudæi ne iŝti quidem sapiunt,sed ad eundem lapidem offendunt: ne exilij quidem calamitas, meliores reddere potuit, liberati statim redeunt ad ingenium. In morbis nos quoq; Deo gratitudinem promittimus, in annonæ caritate,& alijs malis, quam liberati non præstamus.
units.tr: 5. This is a great proof of human weakness: the Jews, not even now made wise, stumble over the same stone. Not even the calamity of exile could make them better; once freed, they at once return to their old nature. In sickness we too promise gratitude to God, and in times of dear food and other troubles, but once delivered we do not perform it.

units.la: 6. Quoniam Deus iustus est,nos peccatores,coram ipso consistere non possumus. Sanctisimi quiq; se peccatores etse confesi sunt.Detestanda igitur illorum est superbia,qui sua me rita alijs precio vendunt.Si legem diuinam, & humanam miseriam rectè intelligerent,clamarent cum Dauide 130.Psalmo : Si iniquitates obseruaueris,Domine,quis sustinebit?Item Psalmo 6.Domine, ne in furore tuo arguas me : Miserere mei Domine, quia infirmus sum. Cum Isaia 64. cap. Et nunc Domine, pater noster es tu: nos vero lutum,& fictor noster es tu,& opera manuum tuarum omnes nos.Ne irascaris Domine valde,nec perpetuo memineris peccatorum nostrorum, ecce respice, populus tuus omnes nos. Cum Ierem.10.cap. Corripe me,sed in iudicio,non in furore,ne in nihilum redigar.
units.tr: 6. Since God is just, we sinners cannot stand before him. All the most holy have confessed themselves sinners. The pride of those who sell their own merits to others is therefore to be detested. If they rightly understood the divine law and human wretchedness, they would cry out with David in Psalm 130: "If you, Lord, should mark iniquities, who could stand?" Likewise in Psalm 6: "Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger; have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak." With Isaiah 64: "And now, Lord, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter, and we are all the work of your hands. Do not be angry, Lord, very much, nor remember our sins for ever; behold, look upon us, all of us your people." With Jeremiah 10: "Correct me, but in judgment, not in anger, lest I be brought to nothing."

units.la: Si verò Esdras fatetur propter violata matrimonia Iudæis pœnas imminere, quid de illis fiet, apud quos multa & magna sceleta publicè impunè grassantur? Cæterum ne propterea desperent,sed Dominum precentur,ut memor suæ misericordiæ, veram eis pœnitentiam largiatur, propter filium suum parcat.
units.tr: But if Ezra confesses that punishments threaten the Jews on account of their broken marriages, what will become of those among whom many great crimes openly run riot unpunished? Yet, lest they despair on that account, let them pray the Lord that, mindful of his mercy, he may grant them true repentance and spare them for the sake of his Son.

units.la: CAPVT X.
units.tr: CHAPTER X.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXV.
units.tr: HOMILY XXXV.

units.la: Ad Esdram multi confluunt, & lachrymas fundunt:Sechanias hortatur Esdram, vt opus fortiter aggrediatur,suamq; operam ei promittit.
units.tr: Many people flock to Ezra and shed tears. Shechaniah urges Ezra to take the work up boldly and promises him his own help.

units.la: QVum autem oraret Esra, & confiteretur flens, & deprimeret sese coram domo Dei, congregauerunt sese ad eum de Israele cœtus multus valde viro- rum & mulierum & parvulorum:quumq; fleuisset populus multo fletu.
units.tr: While Ezra was praying, confessing with weeping, and prostrating himself before the house of God, a very large crowd of men, women and small children gathered around him from Israel, and the people wept with great weeping.

units.la: 2 Tunc loquutus est Sechaniah filius Iehiel, de filijs Elam, & dixit ad Ezra, Nos praevaricati sumus in Deum nostrum, quod duximus mulieres alienigenas de populis terrae: at nunc spes est Israeli super hoc.
units.tr: 2 Then Shechaniah son of Jehiel, of the sons of Elam, spoke and said to Ezra: "We have trespassed against our God, in that we have taken foreign women from the peoples of the land. Yet now there is hope for Israel in this matter.

units.la: 3 Nunc ergo percutiamus foedus cum Deo nostro, quod eijciemus omnes mulieres, & natos ex eis, secundum consilium Domini, & (virorum) timentium praeceptum Dei nostri: & secundum legem fiat.
units.tr: 3 Now therefore let us make a covenant with our God that we will put away all the women and those born of them, according to the counsel of the Lord and of those who fear the commandment of our God; and let it be done according to the law.

units.la: 4 Surge, quia ad te pertinet res, & nos (erimus) tecum: confortare, & fac.
units.tr: 4 Arise, for the matter belongs to you, and we will be with you. Be strong, and act.

units.la: SVPERIORE Capite dictum est, populum, principes & ipsos sacerdotes, graviter peccasse ducendo vxores Ethnicas. Deinde quid Esdras fecerit cum hoc intellexisset. Paucis hoc loco repetitur, quod ardentes preces effuderit ad Deum: quodq; confessus sit sua & populi peccata. Additur, quod supra non est dictum, eum profudisse lachrymas, & humi prostratum iacuisse coram templo. Quae omnia eo pertinent, ut populus in se descendens, poenitentiam agat.
units.tr: In the previous chapter it was said that the people, and even the princes and the priests themselves, had sinned gravely by marrying heathen wives, and then what Ezra did when he understood this. Here it is briefly repeated that he poured out fervent prayers to God, and confessed his own and the people's sins. There is added something not said above: that he shed tears and lay prostrate on the ground before the temple. All these things serve to make the people go into themselves and do penance.

units.la: Sequitur quid his effecerit Esdras. Primo loco aggregatus est ad ipsum maximus coetus virorum, mulierum & puerorum: qui etiam ipsi in lachrymas soluti sunt. Confluxerunt alij propter nouitatem & insolentiam rei, alij propter commiserationem vt eum consolarentur, lachrymas vero cogitatio malorum futurorum praecipue eis videtur excusisse.
units.tr: Next comes what the people did in response to this. First, a very large gathering of men, women and boys came together to him, and they too dissolved into tears. Some came together because of the novelty and strangeness of the matter, others out of pity, so that they might console him; but the thought of the evils to come seems chiefly to have wrung tears from them.

units.la: Discimus ex his verbis, quantam vim exemplum procerum ecclesiae habeat. Vnicus Esdras suo loco commouit totum populum, qui durę ceruicis passim in scripturis appellatur, idq; in re tam magna & ardua. Quid si plures Esdrae fuissent? Idem de Mardocheo in libro Hester legitur. Si principes illa faciunt, quae aliis praescribunt, obsequentem plerunq; habent populum.
units.tr: From these words we learn how great a power the example of the leaders of the Church has. Ezra alone moved the whole people, which is everywhere in Scripture called stiff-necked, and this in a matter so great and arduous. What if there had been several Ezras? The same is read about Mordecai in the book of Esther. If the leaders do what they prescribe to others, the people generally obey them.

units.la: Accusanda est illa hominum nostro tempore socordia, qui bus cum quotidie miserabilis status fidelium qui ab Antichristo vexantur, imo suum met exitium ob oculos positum sit: tamen ne lachrimula illis excidit.
units.tr: That sloth of men in our own time is to be condemned: though the miserable state of the faithful, who are harassed by Antichrist, lies daily before their eyes, and their very own ruin is set before them, yet not a little tear falls from them.

units.la: Secundo loco Sechanias vir egregius, cuius genus vno verbo indicatur, prodit, ac primum cofitetur & se & alios peccasse aduersus Deum. Appellat Deum suum etiam postea, quod non caret Emphasi,qui eos tot tantisq; beneficijs affecerit, qui lege ipsis dederit,&c. Qua in re peccarunt?quod duxerunt vxores ex proscriptis gentibus.Non dicit,(e atq; alios hoc bono consilio fecisse: vicinas enim gentes hac via Iudæos cóciliare voluisse:non accusat Efdram,quod nimis rigidus fit.Non dicit:Quod factum est,infectum fieri non potest, aut aliquid huius generis, sed peccatum ingenuè confitetur.
units.tr: Second, Shechaniah, an outstanding man whose family is indicated by a single word, steps forward, and first confesses that both he and others have sinned against God. Afterwards he also calls God "his God", which is not without emphasis, since God had bestowed so many and great benefits on them, and had given them the law, and so on. In what did they sin? In that they married wives from the peoples who had been condemned. He does not say that he and others did this with a good intention, for they wished to win over the neighbouring nations to the Jews in this way. He does not accuse Ezra of being too strict. He does not say: "What has been done cannot be undone," or anything of that kind, but he frankly confesses the sin.

units.la: Deinde spem facit Efdræ quod peccatum illud corrigi posse. Semper enim sunt, etiam in vulgo, qui rationibus idoneis mouentur,&c in viam redeunt.
units.tr: Then he gives Ezra hope that this sin can be corrected. For there are always some, even among the common people, who are moved by sound reasons and return to the right way.

units.la: Tertio quid faciendum videatur aperit. Nunc ergo percutiamus fœdus cum Deo nostro, quod eiecimus omnes mulieres et natos ex eis, secundum consilium Domini, et timentium præceptum Dei nostri et secundum legem fiat. karaph pepigit, percussit item incidit, discidit. Solebant enim Iudæi in fœderibus vitas ferire. Genesis 15. & Ieremiæ 34. Sextus Pompeius fœdus appellatum ab eo scribit, quod in paciscendo fœdere, hostia necaretur. Apud Romanos porcam fœdè, hoc est, crudeliter silice percutiebant. Unde illud Vergilij, Et cæsa iurgebant fœdera porca, etc. Item moris fuit fœdera æri vel lapidi incidere, ut posteris quoq; nota essent. Non autem putandum est quod Iudæi hoc loco nouum fœdus inierint; sed quod vetus innouarint, quod Deus inierat cum Israelitis. Hoc fœdus vel pactum duo habet capita. In primo pollicetur eis, quod Deus ipsorum esse velit; in altero exigit à suis fœderatis, ut sint populus suus, ut faciant quæ præcipit, ut caueant sibi ab illis quæ vetat. Perfidi hoc fœdus ruperant, renouandum igitur dicit, hoc est, sacramento adstringendos Iudæos, ut cum alia corrigant, tum vxores alienigenas dimittant. Vult autem renouari fœdus secundum consilium Dei, & eorum qui verbum Dei timent, hoc est, piorum. Psalmo 61. Tu dedisti hæreditatem timentium nomen tuum, hoc est, quæ manet omnes cultores Dei, vt legi congrua fiant. Vtile esset hodie quoq; à pagis, oppidis, regnis,& etiam à singulis hominibus fœdus illud renouari, vt expellerentur, scortatio, auaritia, &c.
units.tr: Third, he shows what seems to be needed. "Now therefore let us make a covenant with our God, that we will put away all the women and those born of them, according to the counsel of the Lord and of those who fear the commandment of our God; and let it be done according to the law." Karath [כרת] means to strike a covenant, and also to cut or divide, for the Jews used to cut animals in two when making covenants. See Genesis 15 and Jeremiah 34. Sextus Pompeius writes that the word foedus (covenant) was so called from the fact that a victim was slain in making a covenant. Among the Romans they struck a sow with a flint stone, that is, they slew it cruelly; hence the line of Virgil: "And the covenants were confirmed with the slain sow," and so on. It was also the custom to engrave covenants on bronze or stone, so that they would be known to posterity as well. We must not think, however, that the Jews here entered into a new covenant, but that they renewed the old one which God had made with the Israelites. This covenant or pact has two parts. In the first, God promises them that he wishes to be their God; in the second, he requires of those bound to him that they be his people, that they do what he commands, and that they guard themselves against what he forbids. The faithless had broken this covenant, so he says it must be renewed, that is, that the Jews must be bound by oath, so that they may correct other things, and also put away their foreign wives. He wishes the covenant to be renewed according to the counsel of God and of those who fear God's word, that is, of the godly. Psalm 61: "You have given the inheritance of those who fear your name," that is, the one which remains for all worshippers of God, so that they may be made to agree with the law. It would be useful today too, that this covenant be renewed by villages, towns, kingdoms, and even by individual men, so that fornication, avarice and so on might be driven out.

units.la: Hæc est optima regula instituendi & emendandi ad παιδείαν & ἐπανορθῶσιν, vt verbo & legi Dei omnia conformentur.
units.tr: This is the best rule for instructing and correcting, for paideia [παιδεία] and epanorthosis [ἐπανόρθωσις], so that all things may be conformed to the Word and the law of God.

units.la: Quarto loco Sechanias hortatur Efdram, vt graviter rem aggrediatur. Iubet eum surgere omissis querelis & lamentis. Licet enim sanctos sæpe legamus plorasse, tamen modus illa in re est tenendus. Deinde cum hortatur, vt de corrigendo hoc peccato agere incipiat. Hoc enim sui muneris esse, qui magnæ sit apud regem authoritatis, & sacerdos. Nos sæpe reijcimus in alios quò domnium, & præcipuè nostrum est officium, vt nostrę quieti consulamus. Politici dicunt esse munus ministrorum ecclesiæ, hæc vel illa facere: hi dicunt, ad illos pertinere. Spondet suam & populi operam & opem illi non defuturam. Homines etiam infimæ conditionis possunt aliquando bonæ causæ prodesse. Incitat vt forti & excelso animo, rem quantumuis difficilem capessat.
units.tr: Fourth, Shechaniah urges Ezra to take the matter up seriously. He bids him rise, leaving off complaints and laments. For although we often read that the saints wept, yet a measure must be kept in such matters. Then he urges him to begin to deal with correcting this sin, for this is the duty of one who has great authority with the king and is also a priest. We often shift onto others what is especially our own duty, namely to look to our own peace. Politicians say that it is the business of the ministers of the Church to do this or that; these men say that it belongs to those others. He promises that his own and the people's effort and help will not be lacking to him. Men of even the lowest condition can sometimes be of service to a good cause. He encourages him to take up a matter however difficult with a brave and lofty spirit.

units.la: Ideo autem vxores exteræ dimittendæ erant, quòd coniugia illa contra legem contracta, ideoq; non vera & legitima erat. Christus Matth. 5. & 19. dicit: Dico vobis quòd quicunq; repudiauerit vxorem suam, nisi ob stuprum, & aliam duxerit, is commit adulterium. Et qui repudiatam (scilicet non intercedente legitima causa) duxerit, is adulterium committit.
units.tr: The foreign wives had to be put away because those marriages had been contracted against the law and therefore were not true and lawful. Christ says in Matthew 5 and 19: "I say to you that whoever puts away his wife, except for fornication, and marries another, commits adultery; and whoever marries one who has been put away (that is, without a lawful cause intervening) commits adultery."

units.la: Vsus.
units.tr: Usus.

units.la: 1. Deum semper excitare viros bonos, quibus curæ est correctio scelerum, vt iram Dei auertant. De hoc Sechania cuius laudes in ecclesia perpetuò celebrabuntur, nihil Esdras fortasis sciebat: certè non expectare potuit se ab eo iuuandum.
units.tr: 1. God always raises up good men who care for the correction of sins, so that they may turn away the wrath of God. Of this Shechaniah, whose praises will be celebrated forever in the Church, Ezra perhaps knew nothing; at any rate he could not have expected to be helped by him.

units.la: 2. Etsi nos quoq; peccauerimus, iungamus tamen nos sem per melioribus. Multi cum sciant se ijsdem vitijs laborare, quibus alij quos coercere debebant, nolunt officium suum facere. Cum Israelitæ adorassent vitulum, Exod. 32. conflatilem, & Moses pœnas de illis sumturus esset, qui factum defendebant, filij Leui se iunxerunt Mosi, qui etiam idololatriam exercuerant, contra seditiosos. Sechanias etiam vxorem Ethnicam videtur habuisse, tamen pro se & alijs promittit, se suo officio non defuturum.
units.tr: 2. Even if we too have sinned, let us nevertheless always join ourselves to the better sort. Many, though they know they are afflicted with the same vices as those whom they ought to restrain, are unwilling to do their duty. When the Israelites had worshipped the molten calf (Exod. 32), and Moses was about to exact punishment from those who defended the deed, the sons of Levi joined themselves to Moses, though they too had practised idolatry, against the seditious. Shechaniah also seems to have had a foreign wife, yet he promises on his own behalf and on behalf of others that he will not fail in his duty.

units.la: 3. Non statim de populis, vel etiam malis hominibus est desperandum. Etsi obstinati in sceleribus esse videantur, vt nulla conuersio in melius sit speranda: tamen facilè potest fieri, vt Deus tangat corda eorum. In 2. ad Timotheum 2. capite: Seruum Domini non oportet pugnare, sed placidum esse erga omnes, propensum ad docendum, tolerantem malos cum mansuetudine, erudientem eos, qui obsistunt, si quando det illis Deus pœnitentiam ad agnoscendam veritatem, & resipiscant è diaboli laqueo, capti ab eo ad ipsius voluntatem. Quis putasset vel hunc Sechaniam vel populum, posse in viam reuocari?
units.tr: 3. One must not despair at once of the peoples, or even of wicked men. Even if they seem obstinate in their sins, so that no conversion for the better is to be hoped for, nevertheless it can easily happen that God touches their hearts. In 2 Timothy 2: "The servant of the Lord must not strive, but be gentle towards all, apt to teach, patient towards evil men, instructing those who oppose him, if perhaps God may give them repentance to acknowledge the truth, and they may come to their senses out of the snare of the devil, having been taken captive by him to his will." Who would have thought that either this Shechaniah or the people could be brought back to the way?

units.la: 4 Non solum alios hortari debes data occasione, vt suum faciant officium: sed vbicunq; potes opera tua prodesse Reipublicæ vel ecclesiæ, aut etiam priuatis hominibus, ne patiaris eam à te desiderari, intuere huius Sechaniæ exemplum.
units.tr: 4. You ought not only to exhort others, when occasion offers, to do their duty, but wherever you can, let your work benefit the commonwealth or the Church, or even private persons, lest you allow it to be missed from you. Look to the example of this Shechaniah.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXVI.
units.tr: HOMILY XXXVI.

units.la: Esdras rem aggreditur, indicuntur comitia.
units.tr: Ezra undertakes the business; an assembly is called.

units.la: 5 Surrexit itaq; Esdra, & adiurauit principes sacerdotum ac Leuitarum vniuersumq; Israelem, vt facerent secundum verbum hoc: & iurauerunt.
units.tr: 5 So Ezra rose up and made the chief priests, the Levites and all Israel swear that they would act according to this word. And they swore.

units.la: 6 Surrexit inquam Ezra a facie domus Dei, & abijt in cubiculum Iehohanan filij Eliasib: abijt inquā illuc, & panem non comedit, nec aquam bibit: lugebat enim ob præuaricationem (filiorum) transmigrationis.
units.tr: 6 Ezra, I say, rose up from before the house of God and went into the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. He went there, I say, and neither ate bread nor drank water, for he mourned over the transgression of those (sons) of the captivity.

units.la: 7 Et voce præconis significarunt in Iehudah & Ierusalaim omnibus filijs transmigrationis, vt congregarentur in Ierusalaim.
units.tr: 7 And by the voice of a herald they gave notice in Judah and Jerusalem to all the sons of the captivity that they should gather together at Jerusalem.

units.la: 8 Quicunque vero non veniret intra triduum, iuxta consilium principum & seniorum, periret vniuersa substantia eius, ipseque separaretur à cœtu transmigrationis.
units.tr: 8 Whoever did not come within three days, according to the counsel of the princes and elders, his whole property would be forfeit, and he himself would be separated from the assembly of the captivity.

units.la: Esdras eximius seruus Dei, suo exemplo omnes homines, in primis vero proceres docet, quomodo affecti esse debeant flagitijs publice grassantibus, nempe dolorem suum quisque testari debet, deq; corrigendis illis sedulo cogitare. Additur consolatio, quod Deus semper alios quoq; excitaturus sit, qui bonorum conatus adiuuent. Accurrerunt multi ad Esdram qui συμπαθειαν suam testati sunt, inter quos Sechanias fuit. Is hortatus est Esdram vt negotiū hoc fortiter aggrediatur, suam quoq; opem illi promittens.
units.tr: Ezra, the outstanding servant of God, by his own example teaches all people, and especially the leading men, how they ought to be moved by sins that rage openly in public: each one must bear witness to his grief and think earnestly about correcting them. Consolation is added, that God will always stir up others also who will support the efforts of good men. Many ran to Ezra and bore witness to their sympathy [συμπάθειαν], among whom was Shecaniah. He urged Ezra to take up the business boldly, promising his own help as well.

units.la: Sequitur quomodo Esdras se gesserit, & quid alij quoq; fecerint. 1. Esdras surrexit, & iureiurando præcipuos sacerdotum & Leuitarum obstrinxit, totumq; Israelem, vt agerent secundum hoc verbum, hoc est, vt dimitterent vxores alienigenas. Non obligandi sunt homines contra Dei verbum. Iusiurandum enim non vinculum debet esse iniquitatis. Qui iusiurandum praestant, Deum quasi testem constituunt, quod non fallere velint, & petunt ut puniat fallentes.
units.tr: Next comes how Ezra conducted himself and what the others also did. (1) Ezra rose up and bound the chief priests and Levites by oath, and all Israel too, that they would act according to this word, that is, that they would put away their foreign wives. Men must not be bound against the word of God. For an oath ought not to be a bond of iniquity. Those who take an oath make God their witness that they wish not to deceive, and they ask that he punish deceivers.

units.la: Ex hac historia facile intelligi potest, quanta dignitas apud veteres fuerit iusiurandi: non enim dubitat Esdras, quin id facturi sint, ad quod se iure iurando obstrinxerunt. Ezras exigit ab illis iusiurandum: quia a rege Persico magnam potestatem acceperat, non quod politici a sacerdotibus & Leuitis iusiurandum exigere non potuerint. Vt hodie clerici de nescio qua immunitate gloriantur, nec nisi suo competenti iudici, vt loquuntur, iusiurandum dare volunt. Praecipui ex sacerdotibus & Leuitis iurarunt in re magna, honesta, & quę fieri potuit. Iurarunt & alij, & sponte obtemperarunt: Iuramus & nos. Christus enim iusiurandum non sustulit Matthaei quinto capite. Hoc dolendum est, quod multi interposito per Dei nomen iureiurando aliquid confirmantes, fidem datam non seruant.
units.tr: From this story it can easily be understood how great was the dignity of the oath among the ancients. For Ezra does not doubt that they will do what they have bound themselves by oath to do. Ezra exacts the oath from them, because he had received great authority from the Persian king; not that civil magistrates could not have demanded an oath from priests and Levites. Today clerics boast of I know not what immunity, and are unwilling to give an oath except to their own competent judge, as they put it. The chief men among the priests and Levites swore concerning a great, honourable matter that could be done. Others swore too, and of their own accord obeyed. We too swear: for Christ did not abolish the oath, in Matthew chapter 5. It is to be lamented that many, confirming something by an oath taken in God's name, do not keep the faith they have given.

units.la: 2 Esdras ab area templi, vbi prostratus iacuerat, se contulit in conclaue Iohanan, illo die neque panem comedit neque aquam bibit, hoc est nihil edit neque bibit. Hebraei per panem quemlibet cibum: per aquam quemlibet potum intelligunt: ȷ. Regum decimotertio capite. Causa subiungitur quia in luctu erat, propter illos qui liberati ex captiuitate, se tam male gesserant. Solebant autem qui in magna tristitia versabantur, ieiuna re. Rebus asperis, publice etiam ieiunia indicta sunt. Exempla passim sunt obuia. Quid vero nos periculosis temporibus facimus? Quotusquisque est qui sponte ieiunet: vel propter sua, nedum aliorum peccata, luctum suscipiat? Quid tam triste accidere potest, vt quidam vel semel sibi a compotationibus temperent? Quin multo mero tristitiam depellunt. Papistae merito euangelicos ea in re accusant: quod ieiunia fere nulla habeant, interim vero non considerant quomodo ipsi ieiunent.
units.tr: 2 Ezra withdrew from the court of the temple, where he had lain prostrate, into the chamber of Jehohanan; on that day he neither ate bread nor drank water, that is, he took no food and no drink. The Hebrews understand by bread any food whatever, and by water any drink: see 1 Kings chapter 13. The cause is added: he was in mourning on account of those who, freed from captivity, had behaved so badly. Those who were in great sorrow were accustomed to fast. In harsh circumstances, public fasts were also appointed. Examples are everywhere to be found. But what do we do in dangerous times? How few are there who fast of their own accord, or take up mourning, not to mention for their own sins, let alone those of others? What can happen so sad that some would refrain from drinking parties even once? Indeed, they drive away sadness with plenty of wine. The Papists rightly accuse the evangelicals in this matter, that they have almost no fasts; yet meanwhile they do not consider how they themselves fast.

units.la: 3 Indicitur conuentus, vbi circumstantiae illae obseruandae sunt, a quo, quomodo, qui, quonam, quando conuocati sint. Iuferunt principes & seniores, vt mox sequitur vocari, nimirum per precones, omnes viros in Iuda & Ierusalem, qui ex captiuitate reuersi erant, vt intra triduum Hierosolymis congregarentur, quo communi consensu transgressio legis emendaretur. Ad verbum est, Et transfire fecerunt vocem in Iuda: nostri dicunt, sy habend ein rufflassen gon/oder habend lassen vrrufen Statuitur. tuitur duplex poena contra inobedientes & contumaces, qui intra hoc tempus non veniant, ciuilis & ecclesiastica. Ciuilis fuit quod facultates eorum diripiendæ sint. Ad verbum, Perdetur vel anathemati subijcietur omnis substantia eius. בחרם Charam significat occidere, cuertere, ita aliquid perdere, vt nulla vtilitas ex eo amplius percipi posit. Chærem occisio, excisio, interfectio, anathema reddunt. Septuaginta anathemata vocant ἀφιερώματα donaria, hoc est, quæ dijs consecrata suspenduntur in parietibus & columnis templi, &c. ab ἀνάθεμα ut ἀνάθημα, quia ab hominum vsu exempta fuerunt. Sensus igitur est, opes in fiscum referentur, vel à Deo consecrabuntur.
units.tr: 3 An assembly is called, and in it the circumstances must be observed: by whom, how, who, where, and when they were summoned.
