The princes and elders issued the order, as follows directly, that is, by heralds, that all men in Judah and Jerusalem who had returned from captivity should be summoned to gather at Jerusalem within three days, so that by common consent the transgression of the law might be remedied. Literally it reads, "they caused the voice to pass through Judah"; our people say, "to have a proclamation made" or "to have it cried out." A twofold penalty is laid down against the disobedient and the stubborn who do not come within this time: a civil and an ecclesiastical penalty. The civil penalty was that their goods were to be seized. Literally: "all his substance shall be lost or devoted to destruction" [בחרם, Charam]. Charam means to kill, to overthrow, thus to destroy something so that no further benefit can be drawn from it. They render charam as slaying, cutting off, killing, or anathema. The Seventy call the anathemata "dedicated offerings" [ἀφιερώματα], that is, things consecrated to the gods and hung on the walls and columns of the temple, etc., from anathema as anathema [ἀνάθημα], because they were removed from human use. The sense, then, is that the goods are carried into the treasury, or are consecrated to God.

units.la: Ecclesiastica vel spiritualis poena fuit, vt excludantur à coetu captiuorum, hoc est, ab ecclesia reuersorum ex captiuitate Babylonica. Idem esse videtur quod Ioannis nono capite ἀποσυνάγωγον fieri, excludi à synagoga: nos dicimus, excommunicari. Ideo autem duplex poena fuit constituta, vt si quem vna non moueret, saltem altera ad obedientiam adigeret. Legibus vero sanctio additur, hoc est, poena qua transgressores afficiendi sint. 1. Samuelis vndecimo capite, Saul conscidit par boum, & fruitris in singulas tribus misisis, mandat vt ad bellum Ammoniticum secum veniant, qui secus fecerit, ita se facturum bobus eius. Edictis hodie quoq; adduntur poenæ, quod nisi hoc vel illud subiecti faciant, bona eorum in fiscum redigenda, aut ipsi in exilium eijciendi sint, &c.
units.tr: The ecclesiastical or spiritual penalty was that they should be shut out from the assembly of the captives, that is, from the church of those who had returned from Babylonian captivity. This seems to be the same as being made "put out of the synagogue" [ἀποσυνάγωγον] in John chapter 9, that is, excluded from the synagogue: we say, excommunicated. The reason a twofold penalty was set was that, if one did not move a man by the first, the second would at least drive him to obedience. A sanction is also added to the law, that is, the punishment by which transgressors are to be afflicted. In 1 Samuel chapter 11, Saul cut a yoke of oxen in pieces and sent the pieces through all the tribes, ordering that whoever did not come with him to the war against the Ammonites would be treated the same way with his oxen. Today too, penalties are added to edicts: unless subjects do this or that, their goods are to be taken into the treasury, or they themselves are to be cast into exile, etc.

units.la: Kssus.
units.tr: Kssus.

units.la: 1 Discimus occasionem quæ ex tempore sumitur, rerum præclarè gerendarum, non negligendam esse. Cum ad Elisabeth magnus hominum concursus fieret, cum lamentarentur, emendationemque vitæ & opem suam promitterent, Deo fretus, admolitur manum. Non dicit, quid tentarem? quia semel perfidi fuistis, semper eritis tales, non agitis ex animo. Nostri proverbium circumferunt, Ferrum dum candet, malleo tractandum esse. Si potes habere auxiliatores contra insidias hostiles: Item propensos ad celerum emendationem, arripe illam occasionem. Diuus Paulus scribit ad Ephesios quinto capite: Videte quomodo circumspecte, ἀκριβῶς ambuletis, non vt insipientes, sed vt sapientes, ἐξαγοραζόμενοι τὸν καιρόν, redimentes occasionem vel opportunitatem, quod dies mali sint. Ad Colossenses quoque quarto capite, Sapienter
units.tr: 1 We learn that an opportunity seized at the right moment for accomplishing things well is not to be neglected. When a great crowd of people gathered around Elisabeth, lamenting and promising amendment of life and their help, he trusted in God and set his hand to the work. He does not say, "Why should I try? You have been treacherous once, so you will always be such; you do not act from the heart." Our people circulate the proverb that iron must be worked with the hammer while it is hot. If you can have helpers against hostile plots, and people inclined to quick amendment, seize that opportunity. Saint Paul writes to the Ephesians in chapter five: "See that you walk carefully [ἀκριβῶς], not as the unwise but as the wise, redeeming the time [ἐξαγοραζόμενοι τὸν καιρόν], or the opportunity, because the days are evil." Also to the Colossians in chapter four: "Wisely

units.la: Occasio ob ferunda. ambulate, inquit, erga extraneos, opportunitatem redimentes. Metaphora sumpta est ab iis, qui conuenienti tempore res ne cessarias emunt.
units.tr: Occasion to be seized. "Walk," he says, "towards outsiders, redeeming the opportunity." The metaphor is taken from those who buy necessary goods at a convenient time.

units.la: 2 Constantiæ exemplum in Esdra obseruandum est, non duntaxat ad breue tempus serió egit: sed perseuerauit donec rem perfecit.
units.tr: 2 The example of constancy in Ezra is to be observed: he did not merely act earnestly for a short time, but persevered until he finished the business.

units.la: 3 Fructus quis sit exhortationum videmus ex hoc loco. Sechaniæ enim adhortatio nô frustranea fuit. Quare nos inuicem ad pietatis & virtutis studium incitemus: cohortationes item ex Dei verbo factas, fide amplectamur.
units.tr: 3 We see from this passage what fruit exhortations bear. For the exhortation of Shechaniah was not in vain. Therefore let us stir one another up to zeal for godliness and virtue; and let us also embrace with faith the exhortations made from the word of God.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXVII.
units.tr: HOMILY XXXVII.

units.la: Venisse omnes ad comitia: & quid in illis actum sit ostenditur.
units.tr: That all came to the assembly, and what was done there is shown.

units.la: 9 Congregati sunt itaq; omnes viri Iehudah & Beniamin in Ierusalaim intra triduum illud, vicesima (die) mensis (ipse (erat) mensis nonus) sederunt q; vni- uersus populus in platea domus, tremente propter rem illam, & propter pluuias.
units.tr: 9 So all the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered together at Jerusalem within those three days. On the twentieth day of the month (this was the ninth month), all the people sat in the open square of the house, trembling both because of the matter and because of the rain.

units.la: 10 Surrexit itaq; Ezra sacerdos, & dixit ad eos, Vos prœuaricati estis, quòd duxistis mulieres alie- nigenas, vt adderetis delicto Israelis.
units.tr: 10 Then Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, You have transgressed and married foreign women, to add to the guilt of Israel.

units.la: 11 Quapropter nunc date confessionem Iehouæ Deo patrum vestrorum, & facite voluntatem eius, & separamini à populis terræ & ab vxoribus alieni- genis.
units.tr: 11 Now therefore make confession to the LORD God of your fathers, and do his will, and separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign wives.

units.la: 12 Et responderunt totus cœtus, ac dixerunt vo- ce magna, sic secundum verbum tuum nobis est facien dum.
units.tr: 12 And all the assembly answered and said with a loud voice, As you have said, so must we do.

units.la: 13 At populus multus est, & tempus pluuiarum est, neq; est vis ad standum foris: adhæc opus non est diei vnius, neq; duorum, quia multi sumus qui prœuari- cati sumus in hoc.
units.tr: 13 But the people are many, and it is the season of rain, and we cannot stand outside. Nor is this a work of one day or two, for we are many who have transgressed in this matter.

units.la: 14 Stent obsecro principes nostri in vniuerso cœ- tu, & quicunq; in vrbibus nostris (fuerit) qui duxerit vxores alienigenas, veniat temporibus statutis, & cum cum eis (sint)seniores singularum urbium, & iudices earum, donec auertamus iram furoris Dei nostri a nobis propter hoc.
units.tr: 14 Let our princes, I beg you, stand for the whole assembly, and let all who in our cities have taken foreign wives come at the appointed times, and with them the elders of each city and its judges, until we turn away the fierce anger of our God from us because of this.

units.la: Diximus comitia a senioribus indicta esse Hierosolymam sub graui poena: iam sequitur omnes ibi convenisse, item quid actum sit commemoratur, nempe eos consultasse de amendo hoc scandalo.
units.tr: We have said that the assembly was summoned to Jerusalem by the elders under heavy penalty. Now it follows that all gathered there, and it is recorded what was done, namely that they took counsel about remedying this scandal.

units.la: 1 Omnes viri Iuda & Beniamin tempore constituto, nempe 20. die mensis 9. (qui Cisleu dicitur, & partim Nouembri, partim Decembri respondet) Hierosolyma venerunt: & universus populus sedit in vijs, vel platea coram templo, hoc est in area, atrio, vel vt iam loquuntur, in ca mpo ecclesiastico.
units.tr: All the men of Judah and Benjamin came to Jerusalem at the appointed time, that is, on the twentieth day of the ninth month (which is called Kislev, and corresponds partly to November and partly to December). And all the people sat in the streets, or in the square before the temple, that is, in the court, the courtyard, or, as they now say, in the ecclesiastical field.

units.la: Trementes propter rem ipsam & pluuias.) Causa tremoris illius duae erant, vna naturalis, altera spiritualis. Spiritualis, propter rem, hoc est, negotium illud ob quod illuc conuenerant, id est propter admissi sceleris conscientiam, & vltionis diuinae metum. Deus bone, quam pauci hodie sunt qui propter scelera sua tremant: non desunt qui potius de illis glorientur. Naturalis, propter frigus hybernum, & pluuias. Ey schu bertend.
units.tr: Trembling because of the matter itself and the rains. There were two causes of that trembling, one natural, the other spiritual. The spiritual cause was the matter itself, that is, the business for which they had assembled there, namely the consciousness of the wickedness they had committed and the fear of divine vengeance. Good God, how few there are today who tremble on account of their sins! There is no shortage of those who rather boast of them. The natural cause was the winter cold and the rains. Ey schu bertend.

units.la: 2 Quid actum sit in his comitijs.
units.tr: 2. What was done in this assembly.

units.la: 1 Esdras, ita nimirum volentibus proceribus, surrexit, & negotium retulit ad populum, & proposuit in consultationem. Rem paucis completitur. Primo peccatum eis ponit ob oculos, deinde consulit ipsis quo pacto se gerere debeant. Vos, inquit, praevaricati estis.) Hoc est, perfide egistis: mox specialius exprimit, quibus in rebus peccarint. Quod duxistis mulieres alienigenas.) Non omnes culpae erant obnoxij, tamen ad omnes hoc dicit. Nam si diutius hanc foeditatem tulissent, tales iudicandi erant. Vt adderetis delicto Israel.) Sic enim delicta noua accesione auxistis: adiecistis ad cumulum peccatorum vestrorum, gliche clo ob ir nit sunst gnug sunden vffud heitinb. Mox hortatur eos vel consulit, vt Deo, quem Deum patrum eorum Emphatice vocat, confiteantur: scilicet sua peccata, agnoscant culpam, non extenuent, dicentes: Vxores nostrae priores, morosae, rixosae, deformes &c. fuerc. Vel, vt confiteantur Domino, hoc est, eum celebrent & laudent, agnoscendo sua peccata, & bonitatem eius laudando. Deus enim glorificatur agnitione & confessione peccatorum. Iosue septimo capite, Iosue dicit ad Achanem, Fili mi, da quaeso gloriam Iehouae Deo Israel, & da ei confessionem,atq; indica mihi quid feceris,&c.
units.tr: 1 Esdras: with the nobles evidently agreeing, he rose, brought the matter before the people, and laid it open for their deliberation. He sums it up in a few words. First he sets their sin before their eyes, then he advises them how they ought to conduct themselves. "You," he says, "have trespassed." That is, you have acted faithlessly. Then he states more particularly in what they have sinned: "that you have taken foreign women." Not all of them were guilty, yet he speaks to all of them, for if they had tolerated this foulness any longer they would have been judged in the same way. "So that you add to the guilt of Israel." For by this new addition you have increased their offences and added to the heap of your sins (German gloss: as if your own sins were not already enough without heathen ones). Next he exhorts them, or advises them, to make confession to the Lord, whom he emphatically calls the God of their fathers. That is, they should acknowledge their own sins and not minimise their guilt, saying, "Our former wives were troublesome, quarrelsome, ugly," and so on. Or they should confess to the Lord, that is, praise and glorify him, by acknowledging their sins and extolling his goodness. For God is glorified by the acknowledgement and confession of sins. In Joshua chapter 7, Joshua says to Achan: "My son, give, I pray you, glory to the LORD God of Israel, and make confession to him, and tell me what you have done," and so on.

units.la: Et facite voluntatem eius.) Non tyrannidem affectamus, non imperium in vos,non lucrum quaerimus, sed vt faciatis quod Deus vult,quo ad coniugia & alia. Isaiae primo capite,Cessate a malo,& discite bonum facere.
units.tr: "And do his will." We are not aiming at tyranny, we are not seeking dominion over you, nor are we seeking gain; rather, that you should do what God wills, in matters of marriage and other things. Isaiah chapter 1: "Cease to do evil, learn to do good."

units.la: Et separamini a populis terrae & ab uxoribus alienigenis.) Quorum comercium Deus tam diligenter vetuit. Numeri 35. Deut. 7. Iosue capite 23. Praecauete igitur diligentissime vobis,vt diligatis Iehouam Deum vestrum: Quod si auertendo auersi fueritis,& adhaeseritis resiliuis gentibus istis, reliquis inquam istis, quae sunt nobiscum: & affinitatem contraxeritis cum eis,& ipsae vobiscum: Iam nunc scitote quod posthac Iehoua Deus vester non expellet omnes gentes istas a facie vestra: sed potius erunt vobis in laqueum & offendiculum, & flagellum in lateribus vestris,& in spinas in oculis vestris, donec pereatis e terra optima ista quam dedit vobis Iehoua Deus vester, &c. Non autem poteritis ab eis separari, nisi ejeceritis vxores alienigenas. Disparcultus dirimit contracta coniugia. Libellus repudij Iudaeis fuerat permissus, non tanquam quid licitum: sed tanquam minus malum, Deuteronomij vigesimo quarto capite.
units.tr: "And separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign wives." God so diligently forbade such dealings: Numbers 35; Deuteronomy 7; Joshua chapter 23. Take the greatest care, therefore, to love the LORD your God. But if you turn aside and cleave to the remnant of those nations, I mean those who are still among you, and make marriages with them, and they with you, then know for certain that the LORD your God will no longer drive out all these nations from before you; but they will be a snare and a stumbling-block to you, and scourges in your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land which the LORD your God has given you, and so on. You cannot be separated from them unless you cast out the foreign wives. Divorce dissolves marriages already contracted. A bill of divorce had been permitted to the Jews, not as something lawful, but as the lesser evil: Deuteronomy chapter 24.

units.la: 2 Quid responderit populus. Habita nimirum prius deliberatione, totus discedit in sententiam Esdrae: tantum petit dilationem bcgarend cines vfffdylag6/non vt res in spongiam abeat,vt hodie astuti homines solent res in aliud tempus reijcere,vel,vt interea ei insidias struant: sed quia vno die confici non poterat.
units.tr: 2 What the people answered. Clearly, after deliberation had first taken place, the whole assembly agreed with Ezra's judgement. They only asked for a delay, not so that the matter might come to nothing, as clever men today are wont to put things off to another time, or so that they might lay plots against him in the meantime, but because it could not be finished in a single day.

units.la: Et responderunt totus coetus,ae dixerunt voce magna, sic sicut dum verbum tuum nobis est faciendum.) Non vt in huiusmodi causibus fit,diuersae sunt sententiae, sed quasi vno ore omnes alta voce diserte dicunt,omnino sic agendum vt Esdras dixit. Multis nihil placet quod a verbi ministris proficisci tur. At populus multus est, & pluuiarum tempus est, neq; est vis ad standum foris.) Petunt translationem loci, temporis, personarum,causis redditis. Non sunt vires populo, vt constat sub dio propter imbrem. Exercitus quoque tempore pluuio, vix possunt contineri a ducibus in aperto campo. Si castra mouentur tempore pluuio, & iter faciendum est,praesertim nocturno tempore, milites valde sunt impatientes, & maledicunt suis ducibus, &c.
units.tr: "And the whole assembly answered and said with a loud voice, 'As you have said, so we must do.'" It was not as happens in such cases, when opinions differ; rather, all speak with one voice, plainly and loudly, that it must be done altogether as Ezra has said. Many people dislike anything that comes from the ministers of the Word. "But the people are many, and it is the time of rain, and there is no strength to stand outside." They ask for the matter to be moved to another place, time and persons, giving their reasons. The people have no strength to stand in the open under the rain, as is clear. Armies too, in rainy weather, can scarcely be kept in check by their leaders in the open field. If camp is struck in rainy weather and the march must be made, especially by night, the soldiers become very impatient and curse their commanders, and so on.

units.la: Adhaec dicunt, hoc negotium non vno aut altero die expediri pediri posse,quia multi sint qui hac in re peccarint, quòd alie- nigenas vxores duxerint. Confultum igitur fore , vt aliquot delectis viris,nomine totius coetus , illa censura & disquisitio- nis negotium committatur , qui illis quos hinc inde vxores in vrbibus alienigenas duxisse constet , idoneo tempore diem & horam dicant , quaad consistorium vel forum matrimoniale veniant,& vna cum eis seniores & iudices singularum vrbium (nam iudices priuilegio regio constituti erant) donec iram Dei à fe auertant , hoc est , per poenitentiam suam placent Deum ipsis iratum & infestum. Volunt vt ferió in hoc negotio agatur.
units.tr: Moreover they say that this business cannot be settled in one or two days, because there are many who have sinned in this matter by taking foreign wives. It would therefore be well to entrust the work of this examination and inquiry to some chosen men, in the name of the whole assembly, who should appoint a suitable day and hour for those whom it is established have taken foreign wives in the towns here and there to come to the consistory or matrimonial court, and together with them the elders and judges of each town (for the judges had been appointed by royal privilege), until they turn away God's anger, that is, until they appease God, who is angry with them and hostile, by their repentance. They wish the matter to be handled quickly.

units.la: Vsus.
units.tr: Use.

units.la: 1 Quæ totius Ecclesiæ sunt, ad totam Ecclesiam referen- da esse. Esdras ad totum populum refert negotium illud de matrimonio ( ad omnes enim pertinebat ) non vi agit & im- perio. Diuus Petrus in Actis primo capite, conuocata tota multitudine fidelium , cum ea agit de surrogando Apostolo in locum Iudæ proditoris. Capite sexto amicè agit cum to- ta Ecclesia de publicis opibus : & liberam omnibus dicendi facultatem permittit. Aut si ab Ecclesia paucis ad vitandam confusionem, & alia pericula eæ res committantur, illi ad re- gulam verbi Dei omnia debent comparare. Qui successione Apostolorum falso gloriantur,pro suo arbitrio, imò libidine e- tiam illa obtrudunt alijs,quæ ex diametro cum verbo Dei pu- gnant. Non rebus in medium propositis , cum tota Ecclesia consultant:sed Ecclesiæ Domini superbè dominantur. In libe- ris rebus publicis,ad conseruandam concordiam non parum facit,si res communes quæ magni sunt momenti, non à pau- cis tractentur , sed ad plebem quoque referantur. Si pauci consenientes decernant quod alijs præscribant nolentibus volentibus , magnæ simultates sæpe,etiam seditiones ori- antur.
units.tr: 1 Those things which belong to the whole Church are to be referred to the whole Church. Ezra refers that matter of marriage to the whole people (for it concerned all of them), and does not act by force and command. Blessed Peter, in the first chapter of Acts, having called together the whole multitude of the faithful, deals with them about choosing an apostle in place of Judas the traitor. In the sixth chapter he deals kindly with the whole Church about the public funds, and allows everyone the freedom to speak. Or if such matters are committed by the Church to a few, to avoid confusion and other dangers, those few must prepare everything according to the rule of the Word of God. Those who falsely boast of succession from the Apostles impose on others, at their own pleasure, and indeed by their lust, things that flatly contradict the Word of God. They do not lay matters before the people and consult the whole Church, but proudly lord it over the Church of the Lord. In free commonwealths, it contributes not a little to keeping concord if matters of common concern, which are of great importance, are not handled by a few but are also referred to the common people. If a few agree to decree what they prescribe to others who are unwilling, great enmities, and often even seditions, arise.

units.la: 2 Exemplum præclarum habemus obedientiæ populi er- ga suum magistratum. Populus frequens adfuit loco & tem- pore præscripto : nihil deterritus difficultate temporis : clarè autem testatur sibi consilium Esdræ probari. Non dicunt,ago videamus quis nobis imperare velit , vt vxores nostras abiga- mus &c. nostrum plures sunt. Semper erunt qui bonis consi- lijs obsequantur.Subiecti statim in rebus verbo Dei consenta- neis,obsequantur suis dominis,non tumultuentur.
units.tr: 2 We have an outstanding example of the obedience of the people towards their magistrate. The people came in full numbers to the place and time appointed; not deterred by the difficulty of the time, they clearly bore witness that they approved Ezra's counsel. They do not say, "Let us see who wants to command us to put away our wives," and so on. There are many of us. There will always be those who obey good counsels. Subjects, when matters are in agreement with the Word of God, should obey their lords at once and not make tumult.

units.la: 3 Verae poenitentiae exemplum proponitur nobis in hoc populo, ad quam praecipue requiritur, vt peccatorum nostrorum grauitatem agnoscamus, & gloriam Deo demus, quod ipse iustus sit, nos peccatores: Vtque vitemus mala, & bona faciamus. Illi enim vxores quas contra verbum Dei duxerant, iussu seniorum, à se dimittunt, &c.
units.tr: 3 In this people we are set an example of true repentance, for which it is especially required that we acknowledge the gravity of our sins, and give glory to God, that he is just and we are sinners; and that we avoid evils and do good. For those men put away from themselves, by the command of the elders, the wives whom they had taken contrary to the Word of God, and so on.

units.la: Multum autem ad poenitentiam facit exemplum procerum. Fructus quoq; poenitentiae hic insignis est, quod per eam Deus placatur.
units.tr: The example of the leading men contributes much to repentance. The fruit of repentance is also remarkable here, that through it God is appeased.

units.la: 4 Multitudo & authoritas peccantium: item diuturnitas temporis, peccata non excusant. Multi erant, vt ipsemet fatetur qui duxerant vxores alienigenas: haec matrimonia diu durarant, primarij viri illa nō reprehendisse leguntur: at haec omnia non possunt rectum efficere, quod sua natura prauum existit. His rebus hodie falsam religionem & vitiosos mores multi defendere conantur. Propter haec ipsa non conniuendum est ad flagitia, quasi seditiones oriturae sint, si flagitiosos castigare voluerimus, &c.
units.tr: 4 The number and authority of those who sin, and likewise the length of time, do not excuse sins. There were many, as he himself confesses, who had taken foreign wives; these marriages had lasted a long time, and we read that the chief men did not rebuke them. But none of these things can make right what is wrong by its very nature. Today many try to defend false religion and corrupt morals by these same arguments. For this reason we must not wink at wickedness, as if seditions would arise if we wished to punish the wicked, and so on.

units.la: 5 Quales iudices sint deligendi qui causas matrimoniales tractent. Hi volunt vt primarij deligantur, item vt seniores quoque & iudices ex oppidis illis adsint, ex quibus citabantur qui alienigenas duxerant, vt res grauiter ageretur. Solent quidam iudices matrimoniales per iocum deligere, illos maximè quos sperant moechis & scortis parsuros esse.
units.tr: 5 What kind of judges should be chosen to deal with matrimonial causes. They want the leading men to be chosen, and likewise the elders and judges from those towns from which those who had taken foreign wives were summoned, so that the matter might be handled seriously. Some matrimonial judges are wont to choose, in jest, those whom they hope will spare adulterers and prostitutes.

units.la: 6 Esdras iubet, illos dimittere vxores alienigenas, Deus iubet te meretrices, ebrietatem, superbiam & alia scelera relinquere, Deo itaq; obtemperemus.
units.tr: 6 Ezra commands them to put away their foreign wives; God commands you to leave off harlots, drunkenness, pride and other crimes. Let us therefore obey God.

units.la: HOMILIA XXXVIII.
units.tr: HOMILY XXXVIII.

units.la: Exequuntur quae in comitijs populi decreta sunt.
units.tr: They carry out what was decreed in the assembly of the people.

units.la: 15 Veruntamen Ionathan filius Asahel, & Iahaziah filius Thicuah, constituti fuerunt super hoc, & Mesullam, & Sabethai Leuites adiuuerunt eos.
units.tr: 15 Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahaziah son of Tikvah were appointed over this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them.

units.la: 16 Et fecerunt ita filij transmigrationis, & separatifunt, Ezra, & viri principes familiarum per domum patrum suorum, & vniuersi ipsi per nomina: sederunt itaq; die prima, mensis decimi, vt quaererent rem.
units.tr: 16 So the children of the exile did so, and Ezra, with the heads of the families by their fathers' houses, and all of them by name, were set apart. They sat down on the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter.

units.la: 17 Perfecerunt q; negotium ipsum in omnibus viris qui duxerant vxores alienigenas, vsq; ad diem primam mensis primi.
units.tr: 17 They finished the business with all the men who had married foreign wives, by the first day of the first month.

units.la: 18 Et inuenti sunt de filijs Sacerdotum, qui duxerant vxores alienigenas: de filijs Iesua filij Iosadac, & fratrum eius, Maaseiah, & Eliezer, & Iarib, & Gedaliah.
units.tr: 18 And there were found among the sons of the priests who had married foreign wives: of the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers, Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib and Gedaliah.

units.la: 19 Et dederunt manum suam vt educerent vxores suas: & qui dereliquerant, (venerunt) cum ariete pecorum pro delicto suo.
units.tr: 19 And they gave their hands that they would put away their wives, and being guilty, they offered a ram of the flock for their trespass.

units.la: 20 Et de filijs Immer, Lanani, & Zebadiah.
units.tr: 20 And of the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.

units.la: 21 Et de filijs Harim, Maaseia, & Elijah, & Semaaiah, & Iehiel, & Vzziiah.
units.tr: 21 And of the sons of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel and Uzziah.

units.la: 22 Et de filijs Pashur, Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ismael, & Nethanel, Iozabad, & Elasah.
units.tr: 22 And of the sons of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad and Elasah.

units.la: 23 Et de Leuitis, Iozabad, & Simi, & Celaiah (ipse(est) Celitah, Pethahiah, Iehudah, & Eliezer.
units.tr: 23 And of the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah and Eliezer.

units.la: 24 De cantoribus vero Eliasib: & de ianitoribus Sallum, & Telem, & Vri.
units.tr: 24 Of the singers, Eliashib; and of the gatekeepers, Shallum, Telem and Uri.

units.la: 25 Et de Israele: de filijs Paros, Ramiah, & Iezijah, & Malchijah, & Mijamim, & Elazar, & Malchijah, & Benaiah.
units.tr: 25 And of Israel: of the sons of Parosh, Ramiah, Jeziah, Malchiah, Miamin, Eleazar, Malchijah and Benaiah.

units.la: 26 De filijs autem Elam, Matthaniah, Zechariah, Iehiel, & Abdi, Ieremoth, & Elijah.
units.tr: 26 Of the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth and Elijah.

units.la: 27 Et de filijs Zatthu, Elioenai, Eliasib, Mat thaniah, & Ieremoth, & Zabad, & Aziza.
units.tr: 27 And of the sons of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad and Aziza.

units.la: 28 De filijs praeterea Bebai, Iehohanam, Hananiah, Zabbai, & Athlai.
units.tr: 28 Also of the sons of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai and Athlai.

units.la: 29 De filijs autem Bani, Mesullam, Malluch, & Adaiah, Iasub, & Seal, Ieramoth.
units.tr: 29 And of the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal and Jeremoth.

units.la: 30 Et de filijs Pahathmoah, Adna, & Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Matthaniah, Besalel, Bimmi, & Menasseh.
units.tr: 30 And of the sons of Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui and Manasseh.

units.la: 31 De filijs vero Harim, Eliezer, Ishijah, Malchijah, Semaiah, Simon.
units.tr: 31 Of the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Ishijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon.

units.tr: 32 Benjamin, Malluch, Shemariah.

units.tr: 33 Of the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, Shimei.

units.tr: 34 Of the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram and Uel.

units.la: 35 Benaiah, Bediah, Chelhu,
units.tr: 35 Benaiah, Bedeiah, Kelluhi,

units.la: 36 Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliasib,
units.tr: 36 Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,

units.la: 37 Matthaniah, Matthenai, Iaasan,
units.tr: 37 Mattaniah, Mattenai, Jaasu,

units.la: 38 Et Bani, & Bimmi, Simi,
units.tr: 38 And Bani, and Binnui, Shimei,

units.la: 39 Et Selemiah, & Nathan, & Adaiah,
units.tr: 39 And Shelemiah, and Nathan, and Adaiah,

units.la: 40 Machnadebai, Safui, Sarai,
units.tr: 40 Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,

units.la: 41 Azarel, & Selemiahu, Semariah,
units.tr: 41 Azarel, and Shelemiah, Shemariah,

units.tr: 43 Of the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jadau, and Joel, Benaiah.

units.la: 44 Omnes hi acceperunt vxores alienigenas: (qui hujusdam) autem ex eis erant mulieres quae posuerant filios.
units.tr: 44 All these had taken foreign wives, and some of them were women who had borne children.

units.la: DE exequutione illorum, quae in comitijs decreta sunt, iam deinceps agitur. Primùm enim indicatur, qui & quales censores sint constituti. Deinde quo pacto se gesserint. Praefecti sunt huic negotio, Ionathan & Iahazias principes Israelis: quibus duo Leuitæ additi sunt, qui nimirum Dei legem eis suggererét. Et fecerunt ita filij transmigrationis.) Sicut inter eos convenerat, dimissus est conuentus constitutis certis hominibus, qui decretum concilij exequerentur. Separati sunt, hoc est, selecti, Esdras & viri nominati, id est, insignes, nobiles, illustres, nambaffte leiit/precipui patres familiarum, vel pernomina.) hoc est, nominatim sunt designati, qui praefecti fuerunt huic negotio. Hi omnes censores vel iudices in foro matrimoniali sunt constituti.
units.tr: Now follows the carrying out of what was decreed in the assembly. First it is shown who and what sort of censors were appointed. Then how they conducted themselves. Jonathan and Jahaziah, leaders of Israel, were put in charge of this business, and two Levites were added to them, who were to set the law of God before them. And the children of the exile did so. As had been agreed among them, the assembly was dismissed once certain men had been appointed to carry out the decree of the council. They were set apart, that is, chosen: Ezra and the men named, that is, the notable, noble, illustrious, and chief heads of families (the Hebrew word is nambaffte leiit), or by name, that is, they were designated by name, those who were placed in charge of this business. All these men were appointed as censors or judges in the matrimonial court.

units.la: Quomodo hi delecti viri se gesserint. Non quia negotium illud plenum erat invidia, reiecerunt à se: sed dicuntur illud exequuti esse, sed diffecq; die prima mensis decimi, Cisleu, vsq; ad diem primum mensis prim, qui Abib & Nisan appellatur. Triù itaq; mensium tempus consumpserunt in hoc negotio. Reos vocarunt, re non diu protracta: & omnes quidem, qui vxores alienigenas duxerant, vocarunt, nemini propter potentiam vel authoritatem parcentes.
units.tr: How these chosen men conducted themselves: they did not put the business aside because it was full of ill will, but they are said to have carried it through, and they finished it from the first day of the tenth month, Kislev, to the first day of the first month, which is called Abib or Nisan. They spent three months on this business. They summoned the accused, without dragging the matter out long, and they summoned all who had married foreign wives, sparing no one because of power or authority.

units.la: Quæri hoc loco posset, an non iudices illi, breuiore tempo-ris sparis spacio potuissent hoc negotium perficere: quid opus erat omnes vocare:cur nō promulgarunt decretum,vt omnes quot quot vxores Ethnicas duxissent,eas statim dimitteret?Respondeo,eos omnia explorata habere voluisse, quo ad illa coniugia, deinde de alijs quoq; rebus tractandum fuisse:Iudæos enim imi tatos fuisse mores Chananæorum in multis,ex initio 9. cap.videtur colligi.
units.tr: Here one might ask why those judges could not have finished the business in a shorter time, why it was necessary to summon everyone, and why they did not publish a decree that all who had married foreign women should dismiss them at once. I answer that they wanted to have everything examined concerning those marriages, and that other matters also had to be dealt with, for it appears from the ninth chapter at the beginning that the Jews had in many ways imitated the customs of the Canaanites.

units.la: Quis vero fuit eucatus?Inuenerút inter filios sacerdotum & Leuitarum,qui vxores exteras duxerant. Ponútur pontificij generis Iesu pontificis maximi nepotes.Nostris quoq; tempo-ribus ministrorum ecclesiæ liberi , aliquando diffolutius vi-uunt alijs.
units.tr: Who indeed was involved? They found among the sons of the priests and the Levites those who had married foreign wives. The grandsons of Jeshua the high priest are named, the offspring of the pontiffs. In our own times too, the children of ministers of the Church sometimes live more loosely than others.

units.la: Additur autem manus suas cito dedisse, & vxores suas dimisisse. Dare manus significat se dedere, & victum agnoscere. M. Tullius: Ad extremum det manus, vinciq; se patiatur. Vel, data manu promiserunt,se dimissuros vxores peregrinas. Cum arietepecorum pro delicto suo.) Scilicet venerunt,vel expiarunt peccata sua holocausto coram toto populo suum peccatum confitentes & damnantes.
units.tr: It is added that they quickly gave their hands and dismissed their wives. To give hands signifies to surrender oneself and acknowledge defeat. Cicero: "At last let him give his hands and suffer himself to be bound." Or, having given their hand, they promised that they would dismiss their foreign wives. With a ram of the flock for their trespass. That is, they came, or made atonement for their sins with a burnt offering before the whole people, confessing and condemning their sin.

units.la: Subijcitur Catalogus illorum qui alienigenas vxores duxe-runt : & primo loco ponuntur sacerdotum & Leuitarum filij, deinde proceres & v alius.
units.tr: A catalogue follows of those who had taken foreign wives, and first place is given to the sons of the priests and the Levites, then to the nobles and the rest.

units.la: Additur in calce capitis, aliquot ex his vxoribus,suis mari-tis filios peperisse.Quod facit ad amplificandam eorum obedi-entiam. Etenim neq; pietas in sobolem, neq; affectus erga vxo-res obstitit, quo minus facerent quod Esdras ex verbo Dei do-cebat. Nominantur in vniuersum 112. qui contra legem se com-miscuerunt cum alienigenis.
units.tr: At the end of the chapter it is added that some of these women had borne sons to their husbands. This serves to magnify their obedience. For neither love of offspring nor affection for their wives stood in the way of their doing what Ezra taught from the word of God. In all 112 are named who had defiled themselves against the law by mixing with foreign women.

units.la: Vsus.
units.tr: Use.

units.la: 1. Colligimus ex his verbis,opus esse in populo viris, qui bus censu a morum ac disciplinæ committatur. Nam vt in hoc populo multi mulieres legitimas reiecerunt,& duxerunt exteras : ita multa alia contra bonos mores fiunt. Habent quaedam vrbes forum matrimoniale, quod disciplinam custodire debet, item suos inquisitores, nachgenger. Apud Romanos cura morum ad censores spectabat.Quorum tanta fuit authoritas,vt quos indignos iudicaret,senatu amouerent. In corrigendis moribus sueri erant. Græci quoq; suos magistratus habuerunt, qui legum morumq; diligentem rationem haberent. Nomophylaces præpositi erant legibus feruandis. Iuuenum moribus præfecti fuerunt Sophroniftæ, mulieribus Gynæcocofmi, qui in parum modestas animaduerterent. Corinthus legem habuit sumtua-riam, quæ damnauit otium, cuius sit mentio apud Athen. 6. lib. & in Erasmi Chiliadibus, si quis splendide obsonabat, interro-gabant vnde haberet, &c.
units.tr: 1. We gather from these words that there is need, among the people, of men to whom the censorship of morals and discipline should be entrusted. For just as many men in this people put away their lawful wives and took foreign ones, so many other things are done against good morals. Some cities have a marriage court, which ought to guard discipline, and likewise their own inquisitors, nachgenger. Among the Romans the care of morals belonged to the censors, whose authority was so great that they removed from the senate those whom they judged unworthy. They were severe in correcting morals. The Greeks too had their magistrates, who kept a careful watch over laws and morals. The Nomophylakes were set over the keeping of the laws. The Sophronistae were appointed over the conduct of young men, the Gynaecocosmi over women, who punished those who were too immodest. Corinth had a sumptuary law, which condemned idleness; there is mention of it in Athenaeus, book 6, and in Erasmus's Adages: if anyone gave a splendid banquet, they asked where he got the money, and so on.

units.la: Quales vero deputandi sint inquisitioni & censuræ, etiam ex hoc loco potest elici. Iudæi pios magnæq; fidei viros delege-runt. Iosephus dicit, non deleētos fuisse qui eidem sceleri obno-xij fuerint: nam qui alios corrigere vult, debet immunis esse ab illis sceleribus, propter quæ alios reprehendit.
units.tr: What kind of men ought to be chosen for inquiry and censure can also be drawn from this passage. The Jews chose pious men of great faith. Josephus says that those who were liable to the same crime were not chosen; for whoever wishes to correct others ought to be free from those very crimes for which he reprehends them.

units.la: Qui ordinantur, hoc onus in se recipiant, etsi coniunctum sit cum magna molestia, odio, inimicitijs. Quisq; enim illa face-re debet, quæ ad patriæ salutem & ecclesiæ conseruationem per-tinent.
units.tr: Those who are appointed should take this burden upon themselves, even though it is joined with great trouble, hatred and enmities. For each one ought to do those things which pertain to the safety of the homeland and the preservation of the Church.

units.la: Sedulò autem & non perfunctorie suum faciant officium. Inquirant, vt illi, sceleratos, sacrilegos, surarios, & adulteros, idq; celeri-ter, rem non pretrahant in multos menses. Omnes autem cor-rigant, non tantum homines infimæ conditionis: quidam cessant cum ad coryphæos scelerum ventum est.
units.tr: Let them perform their duty carefully and not carelessly. Let them search out, as those men did, the wicked, the sacrilegious, thieves and adulterers, and do so quickly, not dragging the matter out for many months. Let them correct all, not only men of the lowest rank: some hold back when they come to the ringleaders of wickedness.

units.la: 2. Imitanda est probitas & modestia filiorum sacerdotum & Leuitarum. Antea offenderant suo exemplo alios, vt fit, iam cito præbuerunt manus, & peccatum suum publicè sacrificio oblato testati sunt, vnde populus quoq; obsequetior factus est. Nec pudeat quenquam suum errorem vel peccatum suum fa-teri & emendare.
units.tr: 2. The uprightness and modesty of the sons of the priests and Levites is to be imitated. Earlier they had given offence to others by their example, as happens, but now they quickly gave their hands, and by offering a sacrifice they publicly testified to their sin, whence the people also became more compliant. Let no one be ashamed to confess and amend his own error or sin.

units.la: 3. Ingentem vero consolationem ex hoc loco elicimus, quòd Deus in rebus arduis & difficilibus, felicè dare successum velit & possit, breui enim omnia perfecit Esdras. Si diligentius consideremus, res fuit maxima, & cum ingenti periculo coniun-cta. Quis non putaret Esdram rem impossibilem moliri? Quis enim nescit vel à scortis suis homines vix posse auelli, nedum ab vxoribus quas putabant se iusto titulo habere, & ex quibus aliquot iam liberos sustulerant. Dicere poterant, inde atrox bel-lum oriturum: vicinos enim non recepturos filias corruptas, sed potius arma eis illaturos. Multi erant & præcipui, qui hac in re peccauerant. Liberos non libenter dimittimus: diu habue-rat exteras mulieres. Crudelis Esdras videri potuit, qui liberos & fœminas à maritis & parentibus diuellere conaretur. Quia vero Esdras hæc coniugia non vera esse intelligit, sed aduersari legi diuinæ, non desperat, rem fortiter & prudenter aggreditur, & ad optatum finem deducit. Dedit enim Deus suam gratiam, vt vnanimi consensu res fuerit perfecta. Ne vnus quidem fuit in illis comitijs, qui seditiose se ei opposuerit, aut sibi iniuriam fieri questus fit.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, from this passage we draw a great consolation: that God is willing and able to grant success in difficult and arduous matters, for Ezra accomplished everything in a short time. If we consider more carefully, the matter was very great and joined with immense danger. Who would not have thought Ezra was attempting an impossible thing? For who does not know that men can scarcely be torn even from their harlots, much less from wives whom they thought they held by a just title, and by whom they had already brought forth several children? They could say that a fierce war would arise from this, for the neighbours would not receive their corrupted daughters, but would rather bring arms against them. Many were both prominent and had sinned in this matter. We are not willing to let go of our children: they had long had foreign women. Ezra might have seemed cruel, in trying to tear children and women away from husbands and parents. But because Ezra understood that these marriages were not true, but opposed to the divine law, he did not despair; he undertook the matter bravely and prudently and brought it to the desired end. For God gave His grace, so that the business was completed with unanimous consent. There was not even one in those assemblies who opposed him seditiously or complained that an injury was being done to him.

units.la: Multa nos hodie absterrent, ne flagitia grassantia corrigamus. Querimur rem esse periculi plenam, nos esse paucos, neminem nobis esse auxilio, cum operi manum nunquam admouerimus. Quid patrum memoria accidit? nonne pauci heroes religionem oppressam tyrannide Antichristi, repurgarunt, pulsa superstitione? Quid adhuc pauci interdum faciant, vt prius uatis suis commodis consulant, notum est. Si idem agerent in corrigendis vsuris modicis, ebrietate, adulterijs & alijs sceleribus, Deus bone quid non efficerent? Sed quia vacui fide & igna ui sunt, in omni via iacet leo, sub omni lapide latet scorpius. Nō cogitant Deum hodie quoq; pijs conatibus adesse velle. Si non primo die assequamur quòd volumus, forte alio tempore nobis dabitur, modo officium nostrum faciamus.
units.tr: Many things today deter us from correcting the crimes that are rampant. We complain that the matter is full of danger, that we are few, that no one helps us, since we have never laid a hand to the work. What happened in the memory of our fathers? Did not a few heroes, when the religion was oppressed by the tyranny of Antichrist, cleanse it and drive out superstition? What the few still sometimes do, seeking first the advantages of their own, is well known. If they did the same in correcting moderate usury, drunkenness, adulteries and other crimes, good God, what would they not accomplish? But because they are empty of faith and strength, a lion lies in every way, and a scorpion lurks under every stone. They do not think that God wishes to be present today also to pious efforts. If we do not attain on the first day what we want, perhaps it will be given to us at another time, provided we do our duty.

units.la: Celebrem fore gloriam illorum, qui suo munere recte funguntur et à sceleribus abstinent, ex hoc catalogo colligitur.
units.tr: The renown of those who discharge their office rightly and abstain from wickedness is seen to be famous from this catalogue.

Line 39: for "devastation" read "Sal". Fol. 34, col. b, line 19: read "was upon them". Fol. 47, col. b, line 35: "showing how". Fol. 48, line 1: read "were opposing". Fol. 54, col. b, line 13: "he has not received the crown". Fol. 55, line 34: "yet very greatly". Fol. 59, line 24: "it is no wonder". Fol. 81, line 10: "excessive usury". The remaining minor errors, anyone can easily correct.
